“We all have bad games, we all make mistakes, but there’s no excuse not to give your maximum.

”For West Ham to get a result against Millwall, every player is going to have to give 100 per cent because Millwall definitely will.”

Sports.title: 'I lost to Ben Shelton at the US Open but I couldn't watch the final because of Alexander Zverev'
Sports.content:
'I lost to Ben Shelton at the US Open but I couldn't watch the final because of Alexander Zverev'

The tennis star has hit out at Alexander Zverev after the German won the US Open this month

View 3 Images Tallon Griekspoor has had his say on Alexander Zverev (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Tennis star Tallon Griekspoor launched an astonishing take-down of US Open champion Alexander Zverev. Top seed Zverev won his second Grand Slam this season as he followed up his success at the French Open with victory in New York on September 13.

‌



The German defeated first-time grand slam finalist Ben Shelton 6-3, 7-6(2), 5-7, 6-2 in the Flushing Meadows showpiece. World No. 55 Griekspoor, who was beaten in the first round by Shelton, hit out at Zverev for constantly slowing the game down by bouncing the ball before serving and claimed he couldn't watch the final.

‌



"The US Open final? Pretty mediocre," Griekspoor told De Telegraaf. "There were other sports going on, and I honestly struggle to watch Zverev. He bounced the ball 400 times before every serve. It was extreme, but clearly it worked for him. Maybe I should try it too.”

‌



Ahead of the final, ESPN claimed the German player had bounced the ball an incredible 13,000 times across six matches. Shelton himself even criticised the routine after the final.

Giving his take on the match itself, Griekspoor added: "Shelton was very inconsistent and gave away two or three free points every game. You can see what a first Slam final can do to a player. Zverev wasn’t exceptional, but he served really well. The second-set tiebreak was crucial.”

US Open champion rushed for emergency surgery days after lifting title READ MORE :

John McEnroe slammed for 'unprofessional' comments immediately after US Open final READ MORE :

Shelton beat defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-final and American star Frances Tiafoe in the last four. The US Open was Alcaraz’s first tournament since April after being ruled out for four months with a serious wrist injury.

‌



View 3 Images Alexander Zverev has been criticised by a fellow professional (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Dutch talent Griekspoor believes the American was lucky to beat the Spaniard. He said: “Alcaraz should have beaten him in the quarter-finals, but he played a nightmare fifth-set tiebreak.

"Then he walked off the court smiling. That made me feel like his expectations were different. He hadn’t arrived at the tournament at his best, so I think he and his team were already satisfied."

‌



He didn't stop there. Asked if Zverev can pose a genuine threat to a fully fit and firing Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner, the current world No. 1, he said: “Absolutely not. It doesn’t even cross my mind.

View 3 Images Alexander Zverev beat Ben Shelton in the final (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

"I hope they both get back to their best soon. But if either of them goes out during a tournament, Zverev is always there to take advantage. I wouldn’t be surprised at all if he ended up winning four or five Grand Slam titles.”

Article continues below

On Friday, Griekspoor walked back his comments on Zverev via X. He posted: "It's starting to get out of hand. I normally don't react here, but it's starting to get out of hand (laughs).

"I was just saying it was hard (the US Open final) to watch because of the endless bounces. Nothing but praise for Sascha for everything he has accomplished this year!"

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola sends fresh Florian Wirtz Liverpool plea after Jurgen Klopp warning
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola sends fresh Florian Wirtz Liverpool plea after Jurgen Klopp warning

Andoni Iraola was speaking to the media on Friday afternoon to preview Liverpool Premier League game against Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium this weekend

View 2 Images Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola (Image: (Andrew Powell/Liverpool FC via Getty Images))

Andoni Iraola has called on Florian Wirtz to be judged like everyone else as his performances for Liverpool continue to come under scrutiny. The Reds won the battle to land the German international last summer when they paid a then British-record £116m to sign him from Bayer Leverkusen.

‌



But the 23-year-old struggled to settle in his first season at Anfield, ending with seven goals and 10 assists in 49 appearances across all competitions. And his performances so far this season have also come under scrutiny as the attacking midfielder only has one assist to his name.

‌



However, defending Wirtz on Friday afternoon, Iraola said: “He should be judged like everyone else, he works. How does the team play when you are on the pitch?

‌



“I am very happy with Florian, he understands what we need in every aspect of the game. We want to add assists and goals but he is helping us in all areas."

Sports.title: Police prepare for derby trouble as Millwall vs West Ham and Wolves vs West Brom return
Sports.content:
Police forces are expected to have their work cut out this weekend, with derby matches in the Championship and beyond. Saturday's early kick-off sees Millwall take on West Ham for the first time in over 14 years before Wolves and West Brom renew their rivalry at 12pm on Sunday.

Eyes were drawn to mid-September as soon as the fixture list was confirmed in June. Both West Ham and Wolves came down from the Premier League and these clashes were among the first that fans looked for.

The scheduling has given officers, the Metropolitan Police in particular, a huge task, as they work to prevent trouble and stop tensions from boiling over. Not to mention the rest of the weekend's London fixtures which include Brentford versus Chelsea on Friday night and Fulham against Manchester United on Sunday afternoon.

But it's not just forces across England braced for trouble either. In Glasgow, Celtic and Rangers will clash at Parkhead just one week after doing so at Ibrox.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Millwall vs West Ham

February 2012 marked the last time that these two London clubs faced off. To sum up the rivalry, former West Ham captain Julian Dicks was hit by a brick while defending a corner away to Millwall in December 1998.

The Met are planning to deploy roughly 400 officers in an around The Den which is four times the usual number. Officers will be in riot gear, although won't have shields, and each of them will be trained to deal with public disorder.

‌



Dog units, mounted police and live facial recognition cameras will also be used as part of the operation. Rival fans will be told to use specific Tube and rail stations travelling to and from the game.

View 6 Images Similar scenes to 2012 are expected before Millwall play West Ham (Image: Matthew Lloyd/Getty Images)

The Met also issued a statement ahead of Saturday's match which read: "On Saturday, 19 September at 12:30hrs, @MillwallFC face @WestHam at the Den - the first time the two clubs have met since 2012. We want fans to enjoy the match safely and have worked with both clubs to help this happen.

"As with any fixture, the Sporting Events Act 1985 is in place, which means entering or attempting to enter a ground while intoxicated is strictly prohibited. A Section 35 dispersal order will also be in place, allowing officers to remove anyone causing disorder. It will cover this area (below)."

‌



A League Cup tie between the teams in 2009 saw one man stabbed. Play also had to be stopped three times due to fans invading the pitch.

This week, injured West Ham midfielder Tomas Soucek was filmed being threatened by a Millwall fan. In a video clip shared on social media, Soucek was warned: "If I see you at the Den next Saturday I'm going to cut your f***ing face off, you c***."

View 6 Images West Ham star Tomas Soucek was threatened by a Millwall supporter (Image: Dave Benett/Getty Images for BGC Group)

Wolves vs West Brom

Fans of these two Midlands clubs haven't needed to wait very long for this fixture to come back around. They last met in the FA Cup in January 2024, as Wolves won 2-0 at The Hawthorns.

‌



But that wasn't the story. The players were forced to leave the pitch for 35 minutes after violent fights broke out, with missiles also thrown.

In a joint statement published on Thursday, both Wolves and West Brom reminded supporters that a total of 43 people were arrested, with 12 of them were charged and sentenced by the courts. One Football Banning Order was issued while five supporters received permanent club bans.

View 6 Images The game was stopped for over half an hour last time Wolves faced West Brom (Image: Jack Thomas - WWFC/Wolves via Getty Images)

It is the first time that these two arch enemies have met at Molineux - in front of supporters - since February 2012, with the Baggies winning 5-1 and pushing Wolves further towards relegation.

‌



The two clubs also asked that home and away supporters only use tickets purchased through official channels and urged them to sit in the correct areas at Molineux. The statement added: "Both clubs have worked closely with the Safety Advisory Group, local authorities and police to ensure appropriate arrangements are in place for the fixture.

"Supporters can expect enhanced stewarding, policing, robust ticketing controls and additional safety measures designed to protect everyone attending the match while allowing both sets of fans to enjoy the occasion."

View 6 Images Violence broke out between fans and police at The Hawthorns (Image: Getty Images/Getty Images)

Celtic vs Rangers

Those who joke that there's an Old Firm derby every week will be feeling smug right now. The pair of Glasgow heavyweights met for another bout last Sunday, with Rangers winning 3-0 at Ibrox in the Scottish League Cup.

‌



Now it's Celtic's turn to host their bitter rivals, as the teams resume their Scottish Premiership campaign. After ugly scenes during an Old Firm last season, no away fans will be permitted in games involving Celtic and Rangers this term.

But there were still arrests at the weekend. A Police Scotland officer was assaulted during the match at Ibrox and a 28-year-old man was cuffed in connection with the incident.

View 6 Images No away fans will attend the Old Firm derbies this season (Image: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Police made a total of four arrests during the one-sided quarter-final, including a 55-year-old man for sectarian abuse. Chief Superintendent Stevie Dolan thanked the 'majority of fans' for their behaviour, although he noted: "A small number of offences were detected during the course of the event.

‌



"These included one instance of police assault and a separate incident involving sectarian abuse. Behaviour such as this is never acceptable and will not be tolerated."

Sports.title: PGA Tour caddie quits job midway through round as he drops club, throws bib and storms off
Sports.content:
PGA Tour caddie quits job midway through round as he drops club, throws bib and storms off

One of the players was left dumbfounded by his caddie's behaviour

View 2 Images The golfer's caddie disappeared halfway through the opening round (Image: Getty Images)

The Biltmore Championship Asheville is up and running but the PGA Tour event was one to forget for Cliff Ellis. The caddie was carrying Alejandro Tosti's bag for the tournament but decided halfway through the round that he'd had enough.

‌



Tosti started his round on the 10th hole and was on the 18th when Ellis dropped the Argentine's club bag. He then proceeded to throw away his bib before walking off, it has been claimed.

‌



The South American golfer tried to see the funny side when asked about the matter by Golfweek. "He couldn’t keep up with eight pars in a row,” he wrote in a text to the publication, followed by three sideways laughing emojis.

‌



Tosti, who shot one over par in the opening round, has been known for his unpredictable reputation on tour and has worked with a number of different caddies during his career. Golfweek reported that there was tension between him and Ellis earlier in the week, though further details were scarce.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Tiger Woods makes first public golf appearance since car crash after taking break for treatment READ MORE :

During the Valspar Championship in March, Tosti had Joaquin Ali on caddying duties. It was there that he shared the message 'Need a wife' in all caps on Ali's back.

‌



“So the ladies that volunteer here were asking me, ‘do you have a wife’, I said ‘no’ and it came from there," he said at the time. "A lot of people were asking if it was my caddie that was needing a wife, but, no, it’s actually me.

“A lot of people were taking pictures and making fun of him and asking what was going on and, yeah, it was fun. I offer a lot of good stuff. I love cooking. I fly planes. I can play golf and have fun.”

View 2 Images Tosti carded a one over par opening round (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

The situation with Ellis wasn't the first time Tosti has courted drama, though previously his fellow players have been on the other side of it. In 2024, he was involved in what commentators described as a 'wild scenario' after a face-off with playing partner Tony Finau over who should putt first.

"You can cut the tension with a knife between Finau and Tosti right now," on-course announcer John Wood said of the pair. "They had another instance right there where they were trying to figure out who was away.

"Tony just pointed at him and walked away. Tosti kind of smiled as if to say 'You're kidding right?' It's just completely icy, it is not comfortable between those two at all. It's just tension."

Sports.title: Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac brutally mock Spygate saga ahead of Wrexham vs Southampton
Sports.content:
Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac brutally mock Spygate saga ahead of Wrexham vs Southampton

Wrexham and Southampton meet in the Championship this weekend and the Red Dragon's Hollywood owners have made some mischievous digs over the Spygate scandal

View Image Southampton fans had mocked the Spygate saga before their team was thrown out of the play-offs (Image: Ed Sykes/Getty Images)

Wrexham co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney have dropped a video poking fun at the 'Spygate' saga ahead of this weekend's meeting with Southampton.

‌



The Saints were expelled from the Championship play-offs after beating Middlesbrough to reach the final and docked four points after an intern was found observing their opponents during a training session, with further charges brought against the club for similar offences earlier in the season ahead of games against Oxford and Ipswich Town.

‌



Wrexham were one of the teams who narrowly missed out on a play-off spot last season, finishing seventh in the Championship.

‌



This time around, the club owned by Hollywood stars Reynolds and McElhenney - now also known by just Mac - are eager to go one better and reach the Premier League - and they have already stoked the flames ahead of a big game against Tonda Eckert's side.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



In the short video, which BBC Sport claims has not been well received by senior EFL figures, Reynolds and McElhenney make quips about privacy in a skit to promote their primary sponsor, Firefox.

After emerging from behind a tree with McElhenney, Reynolds says: "Today, for no particular reason, we want to talk about the importance of privacy." McElhenny then adds: "Specifically, how to prevent spies from seeing what you're doing."

The duo go on to namedrop Oxford, Ipswich and Middlesbrough after stating privacy is "important to people everywhere" before plugging Firefox's stance on privacy.

‌



Wrexham previously aimed a jab at Southampton when the Championship fixtures were unveiled, saying "check training ground" along with an asterisk that added "for unauthorised visitors" for the September block to tie in with the fixture against Southampton.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

While Eckert is still waiting to discover his punishment for the scandal, it has seemingly not hampered Southampton's start to the new campaign, with the Saints quickly wiping out their four-point penalty. They sit ninth on 10 points after winning four of their seven games, scoring 18 goals in the process.

‌



Phil Parkinson, Wrexham's manager, insists his only focus is on getting a result with all the talk of last season's controversial season conclusion put to bed. "We're the team which obviously were affected because we were seventh, but we accepted the EFL decision on that," he said.

"Southampton got punished for it and they've had to accept their punishment and move on.

"That's all I can say on it really, it's gone. We're concentrating on what we've got to do and likewise they're the same."

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney lands new job as BBC announce Man Utd legend's return
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney lands new job as BBC announce Man Utd legend's return

Wayne Rooney has been on everybody's screens as a pundit over the last year, but it now appears the Manchester United icon will be taking up a different challenge

View 4 Images Wayne Rooney will once again be a regular on the BBC (Image: BBC SPORT)

Manchester United icon Wayne Rooney will have his football knowledge put to the test in a new BBC show fronted by himself. The ex-England captain will be the protagonist of the new visualised podcast named 'Can You Beat Wayne Rooney?'

‌



It's the latest television project of the Three Lions' second highest goal-scorer, after he opened up his home to Disney's cameras for a new fly-on-the-wall documentary named 'The Real Rooneys'. Away from the streaming service, Rooney will be back with the tax-payer funded broadcaster for his latest project.

‌



He will face a new famous opponent every week in a test of football trivia with comedian Alex Brooker playing host on BBC Sport's Football YouTube channel and BBC iPlayer.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

In a statement, the BBC summed up the new show by writing: "While guests will arrive convinced they can beat him, every question unlocks a story from Wayne's extraordinary journey through football, taking audiences behind the scenes of dressing rooms, title races, international tournaments and some of the sport's most iconic moments.

"Whether revisiting famous goals, legendary teammates or career-defining matches, Can You Beat Wayne Rooney? offers football fans a unique opportunity to hear the stories behind the headlines while watching Wayne's competitive side emerge as he tries to protect his reputation against a fresh challenger every week."

‌



This is not the first time he has had his own show with the Beeb, as he fronted 'The Rooney Show' but the last episode of the series aired on July 17th. It's also suggested the new show has been inspired by the time Erling Haaland challenged him to row across New York's Hudson River, after Rooney pledged to do so if Norway beat Brazil in the World Cup, which they went on to do 2-1.

4 View 4 Images Rooney rowed across the Hudson River in New York after Haaland scored twice against Brazil (Image: bbcsport/Instagram) 4 View 4 Images It appears the show was inspired by Rooney's wager with Haaland (Image: bbcsport/Instagram)

‌



Speaking about his latest television venture, Rooney also said: "Anyone who knows me knows I’m competitive, whether it’s on a football pitch, playing paddle or on a golf course and even rowing on the Hudson River.

"When Erling called me out to honour my challenge after Norway beat Brazil, there was no way I was backing out. That’s probably why I know I’m going to enjoy this series so much.

"We’ve evolved the podcast to lean into that competitive side of my personality, because I know that’s something the people love to see. Every guest will turn up thinking they can beat me and, honestly, I don’t like losing.

‌



View 4 Images Rooney had his own show on the BBC throughout the World Cup (Image: 2026 Xavier Laine)

"A single question can take you straight back to a dressing room, a match or a moment you haven’t thought about in years. We’ve got some great guests lined up, plenty of laughs and some fantastic football conversations."

Rooney has fully steered into television and punditry after enduring some difficult moments as a manager. He has not been in charge of a club since he left Plymouth Argyle in 2024, a short seven-month spell which proceeded a nightmare 83-day run as Birmingham City manager.

Sports.title: Man Utd board held emergency meeting before sacking boss as Michael Carrick parallels emerge
Sports.content:
Man Utd board held emergency meeting before sacking boss as Michael Carrick parallels emerge

Manchester United fans have seen it all before following a poor start to the season under Michael Carrick

View 3 Images The pressure is mounting on Michael Carrick (Image: Getty Images)

It's hard to ignore the prospect of history repeating itself following Manchester United's stuttering start to the season under Michael Carrick. You know the script: Popular former player jettisoned in to lift a squad which had just seen an outspoken Portuguese head coach sacked.

‌



Said coach leads an upturn as interim boss and lands the job full-time to much fanfare, only to struggle when the pressure mounts and the results tail off. Sounds familiar, doesn't it?

‌



For Carrick replacing Ruben Amorim, read Ole Gunnar Solskjaer coming in for Jose Mourinho. It should be too early in the season for the United board to consider a change.

‌



But Sir Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS group, which runs the football side of the club, and the Glazers will be concerned after two defeats in four league games were followed by the Carabao Cup collapse against Brighton.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

In Solskjaer's case, the final straw was a 4-1 defeat at Watford in November 2021, the team's fourth defeat in five games. The credit the Norwegian had in the bank for leading the team to a runner-up finish - albeit a distant one - was running out.

‌



Michael Carrick is already under pressure at Man Utd - another defeat would be unthinkable READ MORE :

Kieran McKenna spotted in Man Utd directors' box as pressure on Michael Carrick READ MORE :

An emergency board meeting, which lasted several hours, was called after the Watford game, with Joel Glazer rubber-stamping the decision to dispense with Solskjaer. Almost five years on, Carrick could really do with a victory to take into the extended international break, which begins following Sunday's visit to struggling Fulham.

He claims not to feel under pressure, but he acknowledged the mounting external scrutiny after the Brighton humiliation. Carrick pointed to Everton's last-gasp equaliser and Manchester City's controversial derby winner, but he knows a reaction is needed.

View 3 Images Defeat to Fulham this weekend will leave Carrick under serious pressure

‌



He said: "Of course we can turn it around. We’ve got some really good players and it feels bad at the moment because we haven't had a great week, or two or three weeks.

"But it doesn't mean you can't win another game of football quickly, so there's that side of it. I mean, the players have shown before what they're capable of doing and we have as a group.

View 3 Images United have endured a poor start to the season

‌



"It doesn’t count for much; it's always about what happens next. What you're doing in the moment, what you're doing next, so that's the ultimate challenge. Always has been here, always will be here.

"It's all about what you do next and dealing with the moments, and the ups and the downs. We've certainly got to deal with this moment in a good way."

But the way things panned out with Solskjaer means Carrick cannot afford to relax, regardless of the esteem in which he is held.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel's baffling World Cup regret that left England fans stunned
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel's baffling World Cup regret that left England fans stunned

Thomas Tuchel is now focusing on England's Nations League campaign, which begins with a visit from Spain on September 26

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel has one regret from the World Cup (Image: Ryan Pierse - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel regrets not eating grass from the pitch following England's win over Mexico at the World Cup. The Three Lions boss will select his Nations League squad on Friday after collecting a bronze medal in the summer.

‌



A 3-2 win against Mexico was one of England's most memorable results, with Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane both scoring to send Tuchel's men into the quarter-finals to face Norway.

‌



While reminiscing on the result, Tuchel has revealed that he wishes he tasted some of the pitch to keep the memory forever inside him. Speaking on the FA’s official website, the German manager said: "If you needed any proof of what it meant to these players and how they were with each other, it was the moment when Jordan (Henderson) fell over and broke his arm (after the final whistle).

‌



"Like within a second, every single player was there stopping the celebrations, building a shield, protecting Jordan, not going nowhere in full empathy. It was just so special.

"I texted a friend after the match and I just wrote that I regret that I didn’t eat some grass after the match to keep something (from the experience) in my body forever. That was the feeling. That was the moment."

Despite falling to Argentina in the semi-final, Tuchel believes the bond has now formed between himself and the players. Describing the potential success on the horizon, the 52-year-old explained: "There’s a huge bond to these players, it feels like they are my players now.

‌



"This is the beauty of it, when you have a manager and you have success and you have painful moments together. You have so much time together and you create a natural bond. I’m happy to see them, I’m happy to challenge them.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

View 2 Images Tuchel wanted to eat some of the grass from the pitch (Image: Michael Regan - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



"I’m happy to push them and very proud to be a part of that. I’m excited to work with these players. I’m excited to have new young players that we can bring into camp and they can learn.

"I think we got another step closer and I think we’re there. It’s very difficult to prepare for a World Cup in the US. But I think it’s possible to prepare for a Euros.

"The target is to have another ten matches. We had ten matches in the US, eight wins, one draw, one painful loss. But that is something to build on. We have all the right to hold our heads high and go with courage and positivity into the next challenges."

Sports.title: Somerset title hopes suffer major blow in Yorkshire defeat as Notts also lose
Sports.content:
Somerset's hopes of becoming county champions for the first time in their history took a major blow as they collapsed to a costly defeat at the hands of Yorkshire.

Top of the County Championship Division One table heading into the penultimate round of matches, Somerset saw rivals Warwickshire wrap up a two-day victory against Essex but failed to keep pace at Headingley.

Chasing 287 - the highest score of the match - they were bundled out for 101 on the final day. Resuming on 73-3 they collapsed horribly as their final seven wickets fell for 25 runs in less than 13 overs.

Ben Cliff took three of them as he finished with 3-29 after taking 8-76 in the first innings, while Ben Coad claimed 4-33 and Matthew Revis 2-7.

Image: Yorkshire's Ben Cliff celebrates taking 11 wickets in the match against Somerset (SWpix.com)

The 185-run defeat leaves Somerset chasing from behind heading into their season-ending fixture against Surrey and one step further away from ending their 135-year quest for the county game's top prize.

Notts beaten by Sussex

Warwickshire will take an 11-point lead into the final round with Nottinghamshire also suffering a heavy defeat, while Hampshire have been relegated.

Notts could only set Sussex 76 to win at Hove and, although they grabbed a couple of early wickets to reduce the hosts to 14-2, Sussex secured a seven-wicket win just after the lunch break.

Sports.title: Weekend Winners: Almekarem backed for handicap glory at Newbury
Sports.content:
Ahead of a busy Saturday from Newbury, the Weekend Winners panel previewed the big Dubai Duty Free Handicap, which is live on Sky Sports Racing at 2.47pm.

Having claimed a 17-runner handicap at Doncaster's St Leger meeting, Almekarem heads the betting (at the time of writing) for Sir Mark Prescott, despite a 5lb hike in the weights from his Town Moor appearance.

Boyfriend is another who has been penalised by the handicapper following positive recent runs, while Balzac looked to have rediscovered his mojo after being gelded when a runner-up at Ascot earlier this month.

Rossa Ryan and Ralph Beckett team up with Gonna Fly, and Jamie Spencer gets on board Stem, who will look to build on a positive third at Sandown the last day.

Declan Rix...

"I think I know how this race is going to work out, even though there are plenty of runners lining up for this year's renewal. I think you need one that will settle behind this strong pace and I am going to side with Almekarem after he landed a nice handicap at Doncaster last week.

Image: Almekarem won at Doncaster under Luke Morris

"The horse has got gears, with the family having plenty of progression with triple-digit-rated siblings. He heads the market, but I think he is on a rapid improve and can take the beating on the back of a good performance last week."

Host Kate Tracey...

"I am with the Richard Hannon-trained Stem, who I think is a little bit forgotten about here. He ran in the competitive Spring Mile at Newbury - where he ran well and the form of that race has worked out throughout the season.

"He's running over 10 furlongs after being ran over eight [and 12] furlongs [so far this season]. I think he has every chance of running his race and at 8/1, I think he's a solid proposition at those odds."

Sam Boswell…

"I'm siding with a winner of the Polish Oaks - which isn't something I say every day - in Merveilleux Lapin for Owen Burrows. She has been largely consistent since joining the yard without winning and I think she's a shade over priced here.

"She bumped into some progressive types at Ascot last time and although the Burrows stable form isn't as good as I was hoping recently, he did have a nice winner the other day at Yarmouth. At 16/1, she will probably be the value play for me."

Sports.title: 'Embrace the chaos' - What we learnt from Tuchel's England picks
Sports.content:
Where does Palmer fit?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Tuchel explains why he recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold

Cole Palmer's form at the start of this season for Chelsea has been irresistible. Four goals and two assists in six games, and his link-up play with England team-mate Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro has been sensational to watch.

"Cole has his numbers back," said Thomas Tuchel at his press conference. "Assists, decisive goals. I think he has a point to prove."

The England boss really had no choice but to recall him after leaving Palmer out of his World Cup squad.

The omission may have ultimately helped Palmer, who was hit by injury and looked a shadow of himself last season following the previous summer's Club World Cup. Rested, refreshed and back towards his best.

Could even a below-par Palmer have helped England in North America? There will be many that will argue his case.

But the question now is how and where does Tuchel use Palmer going forwards?

Jude Bellingham locked down the No 10 role at the World Cup. The Real Madrid ace was one of the tournament's stars. Meanwhile, Bukayo Saka is back fit and firing for Arsenal on the right. Anthony Gordon is excelling at Barcelona on the left wing after impressing there for England in the summer.

Rogers, too, has been a key figure for Tuchel. Finding a way to get the two Chelsea attackers together on the pitch will be an exciting challenge for the England boss, who has an abundance of attacking options.

Peter Smith

Tuchel promises Mainoo minutes

Image: Kobbie Mainoo in action for Manchester United against Ipswich Town

Kobbie Mainoo's inclusion comes after he was the only outfield player not to play a single minute during England's World Cup campaign. This time, Tuchel promises it will be different for the Manchester United midfielder, who has started the season strongly.

"I expect him to be on the pitch and it's my duty to get him on the pitch," said the England boss. "That was totally on me. He didn't put a foot wrong during the World Cup.

"He was class in behaviour on the training pitch. There was big competition; we played Reece (James) in central midfield also. Elliot Anderson is amazing for us; Declan Rice is a very unique player.

"We trusted them more than we trusted Kobbie. It was difficult for him. It was on me."

The competition for places in England's midfield remains fierce. But clearly Mainoo is a part of Tuchel's plans and there are no hard feelings. The nature of the camp, spanning three weeks and including four fixtures, should allow him chances to prove his worth.

Nick Wright

Trent's shock selection

Image: Alexander-Arnold (left) pictured with Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers

It should not be a shock to see an Englishman playing for Real Madrid selected in the England squad but Trent Alexander-Arnold's selection is exactly that.

This marks a massive shift from Tuchel, who previously said Alexander-Arnold was not the profile of right-back he wanted in his side and repeatedly declined to select the former Liverpool star - even when Tino Livramento suffered a pre-World Cup injury and Tuchel had the opportunity to call up a replacement.

Questions over why Tuchel overlooked the technical 27-year-old reoccurred when the England boss questioned the natural ability of Three Lions players to be able to retain the ball and control games under pressure.

Alexander-Arnold had not been in an England squad since the summer of 2025 so what has changed?

"He was never non-selectable," said Tuchel when asked about Alexander-Arnold. "Now is his chance to show, come to camp, be the best version of himself. He comes as a right-back for us."

His performances for Real Madrid this season did not shift the needle alone.

He has one assist from five appearances and his deployment in midfield for the Champions League win over Inter Milan was a reminder of the continuing conundrum managers are having in getting the most out of Alexander-Arnold's potential.

Real boss Jose Mourinho used Alexander-Arnold in central midfield due to injuries and applauded his application - but also noted how he had lost possession and noted the physical challenge of the role.

Last season, Alexander-Arnold was battling with Dani Carvajal for the right-back spot at Real Madrid. This season it is summer signing Denzel Dumfries challenging him for the place.

The brilliant on-the-ball ability remains but defensive concerns continue. How Tuchel uses Alexander-Arnold - and what this change of stance means longer term - will be an intriguing narrative through the international break.

Peter Smith

If England cannot control games, why not 'embrace the chaos'?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tuchel reveals he was told his job was safe before the Mexico game at the World Cup

Tuchel was critical of England's 'DNA' after the loss to Argentina, suggesting the players were unable to control high-pressure matches with possession in the way a team like Spain can.

The return of technical players Palmer and Alexander-Arnold to his squad seemed to be an admission he had left some of the best English players at looking after the ball out of the group. But in his press conference on Friday Tuchel hinted that perhaps it is better for England to go the other way - and "embrace the chaos".

"The more I reflect on it [the Argentina loss], it's more buying into our strengths and playing more like in the second half against Croatia, or first half against France," said Tuchel. "We get a lot of value out of it [this style]. This is what the Premier League reflects.

"Football is about adapting to situations, and football without any control is sometimes hard to digest for a coach. If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it's one of their nicest experiences ever to watch a football match.

"Maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control - maybe we need more chaos, to embrace the chaos. Maybe it brings out the best.

"We will adjust our style but always to put the strengths of the players on the first priority."

Peter Smith

Gibbs-White crowded out in No 10 battle

Image: Morgan Gibbs-White scored 15 Premier League goals last season

Morgan Gibbs-White can feel justifiably aggrieved by his omission. The 26-year-old was outstanding last season for Nottingham Forest, racking up 15 Premier League goals and registering four assists. He has continued in the same vein this term.

Gibbs-White continues to face intense competition for places in the No 10 position. Palmer has been recalled to a squad which already features Bellingham, Rogers and Eberechi Eze. Tuchel says the numbers do not add up.

"He was close but it's always the same," he said. "It makes no sense to choose three, four or five No 10s. It just doesn't help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan is in. He ended the season strongly and was the key player for Forest to not be relegated."

Gibbs-White might wonder why Eze was preferred. The Arsenal man has not started a Premier League game this season and produced roughly half as many Premier League goal involvements as Gibbs-White last term. But all Gibbs-White can do is keep pushing, and be ready if the recalled Palmer does not deliver.

"It's one thing to be chosen, like Cole, and get your ticket back to the squad, but it's another thing to perform for England," added Tuchel. "Cole, especially, needs to step up when he comes and show these kinds of numbers and performances to get his place, keep his shirt and justify the nomination."

Nick Wright

Foden's England future in doubt?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Ref Watch verdict on Phil Foden's Manchester derby red card

Gibbs-White is not the only No 10 to have been crowded out. Phil Foden is also on the outside looking in having been overlooked for Tuchel's World Cup squad too.

The Manchester City star was included in Tuchel's squads in March of this year and November of 2025, but this omission comes after an encouraging start to the season was interrupted by his red card in last weekend's Manchester derby.

Foden now faces an almighty battle, in an area of the pitch in which England are well stocked, to win Tuchel over and earn a place back in his plans. His latest omission, as Tuchel returns to other technicians such as Alexander-Arnold, will feel painful.

Nick Wright

Is Tuchel embracing England's next generation?

Image: Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha celebrates after scoring last season

The England manager has pivoted from the experienced squad he selected for the World Cup and made a marked effort to give chances to a plethora of young talent in his latest camp.

Veteran England presences like Jordan Henderson, Ivan Toney and Ollie Watkins have been omitted, leaving room for the inclusion of Myles Lewis-Skelly, Alex Scott and Rio Ngumoha - all of whom are under the age of 23, with the latter having turned 18 less than a month ago.

Ngumoha's inclusion is without doubt the most eye-catching.

The teenage sensation travelled with England's squad to Florida for their pre-tournament training camp and has appeared in five of Liverpool's six games to start the season, impressing enough to be called up even without recording a goal contribution thus far this campaign.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player An emotional Ngumoha receives his debut England cap from Jude Bellingham following an impressive performance against New Zealand. Credit: @England

Perhaps easier choices were that of Lewis-Skelly and Scott in the midfield. The former has excelled for unbeaten league leaders Arsenal, recording two assists from deep-lying midfield and keeping £75m summer signing Bruno Guimaraes out of the champions' starting line-up.

Scott has continued to build on an impressive 2025/26 campaign in which he represented arguably the key component in a Bournemouth side that qualified for European football for the first time. Those performances - alongside earning him his place - meant he was linked to high-profile suitors like Chelsea and Manchester United throughout the summer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Peter Smith explained why so many clubs were after Bournemouth's Alex Scott

"We had three players in prep camp with us [before the World Cup], Alex Scott, Rio Ngumoha and Josh [King], all three of them were fantastic members of the squad," Tuchel said.

"Not only because they were nice and reliable and excellent characters, but they showed the quality, courage and curiosity on the pitch, which was very nice to see."

Whether Tuchel ushers in new tactics remains to be seen - but his first England squad since the World Cup has shown a willingness to at least include new players.

Noah Langford

Sports.title: Why Klopp's 'one of 83 million' cap was significant
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp has named two separate Germany squads for the upcoming Nations League matches in his first act as head coach.

Ahead of the four matches against Netherlands, Serbia and Greece (two), Klopp has called up 44 players in two different groups.

That list comprises 16 players who have yet to make an international appearance for Germany, including Said El Mala of Cologne, Max Rosenfelder, Philipp Treu and Derry Scherhant from Freiburg and Celtic midfielder Mika Baur.

Other notable decisions include the omission of Stuttgart forward Deniz Undav, explained by Klopp as fitness-related, and his announcement that captain Joshua Kimmich will be used as a midfielder, having previously been utilised as a right-back by Julian Nagelsmann.

Nagelsmann resigned as Germany's head coach following their World Cup last-32 stage elimination by Paraguay.

Marc-Andre ter Stegen, currently on loan at Ajax from Barcelona, has been confirmed as first-choice goalkeeper, while there are recalls for Karim Adeyemi, Leeds United's Anton Stach and Brentford forward Kevin Schade.

One squad will be used for the first two games, against Netherlands in Amsterdam next Thursday, September 24, and against Greece in Augsburg three days later, on September 27.

The second group will be used for the match against Serbia in Munich on October 1 and the away trip to face Greece, in Thessaloniki on October 4.

Image: Klopp's hat read 'one of 83 million' in the German colours

Klopp also had a political message at his press conference, wearing a baseball cap which read "one of 83 million" in the colours of the German flag. The country is enduring a fractious political period and the far-right Alternative for Deutschland party recently achieved a significant electoral victory in Saxony-Anhalt.

In response, Klopp used his press conference to preach unity. Asked about his cap and its significance, he said: "We need to rediscover the fun in all of this. I hope I won't have to talk about political matters in the future. But I want to reclaim the flag for us. So that people feel happy and fortunate to live in this wonderful country.

"I don't want to leave national pride to the wrong people. It fills me with pride to do this job. When we spend time focused on football, it's meant to foster a sense of community and make us feel better. We have to create that atmosphere. But we also need people who embrace it."

What was the significance of Klopp's cap?

Klopp's baseball cap is going to be interpreted as a response to the state election results in Saxony-Anhalt. The far-right AfD party won over 43 per cent of the popular vote and a majority, furthering a trend for their growing support in the region and across east Germany as a whole.

But this is just the most recent issue and, in any case, the AfD cannot be described as only having prominence in the old east. Their anti-immigration, nationalistic rhetoric plays in other parts of the country, too, particularly in areas of industrial decline and that Saxony-Anhalt election result did not occur in isolation; the AfD has been polling strongly at state and federal level for several years. For many, that is a source of considerable angst and the basis for anger and division.

But there is a more general issue, too. What is the acceptable form of patriotism in Germany? What does the flag mean to different people? The legacy of national socialism makes these issues highly complicated to begin with, but as the country changes and deals with modern issues such as multiculturalism, symbols of nationalism or declarations of national pride can be interpreted in different ways or co-opted with malignant intent.

That nebulousness is a symptom of a divided nation. There are many different perspectives on what Germany is and what it should be. Not forgetting, of course, that it is a federal country to begin with, built from states with their own regional identities and, consequently, contrasting perspectives on the changing political climate.

Sports.title: Richards looks to relaunch world championship charge against Kalajdzic
Sports.content:
Craig Richards returns to his home city of London for a crucial fight when he boxes at the Copper Box Arena on September 26, live on Sky Sports.

Richards fights Belgrade's Radivoje Kalajdzic in the chief support to Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton.

The man from Crystal Palace is determined to beat Kalajdzic to return to world championship class.

Kalajdzic is a top-quality operator who is coming off an excellent knockout win over former WBC world champion Oleksandr Gvozdyk. He has previously boxed Artur Beterbiev and knocked out former world title challenger Sullivan Barrera too.

Image: Experienced Richards can be a force at light-heavyweight

"I think going out there and putting on a statement performance against him puts my name in a hat for that world title, 100 per cent," Richards told Sky Sports. "I'm locked in. I'm ready to do a job.

"I want to be world champion."

In 2021, Richards challenged Dmitry Bivol for the WBA light-heavyweight title, losing on a unanimous but closer than expected decision. Bivol subsequently established himself as the best in the division when he beat Beterbiev.

That is the level Richards wants to get back to.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Richards says his friend Eberechi Eze is an example of how a sportsman should behave and despite his growing fame he always has time for others

"My story hasn't been written yet," the Londoner declared. "I didn't do all of this and sacrifice everything to not accomplish my goals to be a world champion.

"So I feel like I should get a reward. I'm not being entitled, but I feel like the work I put in, I should get something back out of it. And that's to be world champion.

"For sure, co-main-event fight in front of a home crowd, you know it's a good place to start.

"Execute on the night and we move forward from there."

Watch Craig Richards vs Radivoje Kalajdzic live on Sky Sports on September 26.

Sports.title: Doyle: Arapaho can strike gold in Newbury's Mill Reef Stakes
Sports.content:
Our ambassador Hollie Doyle previews a busy Saturday which features the Group Two Mill Reef Stakes at Newbury – live on Sky Sports Racing.

Dods gelding to strike gold in Mill Reef

Michael Dods has been bullish about his unbeaten gelding Arapaho Gold, who can make it five wins out of five in the Dubai Duty Free Mill Reef Stakes (2.12) at Newbury on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Racing.

The impressive Gimcrack winner - according to the Darlington trainer the best juvenile he's ever had - boasts by far the best form in the race and proved his liking for this course and distance when he won the Listed Rose Bowl earlier in the season.

Image: Arapaho Gold, ridden by Connor Beasley, on the way to winning the Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack at York

Godolphin's Nabati looked most progressive until coming unstuck in the Listed Flying Scotsman Stakes at Doncaster only last week. Charlie Appleby is backing him up quickly with something to prove at this level.

Starlust to capitalise on drop in grade

I'm keeping a close eye on the revitalised Breeders' Cup winner Starlust in the Dubai International Airport World Trophy Stakes (1.02) at Newbury.

Ralph Beckett's sprinter, who stole the glory in Del Mar two years ago before an unsuccessful stint at stud, has run two big figures at the top level in the Nunthorpe and the Flying Five in Ireland last weekend so poses a threat to all in this lower grade.

Back on an easier track, he can get his head back in front at the possible expense of Shagraan, who can outrun his odds in the first-time cheekpieces. Clive Cox's gelding was second in this race last year and will enjoy the underfoot conditions.

Legend can bounce back to winning form

Roaring Legend proved he retains plenty of ability when going down narrowly to last weekend's Mallard winner Valedictory at Newmarket in the summer and can go one better in the Dubai Duty Free Autumn Cup Handicap (1.37) at Newbury.

Olly Murphy's eight-year-old is a fresh horse - a comment that applies to Alan King's Insanity. I've always liked this gelding who is well handicapped on the pick of his more recent form.

Primo Lara has Ryan Moore up which will attract plenty of market interest but this looks much tougher than the all-weather race he won at Kempton earlier this month.

Newbury a hot date for Boyfriend

Richard Hannon holds the key to the Dubai Duty Free Handicap (2.47) at Newbury with the consistent Boyfriend and stable companion Stem.

The former was quite unlucky at Salisbury when things got quite congested but he stayed on well and might have gone closer with a clear run. Compensation way well await.

Stem produced a good run at Sandown last time and has won at Newbury before, while Jane Chapple-Hyam's Balzac posted a much-improved run at Ascot after being gelded and looks another big player.

Haggas grey has strong Gold Cup chance

Binhareer is a stakes horse in the making so I'm expecting big things from him in the Ladbrokes Ayr Gold Cup (3.40) at Ayr on Saturday.

William Haggas' grey ran a super race in the Group Three Hackwood Stakes at Newbury in July off an unchanged rating of 103 and my husband Tom Marquand is looking forward to getting back on him in handicap company.

A course and distance winner in easy ground last year, he's on top of my shortlist along with Far Above Dream who went agonisingly close in a hot handicap at York last time. That form was franked when the third Coul Angel bolted up at the Curragh last week.

At a bigger price, I wouldn't rule out Richard Spencer's Run Boy Run, who won the race 12 months ago off a lower rating and could be dangerous in first-time blinkers if he's drawn on the right side in stall 23.

Hats off to Sam in Silver Cup

I'd love to see Sam England win the Ladbrokes Ayr Silver Cup Handicap (2.30) with the in-form Trilby who is another strong chance for Tom (Marquand).

He won well at Beverley before staying on nicely at Haydock, hitting the line really hard, and the quicker they go the better for the six-year-old who is on a nice mark despite his five-pound penalty.

Wathnan Racing's Deep Havana also shoulders a penalty but won well at Thirsk off a long lay-off and can improve on that, while Julie Camacho's Havana Blue should play a leading role after winning so impressively at Ascot.

Getting back on simulator my biggest milestone

I'm delighted to report that in the past two weeks I've really turned the corner in my recovery from the broken leg I sustained at Bath in May.

For a while I wasn't seeing the progress I was hoping for which was quite worrying - my knee and ankle just weren't working together - but I'm starting to see good results now which is very satisfying.

The biggest milestone was getting back on the simulator a few weeks ago. Initially I couldn't even get my foot up in the iron but it feels good to be taking such a big step back towards riding again.

Even from the outset I was determined not to let myself lose too much condition, hoping that I would be able to regain fitness faster once I started to increase my rehab, which has been quite exhausting.

I've been doing an hour in the gym every day at Oaksey House in Lambourn, followed by physio sessions and work in the hydro pool. I've also been back on the exercise bike which has been great for boosting my cardio.

I'm definitely ticking every box and seeing the results of my hard work so I'm hoping to be back doing what I love in a matter of weeks, rather than months.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

2h ago 07.49 EDT Russia to return to Fifa competition in boys' Under-15 World Cup Russia are poised to compete in a Fifa event for the first time since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The country was listed on Friday among the entrants for the boys’ Under-15 World Cup and Festival which is being hosted in Azerbaijan next month. Russian national teams and club sides were banned from Fifa and Uefa competitions in the wake of the invasion. Though Fifa lifted the ban on Russia’s under-17s in 2023, this under-15 tournament marks the first time they will have actually played. Russia have been drawn in a group alongside Turkey, as well as Afghanistan, Djibouti, Sierra Leone and Sudan. The FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival is a new festival-style competitions for boys (2026), girls (2027) and both (2028 onwards) be open to all 211 Fifa Member Associations, regardless of size or footballing tradition. To align with the development needs of U-15 players, the matches are shorter in duration, played on smaller pitches, with teams comprising – for the 2026 edition at least – eight players. The Fifa council agreed last December that the under-15 event would be open to teams from all of its 211 member associations. In July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) dropped its recommendation for global sports federations like Fifa to ban Russia. In February, the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, told Sky News the Russia ban had “not achieved anything” and had just created “more frustration and hatred”. Ukraine’s sports minister Matvii Bidnyi described Infantino’s remarks as “irresponsible” and “infantile”. 3h ago 07.22 EDT This time tomorrow we will be 8 minutes away from kick-off at The Den where West Ham and Millwall will renew their rivalry. The Metropolitan police have been granted special powers to tackle violence as the south and east London teams meet again for the first time in 14 years. double quotation mark There is nothing to glorify here. This will be the 100th competitive meeting, if discontinued, minor tournaments are included, and anyone failing to see the logic behind the rivalry can be forgiven. The sides are not on each other’s doorstep and Millwall are south of the Thames, meaning Crystal Palace and Charlton are more obvious enemies. Yet it is not really about football. The tribalism runs deep, dating back to when the clubs were formed by rival shipbuilding firms at docks on the Isle of Dogs in east London, and is more down to hooligan elements than anything that happens on the pitch. There have been many occasions when the nastiness has spiralled out of control. Hooliganism was rife in English football during the 1970s and 1980s and Millwall and West Ham had fearsome firms. Trouble erupted when the sides met at the Den for a testimonial for the Millwall defender Harry Cripps in 1972. The toxicity grew and a Millwall fan, Ian Pratt, died after a clash with West Ham fans at New Cross station in 1976. It is worth keeping in mind when people try to hype up this fixture. Stories about who was top dog on the terraces back in the day are not that interesting. Read more from Jacob Steinberg below. Fear and loathing linger as Millwall and West Ham resume ferocious rivalry Read more View image in fullscreen Police remove fans who began fighting during the West Ham and Millwall game at Upton Park in 1978. Photograph: PA View image in fullscreen And fans make their feelings heard during their Championship match against West Ham much later. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy Share Updated at 07.22 EDT

3h ago 06.51 EDT De la Fuente announces squad from city at centre of migration crisis Spain coach Luis de la Fuente announced his Nations League squad from Ceuta on Friday in a show of support for the Spanish city in northern Africa that has become the centre of a migration crisis. For his first squad announcement since Spain won the World Cup , De la Fuente revealed his list in a video featuring him in Ceuta accompanied by residents of the Spanish exclave. In late July, over 70,000 people pushed across the border from Morocco, with more than 100 dying in the chaos. Most quickly returned, but a few thousand remain in the city of just over 80,000. De la Fuente did not directly mention the border crossing or its impact, but he did say: “This is Ceuta, this is Spain.” It echoed the rise in sentiment in Spain that Ceuta – a territory that until the mass crossing was mostly an afterthought for most mainland Spaniards – needs to be supported. Spain open the Nations League against England at Wembley Stadium on 26 September, when its players will wear two stars on their shirts for the first time after winning a second world title. After visiting London, Spain will host Croatia on 29 September and the Czech Republic on 3 October, before visiting Croatia three says later. Del la Fuente kept his World Cup squad mostly intact. Inter Milan goalkeeper Josep Martínez replaced Barcelona’s Joan García, who is out with a minor knee issue. Real Madrid defender Dean Huijsen is in for Marcos Llorente, who retired from international soccer. Fermín López replaced fellow Barcelona midfielder Gavi, while Espanyol striker Roberto Fernández got his first call-up, replacing Borja Iglesias. Ceuta is one of two Spanish territories on the north African coast along with Melilla. Ceuta has been in Spanish possession since 1580. Christians and Muslims, Spanish and Moroccan residents and day workers all live there in relative harmony behind a border fence that many migrants from across Africa attempt to cross or swim around for a better life in Europe. We have critical reviews that will stay, of course, behind closed doors. I am the biggest critic of myself and reflection is sometimes necessary to get better and experience is a crucial part of coaching, so this is where we are. I tell you something, 99.9% of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists and tactical things. They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated. This is the feedback that I get and it’s 99.9% and I think this is what we created and this is how it should be. This is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. This is the feedback that I get. It makes me proud, it makes me happy because we share, even if it’s just in the cab or in the coffee place or in the supermarket, you share these little moments and you understand that it actually meant something and that what the players built was transmitted and this is what we want to build. Share Updated at 06.35 EDT

4h ago 06.20 EDT Here’s Tuchel on Trent Alexander-Arnold’s return. These are from the FA website. double quotation mark It’s an opportunity for Trent of course, He had a good start to the season, I would say. He started some matches for Real Madrid. They have good results and it’s a chance for him to claim what he feels is yours, his place on the right side, so here we go. It’s a long camp, four matches and we’re happy to have him back. Share

4h ago 06.18 EDT More from Tuchel on a couple of players who were close but didn’t make it. That’ll be Arsenal’s Ben White and Fulham’s Josh King. double quotation mark Ben pulled out with an injury. He had a fantastic start with Arsenal to the season and was back to his very best on the side as a pair especially with Bukayo Saka which could be very valuable for us to have two players on the side but he was unfortunately not available for the World Cup and is not available now. It is unfortunately a little bit of a story with Ben that in the decisive moments or in the moments when we do the call-ups he is not available. Nice that you mentioned Josh King because we had three players in prep camp with us in the U.S. - Alex Scott, Rio (Ngumoha) and Josh… all three of them were fantastic members of the squad not only because they were nice and reliable and excellent characters but they showed the quality and the courage and the curiosity on the pitch which was very nice to see. Josh especially had a fantastic start to the season with Fulham which was very, very close but in the end it felt like we keep the squad tight and give the players that come into camp, let’s say on Josh’s position, on the number 10 position with Cole (Palmer) and with Jude (Bellingham) so they have our trust and Josh is therefore with under-21s but he was very close and is on the radar. Share

4h ago 06.14 EDT Thomas Tuchel is speaking to the press. He’s asked if the door is always open to those who didn’t make it. double quotation mark The door is always open. Yeah, 100%. The door is always open. The door is always open first and foremost through performance and then on the same level through behaviour and commitment to the team spirit because we build something very special. First, before we did the nomination in the last month I thought we have more of a continuation of the World Cup squad but then a lot of members of our World Cup squad I just wrote it down, Reece (James), Dan (Burn), Dean Henderson, John Stones, Hendo (Jordan Henderson), Djed Spence can’t be with us due to injuries so it is not like a full continuation. We have to... new players will step up because these players were crucial, crucial for us in building the brotherhood, in building the spirit and taking care of the mentality that took us a long way in the tournament and we will not negotiate on that, we will not give in on that and compromise on that. So other players will step up, this is basically how I see this camp, other players will step up, players will step up and get a lot of minutes so my mindset at the moment is not to change too much within the formations, within the match if possible but be also of course reliable and of course if it doesn’t make sense to play the players too much we will not overload them. And coming back to your questions the door is always open and the door is always open to impress and the door is always open to take the place. View image in fullscreen Thomas Tuchel talks to the media at Wembley. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at 06.52 EDT

4h ago 06.06 EDT Thanks Dom. Let’s go back to the Tommy T debate. Dan Pressland offers some support for the German. double quotation mark As disappointed as I was by the Argentina semi, I feel compelled to offer at least some pushback against the criticism of Tuchel. The Mexico match felt to me like one we would have lost under Southgate, and are we really in a position to fire someone who was ten minutes away from getting England to the World Cup Final? I would argue that finishing third despite clearly having room to improve is a cause for optimism rather than recriminations, and unlike Southgate I have some faith Tuchel is capable of learning from his mistakes. Only time will tell, of course, but I think giving him another chance is reasonable. Share

4h ago 06.00 EDT And hear to guide you through that presser, and more updates, is David Tindall. Over to you, good sir. Share

4h ago 05.57 EDT Thomas Tuchel’s press conference is live from 11am BST so stay tuned for updates that. It should be interesting to hear him asked about the likes of Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer, and what has changed his mind on those players and others. Lewis Hall is definitely one I’d like him to be questioned on. The Newcastle left-back was supreme last season and surely merited a World Cup spot given the lack of other left-backs selected. What has changed between then and now? Share

4h ago 05.44 EDT An email from Adrian Riley has highlighted another glaring omission from Tuchel’s England squad: double quotation mark I thought one of England’s most improved players at the World Cup was Djed Spence, after being surprised he made the squad. Now, sold by Tottenham, dropped by England. I get that he wanted more playing time than he was getting at Spurs, but why isn’t he in the squad? Spence did have an injury, Adrian, which has meant he’s not yet played for Inter. It will be interesting to see whether he features against Roma tomorrow. Share

4h ago 05.39 EDT Arteta: Pro Ref must 'try to improve' after Arsenal meeting Ed Aarons Mikel Arteta has refused to divulge the details of Arsenal’s meeting with Pro Ref after they complained about the penalty awarded to Sunderland last week. It is understood that the referees’ body has been in touch with the Premier League champions after they requested clarification over the decision at the Stadium of Light in Arsenal’s 2-0 win. “This is a conversation that will remain private as usual,” said Arteta. Asked whether he wanted Pro Ref to apologise like it did to Manchester United after Erling Haaland’s goal was incorrectly awarded in last week’s Manchester derby, he said: “It’s not about the apology, it’s just agreeing that the decision should have been different or not. Maybe they have a different opinion and try to improve and move forward together.” View image in fullscreen Mikel Arteta, there, in typically animated touchline mode at Sunderland. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters Share

5h ago 05.28 EDT It’s worth mentioning that Dan Burn, Dean Henderson, Jordan Henderson, John Stones and Ben White are all injured, so might have been picked otherwise. We know Tuchel loves having Henderson (the midfielder) in his squad. Another startling absence is Reece James, who isn’t believed to be injured. Tuchel could simply be managing his minutes, given how many fitness issues the Chelsea captain has had. Share

5h ago 05.21 EDT Your emails are now pouring in – mostly on the subject of England’s World Cup failings rather than this squad announcement, but there’s time. David Hopkins weighs in on the Tuchel debate: double quotation mark Just to join in the Tuchel pile-in, wasn’t the specific selling point that he would be the one to get England over the line in tight games, in the way that Southgate couldn’t? It looked like maybe that was happening in the Mexico game (albeit through the medium of Dan Burn’s massive head), but the Argentina cave-in was far worse than any of Southgate’s perceived inertia. I was genuinely surprised he hadn’t been sacked when I woke up the next morning, and I’m not sure his chippy interviews since will have bought him much goodwill. Share

5h ago 05.13 EDT Morgan Gibbs-White, Harry Maguire and Phil Foden, then, are the main players out in the cold, having also been shunned by Tuchel in the summer. It’s also interesting that Tuchel has retained Kobbie Mainoo, who has started the season brightly for Manchester United, having taken him to the World Cup without giving him any minutes. Surely Mainoo will feature in the coming four games at some point. It seems Elliot Anderson and Declan Rice will remain Tuchel’s first choice midfield duo, but then there is Mainoo, Lewis-Skelly – who is considered a midfielder rather than a left-back – and Scott to compete with. Share

I make that eight players who weren’t in the World Cup party involved: Alexander-Arnold, Branthwaite, Hall, Lewis-Skelly, Scott and Calvert-Lewin. Seems a bit embarrassing that he’s still there, naming squads, trying to battle our ‘loser’ DNA. When we already know, that when it really comes down to it, he’s a bottle job. 5h ago 04.44 EDT A few outlets are reporting that Alex Scott is set to be named in the England squad. The Bournemouth midfielder has started the season impressively, after being linked with Chelsea and others in the summer, and registered a Player of the Match performance in the Cherries’ win over Real Sociedad in the Europa League last night. The 23-year-old is uncapped at senior international level, though has represented England Under-21s on 11 occasions. Born in Guernsey, he came through the ranks at Bristol City after moving from the Channel Island. Share

6h ago 04.30 EDT It’s been a harrowing start to the season for Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos. Manchester United’s women are bottom of the WSL after two games, Michael Carrick is already under pressure after an unconvincing early spell in the Premier League was compounded by a League Cup defeat to Brighton in midweek, while Sir Jim’s other football projects, Nice and Lausanne, are both also rock bottom of their respective leagues in France and Switzerland. “Built for more,” is a slogan Ineos have used in the past. The aforementioned teams sure need a bit more than they’ve produced so far this season. Share

6h ago 04.16 EDT Tom Garry Manchester United women’s head coach, Eva Olid, says her side’s difficult start will help them become stronger and that she is undeterred by criticism of their opening two defeats. The former Hearts manager, who arrived at United in August, endured a 5-0 loss against Chelsea last Sunday after beginning with a 2-1 defeat at London City Lionesses. “The beginning, how you start, doesn’t define you [for] the rest of the season,” Olid said before Saturday’s tough-looking trip to face Arsenal.



“Two or three matches don’t define you, how you are or how you are going to be as a team. There have been transition changes but we know where we go, the direction and we know how we are doing will give us the success in the long term. “All the teams, through the season, have a difficult moment. Our difficult moment is the start. But we are learning as a team to grow because the difficult moments make you grow. And once we are past this difficult moment and start our momentum, we will be so much better than without the difficult moment.” View image in fullscreen Eva Olid has not enjoyed a good start in charge of Manchester United. Photograph: John Walton/PA Share

6h ago 04.06 EDT The England squad should be announced at 10am (BST), with Tuchel chatting to the media at 11am. The expectation is that Chelsea’s Cole Palmer will be named in that squad, having of course missed out on the World Cup. It will be interesting to see who else comes in from the cold, and who doesn’t make the cut. Alex Scott and Morgan Gibbs-White are two names in contention. Share

Sports.title: Fear and loathing linger as Millwall and West Ham resume ferocious rivalry
Sports.content:
Absence has not made the heart grow fonder. Millwall and West Ham meet for the first time in 14 years on Saturday, but it is not going to be a joyous reunion at the Den. The atmosphere will be ferocious and the main hope is that the focus is on the football rather than any nonsense away from the pitch.

These two have plenty of previous, even though they so rarely play each other. The most glaring example is the shocking disorder inside and outside Upton Park when Millwall lost in the second round of the League Cup at West Ham’s old ground in August 2009. A 44-year-old man was stabbed in the chest as trouble raged outside and riot police struggled to maintain order during the game, with play suspended briefly when home supporters invaded the pitch after one West Ham goal.

View image in fullscreen Police try to control Millwall supporters outside Upton Park station after disturbances following a defeat at West Ham in October 1978. Photograph: PA

There is nothing to glorify here. This will be the 100th competitive meeting, if discontinued, minor tournaments are included, and anyone failing to see the logic behind the rivalry can be forgiven. The sides are not on each other’s doorstep and Millwall are south of the Thames, meaning Crystal Palace and Charlton are more obvious enemies. Yet it is not really about football. The tribalism runs deep, dating back to when the clubs were formed by rival shipbuilding firms at docks on the Isle of Dogs in east London, and is more down to hooligan elements than anything that happens on the pitch.

View image in fullscreen West Ham’s Jack Collison exhorts fans to return to the stands after a pitch invasion at their League Cup tie against Millwall in 2009. Photograph: Stephen Hird/Reuters

There have been many occasions when the nastiness has spiralled out of control. Hooliganism was rife in English football during the 1970s and 1980s and Millwall and West Ham had fearsome firms. Trouble erupted when the sides met at the Den for a testimonial for the Millwall defender Harry Cripps in 1972. The toxicity grew and a Millwall fan, Ian Pratt, died after a clash with West Ham fans at New Cross station in 1976. It is worth keeping in mind when people try to hype up this fixture. Stories about who was top dog on the terraces back in the day are not that interesting.

The 2009 game was disturbing and frightening. In March 2004 there were police horses on the pitch when West Ham fans rioted and ripped up seats during a 4-1 defeat at the Den. Away fans were not allowed in the lower tier when West Ham returned eight months later. West Ham have only 1,774 tickets on Saturday. The Metropolitan police will have measures in place to try to keep opposing fans apart. The dedicated walkway linking South Bermondsey station to the away end acts as a coolant.

The mood will still be tense. There is an odd dynamic to the game. West Ham have at times found it awkward because some of their fans care far more about beating Chelsea and Tottenham. But a trip to Stamford Bridge or N17 is a familiar experience. Going south of the river to Millwall is somehow viewed as different, the short train ride from London Bridge treated as an intrepid journey into some hostile alien planet.

View image in fullscreen Millwall revel in underdog status against West Ham. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

Perhaps the irregularity of the game adds to the mystique. It has happened 18 times in the league since the second world war and only in 1988-89 have the teams been together in the top flight. Millwall stayed up that season but West Ham were relegated, which is usually required for the game to take place. West Ham have generally done something wrong if they are looking for Millwall when the fixture list comes out.

It pits Millwall as underdogs, a role they play well. They often rose to the occasion after West Ham were relegated in 2003. Millwall had a decent team – they reached the FA Cup final in 2004 – and picked up two wins and two draws against West Ham before Alan Pardew led the Hammers back into the Premier League in 2005.
