View image in fullscreen Tim Cahill celebrates Christian Dailly’s own goal as Millwall ran out 4-1 winners at the Den in 2004. Photograph: PA /Alamy

It can be hard for West Ham to match up to the intensity. They won at Upton Park when the sides last met, bouncing back from an early Kevin Nolan red card to beat Millwall in February 2012, but tend to struggle in the away game. The Den is tight, compact, intimidating. Millwall are on a five-match unbeaten run at home against West Ham since losing in 1988. They will look to level the odds. West Ham are on a four-game winning run in the league and top the Championship after smashing Wrexham 6-0 last weekend. Alex Neil’s Millwall came close to winning automatic promotion last season but have injuries and are 10th after an inconsistent start.

Logic says West Ham should win. Logic may not count for very much when the game begins.

Sports.title: Why Tottenham are misfiring … and it’s not just down to the lack of goals
Sports.content:
Tottenham have failed to score in their opening four league games for the first time. Two decades have passed since they last drew blanks in four consecutive Premier League matches. While these are outliers, it will take time for Spurs to improve.

Their level of player turnover, from last season to this and from week to week, is a problem. Only four men who played at least half of the league minutes last season have featured in 2026-27. One is Richarlison, who has since been omitted from their Premier League squad. His 15 goal contributions in the league were at least twice as many as any other Tottenham player last season, but he will not be scoring or assisting any time soon.

Richarlison is also the fourth-longest-serving player. Ben Davies, Brandon Austin and Rodrigo Bentancur are ahead of him, and of those only Bentancur is likely to play regularly. Many current starters are relatively new recruits. The 11 players who began the goalless draw with Everton last Saturday had spent an average of 1.3 years with the club. Tottenham have averaged the joint-third-youngest starting XI this season too. They have many players without too much experience, either individually or as a unit.

Roberto De Zerbi has made 12 changes to his starting lineups in the league since the first match, more than any other manager in the division. At four alterations per game, the team is changing more often than it did last season (2.8), when they employed three managers. Little wonder the new-look Tottenham are struggling to gel.

Injuries have not helped, as De Zerbi has mentioned with reference to pre-season. “Micky van de Ven suffered an injury in Australia,” he said. “Domi Solanke the same. James Maddison the same. Mateus Fernandes suffered an injury in Australia. He lost 15 days and it’s not so quick.”

View image in fullscreen Richarlison, pictured against Chelsea in a Sydney friendly, had more goal contributions than any other Spurs player last season – but is not in their league squad. Photograph: Hollie Adams/Reuters

Commercial pressures inevitably influence which countries clubs visit each summer. Chelsea were also in Australia this year, and Aston Villa and Manchester City played friendlies in Asia. But Tottenham were the only club who also went to that side of the world the previous summer. Spurs led the Premier League for days lost to injury in 2025-26 according to Premier Injuries (1,560), with Newcastle (1,271), Arsenal (1,115) and Liverpool (967) also in the top seven; these four clubs were those who went to Asia in summer 2025. High injury tallies may be coincidental but it is fair to question whether another lengthy pre-season trek was right for Tottenham.

Several metrics illustrate their attacking problems. Spurs are capable of getting the ball into dangerous areas, before the next step trips them up.

Their total of 46 completed take-ons leads the Premier League. Only five of these successful dribbles ended with the player creating a chance or taking a shot though. Manchester United have completed 17 fewer take-ons than Tottenham yet have produced tangible output with almost twice as many (nine) chances or shots.

It is similar for high turnovers, which occur when the ball is recovered within 40 metres of the opposition goal to begin a new possession sequence. Spurs have recorded the fourth-most this season (34), but only Coventry (one) have ended fewer of them with a shot (two). Tottenham have produced a goal attempt from 5.9% of their high turnovers when the league average is 19.9%. Nothing is flowing smoothly.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The costliest statistic may concern their productivity in the opposition penalty area. Again, their total of touches in the opposition box – 119, one fewer than Arsenal – looks decent enough. They are often well located to score. But they are taking 3.97 touches per shot in the box, 0.47 more than any other team and 1.15 above average. Everything is taking a beat too long, fatal for many an attacking move.

But look at the makeup of their squad. In terms of Premier League career goals, the 32-year-old left-back Andy Robertson was their top summer signing with 12. Despite being the second-most-expensive transfer in Europe in summer 2024, Solanke still has more goals in the Championship (44) than Premier League (41) and has yet to play the equivalent of 38 full league games for the club across two-plus seasons. Mikey Moore has a quarter of their shots on target (three) in 2026-27, yet played only 90 minutes before going on loan to Cologne.

From once having two of the most accurate shooters in the game in Harry Kane and Son Heung-min, Spurs have filled their roster with men who struggle to hit the proverbial barn door. Most of their squad are at best a few percentage points above league average for shot accuracy, with many of their players below. Chelsea and Bournemouth (24) have had twice as many shots on target as Tottenham this season from no more than nine extra shots in total.

“We have to shoot more, we have to shoot better and we have to finish better the clear situations,” De Zerbi said after the Carabao Cup defeat at Anfield on Tuesday. His team had scored, though an error from Liverpool’s goalkeeper, Giorgi Mamardashvili, played a huge part in Conor Gallagher’s goal. Tottenham cannot rely on opponents making mistakes to bail out their cadre of wasteful attackers. But how long will it take for their mostly young band of new recruits to form an effective unit? Much work lies ahead.

Sports.title: Todd Boehly exits Chelsea diminished after having his fingers burned
Sports.content:
Not since a doomed foray into the thorny world of the transfer market has Todd Boehly had any real influence over the day-to-day at Chelsea. The American exits football as a diminished figure four years on, along with his fellow investor Mark Walter, and the first thing to say is that little will change in the Stamford Bridge boardroom just because Boehly has left the scene.

Clearlake Capital, the US private equity firm founded by Behdad Eghbali and José E Feliciano, was already the majority owner and guiding force. The trio of Boehly, Walter and the Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss had an equal share of a 38.5% stake but have drifted into irrelevance since the BlueCo consortium bought Chelsea from Roman Abramovich for £2.5bn in 2022.

Clearlake, with Eghbali taking a prominent role, called the shots long before Wednesday night’s confirmation that it has full control after buying out Boehly and Walter.

This split has been in the works for a while. It is two years since cracks within the ownership group spilled into public. There was talk of Boehly losing faith in his working relationship with Clearlake. Boehly wanted a resolution. People close to Boehly said he had investors ready to provide capital for a full takeover, although that drew eye-rolling from Clearlake.

Its response was to consider buying Boehly out. Another suggestion from Clearlake was for Boehly to step down as chair and accept changes to governance that would leave the billionaire in little more than a ceremonial role.

No love lost there, then, although there was no immediate sign of movement from either side. A truce followed and Clearlake continued down its path. Eghbali is hugely influential. It is only over the past year that Chelsea fans unhappy with the club’s difficulties in the post-Abramovich era have really started to home in on Clearlake.

Feliciano, who recently became an investor in the Major League Baseball team the San Diego Padres, operates more in the background. Eghbali is more widely seen and was repeatedly targeted with abusive chants by supporters earlier this year.

There was a time when Boehly was the public face of the takeover. Clearlake stood back and watched when Boehly appointed himself interim sporting director after key personnel left in the wake of Abramovich’s departure. How hard could it be? Pretty hard actually. Boehly attracted publicity and was in the limelight. Agents found him personable but wondered whether he knew anything about football.

There was a sense that Boehly’s naivety could be exploited. Chelsea ended up splurging some £300m on a bunch of misfits. The signing of Raheem Sterling on a £325,000-a-week contract became a cautionary tale. Chelsea did not easily shake off the cost of such failures and the sense of chaos grew when Thomas Tuchel was sacked and replaced by Graham Potter at the start of the 2022-23 season.

Boehly has since explained he signed Marc Cucurella from Brighton because he heard that Manchester City wanted the Spain left-back. There is presumably more to thriving as a sporting director than copying your rival’s work.

Boehly had his fingers burned. He became a joke figure, the face of Chelsea’s excess, and made himself unpopular on a wider scale by glibly wondering at a business conference why the Premier League had no All-Star game. Saying Chelsea would beat Real Madrid 3-0 before a Champions League quarter-final in 2023 predictably backfired.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea have only qualified for the Champions League once under Todd Boehly’s tenure. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

It is said that Boehly’s plan was never to become so involved and he always planned to step aside once experts were in place. Chelsea’s strategy has certainly changed since that first window. They have gone from having one interim sporting director to appointing five permanent ones in Paul Winstanley, Laurence Stewart, Sam Jewell, Joe Shields and Dave Fallows. They have handed out long, incentivised contracts and targeted young players.

Eghbali has driven the vision. It has been a bumpy ride at times. Chelsea have qualified for the Champions League once under this ownership. Managers have come and gone. Clearlake sources say important lessons have been absorbed this year. Last summer’s business was better. Chelsea brought in a serious manager, Xabi Alonso, and signed established talent.

Boehly has stood back and watched. Talk of buyouts went quiet until the summer just gone. The spark, it is said, was Walter seeking to liquidate assets to deal with financial issues in the US. The writing was on the wall when he sold his LA Lakers stake.

Boehly and Walter are said to have made a modest profit on their investment in Chelsea. Jonathan Goldstein, a Boehly ally, has also left the board. Wyss has invested in a Clearlake vehicle and has not left the building.

Little will change. Day-to-day operations, leadership and strategy remain the same. The big issue is the stadium question. The exit of Boehly and Walter could lead to movement.

The Guardian first reported in September 2024 that Chelsea were in talks over leaving Stamford Bridge for Earls Court. The Earls Court Development Committee’s separate proposal for the site has not progressed since receiving planning permission. Chelsea’s interest remains, although they have not ruled out finding a way to make the more complicated plan of redeveloping Stamford Bridge work.

Whatever happens will take place without Boehly. Eghbali and Feliciano said in their statement that Boehly “will always be a part of the Chelsea story and family”.

That was a generous take.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Bees sense chance to sting Blues’ backline

Chelsea have not won this west London derby since Brentford’s first Premier League season. Each visit since October 2021’s 1-0 win, Ben Chilwell the scorer, has been a draw. This season has continued the divergence between the clubs’ respective approaches, Brentford’s solidity and continuity contrasting with Chelsea attempting their latest reboot. Kevin Schade, after two well-taken goals at Bournemouth, will fancy facing a defence not yet attuned to Xabi Alonso’s configurations. Only one team has won a Premier League title with a defensive trio: Chelsea’s last title team, in 2016-17 under Antonio Conte. Alonso’s attack has been rather more successful, presenting another challenge for Jannik Schuster. Replacing Nathan Collins, the 20-year-old central defender had a tough examination from Bournemouth’s Evanilson on his first Premier League start, emerging with credit. For Chelsea, João Pedro has three goals and three assists, but doubts surrounding his fitness could lead to Danny Welbeck’s first league start. John Brewin

Brentford v Chelsea, Friday 8pm (all times BST)

2 Spurs and Villa meet in desperation derby

What happens when a very stoppable force meets an extremely movable object? We will be tuning into events at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday to find out as 19th-placed Aston Villa arrive in north London. The teams have scored one goal between them in the league and are desperately hoping for a first Premier League win. The return of Pedro Porro is big for Roberto De Zerbi and that should bring the Archie Gray Experiment at right-back to a merciful end. No Premier League starting XI feels less settled than Spurs – most players look as if they are a mistake or two from being dropped – which has culminated in a side that seems governed by fear and continuously prefers to take the safe option. After coming off the bench against Everton and Liverpool in the past week, the injury-plagued James Maddison will be itching to start and take some sort of initiative for Tottenham. Michael Butler

Tottenham v Aston Villa, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Mateus Fernandes will hope Spurs can get their first league win of the season against Aston Villa. Photograph: Alex Morton/Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock

3 Hürzeler’s scoring express meets champions

When Fabian Hürzeler spoke about Brighton’s success being founded on them being “well structured” after their stirring comeback against Manchester United at Old Trafford on Wednesday, he could have been referring to Malick Yalcouyé. The 20-year-old Ivorian moved to the south coast in 2024 after spending just a few months with IFK Gothenburg in Sweden but had to wait until this season to make his senior debut for Brighton after being sent on loan to Sturm Graz in Austria and then Swansea last season. With Jack Hinshelwood sidelined by injury until after the international break, Yalcouyé has taken his chance in the No 10 role and already found the net twice in the Premier League as Brighton have made a brilliant start. Arsenal are up next for the division’s top scorers – who have 13 goals from their opening four matches – and Mikel Arteta should be wary of the threat posed by Yalcouyé and co as the champions prepare for a fourth away game in succession. Ed Aarons

Brighton v Arsenal, Saturday 3pm

4 Mykolenko form a boost for Moyes

Vitalii Mykolenko’s early-season improvement has gone largely unheralded – and it probably always will be among his detractors – but at a time when David Moyes needs experienced players to step up and defy the constraints of a small squad, the Everton left-back has produced. Having signed a new three-year contract in the summer, and seemingly bulked up, the Ukraine international has kept his critics quiet with several impressive displays for a defence that has four clean sheets in six matches. There remains a problematic lack of cover at left-back after the decision to loan Adam Aznou to Málaga for the season but Mykolenko, the better defender, has eased the concerns that surrounded his position before the new campaign. Ipswich’s new forward recruits, Emersonn and Zian Flemming, will test Everton’s solidity but Moyes’s side will have made an encouraging start should they sign off with a win before the extended international break. Andy Hunter

Everton v Ipswich, Saturday 3pm

5 Jaissle refuses to delete Newcastle blueprint

As befits a lover of direct football, Matthias Jaissle likes to get straight to the point. On Thursday he was asked whether, in the light of Monday night’s 4-1 thrashing at Leeds and a raft of injuries, he was tempted to perhaps switch to a back five or modify his beloved “vertical” approach when Hull visit Tyneside on Saturday. The reply proved unequivocal. “No,” said a manager unafraid to answer questions with a single word. Instead Jaissle expects his young team to retain faith in a wider vision as Newcastle – who signed eight players aged 24 and under this summer – adapt to life after Bruno Guimarães, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon. “It’s a brave journey the club is going on and I’m fully committed in that,” the German said. “If there’s one setback, we shouldn’t delete our journey or our vision. We’re fully committed. We’re fully aligned. We anticipated that something like that against Leeds would happen. It’s on us to respond. But while still believing. We don’t change.” Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Hull, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen ‘We’re fully aligned,’ says Newcastle’s Matthias Jaissle. Photograph: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

6 Delap hopes to impress as Wood regent

Many scoffed at the £45m that was paid for Liam Delap in the summer but Nottingham Forest feels like the perfect place for the striker to regain his form. Forest previously thrived with the now injured Chris Wood as their arrowhead and Delap is something of a younger regent for the New Zealander – powerful, instinctive and willing to bring others into play. During Saturday’s win at Villa, Morgan Gibbs-White and Delap looked as if they already have an understanding and both will be keen to capitalise against a Coventry side that have conceded eight goals in the past two games. After a nervy campaign last season, Forest feel back in the ascendancy and will have been delighted that plans to increase the City Ground’s capacity from 31,000 to 52,500, at an estimated cost of £790m, were approved by the local council on Wednesday. MB

Nottingham Forest v Coventry, Saturday 5.30pm

7 Iraola faces test on south-coast return

After watching Bournemouth make their European bow from afar in San Sebastián, a city Andoni Iraola knows inside out, the Basque head coach will return to his previous club on Sunday. Iraola – whose assistants Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper played for Bournemouth, the former captaining the club into the Premier League in 2015 – led the Dorset club into the Europa League by recording their best-ever finish, sixth. His body of work on the south coast earned him the Liverpool opportunity and a warm welcome is a guarantee. Despite the Cherries’ slow start under Iraola’s successor, Marco Rose, they will pose tricky opposition. The German spent a couple of hours in Iraola’s company before officially starting in June and both will be braced for an all-action contest. Eddie Howe failed to beat Bournemouth in the eight league games he managed against them with Newcastle and Iraola and his staff will expect a tough test. Ben Fisher

Bournemouth v Liverpool, Sunday 2pm

8 Calvert-Lewin: man on a mission

Dominic Calvert-Lewin will be a man on a mission against Crystal Palace at Elland Road on Saturday. Daniel Farke’s centre-forward hopes to become the first Leeds player to score in six consecutive home league games since Arthur Hydes back in 1932. Managers often, quite rightly, say players matter more than formations but, in Calvert-Lewin’s case, Farke’s switch to 3-5-2 late last November proved a road to Damascus moment. Until then he had struggled as the team’s lone striker but, once he was paired with Noah Okafor or Lukas Nmecha, the goals started to flow. Granted, Leeds sometimes play 3-4-3 or, occasionally, revert to a back four but Calvert-Lewin has emphasised the importance of attacking partnerships. After collecting eight points from their opening four games, Farke’s team have registered the best beginning to a top-tier campaign of any Leeds team since David O’Leary’s class of 2001-02. Will it continue at Palace’s expense? Is Hydes’ record under threat? Might 3-5-2 be the answer to ending more strikers’ goal droughts? Louise Taylor

Leeds v Crystal Palace, Sunday 2pm

9 Le Bris plots party crash in Manchester

Manchester City’s maximum 12 points from their first four Premier League games featured 1-0 wins (over Coventry and Manchester United), a 2-1 victory (Bournemouth), and a 4-1 success (Crystal Palace). Conceding only two goals while scoring eight is an impressive record that is only marginally bettered by the champions, Arsenal (one conceded, eight scored in their 12-point tally), and it seems a rosy augury that Enzo Maresca’s team will be genuine title contenders this season. Régis Le Bris, though, plots to halt City’s perfect start, and can draw on guiding Sunderland to a share of the points last season against the FA Cup holders, though that was at the Stadium of Light. In the corresponding fixture at the Etihad Stadium, City cruised to a 3-0 win. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Sunderland, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Enzo Le Fée reacts after scoring against AZ on Sunderland’s midweek European return. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

10 Bobb needs to provide more end product

Oscar Bobb came off the bench against West Ham and fired Fulham into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup with a clinical late winner at the London Stadium on Tuesday night. It was a fine piece of individual play from the Norway winger but he needs to do it more often. The goal was Bobb’s first since joining Fulham last January and a player of his ability should be producing more of an end product. The 23-year-old is a clever dribbler and looked ready to establish himself at Manchester City before a serious injury curtailed his development. The talent is clear. Bobb had a good World Cup and should be full of confidence when Fulham, still seeking their first win in the league this season, host Manchester United. Jacob Steinberg

Sports.title: Kluivert and Rayan rock Real Sociedad as Bournemouth win on European bow
Sports.content:
The first goal that AFC Bournemouth ever scored in Europe could be heard out on the Bay of Biscay. A tradition from Real Sociedad’s old Atotxa ground, once lost but now recovered at Anoeta, dictates that a single flare is set off every time the visitors score while two are lit when the home team do; that way those out to sea know the score. And so it was that at 21.41 on a Thursday night in September 2026, Justin Kluivert found the net and a man named Juan Iturralde ran out into the street to let everyone know what had happened.

Back in Dorset and high in Anoeta, where 2,000 Bournemouth fans sang their way through this most special of occasions, they knew. They had waited their whole lives for this and it was a nice way to mark the history they made, their arrival announced to Europe with fireworks and a 2-1 victory in San Sebastián, the city where it all began for Andoni Iraola, the manager who brought them here.

Iturralde ran into the night three times – he went once more when Rayan made it 2-0 after 20 minutes and again when Sergio Gómez made it 2-1 on 57 – and might have gone more too. After a superb first half, Bournemouth had to hang on, sometimes desperately, in the second. For a while it had seemed a lead would slip away from their grasp for the fifth time in six games this season, but Djordje Petrovic came to their rescue with two astonishing saves from Orri Óskarsson in the final, dramatic minutes. It had been some battle and they had given everything.

That resistance hadn’t appeared necessary an hour or so earlier. Bournemouth had waited 127 years for a first European game and considerably less for their first goal. They had been playing 10 minutes and 43 seconds and when it came they celebrated it twice. A lovely shift of the body from Evanilson started it, the Brazilian receiving and releasing Adrien Truffert. The cross was perfectly placed, bent behind the defensive line for Kluivert to score.

High in the north-east corner Bournemouth’s fans went up but down in the south-west corner the flag did too, it didn’t take the video assistant referee long to prove that was wrong, and allowing them to do it all again while Iturralde set off into the street. Truffert was on the run again soon after, Alex Scott’s glorious long, looped, curling ball dropping into just the right place for Rayan to head the second.

View image in fullscreen Justin Kluivert fires Bournemouth into an early lead. Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty Images

There was an ease about the way Scott had completed the pass – an almost gentle turn of the ankle, the ball delivered as if by hand – and about the way he played. Amid the speed and intensity he glided. Around him, teammates flew everywhere, Marcus Tavernier especially, and Real Sociedad could not keep up. Three times they threatened from dead balls too: Evanilson headed the first off the post, António Silva headed the second wide and Óskarsson just about headed away a third. Songs from the corner sung to a backdrop of frustrated whistles from the rest of Anoeta.

From the home fans there was relief when half-time arrived without the lead being extended. There was also a reaction, a dash from Ander Barrenetxea signalling their intent and an increase in volume. Petrovic made a superb save from Beñat Turrientes on 56 minutes and almost immediately Real Sociedad pulled one back. Gómez’s curling cross bent all the way through, past the outstretched legs and into the far corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This was a different game and a different place now, Real Sociedad’s version of Bad Moon Rising interrupted by an “huuy!” when Gonçalo Guedes’s effort was pushed past the post by Petrovic. Already this season Bournemouth had lost leads against Manchester City, Everton, Newcastle and Brentford, most of them late, and a familiar feeling only increased as Gómez’s fantastic ball sent Guedes through on the left, only for the Portuguese winger to try to cut inside rather than shoot. From the loose ball, Mikel Oyarzabal’s subtle, clipped shot floated onto the top of the bet.

Gómez was not their only problem. Luka Sucic shot wide on 81 minutes and then Gómez slipped Óskarsson in for what should have been the equaliser. Petrovic though saved that and, somehow, stopped the Iceland striker from five yards in the final minute.

Ultimately, the fireworks were finally over on Bournemouth’s famous night as a European journey that was once unimaginable was heard across the sea.

Sports.title: Pino kickstarts Crystal Palace’s Europa League rout of Lech Poznan to ease Sage’s worries
Sports.content:
It was worth the wait for Crystal Palace. After being denied their rightful place in the Europa League last season, Pierre Sage’s side made the perfect debut by brushing aside Lech Poznan with a victory that will take some of the heat off their new manager.

The Frenchman has big shoes to fill in replacing Oliver Glasner after his predecessor won three trophies in the space of 12 months and there had been some talk of disquiet behind the scenes following his decision to drop the teenager Jaydee Canvot at the weekend. But while Palace face a testing trip to face in-form Leeds on Sunday, having conceded 11 goals from their opening four Premier League matches, they were given a big helping hand by their opponents here well before Radoslaw Murawski was sent off late on for a reckless foul on Canvot.

The result was never in doubt after Poznan gifted Yéremy Pino a goal direct from their own throw-in, with Chris Richards and a Jørgen Strand Larsen penalty making the points safe by half-time. Eddie Nketiah rounded off the win with a late fourth and Sage was delighted to have shared in Palace’s historic moment before a meeting with his former club Lyon next month.

“I saw a lot of videos about the fans, especially during the journey in the Conference League last year,” he said. “They were incredible and I want to share the same thing with them this year.”

It’s a measure how quickly things have moved on in south London that Palace didn’t even have the chance to stage a parade to celebrate their Conference League triumph. But after a difficult start to the new campaign, the captain Dean Henderson had urged supporters to “park the negativity” when he signed a contract extension on Wednesday.

View image in fullscreen Jørgen Strand Larsen makes it 3-0 from the penalty spot. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

Poznan’s European campaign started on 21 July and the Polish champions were backed by a vociferous travelling support. They were almost able to celebrate a goal inside the opening two minutes but the captain Mikael Ishak fluffed his lines as Palace showed their defensive frailties again.

As well as some noise around Sage following Saturday’s defeat by promoted Ipswich, there have been concerns about the atmosphere at Selhurst Park after the disbanding of influential supporters’ group the Holmesdale Fanatics. But after Terry Yegbe’s disastrous throw-in helped Palace take the lead, they were treated to two more goals before the break.

Richards headed in a deep corner from Adam Wharton and Strand Larsen dispatched a spot-kick after Pino was brought down by Murawski. There could have been another in spectacular fashion after Yegbe hammered the ball into his own net just before half-time but thankfully for him the assistant flagged for offside against Strand Larsen.

The Poznan fans decided that was the moment to perform the dance they have made famous. After their side’s poor first-half performance, it was no wonder that they preferred to turn their backs. At least they could amuse themselves by letting off a series of flares in the second half just as Pino came close to adding his second of the night.

Ismaïla Sarr’s first appearance of the season was greeted with the odd boo after his hopes of a move to Liverpool were dashed in the transfer window. But the reception for the Senegal forward was largely positive as Nketiah also came off the bench to complete the job on a night that Palace will hope can kickstart life under Sage.

Sports.title: Floyd Samba’s debut double lifts Manchester City to Carabao Cup win over Norwich
Sports.content:
Floyd Samba lit up this tie with a debut that will have the 17-year-old grinning for a while after a superb goal in each half ensured Manchester City advanced to face Brighton in the last 16 in their defence of the Carabao Cup.

Samba has an older brother by a year, Tyrone, who is also in the academy. Their father, Christopher, is a former Blackburn and QPR defender.

With a game featuring speed, awareness and a poacher’s eye, he hopes to make a case for regular first-team game time. Given the elite-level forward competition this will be tough, but tonight was a fine calling card.

Samba said: “A debut like that is mind blowing. I couldn’t believe it – that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me.”

For Enzo Maresca, a sixth successive win maintains a 100% record for his nascent project (barring the Community Shield) and points to how the manager is shrugging off doubts about succeeding Pep Guardiola.

Of Samba, he said: “Satisfying for the two goals, the entire performance he was good. He didn’t play [before] as a 9, we tried in the last two or three days. He is very good at finishing so it was a very good game for him. He is not a 9 for sure but he was good.”

View image in fullscreen Ryan McAidoo (left) congratulates Floyd Samba after he scored Manchester City’s fourth goal against Norwich. Photograph: Nigel French /Apl/Sportsphoto

City host Sunderland here on Sunday. Defeat Régis Le Bris’ side and Maresca will enjoy his three-week international break. You would not bet against them doing so – City are improving with each outing, as they did against Norwich.

Many opponents are blown away at the Etihad, so for the 14th-placed Championship side to initially tap the ball about was impressive.

Maresca’s formation was fluid and reaped a first dividend when Nico O’Reilly’s cross was fumbled by the visiting goalkeeper, Daniel Grimshaw. The ball dropped to Allan and he delivered it back across for Samba to cutely head home.

City doubled their lead when Samba laid the ball off to Ayyoub Bouaddi, the midfielder hit the ball to Rayan Cherki and, as Grimshaw advanced, he beat the keeper to his right.

Watching from the touchline, Philippe Clement hoped his side were not about to crumble as the first half neared its end. He was relieved when Samba, running in, was thwarted by a Grimshaw dive at his feet.

Yet his men ended the period chasing City: an exhausting task that showed the control the hosts exerted. In a sparsely attended tie, this was precisely what Maresca wished – it meant that his main man, Cherki could be rested, as Ryan McAidoo replaced him for the second half.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Everton v Newcastle;

Sunderland v Brentford;

Bradford v Peterborough;

Fulham v C Palace;

Bournemouth v Aston Villa Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Soon, Allan joined Samba in registering on his City bow. From the left, the Brazilian zigzagged in, beat Sam Field once, cut back to beat him again, then found the far corner with a lethal strike.

Maresca will have been displeased after the restart to see a Norwich raid that swooped down the left and had the ball bouncing to Kellen Fisher in the area, but the right-back missed the target.

Fisher’s profligacy was punished when Samba made himself a cert for the player-of-the-match award with a second. He collected the ball inside Norwich’s area and shaped a sweet finish into the far right corner, the helpless Grimshaw watching it sail by.

Maresca was delighted with this and also the wider picture of how his side executed the gameplan. With each win he oversees, the Italian’s authority and stature grow, his appointment appearing ever shrewder.

The game’s closing stages were lit up by McAidoo’s sharp finish: an apt end to an impressive City victory.

Clement said: “After 20 minutes Manchester City started to get a bit annoyed because they could not create anything but then you get the first goal against and we need to defend better. In the second half we were more dangerous – I saw several good individual performances, but it is hard to take – six shots on target, five goals.”

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel explains why he omitted ‘fantastic’ Premier League star from England squad
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has revealed that Josh King only narrowly lost out on the England squad amid stiff competition in attacking midfield.

Tuchel revealed his 27-man selection on Friday ahead of the extended international break, which runs from September 21 to October 6.



4 King was on the cusp of making the latest England squad Credit: Getty

Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer have received call-ups after missing the 2026 World Cup, but Phil Foden has been omitted again.

Three of the five players that joined the pre-World Cup training camp have returned - Jason Steele, Alex Scott and Rio Ngumoha.

Ethan Nwaneri was also involved, but has not been selected on this occasion, with Fulham youngster King also among the absentees.



However, Tuchel has insisted that it was close call and offered the 19-year-old, who has scored two Premier League goals this season, hope for a future England call-up.

What has Thomas Tuchel said about Josh King?

Responding to a question on King's omission, Tuchel said: "Nice that you mentioned Josh King, because we had three players in prep camp with us in the US - Alex Scott, Rio and Josh, all three of them were fantastic members of the squad.



"Not only because they were nice and reliable, and excellent characters, but they showed their quality and their courage, and curiosity on the pitch, which was very nice to see.

"Josh, especially, had a fantastic start to the season with Fulham.

"It was very, very close but, in the end, I felt like we keep the squad tight and give the players that come into camp, let's say in Josh's position, the No.10 position with Cole and with Jude, so they have our trust.



"Josh is therefore with the U21s, but he was very close and is on the radar."

Why has Ben White been left out?

Ben White, who has started in all four Premier League matches for holders Arsenal this season, yet again missed out due to a minor knock.

4 Tuchel has explained why King was not selected on this occasion Credit: Getty

4 He also lamented the latest injury woe that has seen White miss out Credit: Getty



The defender was brought off at half-time in their 2-0 win at Sunderland last weekend with an apparent groin issue and Tuchel says he withdrew from international duty as a result.

"Ben pulled out with an injury," he explained. "He had a fantastic start to the season with Arsenal and was back to his very best on the side as a pair, especially with Bukayo Saka, which could be very valuable for us, to have two players on the side.

"But, he was unfortunately not available for the World Cup, and is not available now.

"It is, unfortunately, a little bit of a story with Ben that, in decisive moments or in the moments when we do the call-ups, he's not available."



Still no room for Gibbs-White

Another notable omission from the latest England squad is Morgan Gibbs-White, who was widely considered to be unlucky to miss the World Cup after scoring 18 goals for Nottingham Forest last season.

He has three goal contributions in four appearances in the 2026/27 campaign thus far, but will not feature in the international break.

4 Gibbs-White was not selected as Tuchel did not want to overload his no. 10 options Credit: Getty

"Close," Tuchel said on Gibbs-White and what his chances of being selected were. "But it's always the same.



"It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five no. 10s, it just does not help anyone.

"We can see the form that Morgan is in, and he ended the season very, very strongly, and was a key player for Forest to not be relegated. We can see him stepping up now."

England begin their Nations League campaign against the world champions Spain at Wembley on September 26.

Two matches versus Czech Republic then come either side of their trip to Croatia, with all four matches coming live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Zinedine Zidane imposes strict new rule in drastic decision for first France training camp
Sports.content:
Zinedine Zidane imposes strict new rule in drastic decision for first France training camp

Zinedine Zidane has banned journalists and cameras from covering the arrival of France players at the Clairefontaine training camp.

The media usually sets up at the training entrance to keep tabs on the likes of Kylian Mbappe and Michael Olise.

2 Kounde often made a splash with his outfits when he rocked up for France duty

In recent years, it's become an impromptu fashion show, with right-back Jules Kounde in particular among those to catch the eye.

However, Zidane has decided to end the spectacle entirely to ensure the players can concentrate on the task at hand.

The newly-appointed Les Bleus boss wants to avoid any potential media frenzies and unnecessary controversies as he looks to build upon the work of former boss Didier Deschamps.

When did Zidane succeed Deschamps?

Deschamps confirmed last January that he would step down as France head coach following the 2026 World Cup.

"In 2026 it will be over. In my head it's very clear," Deschamps said at the time.

"I've done my time, with the same desire and passion to maintain France at the highest level.

"One has to be able to say stop, there's a life after this. The most important is for France to stay at the top as they have been for many years."

Deschamps made history in 2018 as he became just the third person to win the World Cup as both a player and a manager having captained France to glory in 1998 before delivering success in Russia 20 years later.

2 Deschamps' final game was a 10-goal thriller as France finished fourth at the 2026 World Cup Credit: AFP

And he now holds the record for the most games managed in World Cup history, with 27 matches.

Deschamps' final game proved to be the 6-4 third-place play-off defeat to England at the 2026 World Cup.

10 days after France's loss to the Three Lions, Zidane was confirmed as new head coach.

"I've often said it: there's nothing greater than the French national team," Zidane said following his appointment.

"So it's a joy and obviously a great source of pride to become the manager of this French national team."

Zidane's first games as head coach

Zidane will kick off his reign as France boss with the UEFA Nations League meeting with Turkey later this month.

Les Bleus then face Belgium to round off September before a game against Italy at the start of October.

France then round off the extended international break with a second Group A clash with Turkey.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta rejects Jamie Carragher’s claim after being compared to Alex Ferguson
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has shut down claims he is able to influence referees by calling out their mistakes.

It follows comments made by Jamie Carragher following Arsenal's win over Sunderland last weekend.

3 Carragher's remarks comparing Arteta and Sir Alex Ferguson have been dismissed by the Arsenal boss Credit: Getty

The former England defender compared Arteta to legendary Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson due to the manner of his criticism towards the match officials.

Arteta had called the decision to award Sunderland a penalty 'unacceptable' during his post-match media duties.

The Black Cats had been given a spot-kick after Ezri Konsa grappled with Dan Ballard inside the penalty area.

Carragher addressed Arteta's comments during Sky Sports' coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United on Monday night.

Carragher compares Arteta and Ferguson

Likening the Arsenal boss to Ferguson, he said: "This was Mikel Arteta becoming the Sir Alex Ferguson of the Premier League right now.

"He’s the don at the moment, he’s the Premier League champion.

"A lot of new managers about, he’s been in his role for six or seven years and he feels he’s in a position of power to say, ‘It wasn’t a penalty’.

"I don’t think it was a penalty, but it’d be interesting to see how long it takes for another referee to give a penalty against Arsenal in a similar situation.

"I thought it was very interesting in the press conference, one of the journalists made a point about, no matter what question you asked him, he kept going back to the penalty, so he was determined to get the narrative out that this won’t happen again to his club.

"But that’s a manager, we’ve seen it with Sir Alex Ferguson, we’ve seen it with Jose Mourinho."

3 Carragher had likened Arteta's comments to Ferguson's ability to influence officials by criticising them Credit: AFP

Arteta responds

Arteta was asked about Carragher's remarks during his pre-match press conference on Friday.

He spoke to reporters ahead of his side's trip to Brighton this weekend.

The two side's meet at the Amex on Saturday, with kick-off at 3pm.

When asked if it is fair to liken him to Ferguson in the way Carragher did, Arteta said: "No, I think I'm here to try to give my opinion, to defend my club, to give the very best to our players.

"I know that to do so, obviously you guys get asked some questions and we need to respond in the most direct way, I think, and fair way. I will make mistakes sometimes, but I will try to be as fair as possible."

He added: "We discuss many topics in this room, and they're important, all of them, and we have a space to talk, to give our opinions, to have discussions, to have personal conversations, and it's everybody's duty to try to improve the game, and that's what we're here for."

3 Arteta branded the decision to award Sunderland a penalty last weekend 'unacceptable' Credit: Getty

It was reported after the win over Sunderland that Arsenal would be raising the issue with Pro Ref, who oversee refereeing across professional football in England.

However, Arteta refused to confirm whether the Gunners had heard from the body since Saturday.

When asked, he replied: "This is a conversation that will remain private as usual and they have to keep that one."

As for whether he would like an apology, similar to the one received by Manchester United, he admitted: "It's not about the apology, it's just agreeing that the decision should have been different or not.

"Maybe they have a different opinion and try to improve and move forward together."

Pro Ref admitted to a mistake in the decision to award Erling Haaland's winning goal against United in Sunday's Manchester derby.

The Manchester City striker's goal was awarded by VAR despite initially being ruled out for offside.

Whilst replays showed Haaland was onside, Enzo Fernandez had been offside in the build-up before challenging for the ball.

Sports.title: Premier League star should be fuming over squad decision – Kobbie Mainoo can count himself lucky
Sports.content:
Premier League star should be fuming over squad decision – Kobbie Mainoo can count himself lucky

Nottingham Forest star Morgan Gibbs-White was 'unlucky' not to make Thomas Tuchel's latest England squad.

That's according to talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook, who is a huge fan of the ex-Wolves midfielder.

4 Gibbs-White was overlooked by Tuchel despite his bright start to the Premier League season. Credit: Getty

Tuchel confirmed his picks on Friday as England gear up for UEFA Nations League meetings with Spain, Czechia and Croatia.

The Three Lions boss brought the likes of Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer back into the fold, while youngsters Alex Scott and Rio Ngumoha also made the cut.

What did Thomas Tuchel say about Morgan Gibbs-White?

Tuchel conceded that Gibbs-White, who has chipped in with one goal and two assists from his opening four Premier league games, was close to making the England squad as he explained his decision following Friday's announcement.

He said: "It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five No.10s. It just does not help anyone.

"We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

"It's one thing to be nominated, but it's another thing to perform, this also counts."

However, Crook believes Gibbs-White should have received a call up for the extended international break.

Speaking live on air immediately after the squad was confirmed, Crook said: "Morgan Gibbs-White unlucky again to miss out."

He then added: "And can I just say on Gibbs-White, he must be thinking: 'What do I need to do to get in this England squad?'"

His comments resonated with Forest fan Mick, who called in to discuss his disbelief over the 26-year-old's omission.

4 Forest fans had hoped to see Gibbs-White make the cut following his impressive start to the season Credit: Getty

Mick added that he felt Gibbs-White should have made the cut over Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo.

Mainoo shone for United in the second half of last season, forcing his way into the England World Cup squad.

However, the 21-year-old didn't register a single minute of gametime for the Three Lions in North America over the summer.

What has been said about Morgan Gibbs-White's omission?

Crook agreed with the Forest fan, adding: "I don't disagree, I think he's playing really well for Manchester United.

"But he obviously didn't do enough in training to impress Tuchel at the World Cup.

"So I would take that argument on board, even as the president of the Kobbie Mainoo Fan Club."

4 Mainoo's inclusion has been criticised despite his good form for Manchester United Credit: Getty

talkSPORT's Sam Matterface then had his say on Gibbs-White's omission, as he said: "I think we said this at the World Cup, out of all the players that hadn't been called into the squad, he was the most unluckiest.

"Because he played so well at the end of last season."

Former Three Lions international Gabby Agbonlahor then interjected, as he simply stated: "I don't see him [ever] have a bad game."

Continuing with his view, Matterfacethen remarked: "I always think if he's not picking him, there must be a reason behind it.

"Whether it's that he doesn't fit into that team, whether it's something with the team dynamic, whether the fact that he thinks actually going forward he's not going to use him.

"And if he's not using him, then maybe he is not as malleable around the squad if he's not playing, as if when he's in the starting XI, he's great, and when he's not, it's a bit more difficult, I don't know.

England’s upcoming Nations League fixtures Spain (H) Saturday, September 26 - 7.45pm Croatia (A) Saturday, October 3 - 5pm Czechia (H) Tuesday, October 6 - 7.45pm Czechia (A) Tuesday, September 29 - 7.45pm

"There's all different reasons and I'm not suggesting for one minute that that is the case, it won't just be, 'His stats are great, so put him in.'

"Because if that was the case and we picked the squad on stats, it would be a very different 26."

Having the final say, Crook then said that even though he may not be a starter, Gibbs-White is more than good enough to warrant a place in Tuchel's squad.

He stressed: "There's a difference of being in the squad and being in the team, isn't there?

"Is he going to get ahead of [Jude] Bellingham and [Morgan] Rogers? Probably not. But that doesn't mean he's not worthy of a place in the squad."

Sports.title: Fanatics Collectibles announce Paris store as global expansion continues after London success
Sports.content:
After incredible success in London, Fanatics Collectibles are continuing their global expansion by opening a second store in Paris.

Almost 18 months on from their Regent Street opening, the brand are set to open their doors on Rue Saint-Lazare.

1 Fanatics are set to open their second flagship collectibles store in Paris in October Credit: Fanatics

If the London store, which has welcomed more than one million visitors through its doors since it was opened by Lewis Hamilton, is anything to go by, Parisians are set for an unrivalled collectibles experience.

Due to open on October 23, members of 'The Hobby', as collectors are affectionately known, will be able to instantly access the brand's impressive portfolio of trading cards.

"What we saw in London wasn't just people buying cards, it was collectors building a community around something they love," said David Leiner, President, Trading Cards, Fanatics Collectibles, which owns Topps.

"Paris felt like the natural next step after that response, and France is one of the most exciting markets in Europe for us right now.

"We're not looking to change what's already working for collectors here, we want to add something new to it, a space built around trading cards, community, product and the moments that make collecting special.

"Whether you've been collecting for years or you're just starting out, we want this store to feel like it belongs to you.”

It's also likely those in Paris will enjoy similar perks to those on offer in the London store.

The store in the English capital has had limited edition 'Regency' cards on offer for some qualifying customers, while its Match Attax product has had an exclusive box available in-store.

The opening of France's store may also see a raft of sporting royalty go through their doors.

After Hamilton cut the ribbon, London has seen Adam Wharton, Aaron Ramsey, Dominic Solanke, James Maddison, Robbie Fowler, Alan Shearer, Ashley Young, JJ Gabriel, Georgia Stanway, and new Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo visit.

Away from football, UFC president Dana White, NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, and Super Bowl winner Jason Bell have also been on the scene as well as superstar DJ and producer Steve Aoki.

And, most recently, England and Chelsea legend Ashley Cole joined fans to launch Topps' Flagship Premier League hobby boxes.

The store has also forged links within the trading card community and hosts a regular Trade Night in partnership with the renowned London Card Show.

At the Paris shop, fans will be able to get their hands on products from UEFA Champions League, Formula 1, NBA, NFL, WWE, and MLB, as well as entertainment including Disney, Marvel and Star Wars.

The move is also unsurprising given Fanatics' strong ties with Paris Saint-Germain.

Both Fanatics and Topps have multi-year licensing deals with PSG.

Sports.title: ‘Change of scenery’ – Viktor Gyokeres offered advice by Graham Potter as Arsenal struggles continue
Sports.content:
Sweden boss Graham Potter believes out-of-favour Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres will benefit from the upcoming international break.

The Gunners hitman has endured a tough start to his second season with the north London club, having lost his place in the starting XI to Kai Havertz.

3 Gyokeres has been limited to just 12 minutes of league action this season.

Gyokeres started recent wins over Napoli and Ipswich Town in the Champions League and League Cup, respectively, but drew blanks in both games.

What's more, the former Sporting CP star has been restricted to just 12 minutes of Premier League action this season, and was an unused sub in wins over Coventry, Aston Villa and Sunderland.

However, he's expected to lead the charge for Sweden for UEFA Nations League meetings with Romania, Poland, and Bosnia and Herzegovina in the looming international break.

And national team boss Potter has urged Gyokeres to put any criticism to one side and focus on returning to his best form.

What did Potter say?

"Things happen. Things go up and down, just like life does," Potter said of the striker's attacking showings.

"He’s a Premier League winner. He scored a lot of goals as a number nine for Arsenal.

"He was incredible in World Cup qualifying and had a great World Cup as well.

"Players at this level will always get criticism at some point. But there is no problem here."

Potter continued: "We know how good Viktor is, we know how important he is.

"We love him with the team and I think he has the same feeling. Sometimes a change of context, a change of environment can help a player.

3 Potter is backing Gyokeres to rediscover his best form for Sweden Credit: AFP

"We're all looking forward to having Viktor with us and helping him enjoy his football."

Arteta's comments on Gyokeres

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was asked about Gyokeres and whether he is struggling for confidence ahead of Saturday's game at Brighton.

"No, obviously, especially in the Premier League, he hasn't played that many minutes," Arteta replied.

"But last week he played in Napoli, and he had a good game. I think that's about moments as well.

"We need to give him all the support and confidence that he needs to deliver because we know the player that we have, the capacity that he has to score goals and what he can give to the team."

Arsenal have made a 100 per cent start to the season, winning all seven competitive matches following their midweek 4-2 win at Ipswich.

3 Gyokeres still has the backing of Arsenal head coach Arteta. Credit: Getty

And they'll look to make it five wins from five in the league when they make the trip to the south coast to face the Seagulls this weekend.

But it won't be stroll down the promenade for the Gunners against Brighton, who have proven they are no walkovers with some big results already this season.

Among them are respective 5-0 and 4-0 wins over Coventry and Aston Villa, dumping Manchester United out of the Carabao Cup and taking Chelsea all the way in a 4-3 defeat in the league.

Sports.title: Jason Cundy: I’ve found the worst Premier League club to support – it’s worse than Tottenham
Sports.content:
Jason Cundy surprsingly admitted there is a worse Premier League side than Tottenham - in his eyes at least.

The Sports Bar co-host questioned if there is a point to supporting Everton having watched them in EFL Cup action.

4 Tottenham fans listening to the Sports Bar at 10pm each night know Cundy will usually have something to say about them - or laugh at his Spurs supporting co-host Jamie O'Hara whilst wearing an Ange Postecoglu mask

Cundy is no stranger to donning the famous 'Ange mask' and dishing the dirt on Roberto De Zerbi's men, winding up co-host Jamie O'Hara - a supporter and former player of Spurs - who suggested his beloved side would win the Bundesliga to Cundy's surprise.

The former Chelsea man, though, directed his ire in the direction of Merseyside after Everton fan John called into the show.

Why do Everton annoy Cundy?

"They wind me up," Cundy told John.

"You are the biggest football club of the underachievers in the country.

"You lot are a behemoth of a club, you're a massive football club, but you are the biggest underachievers."

Cundy wondered why they never win anything or, in his eyes, try and win a cup competition.

"Just win something, John. Win something. Everton don't win anything," he continued.

John agreed. "I know they don't. They don't at all. I think this year, one of the advantages of having a small squad is the fact that you can't mess about and start playing reserve players, or resting players.

"That doesn't work for us. It hasn't in the past. We beat Wolves [in round three of the EFL Cup], the same round we got battered by Wolves at Wolves last year.

"[Manager David Moyes] dropped all the first team players, and played a lot of non-starters, and we got battered.

4 Whilst Everton last won a trophy in 1995, they are historically still big owing to their nine league titles won - however, Cundy has said they should be trying to win more Credit: Getty

"That's not the way. That's where we've been falling down."

O'Hara then got involved in the discussion, adding: "Everton are as big as Tottenham right? They're a massive club right? And Tottenham are guff.

"At least we won the Europa League a couple of years ago."

'Like a bad smell'

Cundy turned his attention back to Everton, stating: "At least [Tottenham] pretend to try. They don't even pretend to try.

"I'm going to say it now. I think Everton's the worst club to support. Worse than Spurs.

"They don't even look or feel like they're going to do anything or win anything. They just hang around.

"They're like a bad smell. They literally linger in the Premier League.

4 Cundy said Everton, who compete in the impressive Hill Dickinson Stadium, to be nothing more than 'a bad smell' Credit: Getty

"Everton do nothing. What do they do? What does Everton Football Club do?"

Everton are massive

O'Hara was quick to defend the Toffees, though.

"Well, they're in the Premier League and they've never been relegated. I can't call Everton a bad smell.

"They're a massive football club. They are a huge football club. I like Everton. They are a fantastic football club.

"It's not easy to survive in the Premier League. They've never been relegated. That's an achievement."

4 Moyes has led the Toffees to an unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign so far. Credit: Getty

But Cundy was having none of it, shooting back: "That's exactly it. The point I'm making. They hang around. They just linger.

"They're a bad odour. That's what Everton are. They hang around.

"They used to be [a massive club]. They're not. They're literally living off their history. They don't do anything."

Cundy is referring to Everton's stature in English football in the 1980s when they were the country's top team along with Liverpool.

The reached the FA Cup final three times, winning it in 1984 and then won the European Cup Winners Cup and League title in 1985, winning the league again in 1987.

Bellew responds to Cundy

Former professional boxer and diehard Everton fan Tony Bellew quickly responded to Cundy's remarks about his beloved Toffees.

Replying to a talkSPORT post on X, Bellew wrote: "Cundy the clown is rage baiting again!"

On Cundy's former side Chelsea, he continued: "We have more league titles than your lot! A better stadium than your lot! Oh, and a far better fanbase!

"Everton will rise again, just like your hairline did after visiting Turkey. If your hairline was able to be brought back, then so will Everton."

Moyes has overseen an unbeaten start to the season, though two of their three competitive wins have come against lower-league opposition in the League Cup.

Next up for the Toffees is the welcome of newly-promoted Ipswich Town before the international break.

Sports.title: Coach who left Manchester United tipped to return after six years if Michael Carrick is sacked
Sports.content:
Coach who left Manchester United tipped to return after six years if Michael Carrick is sacked

Manchester United have been urged to consider bringing back former assistant manager Kieran McKenna if Michael Carrick is sacked.

The Red Devils boss is under growing pressure following back-to-back defeats to Manchester City and Brighton.



3 United have been told to consider bringing back a former coach to replace Carrick Credit: Getty

United following up their loss in the Manchester derby by exiting the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night.

Their 3-2 defeat to the Seagulls marked the first time they had lost a home match after leading by two goals for 50 years.

Another defeat away at Fulham on Saturday will only further add to the speculation surrounding Carrick's future.



Who should replace Carrick?

Discussing who could replace him in the Old Trafford dugout, talkSPORT's Alan Brazil has thrown a surprise name into the mix.

The former United forward believes McKenna should be considered for the role.



Speaking on Friday's Breakfast show, Brazil explained: "I think Kieran McKenna. People seem to forget about Kieran.

"He will come back into football, he’s very, very bright and started at Man United."



Asked if McKenna is the answer, he added: "I don’t know. I don’t know what the answer is to Man United."

How has McKenna fared in coaching?

McKenna spent five years with United after first joining the club as a scout in 2016.

Following a spell in charge of the Under-18s side, he became an assistant manager under Jose Mourinho.

3 McKenna spent five years with United before winning three promotions with Ipswich Credit: Getty



The Northern Irishman later worked under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Carrick and Ralf Rangnick before leaving the club in 2021 to take charge of Ipswich Town.

During four-and-a-half years as Tractor Boys boss, McKenna won three promotions, including two to the Premier League.

However, he is currently without a club after leaving Portman Road to take a break from football in June.

McKenna had held talks with Fulham before making the decision, with the Cottagers subsequently appointing Alvaro Arbeloa.



How has Carrick performed at United?

A return to United would see McKenna replace Carrick in the dugout.

The former England midfielder was placed in caretaker charge by the Red Devils in January following Ruben Amorim's sacking.

3 Carrick has already suffered three defeats in all competitions this season Credit: Getty

Carrick went on to win 12 of the remaining 17 matches to guide United to a third place finish and Champions League qualification.

He was rewarded with the permanent job on a two-year deal in May.

However, his honeymoon period appears to have come to a dramatic end at the start of this season.



United have already suffered three defeats in all competitions, with just one win from their opening four Premier League matches.

Sports.title: Premier League press conferences: Liverpool meet with Brentford transfer chief, Unai Emery piles pressure on Roberto De Zerbi and Mikel Arteta defends his furious outburst after Sunderland penalty decision
Sports.content:
It's the final Premier League gameweek before the international break, and managers up and down the country will be speaking to the press.

Daily Mail Sport will bring you all the key news here...

De Zerbi: Kulusevski will be 'like a new signing'

The eagerly-anticipated return of playmaker Dejan Kulusevski will be like a 'new signing' for Tottenham, according to head coach Roberto De Zerbi.

Kulusevski has not played for Spurs since the end of the 2024/25 campaign due to a right patella injury, which has essentially put the career of the Sweden international on hold for 19 months and ruled him out of the summer World Cup.

There finally appears to be light at the end of the tunnel after Kulusevski returned to full training this week.

He first returned in August only to suffer a small setback, but the 26-year-old is back and whilst he is not ready to face Aston Villa on Saturday, a first comeback appearance could be on the horizon in October or November.

The eagerly-anticipated return of playmaker Dejan Kulusevski will be like a 'new signing' for Tottenham, says Roberto De Zerbi

'We have to manage Deki in the best way we can, with the medical staff, physical staff, but it's a great thing for us,' De Zerbi said. 'He's a good player, he's a good guy and he deserves to play again.

'We have to work day by day, also for Deki it's important the international break because when he will be at the top of condition and pass over the injury, I think it's a great signing. A new signing for us, another new signing.'

Kulusevski was arguably Spurs' best player during an injury-affected 2024/25 campaign before he missed the whole of last season due to this long-standing knee problem.

It was a similar story for James Maddison, who sustained anterior cruciate ligament damage last August before he returned ahead of schedule in May to help Tottenham stay in the Premier League.

Maddison's pre-season this time around has been hampered before a shoulder issue at Brentford on the opening day provided a further setback, but after an encouraging cameo in a 3-1 loss at Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, the 29-year-old is primed for more minutes against Villa.

De Zerbi added: 'Listen, James is working with the team in the last 10, 15 days. Maybe less than 15 days and even if he's a technical player, he needs to be fit, to stay in a good condition.

'When he arrives to the best condition, it's very important for us as a personality, as a characteristic, as a quality, as an experience. The quality of his passes are different than the others.'

Pedro Porro and Sandro Tonali sat out Tuesday's defeat to Liverpool but are available for Saturday's lunchtime kick-off.

Spurs are winless and goalless in the Premier League after four matches. However, Villa are below them in the table in 19th with only one point.

De Zerbi said: 'You have to stay calm, to be confident in what you are doing, what the players are doing. They have my full confidence.'

Emery puts pressure on De Zerbi's Spurs

Unai Emery has piled pressure on Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi by backing them to finish in the top four this season.

Emery takes Aston Villa to north London on Saturday with Spurs still seeking their first league goal of the season. Yet Villa have fared even worse: although Emery's men did get off the mark against Nottingham Forest last weekend, they have only one point to Spurs' two.

Villa finished fourth last term with Tottenham narrowly avoiding relegation. Yet given Spurs spent about £300million on transfers during the summer, Emery believes they should be targeting Champions League football next season.

'I expect them to be in the top four,' he said. 'They are in a similar situation to us but they have huge potential. Tomorrow is a huge challenge for us.

Unai Emery has piled pressure on Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi by backing them to finish in the top four

'The capacity to spend money in summer gives us information about which teams are contenders. Hopefully we can fight with Spurs and beat them but at the beginning of the season they are contenders.

'There are always favourites to be in the top four and Tottenham are among them. Not just this year, but in previous years too.'

By Tom Collomosse

Iraola looking forward to Bournemouth return - as club meet with Brentford transfer chief

Andoni Iraola says he was 'buzzing' to see Bournemouth win in the Europa League on Thursday night – and insists he is looking forward to hugging some of his old colleagues.

The Basque boss switched the south coast for Merseyside this summer after a fantastic three years at the Vitality Stadium which culminated in them qualifying for Europe for the first time.

There will be no time for niceties before the match as he takes his new Liverpool side back to his old stomping ground on Sunday needing a win after three draws and one victory to start the Premier League season.

But Iraola is looking forward to a catch-up after the game and said: 'It's going to be, on the personal side, I am really looking forward to it, meeting them and hugging them.

Andoni Iraola insists he is looking forward to hugging some of his old colleagues ahead of his return to Bournemouth this weekend

'Players that I love. People I appreciate so much. I was buzzing for them yesterday in their first European game, I wish them all the best, but there is another part… we need to go there and beat them and leave all the talking for after the game.

'They have not changed too much in terms of names, mostly the same starting XI with very few changes, they lost Marcos Senesi and signed Antonio Silva. Their main ideas and philosophy (is the same), I was lucky to talk to Marco Rose before leaving.

'They continue to be very dangerous.'

Meanwhile, Liverpool have spoken to Brentford transfer chief Lee Dykes about becoming their new sporting director.

But it is nothing more than that at this stage and the Reds are speaking to multiple candidates – both internal and external – to replace recently-departed Richard Hughes, who joined Al Hilal.

Liverpool have a structure in place at the club and Julian Ward, who has held a number of roles including a previous stint as sporting director, is a strong candidate from within the building.

By Lewis Steele

Maresca not getting carried away by City's flying start

Enzo Maresca is refusing to get carried away with Manchester City's flying start to the season, acknowledging pressure could quickly mount if results turn.

City continued their fine run of form by brushing aside Championship Norwich 5-0 to reach the Carabao Cup fourth round on Thursday.

Since losing to Arsenal in the Community Shield, City have won their last six matches in all competitions – a fine start by Maresca after stepping into the void left by Pep Guardiola.

The City manager, whose side next face Sunderland on Sunday, said: 'I'm really happy. I said in the first press conference, for me to be in this club is a privilege and to be in this club after a legend like Pep is a privilege.

'I know if I don't win it's a disaster, and it's normal, but I don't spend my day thinking who was here before and for how many years.

'I'm just here to focus on what we can do better, improve the team and trying to win games.

'I'm very happy with these five or six games in a row but now the main focus is just on the next one and I'm not thinking that we won six in a row because those games are finished. We focus on the next one and then we have the international break.'

City made 10 changes for the visit of the Canaries, who fielded a weakened side themselves.

Teenager Floyd Samba stole the show on his senior debut, scoring twice as he took the place of the rested Erling Haaland at centre-forward.

Enzo Maresca is refusing to get carried away with Manchester City's flying start to the season

Samba also had a hand in a goal for Rayan Cherki while winger Allan Elias, signed from Palmeiras for £34million last month, also scored on his first appearance for the club.

A strong night for the City academy was capped when 18-year-old Ryan McAidoo came off the bench to add the fifth in the last minute.

In all there were seven City academy graduates on the field. Nico O'Reilly, Rico Lewis and Kaden Braithwaite also featured for the hosts, while Dan Grimshaw and Jacob Wright were in the Norwich side.

Maresca said: 'We have different competitions. We have many games and we are just at the beginning of the season.

'The ones that played are going to play Premier League or Champions League games because the season is long.

'It was very important we gave rest to the ones that played back-to-back 90 minutes against Porto and (Manchester) United. Hopefully they can be full of energy for Sunday's game that will be a strong game.'

Samba, the son of former Blackburn defender Christopher, regularly plays as a midfielder but his performance up front offers another potential option.

Haaland is the only out-and-out striker in the first-team squad and, although he is one of the first names on the teamsheet, there will be occasions when alternatives are needed.

Maresca said: 'We have Antoine (Semenyo) there, we can use Phil (Foden) and Rayan Cherki as a false nine. It depends on the gameplan.

'But Floyd played here, he was good and hopefully we can give him more chances.'

Arteta explains his ref criticism

Mikel Arteta said his criticism of the referee's decision to award Sunderland a penalty against Arsenal last weekend was through a duty to 'defend my club' and confirmed they have spoken to Pro Ref.

The Spaniard was incensed after referee John Brooks awarded the Black Cats a penalty for grappling in the area between Dan Ballard and Ezri Konsa.

He was adamant that Ballard had pulled Konsa to the ground and on the day labelled Brooks' decision as 'unacceptable'.

Ahead of Arsenal's Premier League fixture against Brighton on Saturday, Arteta said: 'I am here to try and give my opinion, defend my club, give the very best to my players.

'In order to do so I need to respond in the most direct and fair way. I will make mistakes sometimes but I will try and be as fair as possible.

'We have a space to talk and give our opinions. It's everybody's duty to try and improve the game.'

Arsenal have since spoken to Pro Ref about the matter.

Mikel Arteta said his criticism of the referee's decision to award Sunderland a penalty against Arsenal last weekend was through a duty to 'defend my club'

'We discuss many topics and very important all of them. To talk to give their opinions, and everyone's duty to try and improve the game,' he said.

When pushed on what was said, Arteta replied: 'It is a conversation that will remain private.'

He was also asked whether Arsenal received a direct apology like Manchester United did soon after the Manchester derby defeat to Manchester City: 'It is not about an apology. It is about agreeing that the decision should be different or not.'

Meanwhile, Arteta is optimistic that up to four injured defenders could return for the club's trip to the Amex.

Jurrien Timber, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie all did not feature in the midweek Carabao Cup squad against Ipswich Town.

'Everyone is fine. We still have another training session this afternoon, but I'm very optimistic about all of them,' he said.

'They all want to be involved, and we'll use the final session to make sure they're ready.'

Ben White was forced off at half-time at Sunderland but Arteta indicated all is well with his right back, stating: 'All good. We have another training session.'

By Isaan Khan

Sports.title: England squad announcement: Thomas Tuchel admits the 'door is always open' after handing Trent Alexander-Arnold a shock recall and Cole Palmer is back - but Phil Foden misses out
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer has been called up to the England squad after being controversially omitted from the World Cup.

Real Madrid's Trent Alexander-Arnold was also named in Thomas Tuchel squad after being overlooked in the summer.

'They had a good start to the season. they never did something wrong, we just chose different players,' the England coach said Friday.

Palmer and Alexander-Arnold were among a host of high-profile absentees from Tuchel's World Cup squad, along with Phil Foden, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw. There was still no place Foden, Maguire and Shaw for the upcoming Nations League games.

Liverpool's 18-year-old forward Rio Ngumoha has also been included along with Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott.

Palmer´s recall comes after an outstanding start to the season for Chelsea with four goals in six games.

'He has his numbers back, he has his assists back, he has his decisive goals back so that´s why he´s back in the squad and I think he has a point to prove and same goes for Trent,' Tuchel said.

Alexander-Arnold has long-been considered one of English soccer's best talents, but was left out of the World Cup even after right back Tino Livramento was forced to withdraw with injury.

'He was not with us at the World Cup. We trusted other players. I still stick with this decision,' Tuchel said. 'It is now time to fight for his place, he always said he was up for a fight. It´s on him to prove.'

Tuchel said he was forced into more changes than expected due to the unavailability of a number of his World Cup players, including John Stones Djed Spence and Jordan Henderson.

'The door is always open first and foremost through performance and then on the same level through behavior and commitment to the team spirit because we built something very special,' he said.

England plays world champion Spain, Croatia and two games against Czech Republic in the first international window of the season.

England came third at the World Cup, its best place since winning the tournament in 1966. But Tuchel was criticized for his handling of the semifinal defeat to Argentina when leading 1-0 up until the 85th minute before losing 2-1.
