Sports.title: Snubbed Premier League star's WAG hits out at Thomas Tuchel after her in-form partner's omission from England squad with Instagram post
Sports.content:
Morgan Gibbs-White's partner has reminded Thomas Tuchel of the Nottingham Forest star's impressive start to the Premier League season after he was snubbed by the England boss once again.

Britney De Villiers shared a statistic on Instagram that Gibbs-White is the only player to have created over five chances in a single Premier League game so far this season - a figure that has seemingly been overlooked by Three Lions boss Tuchel as he selected his 27-man squad for the three-week international break.

Forest captain Gibbs-White is against strong competition for the No 10 position - with Jude Bellingham, Cole Palmer and Eberechi Eze getting the nod ahead of him this time around.

His omission from last summer's World Cup squad raised eyebrows, given Gibbs-White was the top scorer among English players in the Premier League last season.

Morgan Gibbs-White's partner has hit out at Thomas Tuchel's decision to omit him

The England boss once again overlooked the in-form Nottingham Forest star ahead of the next round of international fixtures

Britney De Villiers reminded Tuchel that her partner is the only player to have created more than five chances in a single Premier League game this season

Speaking from Wembley on Friday, Tuchel explained that it 'makes no sense' to select more than three No 10s in justifying his decision to overlook Gibbs-White.

It is not the first time the family of a footballer has taken aim at the German coach.

Following Harry Maguire's shock snub from the World Cup squad, his mother Zoe tweeted 'absolutely disgusted' and 'no words'.

Maguire also shared a pointed statement, believing he had done enough to earn a place on the plane to the United States.

'I was confident I could of played a major part this summer for my country after the season I’ve had,' he said.

'I’ve been left shocked and gutted by the decision. I’ve loved nothing more than putting that shirt on and representing my country over the years. I wish the players, all the best this summer.'

Maguire's mother, Zoe, later tweeted 'absolutely disgusted' in response to Tuchel's decision. She replied to her son's tweet, saying: 'You couldn't have done anymore. Hold your head high ...Disgraceful.'

Maguire's brothers Joe and Laurence also waded into the escalating row, with Joe labelling it 'the worst decision I've ever seen' while Laurence described it as a 'shambles'.

Sports.title: 'I went up for a corner at the Old Den and got hit with half a house brick!': West Ham legend JULIAN DICKS on 'horrible' trips to rivals Millwall, the vile (and hilarious) abuse he received and what the Hammers MUST do to win Saturday's clash
Sports.content:
'I went up for a corner at the Old Den and got hit with half a house brick!': West Ham legend JULIAN DICKS on 'horrible' trips to rivals Millwall, the vile (and hilarious) abuse he received and what the Hammers MUST do to win Saturday's clash

Given his status as a West Ham legend and cult hero, it feels appropriate that Julian Dicks is talking about getting hammered.

Not on the pitch and not even in an east London boozer, he means it in the sense of Millwall fans hammering him – by throwing both words and heavy items at him.

This Saturday, the two clubs on either side of the River Thames will play each other for the 100th time but the first in 14 years. It is possibly the fiercest rivalry in the United Kingdom, depicted in the Green Street and Football Factories films as hooligan central.

‘You used to get absolutely f***ing hammered,’ Dicks tells Daily Mail Sport in an interview full of laughs, memories and quite a few F-bombs. ‘And I have no doubt it puts people off their games. No doubt whatsoever.

‘The Old Den was brutal, there was a real hatred. It was horrible. You're coming out of the tunnel, they're spitting on you, they're saying they’re going to kill you, they're going to do stuff to your mum, they're going to give everything towards you. You either f***ing take it to heart or you laugh about it.

‘It's very, very volatile. I remember playing at the Old Den, I think it was 1989 and Paul Ince scored, and I got hit with half a house brick when I went up for a corner!’

West Ham legend Julian Dicks has some colourful memories of playing against Millwall. The local rivals meet this weekend for the first time in 14 years

The former left back made more than 250 league appearances for the Hammers in two stints in the 1980s and 1990s

Ever since West Ham were relegated, this game – which will be free-to-air on ITV at 12.30pm – has been at the forefront of supporters' minds. The Met Police have made special preparations for the match, with officers permitted to remove anyone causing disorder within a radius stretching from Bermondsey to Blackheath, and Wapping to Nunhead.

They will have 400 police on the ground and will use live facial recognition technology to identify potential trouble-makers. In 2009, 54 West Ham fans were banned for life in a League Cup game against Millwall dubbed ‘The Upton Park Riot’.

Dicks knows all about the trouble and hopes the players understand the magnitude of the game. ‘I remember once we beat them 1-0 and us going up to clap our fans,’ explains the former full back, who made more than 300 Hammers appearances and also played for Liverpool and Birmingham.

‘We're walking back and all of a sudden, about 30 police were running up with their batons and shields. I remember thinking, “What the f*** are these doing?”. They've put the shields above our heads because the Millwall fans were just pelting us with everything. Coins, marbles, everything you could think of, it was thrown at us.

'To be honest, I always looked forward to playing against Millwall because you knew that you were in for a game, you knew that the atmosphere would be f***ing horrible and nasty.

‘On the pitch, all the players would give everything they had. They would kick you, they would elbow you, they would do anything to put you off your game. And it's the same with the supporters.

‘I went back to the New Den when I was coaching and I got off the bus and this old girl with a lovely voice shouted to me saying, “Julian? Julian?”. I’ve looked round and she’s said, “You’re a f***ing w****r!”. And she was about 75... You never lose it!

‘And then when my daughter was younger, I walked around where I live with her in a pram and a bloke stopped me in a van. He went, “Are you Julian Dicks? I’m a Millwall fan. I f***ing hate you but I wished you played for Millwall”.'

Dicks is supporting the Every Minute Matters campaign in association with Sky Bet and the British Heart Foundation

‘I went back to the New Den as a coach and this old girl shouted to me: “Julian? Julian?”. I’ve look round and she’s said, “You’re a f***ing w****r!”. And she was about 75...'

Unlike other big rivalries in the UK, such as the Old Firm, this one is not about politics or religion – both sets of fans are very alike and from the same backgrounds. It is hooligan-orientated: wanting to have the hardest firm.

Nuno Espirito Santo’s Hammers had a false start to their return to the second tier, failing to win their first three Championship games, but they have been perfect ever since and travel to the New Den top of the league.

Alex Neil’s Millwall, third last season, are 11th having conceded 13 goals in their last five league outings.

‘There's no reason why West Ham shouldn't win the league,’ adds Dicks. ‘They have a good squad but the only thing that lets teams down is work-rate. Obviously, there's lots of goals in the team of late. But it's about doing it every single game.

‘I go back to Frank (Lampard) at Coventry last season. He didn't have the best players, he didn't have the biggest budget but, f*** me, they worked hard. And they got their rewards.

'West Ham do have a big budget and good players, and now they just need to add that other ingredient.

‘If they do, I have no doubt they will go up. People say it might do them good to go down, it don’t do you no f***ing good, I can tell you! It’s awful to go down but hopefully they bounce back.

Tim Breacker, George Parris and Alvin Martin of West Ham confront Alex Rae of Millwall in a feisty league match in November 1992

The Met Police have been planning for the clash for some time and will have up to 400 officers on the ground around the game

‘Jarrod Bowen will have (father-in-law) Danny Dyer in his ear telling him about all the old days. I remember when I signed from Birmingham, supporters let me know how much this game meant to them.

'I don't mean it in a horrible way, but I used to have fan mail saying: “We want to f***ing beat Millwall, you understand?"

'There is a lot of hatred between the fans. Players like Jarrod know that and hopefully he tells the players. Because, listen, Millwall will be bang up for it.’

As part of the Every Minute Matters campaign, Sky Bet and the BHF have assembled football’s 'toughest ever' five-a-side team to tackle fears around using defibrillators, after 69 per cent of fans said fear could stop them using one during a cardiac arrest. Sky Bet's funding is helping the BHF deliver 400 defibrillators to local communities which will improve the survival chances of around 460,000 people in the UK.

Sports.title: The secrets of West Brom's rise revealed: A new recruitment strategy, James Morrison's extraordinary dedication behind the scenes, the academy conveyor belt and the boardroom rebuild
Sports.content:
Joint top of the Championship with a club legend at the helm and chasing a seventh win this century at the home of their greatest rivals. West Bromwich Albion are on the march again and while these are early days, the turbulence of last season is starting to fade from memory.

On Sunday, West Brom tackle Wolves in one of English football’s great fixtures and Baggies fans head for Molineux feeling positive.

Promising head coach James Morrison has guided Albion to 14 points from seven games, the finances look much healthier and supporters have a team starting to make them proud again.

Most importantly, chairman Shilen Patel and the Bilkul Football group appear to have found their feet, two-and-a-half years into their tenure. There should be no repeat of the chaos of last winter, when Eric Ramsay was sacked after only 44 days in charge.

Albion understand there will be trickier days ahead. Yet nearly two years after their impressive boss Carlos Corberan left for Valencia, they are feeling good about themselves once more. And in Morrison, they might just have found Corberan’s natural successor.

As they prepare for the season’s first Black Country derby, Daily Mail Sport looks at how West Brom are building for the future...

West Brom have made a fine start to the season and sit fourth on 14 points, the same total as league leaders West Ham

Club legend Morrison, who takes his team to rivals Wolves on Sunday, was rewarded with a two-year deal last April after keeping Albion up

A CLEAR PLAN

Even when West Brom were staring at relegation to League One, they already knew which way they would go this season. There were plans for both divisions but the focus was clear – invest in youth.

Finally clear of EFL financial restrictions, Albion paid fees totalling £15million for eight outfield players and of those, only 27-year-old midfielder Felix Horn Myhre was over the age of 23.

Midway through last season, Patel discussed the way forward with director of football Ian Pearce and technical director Dominic Price. The trio concluded that if Albion could stay up, it was the perfect chance to reset.

Karlan Grant had been costing the club £2.5m per season under the terms of his move from Huddersfield in 2020 but this summer, his contract finally expired. Other high earners Jed Wallace, Krystian Bielik and Alex Mowatt departed, along with Daryl Dike and Josh Maja.

Albion know that if summer buys Jimmy-Jay Morgan, Rabby Nzingoula or Kareem Tunde shine this season, they may not be able to keep hold of them. It would also mean selling at a profit – far better than watching a highly-paid player in his late-20s or early-30s drift out of contract.

If money is a player’s motivation, you might as well sign him when he’s young and hungry. The standard pay bracket in the second tier is £10-15,000 a week and West Brom are still striving to lower their wage bill since their parachute payments expired in 2023.

You want a better contract? Perform well and you’ll get one. How about Premier League wages? Attract the attention of those clubs by delivering for Albion. This is surely preferable to signing a wealthy journeyman who, naturally, will have at least one eye on his final ‘big’ contract.

Morrison does not scout the players, but Albion would never sign one he had vetoed. Similarly, his recommendations will be heeded.

Former Manchester United midfielder Toby Collyer was on a list of midfielders presented to Morrison as possible targets. Once Morrison insisted Collyer was the only one he wanted, Albion got the £3m deal done. In the case of Morgan, Nzingoula or Tunde, Morrison was handed the information and gave his approval.

West Brom do not pretend this is a revolutionary strategy. At least it is a strategy, though. Don’t forget that last January, West Brom hired Ramsay on the strength of his interview the previous June. Whatever supporters think of the current offering, at least they understand what the club are trying to achieve.

Jimmy-Jay Morgan, 20, joined the Baggies from Chelsea in the summer and already has five goals to his name in all competitions

Albion paid fees totalling £15million this summer for eight outfield players and of those, only 27-year-old midfielder Felix Horn Myhre (pictured) was over the age of 23

NO MORE 'MOZZA’

Morrison was an Albion hero long before he even thought of management. He played for the club from 2007 to 2019, making 341 appearances.

He immediately started coaching in Albion’s impressive academy and when Sam Allardyce was appointed in December 2020, he promoted Morrison to his own backroom team.

With Albion in freefall last February, Morrison stepped up where others might not have. Since then, he has overseen 21 matches in all competitions, winning nine and losing only four.

Even when Morrison was starting to pull West Brom clear of danger, few at the club genuinely believed he would be the long-term solution. He was still ‘Mozza’ rather than ‘Boss’ or ‘Gaffer’. Indeed, when club staff called him ‘Gaffer’ back then, it was usually in jest.

They would not do that anymore. Morrison was rewarded with a two-year deal last April after keeping Albion up and he made his mark instantly.

When all other football staff departed on holiday at the end of the season, Morrison was at the training ground every day for that first fortnight.

The 40-year-old could not rest until he had finalised his coaching team, now comprising Matt Gill, Gavin Strachan, Tony McMahon and Boaz Myhill, and mapped out exactly what pre-season would look like.

Until that was locked down, Morrison ignored those who urged him to take a break. That appetite for hard work is undimmed: after the 1-1 draw with QPR last Saturday, Morrison granted two days off. While his players and colleagues were recharging, Morrison spent a full day at the training ground on Monday, making plans for Molineux.

When all other football staff departed on holiday at the end of the season, Morrison was at the training ground every day for that first fortnight

Born in Darlington, County Durham and a product of the Middlesbrough academy, Morrison is a pleasing contrast to many modern bosses, with their buzzwords that come straight from a coaching manual.

He is quiet, a good listener, and gives simple messages to players. The basic framework is 4-4-2 but this structure can be tweaked game by game depending on the opponent.

There were some at Albion who believed Morrison may become their manager one day – but many more were unsure. Very few envisaged him managing other clubs after Albion. Perhaps, deep down, Morrison wondered the same.

Now, though, those same observers cannot imagine Morrison in any other role and if he, too, harboured those doubts, they have surely disappeared. The Albion boss certainly isn’t plain old ‘Mozza’ anymore.

ACADEMY BENEFITS

West Brom are close to agreeing a new deal with homegrown midfielder Harry Whitwell, whose contract expires at the end of the season. The 20-year-old has impressed this season and has interest from elsewhere, including Premier League clubs, but Albion officials are very optimistic that he will stay at the Hawthorns.

Even in the tough times, Albion continued to fund their academy and it has delivered. Tom Fellows was sold to Southampton for a possible £10m. Goalkeeper Alex Palmer joined Ipswich in a deal worth up to £4m.

Fans were not happy the club received only £6m when Dara O’Shea moved to Burnley in 2023 but at the time, Albion were probably six months from going into administration.

The respected Training Ground Guru platform recently ranked Albion’s academy – which retains Category One status – the 10th best in the country.

Morgan Rogers is often cited as the one who got away. The England forward is now one of the most expensive players of all time, having joined Chelsea from Aston Villa for £117m last summer. He cost Manchester City only £5m when they took him from Albion's academy aged 17 – yet once a wealthy Premier League club arrive on the scene, youth players are very hard to keep. It is doubtful Albion would have received any more had the matter gone to tribunal.

Under the stewardship of Richard Stevens, who has just completed seven years at the club, the academy is run with care and humility.

Though they lost key staff to Aston Villa during Christian Purslow’s time as CEO at Villa Park, Albion’s academy did not take significant damage. They are confident their methods will send more youngsters to the first team, with Whitwell the latest from the conveyor belt.

Albion have continued to fund their academy and it has delivered with Tom Fellows (right) sold to Southampton for a possible £10m

WHERE NEXT?

It has been a good start – but a start is all it is. It usually takes a little more than that to excite Albion supporters and not even a win over Wolves would have them all betting on promotion.

The most important factor now is that the key people share the same ideas. Mark Miles returned to the club as executive director last February following the departure of Andrew Nestor, who split opinion at the Hawthorns.

Miles has rebuilt the leadership team and the ownership group are prepared to allow their senior staff the space to do their jobs. Revenue was up eight per cent in the last accounts and losses down.

A long way to go, then, but West Brom are definitely heading in the right direction.

Sports.title: Liverpool and Leeds legend Gary McAllister, 61, 'faces financial ruin' after being hit with bankruptcy petition - with Scot involved in tax-avoidance scheme alongside fellow ex-players
Sports.content:
Liverpool and Leeds legend Gary McAllister, 61, 'faces financial ruin' after being hit with bankruptcy petition - with Scot involved in tax-avoidance scheme alongside fellow ex-players

Gary McAllister is facing the threat of financial ruin after being hit with a bankruptcy petition by HM Revenue and Customs.

The Liverpool and Leeds legend, 61, has been taken to court by HMRC over an unpaid tax bill, with the amount owed yet to be disclosed.

As reported by the Telegraph, McAllister is understood to have been among a number of high-profile footballers who invested in film partnerships that were subsequently ruled to be tax avoidance schemes by HMRC.

The schemes offered investors substantial tax relief by using relatively modest investments backed by significant loans.

McAllister has not been accused of deliberately evading tax. His representatives say he believed his tax adviser was handling the matter with HMRC and that he is now seeking to bring the dispute to a swift conclusion.

HMRC has spent years pursuing ex-footballers and celebrities involved in the scheme for unpaid tax.

Gary McAllister is facing the threat of financial ruin after being hit with a bankruptcy petition

A spokesman told the Telegraph: 'We take a supportive approach to dealing with customers who have tax debts and do everything we can to help those who engage with us to get out of debt, such as offering instalment plans. We only petition for bankruptcy as a last resort.'

McAllister, who is widely regarded as one of Scotland's greatest ever midfielders, enjoyed a successful career before his retirement in 2004.

He played a key role during Leeds United's title-winning campaign in 1991-92, helping the Yorkshire club win the last ever English First Division before it was rebranded to the Premier League.

After four years with Coventry City in the mid-1990s, the Scottish later joined Liverpool in 2000 and won the FA Cup, UEFA Cup and League Cup over a two-year spell at Anfield.

His career came to an end at Coventry, where he took on the role of player-manager in 2002, having made more than 150 appearances for the club across two spells.

Chalking up 57 caps over his glittering career, McAllister also captained Scotland for four years and famously missed a penalty against England during his country's 2-0 defeat at the 1996 European Championship.

McAllister is one of several former footballers facing the threat of bankruptcy.

Daily Mail Sport revealed earlier this month that HMRC had filed a petition with the High Court to have former Liverpool star Jamie Carragher declared bankrupt over an unpaid tax bill reportedly worth between £700,000 and £800,000.

The Liverpool legend is understood to have been among a number of high-profile footballers who invested in film partnerships that were later ruled to be tax avoidance schemes

Last year, it was also reported that former Liverpool defender Steve Finnan and ex-Manchester City winger Shaun Wright-Phillips were facing separate bankruptcy petitions.

David James, Wes Brown, Lee Hendrie, Trevor Sinclair and John Barnes are among the former Premier League footballers to have been declared bankrupt by HMRC since 2010.

Sports.title: Extraordinary moment Martin O'Neill shuts down female reporter in 'patronising' and 'condescending' post-match interview after Europa League defeat
Sports.content:
Martin O'Neill has come under fire for his 'patronising' and 'condescending' response to a female TV reporter after he refused to explain his team selection following Celtic's 3-1 loss in the Europa League on Thursday.

The Scottish giants were soundly beaten by Hungarian outfit Ferencvaros in a dismal start to their Europa League campaign, with O'Neill making four changes to the side that lost 3-0 to Old Firm rivals Rangers on Sunday.

Goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo was recalled to the starting XI in place of Sam Johnstone, while Oliver Sorensen, Haissem Hassan and James Forrest were also brought in by O'Neill.

When questioned about his team selection by TNT Sports reporter Connie McLaughlin after the game, O'Neill shut down the journalist in a manner described as 'patronising' and 'condescending' by fans on social media.

'No, I won't talk to you about the thinking behind that there. Sinisalo was always going to play that game as well too,' he told McLaughlin.

'Believe it or not Connie, my job is not to explain every single situation to you, much as you are going to ask and I'm delighted you are.'

Martin O'Neill has come under fire for his 'condescending' interview with a female TV reporter

Fans were angry with O'Neill's 'patronising' manner towards reporter Connie McLaughlin

Celtic were beaten 3-1 by Hungarian outfit Ferencvaros in the Europa League on Thursday

When McLaughlin then suggested that supporters would be asking the same question, O'Neill responded: 'I'll tell the fans through Celtic TV.'

O'Neill has since faced widespread criticism on social media, with many supporters accusing him of being 'misogynistic' as well as supercilious.

Much of the backlash appears to have stemmed from viewers mishearing him call McLaughlin 'honey' when he actually said 'Connie', and the reporter has since taken to Instagram herself in an attempt to set the record straight.

'Glad I came back from Portugal,' she joked sarcastically on her Instagram story after conducting the spiky interview, before clarifying: 'Connie not honey'.

Droves of fans still hit out at O'Neill's patronising manner on social media.

'Very condescending - this type of attitude is what we need to get out the game,' one fan posted to X.

A second added: 'Horrible little condescending man.'

'Embarrassing himself and his club here,' wrote a third.

Another supporter furiously said: 'What a horrible and odious man he's shown himself to be. Not the first time he's spoken to a female reporter like that either.'

True to his word, O'Neill later addressed his team selection on Celtic TV.

'I think, in terms of balancing things, there are one or two players who deserve an opportunity,' he said.

McLaughlin took to Instagram to clarify that O'Neill referred to her as 'Connie' and not 'honey'

Fans hit out at O'Neill on social media, describing his attitude as 'condescending' and 'odious'

'For instance, James starts tonight. He has been an impact player for us and has been really terrific in that time. We have to give him a chance now to start a game.

'Will he last out the match? We do not know. He is 35 years of age, or whatever the case may be, but he has been a great player.

'There are a couple of things we have done tonight. Some players deserve to start in the side, James being one of them. Let us go and see how it goes.'

Sports.title: Inside the Beat Luke Littler auditions: Hundreds of darts hopefuls queue for hours to get their shot at facing star live on Netflix and winning £501k... and even Fallon Sherrock turns up!
Sports.content:
Thousands – filled with hope and confidence – arrive in east London for a chance to win £501,000.

Queues develop after an 8am start in Stratford, snaking around the Olympic Park. All for their shot at beating the most famous darts player around.

The idea of Luke Littler's new big-money Netflix show is simple. Can a novice beat Littler in a leg of darts? Up to 20 will try to do just that live on Netflix on October 30 in the streaming giant's new venture Beat Luke Littler.

Anyone who can topple the reigning world champion and world No 1 will take home a life-changing £501,000. Gary Lineker is the host, with Richard Osman providing expert analysis.

But first – the preliminary rounds, the audition – before the fame. Not just anyone will get an opportunity to potentially upstage Littler.

Contestants are allowed to prepare before a producer bellows out the rules. Another asks questions on camera: 'What would you do with the money? How did you get into darts? Don't answer like this, answer like this.' That's showbiz.

Surrounded by big purple and yellow advertising reading 'Beat Luke Littler' referees set out the rules and take their positions to ensure there's no cheating the automated scoring system.

More than 3,000 hopefuls auditioned for Netflix's 'Beat Luke Littler' in Stratford, London

Up to 20 people will be given the chance to win £501,000 on Netflix - all they have to do is beat Littler in a leg of darts

The aim of the first stage is to complete a leg of darts in 24 throws or fewer. No ifs, no buts, no second chances. It's no easy feat. This part-timer may achieve it on a good day – locked away in his spare room while music plays on late evening. Under this sort of pressure is a different story. As expected, failure was the outcome.

But a lot of these contestants don't crumble under the pressure – they thrive off it.

'I can beat anyone on my day,' one auditionee, who wrapped up his leg in 12 darts, tells Daily Mail Sport. Wrap things up in 12 again on October 30 and he will more than likely find himself £501,000 richer.

Two or three participants make it through to the next stage. They are awarded a green sticker. 'Thanks for coming, and, if you didn't make it, don't worry - it's hard,' shouts another producer.

There are various abilities on show. Some wear jeans and get nowhere close. Others don their own personal darts shirts but struggle for a double. Others ease through – including 'Queen of the Palace' Fallon Sherrock.

For Sherrock, who has won two matches at the World Championship before – it's all part of the day job. She's probably the most famous face here. Anyone who has never held a tour card can enter – Sherrock may have won matches at the Alexandra Palace, but she's never been on the tour.

'I did it in 18,' she tells Daily Mail Sport. 'My scoring wasn't very good, but I took out a 157.

'I don't need the money, but I have always said I would like more opportunities to promote the women's game, and this is the perfect opportunity to do it. Why wouldn't you? It would be stupid for me not to do it.

'The queue was very long. We joined at 8am and got in at near enough 11am. But I can do it - and I do speak to Luke. I know him, I know his mum, his dad, Faith, and they are lovely, genuine people.'

Daily Mail Sport auditioned for the new show - but failed to make it past the first stage

Those with the skill or fortunate enough to make it to the second stage face an interview with the production team, where they will discuss their approach to the challenge, how they would prepare to face Littler, and how they'd perform under pressure.

Even fewer will then make it to the final stage. That involves a chat with an expert judging panel, including 16-time world champion Phil Taylor.

Darts mastermind Barry Hearn walks past. 'Alright, lads?' he quips to the press.

Taylor is in for the long-haul, an 11-hour day in total. 'I think someone will win it,' he says. 'They have got a chance. It's all about holding your bottle on a double.

'It's been different. I've never done anything like this before. It's similar to the X-Factor, but you have to be a bit nicer with this one. I'm not Simon Cowell.

'It's about encouraging the players, especially the youngsters coming through. It's very nerve-wracking for them. But we are looking for confidence, ability, and they have to be dedicated. It's not easy - you have to be so professional now. I was 30 when I first turned pro - some of them now are 13, 14, 15. To ask them to be professional at that age is very difficult.'

Laura Turner (left), Barry Hearn (centre) and Phil Taylor (right) are on the judging panel for the final stage of the audition process

The volume of interest in the show runs in line with the growth of the sport since Littler burst onto the scene

Littler isn't here. He's taking some time off before getting back into action with more Players Championship events and the World Grand Prix among events to come soon.

It's unclear what he really thinks about this show – nothing is really on the line for him compared to the competitors, bar maybe pride.

'If you can go out in 12 darts, and you want to beat Luke Littler in a game of 501, he has to go out in nine, or you're half a million richer,' Taylor tells Daily Mail Sport. 'That's the secret.

'Luke is very laid back, quiet, very talented. Nothing fazes him, but the one attribute he has for me is he isn't bothered about the money. It's a bonus. I was always bothered about the money when I started - I had children, a mortgage to pay.

'I have had a throw with him. Not competitive. But I would love to get my form back, I am practicing a little bit. I am a bit too old now. I love retirement - it's great being at home. I ask my wife if we should go on holiday and we don't want to go away anymore, we travelled that much. I missed my family.'

While speaking to Taylor, one or two more competitors try their luck. One owns an international flavouring company. Another is an electrician. They both have their green stickers and are waiting to speak to producers before potentially being put in front of the judges.

Simple maths says around 600 dart hopefuls will make it through the first stage here in London. That number will be whittled down to barely double figures by the time they have met the judges. The same process will happen in Manchester. Those auditions take place on Saturday at Manchester Central Convention Complex – you can visit BeatLukeLittler.com for more information on how to apply.

Leaving four hours after arriving the queues are still as long. A member of the Netflix production team tells us they think way more hopefuls have arrived than expected.

One thing is obvious: this idea, so far, is a hit. The attraction and attention runs parallel with the rise of darts since Littler burst on the scene. Next month, those that look up to the 19-year-old will have the chance to beat him and win big money. Why wouldn't you turn up?

Watch Beat Luke Littler live on Netflix on October 30

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy statement released after star gets big boost by BMW Championship officials
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy statement released after star gets big boost by BMW Championship officials

Rory McIlroy found himself at the centre of a ruling which potentially set a precedent for the remainder of the tournament

View 2 Images Rory McIlroy's opening round didn't pass without incident (Image: Daniel Weir/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock)

The opening round of the BMW PGA Championship featured an unusual moment involving Rory McIlroy which left commentators scratching their heads. However, following an on-air discussion regarding the rules, the DP World Tour explained the logic behind giving the Masters champion relief at the 14th hole.

‌



McIlroy was two under par through his first four holes when he took on the par-three 14th, his fifth hole of the day after beginning the round on the back nine. He found himself in a bit of trouble, though, dragging his tee shot to the left of the green.

‌



The shot left the Northern Irishman in a tight spot, with his ball on a narrow strip of grass with a fence on one side and a cart path on another. He appeared to have an unplayable lie but the wording of the rules left the Sky Sports broadcast team uncertain when it came to whether he would get relief.

‌



McIlroy demonstrated to an official that he had no reasonable shot with his right hand but might be able to play the ball with his left were it not for the position of the path. The official ruled that, because of the 'reasonable' shot, McIlroy was allowed relief.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Shane Lowry's private text to Rory McIlroy after Irish Open champion skipped celebration READ MORE :

Following the ruling, McIlroy was able to save par. He enjoyed a fruitful front nine to move into the lead at -5 but eventually finished his round three under par, three shots adrift of co-leaders Aaron Rai and Joakim Lagergren.

"To the left of the 14th hole is an immovable obstruction i.e. the cart path. As the stretch of grass near the boundary fence is very narrow, the grass has been tied into the path and is part of the immovable obstruction," DP World Tour told Golf.com.

"If a player has a shot and can play the ball he is entitled to relief, even if the ball is on the stretch of grass. Therefore, in this situation, the player dropped the ball at his nearest point of relief because he could play the ball," the statement continued. Mirror Sport has reached out to the tour for further comment.

Article continues below

View 2 Images McIlroy finished his opening round three off the lead (Image: Daniel Weir/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock)

A couple of late bogeys ended any hope McIlroy had of ending the day in top spot and he admitted his frustration at how the round ended. "A stumble home is a good way to put it," he said.

"I wish I was standing here a couple of shots better. That's what I feel I should be, but overall, I saw some good signs in my game and saw some putts go in, which was encouraging compared to last week. It's definitely a score I can build on."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel backs FA's Gianni Infantino stance and sends message to England star
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel backs FA's Gianni Infantino stance and sends message to England star

Thomas Tuchel was speaking after selecting his first England squad since the Three Lions' suffered more World Cup heartbreak following defeat to Argentina in the semi-final

View 3 Images England boss Thomas Tuchel

Thomas Tuchel has backed the Football Association’s strong stance against Gianni Infantino.

‌



FA chair Debbie Hewitt this week wrote to the beleaguered FIFA president demanding answers over the World Cup sell-off plan and also clarity on why Folarin Balogun’s suspension was overturned.

‌



England boss Tuchel likened the FA’s support for him as to why he also backed their stance and his voice will be loud among the UEFA protest against Infantino.

‌



Tuchel said: “I felt the full support from all my bosses through the World Cup, through the whole tournament.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“There was a moment, a very special moment before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me: ‘We know that anything can happen in a football match and we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico in a World Cup, but don't worry, we see what's going on and we want to continue like this.’

“This was a beautiful moment for me as a coach,” said Tuchel before throwing his weight behind their stance.

“I just told you how I am backed from my bosses, so it's the minimum I can do is back my bosses, I would say,” Tuchel said. “So they have my full support on that and I back their opinion.”

‌



View 3 Images The English Football Association want answers from FIFA President Gianni Infantino (Image: Getty Images)

Meanwhile, the England boss has been promised game time after his England World Cup snub.

Tuchel said he felt a “duty” to play Mainoo in at least one of the four Nations League games after the Manchester United midfielder did not get a single minute for England in the summer.

‌



But Tuchel called him up this time and spelt out just how much he wants to play him after the disappointment of the summer. He said: “I expect him to be on the pitch and it’s my duty to put him on the pitch.

View 3 Images Kobbie Mainoo was a spectator for England at this summer's World Cup (Image: Europa Press Sports/Europa Press via Getty Images)

“That was totally on me, he did not put a foot wrong at the World Cup. He was class in behaviour and on the training pitch.

‌



“It was a big competition. We also played Reecey [James] in midfield, Elliot Anderson is fantastic, Declan Rice is a very unique player. So we trusted them more than we trusted Kobbie.

“It was difficult for him, difficult for me. He got injured before the France game [the third-place play-off] so we could not even give him minutes there which hurt me. Maybe he was more hurt but it was my responsibility.”

Sports.title: England squad LIVE: Palmer and Trent back as snubbed star's partner takes aim at Thomas Tuchel
Sports.content:
Everton have had an unusual start to the season. For all the chaos off the pitch, on it they have been pretty good. Unbeaten across four Premier League games and having safely navigated passage to the last 16 in the Carabao Cup, there is a sense of pride at Finch Farm at the team’s achievements so far.

That work means the club approaches this squad announcement with interest. Jordan Pickford is one of the first names on Thomas Tuchel’s teamsheet, his call-up is a given.

James Garner made his England debut last year and was unfortunate not to make the World Cup squad. Given his ability to act as a defensive midfielder and a genuinely competent right-back, there were times during the competition when his absence appeared an obvious mistake.

Garner underwent hernia surgery in the summer and, while he is nearing full fitness, this might be a squad too early for his return. He suggested that was his belief when speaking to the Liverpool Echo this week - though he could, of course, have been keeping a poker face.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall is in contention for a first call-up. His wonderful form heading into Christmas meant he appeared on course for that accolade before a hamstring injury halted his momentum. He has repeatedly delivered good performances in front of Tuchel and has started the season well. His problem is, under Moyes, he operates in an area England have buckets of talent, but Tuchel has him on his radar and he would deserve a place should he get it.

The big question for Everton is Jarrad Branthwaite. There is no doubt at the club that he has what it takes to become a world class centre back and his performances this season have been colossal. He would have been at the World Cup had he not suffered a miserable campaign with injury. The early signs are that he is over them, but this international break offers a dilemma. A three-week break after his first stretch of games in six months would likely do him good. But David Moyes takes pride in his players being called up and everyone wants Jarrad to make his argument for not just a role in the squad, but progression into the starting XI. He is the future if his body allows him to be.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick points blame for Man Utd struggles and responds to sack question
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick points blame for Man Utd struggles and responds to sack question

Manchester United have won just two of their opening six games in all competitions and there's pressure on Michael Carrick ahead of their clash with Fulham on Sunday

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is happy to take the flack (Image: MUTV)

Steadfast Michael Carrick has told fans to 'blame me' for Manchester United's dismal start to the season. The Red Devils have only mustered four points from their opening four Premier League games ahead of Sunday's trip to Fulham.

‌



Carrick's side were also dumped out of the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle in midweek. United threw away an early two-goal lead and lost 3-2 at home to Brighton, compounding their misery after a controversial defeat to rivals City in the Manchester derby four days prior.

‌



Facing questions over his position already, Carrick came out firing during his pre-match press conference and made it clear that he's happy to take the flack. "It's my responsibility, I'm fine with that," the United manager said.

‌



"It's not a blame game. We always search for things to look at and find the blame, sometimes it gets too much of wanting to find the blame. Blame me, it's no problem, but it's not about blaming people. It's about finding solutions. It's a whole collective thing.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"It's about what you focus on really. I'm totally happy taking responsibility - no problem with that. I know where we want to get to and we want to get there fast.

Carrick also labelled the speculation over his future 'ridiculous', shooting down suggestions that he needs results quickly to avoid the sack. "I think that'll be a lot longer than one or two games of results," he continued.

"I understand, first of all, taking away all that, that's irrelevant for me. I know the club, I know the role, I know what's expected here in terms of playing to a certain standard, playing at a certain level, achieving certain things on the pitch, so I get all that.

‌



"In terms of future and ownership and how long I've got in the job, I'm thinking one part of it, like how long have I got, it's ridiculous to think that way in a position that I'm in, that's just not on the radar.

Is Michael Carrick the right man for Manchester United? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick rubbished speculation over his future (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

‌



"I understand what we need to achieve and where we need to be as a football club for the owners, what they expect, for the supporters as much as anything, I get all that.

"It's two or three games that we haven't had certain results, and two or three games too many because I really hate losing, but that doesn't mean that the world caves in. In some minds it does, it can't for us, because we've got to perform."

Carrick also provided updates on Luke Shaw and Carlos Baleba, saying that both players have a 'chance' to feature at Craven Cottage. Baleba is yet to make his debut for the Red Devils since moving to Old Trafford in August for £70million because of an ankle injury.

Article continues below

"Not totally 100 per cent on either," Carrick explained. "It is really short term [with Shaw] but it is just working towards the game."

Sports.title: Keely Hodgkinson shares strange MRI scan results with 'abnormal' issue found
Sports.content:
Keely Hodgkinson shares strange MRI scan results with 'abnormal' issue found

Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson has admitted to dealing with an unusual injury issue

View 2 Images Keely Hodgkinson has shared an issue that was identified by an MRI scan (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

Keely Hodgkinson has revealed that MRI results show she is competing with an abnormal hamstring. The 800m star is set to end her season at Athlos on Friday.

‌



The Olympic champion started her campaign in impressive fashion, setting a new indoor world record and later claiming the World Indoor Championship title in March. More recently, her season has been defined by second-place finishes to rival Audrey Werro at the European Championships and World Ultimate Championship.

‌



The 24-year-old has refused to make excuses for her losses to Werro but has admitted to suffering a hamstring tear when battling for the European title in Birmingham. The injury occurred just a month after Hodgkinson sustained deep cuts to her knees and jarred her back due to a freak fall in Manchester.

‌



While the latter may have contributed to her hamstring issue, Hodgkinson was still able to make it to the start line for both of her recent duels with Werro. Her quick recovery time was aided by the Team GB star’s hamstring abnormality, which has allowed her to continue competing.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

“My body’s quite literally built differently,” Hodgkinson told The Telegraph. “I have two tendons… where everyone has one tendon. We’re trying to figure out if it’s a strength or a weakness as, when one of them tears, I still have another one because it’s split. It means that you don’t feel the injury until later on when it gets a bit tight.”

‌



Reflecting on her injury during the European Championships, Hodgkinson said: “I was like, ‘Oh, something’s not quite right’ but it didn’t affect me during the race.”

The injury setbacks have contributed to Hodgkinson’s mixed fortunes on the track. However, her unusual hamstring can also work in the British icon’s favour after the issue was identified in 2025.

“Yeah, it’s just how I’m made. We found that on an MRI scan last year when I tore it,” she explained. “As a pro, it means that when one is down, I can still run on the one that works. As a con, maybe it’s slightly weaker than the one that’s [normally] attached.

‌



“You can still run on them. So I haven’t missed any training, I’ve just had to alter my approach. I’ve had to take my foot off the speed, because that’s when it’s most risky. But my body heals very, very well, so I couldn’t really feel anything.”

View 2 Images Hodgkinson will aim to end her season with a win at Athlos (Image: Maja Hitij/World Athletics via Getty Images)

Having claimed the indoor record earlier this season, Hodgkinson had set her sights on eclipsing the overall record of 1:53.28, which has been held by Jarmila Kratochvilova since 1983. Hodgkinson’s personal best currently stands at 1:54.33, while her rival Werro ran 1:53.70 earlier this year.

Article continues below

“I wanted to get this world record. I’m good, but I need someone to help me push to these times,” Hodgkinson said. “It’s too difficult on your own. Audrey’s done incredible this year. I think we will get that eventually. I hope everyone’s enjoyed watching. I’ve still enjoyed competing even though it’s not quite been the season I wanted.”

She is set to sign off for the season at Athlos on Friday, an all-women’s event being held in Barnet. Defending champion Hodgkinson could earn £48,000 ($65,000) for winning the 800m event, while series champions will receive an extra £18,000 ($25,000) and a Tiffany & Co. crown.

Sports.title: Conor Benn is still box office and can come again but he is done at welterweight
Sports.content:
Conor Benn is still box office and can come again but he is done at welterweight

Conor Benn suffered a humbling knockout defeat to Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas, with the British fighter now needing to rebuild his career at the highest level

View 2 Images Conor Benn was knocked out by Ryan Garcia inside two rounds

Conor Benn is doing the right thing taking time out. There is much to process after a crushing defeat like the one he suffered against Ryan Garcia.

Though Benn has made a ton of money, that will be little consolation as he works through what went wrong and how to build back.

He was clearly weight drained against WBC welterweight champion Garcia, who not only showed his pedigree, he exposed Benn’s lack of experience in elite company.

Benn is a better fighter than he appeared but he has not campaigned at the highest level. He needs to accept that and rebuild slowly.

People are doubting him now, calling out his quality. Ok. Own it and use that as motivation. It is pretty clear he is done at welterweight.

Conor Benn questions his future in emotional statement after Ryan Garcia defeat READ MORE :

Chris Eubank Jr ruthlessly trolls Conor Benn in 11 words after Ryan Garcia fight disaster READ MORE :

He fought Chris Eubank Jnr twice at middleweight. Your body adjusts to the heavier weight making it almost impossible to drop two divisions successfully.

Yes he beat a fading Regis Prograis at welter after the Eubank Jnr fights but that is a different proposition to prime Garcia in Las Vegas.

He endured against Garcia the same difficulty Eubank Jnr faced against him. When you shift weight to that degree the sacrifices are just too great. Power, stamina, resistance are all down and you become a tame shadow of yourself.

Benn is still box office. He can come again. But he has to prove himself. I would caution against jumping straight back in against WBO middleweight champion Denzel Bentley.

View 2 Images Benn could take on WBO Middleweight World Champion Denzel Bentley in his next fight

You can see the appeal, an all-British clash for the belt his father once held, but that kind of engagement is the last thing he needs off the back of a devastating loss.

Super welterweight might be a better division in which to find his feet. He should forget going for a world title for now. Garcia can take his pick. He is already calling out Teofimo Lopez, and there is a rematch with Devin Haney to savour.

I take Garcia to win both. Lopez is tagged for May. Garcia is naturally bigger and can fight going forward or backwards. Garcia matches the speed of Lopez and he can use his fast feet and hands to get in and out of range.

I think he is just too strong and explosive for Haney. The real test for Garcia would be Jaron Boots Ennis. He’d have to move up to 154 for that, and wouldn’t be favourite, but what a contest that would be.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta reveals private talks with Pro Ref bosses after Arsenal complaints
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta reveals private talks with Pro Ref bosses after Arsenal complaints

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta pulled no punches after Sunderland were awarded a penalty in last weekend's game and has now been asked about his conversations with Pro Ref

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has spoken with Pro Ref (Image: Sky Sports)

Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Pro Ref have been in touch with Arsenal following his complaints over the penalty decision in last week's win at Sunderland but refused to divulge any further details.

‌



The Gunners came away from Wearside with a hard-fought 2-0 victory courtesy of goals from Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka. But the result could have been very different after Sunderland were awarded a penalty with the game goalless, David Raya instead producing a superb save to thwart Enzo le Fee.

‌



Arteta was irate after the game and insisted the penalty decision, made after Ezri Konsa pulled down Dan Ballard in the area, was "unacceptable".

‌



"This can change the course of a season," he fumed. "It's not acceptable. I have watched it 10 times to make sure, because I watched it live and I said it's not possible to be a penalty because it's a judo roll, that's what it is. This cannot happen.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"In my view. I have been involved in football for 27 or 28 years. It's not a penalty in any game, in any game, in any context in any league. I'm so pleased in one sense, I'm so worried in another."

Jamie Carragher suggested Arteta was speaking from a position of power, likening it to Sir Alex Ferguson. But Arteta responded on Friday, saying: "No, I'm here to try to give my opinion. To defend my club, to give the very best to our players. In order to do so, obviously, you guys ask some questions and we need to respond in the most direct and fair way.

"I will make mistakes, sometimes, but I will try to be as fair as possible.

‌



"We discuss many topics in this room, very important all of them. We have a space to talk, give our opinions, have discussions, have personal conversations. It's everybody's duty to try and improve the game and that's what we are here for."

View 2 Images Arteta slammed the decision to penalise Ezri Konsa for a pull on Dan Ballard (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

When he was then asked if the club had heard from Pro Ref, Arteta responded: "It is a conversation that will remain private."

‌



Manchester United received an apology for the error which saw VAR intervene to allow Erling Haaland's winning goal in the Manchester derby to stand despite Enzo Fernandez being in an offside position in another recent high-profile incident.

On the subject of an apology, Arteta said: "It's not about an apology. It's just agreeing that the decision should have been different or not, maybe they have a different opinion. Try to improve and move forward together."

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy's £9m mansion he retreats to after BMW Championship with famous neighbours
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy's £9m mansion he retreats to after BMW Championship with famous neighbours

Rory McIlroy has been competing at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth Club this week, which is a stone's throw from his luxury residence

View 7 Images Rory McIlroy can walk to his extravagant mansion from this week's event (Image: Getty Images)

Rory McIlroy wrapped up his opening round at the 2026 BMW PGA Championship and then had just a short walk back to his new £9million mansion at Wentworth.

‌



This week's tournament marks McIlroy's first appearance at Wentworth Club since moving into the exclusive gated estate with his wife Erica and their daughter Poppy. It is a substantial advantage for the Holywood-born star who typically depends on his private jet for travelling to and from tournaments.

‌



The six-time Major champion has relocated his main summer base from Jupiter, Florida. McIlroy said ahead of the tournament that playing virtually on his doorstep makes the week feel like a true home fixture.

‌



"It's always nice to be back, I guess even more meaningful now that we have a home here," he said. "It really does feel like a home event. I haven't always had the best of times around the West Course, but certainly over the last few years I've played well here, given myself some chances to win.

"I feel it's a great event. A great field is always assembled, and we always play in front of an amazing atmosphere. Honestly, it's one of my favourite weeks of the year. Looking forward to getting going again."

Shane Lowry's private text to Rory McIlroy after Irish Open champion skipped celebration READ MORE :

McIlroy launched his week on Wednesday with a stunning, flawless 12-under-par 60 to steal the show in the celebrity Pro-Am alongside teammates including Stuart Broad. The back-to-back Masters champion carded nine birdies and an eagle across a breathtaking 10-hole stretch.

‌



His impressive form carried into his opening official round on Thursday, where he completed it with a solid 3-under-par 69. Since his debut at the BMW PGA Championship in 2008, McIlroy has forged an outstanding record, claiming the title in 2014 and finishing as runner-up on three occasions.

View 7 Images The mansion in Wentworth, pictured before a makeover, which Rory McIlroy and his family bought (Image: N/A)

With him now a local resident, that record looks set to improve further. The 37-year-old snapped up the property in 2023 and it was already among the finest homes in the area before the couple embarked on a renovation project.

‌



McIlroy has completely transformed the six-bedroom mansion after leaving their £16.5m residence in Florida. Our photographs were taken prior to the golfer beginning his renovation work, while the property was still on the market in the prestigious estate.

Nevertheless, the stunning features that await the family as they settle into life in the UK are plain to see. "Straight after Augusta, we travelled over to see the house as it was going through the finishing touches," McIlroy said earlier this year. "It was fun to see and we could've stayed in it, but we wanted to get over to Holywood first."

View 7 Images The home cinema at Rory McIlroy's Wentworth home (Image: N/A)

‌



Upon stepping inside, visitors are greeted by a sweeping staircase and a welcoming fireplace, complemented by traditional artwork and an array of rugs across the floors. It's likely that McIlroy and Erica have since put their own stamp on this entrance hall with some personal interior design touches.

Moving through to the living room, the generously sized space features two sofa suites, a plush single armchair and yet another fireplace. The open-plan layout gives the new owners a clear sightline into the seating area from the kitchen.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The couple are also likely to have given the living room a makeover, with McIlroy's impressive trophy collection expected to grace the bookshelves alongside a top-of-the-range entertainment system.

Perhaps most impressive of all is a spectacular home cinema room, large enough to host a proper movie night with friends and family. A vast television dominates one wall, while the remaining walls are painted a deep red, nodding to the charm of classic old-school picture houses.

View 7 Images The bathroom at Rory McIlroy's new Wentworth property (Image: NA)

‌



Plush leather recliners fill the room, along with a small central table, perfect for resting your snacks and drinks during a film. This room, too, will undoubtedly have received the McIlroy treatment, as the family set about modernising the entire property and enhancing its overall value.

The property continues with six bedrooms and an undisclosed number of bathrooms. One bathroom featured online showcases a generous bathtub and a wet-floor shower.

The bathroom is fitted with all-white fixtures, including a floating toilet and bidet. Natural daylight streams through two windows positioned beside the bath, complementing the LED overhead lighting throughout the space.

‌



Another aquatic feature is the spectacular indoor pool, accompanied by a hot tub and floor-to-ceiling patio windows wrapping around half the room. The pool's illumination mirrors the water's shade, with deep blue tones establishing a tranquil environment where McIlroy will likely unwind after his professional commitments.

View 7 Images The entrance hall at Rory McIlroy's Wentworth property, with a grand staircase and open fire (Image: NA)

This represents one of the most contemporary spaces in the entire property and is something the golfer may opt to preserve as is. That said, he might enhance the area by incorporating a sauna or red-light therapy facilities - both popular recovery methods for modern athletes.

‌



McIlroy is believed to have invested up to £14m altogether when factoring in the costs of renovations to extend and modernise the estate. The property's exterior matches its interior splendour, with attractive trees, landscaping and immaculately kept lawns bordering the driveway leading to the residence.

With a home course at one of England's most prestigious golfing establishments, it comes as no surprise that McIlroy counts some of the UK and Europe's most recognisable celebrities among his neighbours.

View 7 Images The indoor pool at the Wentworth property bought by Rory McIlroy

‌



Four-time Major champion and former World No.1 Ernie Els was not only once a resident of Wentworth, having owned a property along the 16th hole, but was appointed the club's "world-wide touring professional" in 2005 and has overseen two major redesigns of the West course.

Back in 1992, the former Duchess of York, Sarah Ferguson, found herself at the centre of a media frenzy involving her American financier boyfriend John Bryan. This led her to seek refuge in the gated community of Wentworth and Romenda Lodge.

Few residents of Wentworth Estate are more celebrated than singer-songwriter Sir Elton John, who first moved there in the 1970s and is renowned for hosting numerous extravagant parties over the years. The cover of his 1974 compilation album Elton John's Greatest Hits was also photographed at his Wentworth home.

Article continues below

View 7 Images The living area, opening into the kitchen at the Wentworth property bought by Rory McIlroy (Image: NA)

Former Ukraine and Chelsea forward Andriy Shevchenko also possesses a £7m residence at Wentworth where, in 2012, he reportedly sought council approval to construct a six-car garage featuring remote-controlled hydraulic ramps to raise or lower vehicles from an underground car park.

His former Chelsea colleague John Terry is another avid golfer and has a property in the vicinity. Another notable Wentworth Estate resident is 2013 US Open champion and ex-World No.1 Justin Rose, who was raised 30 minutes away.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
