World.title: Niger govt cancels APC rally, suspends NSCDC commandant over deaths of detained illegal mining suspects
World.content:
The state government also announced the immediate suspension of the NSCDC State Commandant, Suberu Aniviye, and his team to allow for an impartial investigation into the incident.

Governor Mohammed Bago announced the measures on Friday during a press briefing in Minna on the tragic incident.

Mr Bago described the incident as unacceptable and said the government had commenced steps to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

He also announced the constitution of a committee of inquiry to investigate the incident and determine its cause.

Cause of death not yet established

The governor cautioned against drawing conclusions about the cause of the deaths before the completion of forensic and medical examinations.

He said possible causes being considered include suffocation resulting from overcrowding in the detention facility and exposure to hazardous substances allegedly associated with illegal mining.

“There is no official root cause of these deaths yet. It is too early for anybody to draw a conclusion on the root causes,” Mr Bago said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, forensic examinations, medical assessments, and autopsies were being conducted to establish the scientific cause of death.

Mr Bago said the state government was also compiling a register of the deceased to identify and contact their families.

He assured the victims’ relatives that the government would engage with them and provide the necessary support while the investigation continues.

‘We will probe deeply’

Mr Bago said the government pledged that the investigation would establish what happened.

“Lives of human beings are lives of human beings. Such an unjust government will not tolerate any kind of injustice, and we are going to make sure that we probe this thing deeply until we get to the root of this,” he said.

The governor said that the Director-General of the NSCDC, who is currently outside the country, had delegated his deputy to represent him at engagements related to the incident.

He added that the state government had already met with the senior NSCDC official.

Government urges calm

The governor appealed to youths, and other residents to remain calm and refrain from violence following the incident.

He said the movement of the bodies to a mortuary had heightened emotions among youths, but warned that resorting to violence could worsen the situation.

“We are calling on all the youth to please stay away from violence. It is not going to bring about those who have died. It will rather cost us a lot at the end of the day,” he said.

Mining activities suspended

As part of the government’s measures, Mr Bago ordered the closure of operations at the illegal mining site in the Ema Ushishi area.

He expressed concern over mining activities carried out without adequate technology, safety equipment and protective gear, saying such practices could expose miners to dangerous conditions.

READ ALSO: Over 20 feared trapped in Taraba mining pit collapse

The governor said the government would take appropriate action once the various investigations establish the facts surrounding the deaths.

He also said the state would continue to coordinate with the NSCDC, the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services (DSS), and other relevant authorities to determine the cause of the incident and ensure appropriate measures are taken.

Mr Bago commiserated with the families of the deceased and prayed for the repose of the victims’ souls.

The governor declared three days of mourning in the state as part of measures to honour those who died.

He said the cancellation of the APC rally was intended to allow the state to mourn the deceased and focus attention on the ongoing investigation.

World.title: UK lists 4 countries with highest number of deportations in last 5 years
World.content:
The UK recorded a steady increase in enforced returns after the number of people returned fell sharply during the COVID-19 pandemic, with nationals of five countries accounting for a significant share of returns in recent years.

According to the UK Home Office’s immigration statistics, there were 9,914 enforced returns in the year ending December 2025, representing a 21% increase from the 8,169 recorded in the previous year.

The Home Office’s data tracks the five most common nationalities for enforced returns from the year ending December 2021 to the year ending December 2025.

Here are the four countries whose nationals featured most prominently in the latest figures.

1. Albania

Albanian nationals have consistently been the most common nationality for enforced returns over the last five years, according to the Home Office.

In the year ending December 2025, 2,440 Albanian nationals were subject to enforced returns, accounting for about 25% of all 9,914 enforced returns recorded during the period.

However, the figure was 7% lower than the previous year.

The Home Office said enforced returns of Albanian nationals increased following the signing of the UK-Albania Joint Communique in December 2022, which came after substantial numbers of Albanian nationals arrived in the UK by small boats in 2022.

Foreign national offenders also accounted for more than half of Albanian enforced returns in the latest year.

2. Romania

Romanian nationals recorded the second-highest number of enforced returns among the nationalities highlighted by the Home Office.

There were 1,818 enforced returns of Romanian nationals in the year ending December 2025.

This represented a 20% increase compared with the previous year.

The Home Office said foreign national offenders accounted for more than half of Romanian enforced returns during the latest 12-month period.

Romania’s position in the figures comes amid wider changes to the UK’s immigration system following the end of EU free movement.

3. Brazil

Brazilian nationals recorded 939 enforced returns from the UK in the year ending December 2025.

The figure was 61% higher than the previous year, making Brazil one of the nationalities with the largest increases among the prominent nationalities.

Unlike the figures for Albania and Romania, foreign national offenders accounted for a much smaller proportion of Brazilian enforced returns.

Brazilian nationals have also featured prominently in the UK’s wider return figures. The Home Office recorded 4,759 voluntary returns of Brazilian nationals in the year ending December 2025.

4. India

The number of Indian nationals subject to enforced returns almost doubled to 781 in the year ending December 2025.

India was therefore among the nationalities that recorded a particularly sharp increase in enforced returns during the period.

The Home Office said, as with Brazil, foreign national offenders accounted for a much smaller proportion of Indian enforced returns than they did for Albanian and Romanian nationals.

Indian nationals also recorded a much larger number of voluntary returns, with 8,652 Indians voluntarily returning from the UK during the same 12-month period.

World.title: Mining: Alake mourns death of detainees in Niger, deploys investigators
World.content:
Minister of solid minerals development, Dele Alake.

By Gabriel Ewepu

Barely hours after mourning and calling for the rescue of survivors of Sudan mine collapse that killed some miners, the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, on Friday mourned the death of detainees for alleged illegal mining.

In a statement signed by him, he commiserated with their families, people and government of Niger State and commended Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago for quickly handling the tension it caused in the state.

He said: “It is with profound shock and deep sorrow that I extend my heartfelt condolences to the Governor of Niger State, His Excellency, Mohammed Umaru Bago, and the entire people of the state over the tragic loss of lives among detained citizens in Minna.

“The loss of any life is a deeply painful occurrence, and a tragedy of this magnitude affects us all.

“During this solemn period of state mourning, my thoughts and prayers are with the bereaved families and the communities bearing the weight of this grief.

“I commend Governor Bago’s swift administrative response in declaring a period of mourning and establishing an investigative framework to uncover the full circumstances of this unfortunate incident.

“A thorough, transparent, and independent inquiry is vital to ensure accountability and prevent any recurrence of such distress in our detention and correctional facilities.

“Given the allegation that the detained persons were arrested on suspicion of carrying out illegal mining, I have deployed a high-powered team of officials to Niger State to investigate the circumstances and ascertain the facts of the matter.

“The team will collaborate with other investigators to provide a comprehensive report on the incident.

“May the Almighty comfort the families affected and grant the souls of the departed eternal rest.”

World.title: Miners’ death: Nasarawa launches manhunt for mining companies recruiting minors
World.content:
By Edwin Phillip, Lafia

Nasarawa State Government has launched manhunt for illegal miners and mining companies who are in the habit of recruiting minors and underage workers at their sites and without recourse to industrial safety and welfare of the workers.

Commissioner for Environment, Mining and Natural Resources, Margaret Elayo, stated this in her office, while speaking to journalists in reaction to the death of young miners in the custody of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Niger State.

Elayo said the manhunt became necessary after receiving videos from the permanent secretary of the ministry, where underage persons were seen to be undertaking mining activities around the Wamba Local Government Area of the state.

She said, “Yesterday, the permanent secretary reached out to me like about 9 or 9.30pm and sent a couple of videos as it related to my state, Nasarawa State and I felt it is necessary for me to speak on it so that we can be guarded and use some of these challenges that other people are experiencing for us to be guarded so that the same mistakes will not be repeated in Nasarawa State.”

“So like I said, about 37 youths passed on; my condolences to the Niger State Government. Having said that, illegal mining is unacceptable regardless of who you are; very, very unacceptable. I have talked about this so many times and I believe you guys will bear me witness that we have called and you have been backing the state up as it relates to these issues when it comes to mining,” she reiterated.

Speaking further, she said Governor Sule has reiterated that the blessing of Nasarawa State with abundant mineral resources should not be exploited by investors and middlemen to the detriment of the environment and the people of the state.

“I have noticed that our people are still not listening, including the investors, and the purpose now for this information is I am going to take a very drastic decision that at the end of the day, it’s either you are here to support Nasarawa State’s growth or we will make sure that we treat you according to the nonsense that you are bringing to our state,” she warned.

According to her, most mining companies do not have the license to begin mining activities but only to make prospects but they go ahead to begin full-scale mining.

“I have gone to some mining sites that I shut down because of the kind of people I see there. You have a lot of youth who don’t have jobs that you can train above 18 that you can engage to do some of this work after proper training and making sure that you provide them with the necessary gadgets to even go into the site.

“But because of our gains and our selfish interest, we just go into any community, we get licensed and then we start mining and degrading, making the environment uncomfortable for the citizens in the community,” she revealed.

The commissioner therefore called on citizens and stakeholders to report cases of illegal mining activities in their area, adding that refusing to report such activities will be seen as being an accomplice.

“With the investment Engineer A. A. Sule has done in Nasarawa State, the last thing we need is for anybody to come and mess it up. So I want to appeal to the people; I’m also pleading and appealing to everybody responsible or those who have this opportunity to be in our state to benefit from the wealth to be guarded because when I step out, be rest assured, you are not doing right; we will show you the other side of not being good,” she appealed.

World.title: Top 10 budget-friendly iPhones students can buy in 2026
World.content:
For students who want to own an iPhone without spending a fortune, there are several models available.

While Apple’s newest iPhones can cost well above the ₦1 million mark in Nigeria, older models have become considerably more affordable in the used and certified-refurbished market.

The iPhone 13, while the iPhone 12 and iPhone 11 families offer even cheaper alternatives. Prices vary according to storage capacity, battery health, condition and whether the device is new, used or refurbished.

Here are 10 iPhones students can consider with a budget of ₦500,000 or less.

1. iPhone 13

The iPhone 13 is one of the more recent iPhones students can consider within this budget.

It is powered by Apple’s A15 Bionic chip and features a 6.1-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display. The phone has a dual-camera system consisting of a 12MP main camera and a 12MP Ultra Wide camera.

The iPhone 13 also supports 5G, making it suitable for students who want a relatively modern device that can handle demanding applications and fast mobile connectivity.

For students, its combination of performance, display quality and camera capabilities makes it suitable for everything from taking lecture notes and attending online classes to gaming and content creation.

2. iPhone 12 Pro Max

Students who want a large display and more advanced camera hardware can consider the iPhone 12 Pro Max.

The device features a 6.7-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display and is powered by the A14 Bionic chip. It has a triple-camera system with Wide, Ultra Wide and Telephoto cameras, along with a LiDAR Scanner.

The large screen can be particularly useful for students who frequently read PDFs, watch lectures or work with documents on their phones.

It also supports 5G and MagSafe accessories.

3. iPhone 11 Pro Max

The iPhone 11 Pro Max remains an option for students who want a large OLED display and a capable camera system.

It comes with a 6.5-inch Super Retina XDR display and Apple’s A13 Bionic chip. At the rear is a triple 12MP camera system comprising Wide, Ultra Wide and Telephoto cameras.

Although it is an older model, the A13 Bionic remains capable of handling everyday applications, social media, photography and streaming.

Its main attraction for students is the combination of a large OLED screen and a versatile camera system.

4. iPhone 12

The iPhone 12 is another option for students looking for a relatively modern iPhone.

It introduced a redesigned flat-edge body and features a 6.1-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display. The phone is powered by the A14 Bionic chip and supports 5G.

Its dual-camera setup includes a 12MP Wide camera and a 12MP Ultra Wide camera.

The iPhone 12 also uses Apple’s MagSafe accessory system and has a design that remains similar to newer iPhone generations.

5. iPhone 11 Pro

The smaller iPhone 11 Pro offers many of the features found on the 11 Pro Max but in a more compact form.

It has a 5.8-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display and runs on the A13 Bionic processor.

Its triple-camera system gives students greater flexibility when taking photographs, whether they are capturing people, landscapes or objects from a distance.

It is worth considering for students who want an OLED display and a more compact phone.

6. iPhone 11

The standard iPhone 11 is another popular option in the used market.

It features a 6.1-inch Liquid Retina HD LCD display and is powered by Apple’s A13 Bionic chip.

The phone has two 12MP rear cameras, including Wide and Ultra Wide lenses, and supports features such as Night mode and 4K video recording.

Although it does not support 5G, the iPhone 11 can still handle common student activities, including social media, messaging, video streaming, photography and online learning.\

7. iPhone XR

The iPhone XR can appeal to students looking for a relatively inexpensive entry into Apple’s Face ID-equipped iPhone range.

It has a 6.1-inch Liquid Retina HD display and uses the A12 Bionic chip.

The phone features a single 12MP rear camera and supports Face ID, making it considerably different from older iPhones with a physical Home button.

However, because of its age, students buying an XR in 2026 should pay particular attention to battery health and the device’s overall condition.

8. iPhone XS Max

The iPhone XS Max is another option for students who prefer a large display.

It features a 6.5-inch Super Retina OLED display, Apple’s A12 Bionic chip and a dual-camera system.

The phone also introduced several premium features for its generation, including Face ID, an IP68 water-resistance rating and a stainless-steel frame.

Its large OLED screen makes it suitable for watching videos, reading documents and browsing the internet.

9. iPhone XS

The standard iPhone XS provides many of the features of the XS Max in a smaller body.

It has a 5.8-inch Super Retina OLED display, A12 Bionic chip and dual 12MP rear cameras.

It also supports Face ID and wireless charging.

For students who prefer compact smartphones, the XS can still serve as an everyday device for communication, social media, photography and entertainment.

10. iPhone X

The iPhone X is the oldest model on this list but remains available in Nigeria’s used smartphone market.

It was Apple’s first iPhone to introduce the now-familiar Face ID design and features a 5.8-inch Super Retina OLED display.

The device is powered by the A11 Bionic chip and has a dual rear-camera system.

However, students considering the iPhone X should be more cautious about its age. Battery condition, storage and software compatibility are particularly important when buying one in 2026.

World.title: Lagos youths trained to spot fake news, manipulated content
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

No fewer than 50 youths in Lagos State have been trained to identify fake news, impostor content, misleading headlines, manipulated or altered media, fabricated information and content presented out of context.

The training comes against the backdrop of growing concerns over the spread of misleading information online. Around 75 per cent of internet users in Nigeria frequently encounter fake news on digital platforms, severely affecting public trust in online media.

Studies such as the Abuja Public Trust Study indicate that three out of four respondents regularly encounter misleading information.

Therefore, the Naija Collective organised a three-day media literacy workshop aimed at equipping young people with the skills to critically assess information and identify misinformation, disinformation and fake news.

The workshop featured sessions on the media landscape, critical reading, information verification and the responsible consumption of media content.

The final session focused on fact-checking and was facilitated by media communications strategist and trainer, Abdulkerimu Oare, who took participants through practical steps and tools for verifying information.

Oare introduced the CRAAP framework — Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy and Purpose — as a tool for evaluating the credibility of information.

He explained that fact-checkers should consider how recent information is, whether it is relevant to the issue being discussed, the authority or credibility of its source, the accuracy of the claims and the purpose behind the content.

Participants subsequently engaged in a practical exercise designed to test their understanding of the lessons. They were divided into five groups and tasked with debriefing and analysing a news item, examining its claims and identifying possible red flags.

Oare said: “Over the past two days, we’ve covered issues around the media landscape, teaching young people how to read critically and investigate the content that’s in front of them. However, today, day three, was all about fact-checking.

“We tried to also explore all the typical shortcomings that they can identify from information that’s presented to be legitimate when it’s not.

“The participants showed great interest and they also displayed that the knowledge gained wasn’t lost, as they all actively participated in the exercises and scenarios before them,” he said.

One of the coordinators, Nosike Nwigene, said the organisers hoped the workshop would be the first of several editions.

Nwigene said the programme was particularly timely ahead of the coming elections, when young people could be exposed to large volumes of misleading or deceptive information.

“We’re hoping that this is the first of many. We also have election experience and obviously disinformation is a big part of how people digest and perceive information,” Nwigene said.

According to Nwigene, the decision to organise the workshop was partly informed by the need to help young people build resilience against misleading information that could circulate during election periods.

“We felt this was important because elections are coming and a lot of people are going to be susceptible to all sorts of content, and it’s good to help them build resilience in it, basically,” Nwigene said.

One of the participants, Omotolani Olufumbi, described the workshop as impactful, saying she had gained practical knowledge on how to identify and verify questionable information.

“Now I know how to spot fake news and I also know how to detect whether news is actually true or false,” Olufumbi said.

World.title: Gov Bago declares 24-hour curfew following unrest over miners’ deaths
World.content:
Niger State Governor, Umaru Bago, has imposed a 24-hour curfew across Minna, the state capital, following unrest reported in parts of the city.

The curfew takes effect immediately after Friday’s Jumu’ah prayers and will remain in force until further notice.

The directive requires residents to remain indoors and refrain from unnecessary movements throughout the period.

Security agencies have also been directed to enforce the curfew and take measures to protect lives and property across the metropolis.

The development followed Thursday’s protest and unrest linked to the deaths of suspected illegal miners who reportedly died while in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, in Minna.

The unrest prompted the state government to impose the curfew as authorities move to contain the situation.

Residents have been urged to remain calm and comply with directives issued by security agencies.

The government is expected to provide further updates on the situation as developments unfold.

World.title: England can build on World Cup ‘spirit’, says Tuchel
World.content:
England’s German head coach Thomas Tuchel attends a press conference at Wembley Stadium, north west London, on September 18, 2026, ahead of their Nations League fixture against Spain. (Photo by Brook Mitchell / AFP) / NOT FOR MARKETING OR ADVERTISING USE / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE

Thomas Tuchel said England will build on the “fantastic spirit” of their World Cup campaign as he targets glory on home soil at Euro 2028.

The England boss was speaking at Wembley after naming a 27-man group for a four-game Nations League camp, starting with a clash against world champions Spain on September 26.

It comes just nine weeks after the end of the World Cup, where England conceded two late goals in a painful semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold and Chelsea forward Cole Palmer were the headline picks after both were controversially overlooked for the World Cup.

Tuchel also included Liverpool’s teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, uncapped Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite in his first squad since the tournament in North America.

A number of players who were in the World Cup squad including John Stones, Djed Spence, Dan Burn, Jordan Henderson and Dean Henderson missed out through injury.

Former Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Tuchel said he did not see the Nations League as a new start, instead focusing on continuity.

“I feel that it’s not a new beginning that we are starting now, so we build on a solid and very valuable foundation, and the target is to win the home Euros,” he told reporters on Friday.

Euro 2028 will be co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales, and Ireland.

The German said his side’s ultimate failure at the World Cup had left him unfulfilled but stuck by his squad picks.

“I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic,” he said.

“I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.”

Tuchel said Palmer had impressed for Chelsea early in the season.

“He has his numbers back, he has assists back, he has decisive goals back, so that’s why he’s in the squad and I think he has a point to prove,” he said.

“The same goes for Trent. He was never off the list, he was never in a non-selectable class, and he has this chance to show, to be the best version of himself.”

Tuchel said it was his “duty” to play Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo after he failed to feature for a single minute at the World Cup.

The England boss welcomed the challenge of taking on Spain at Wembley.

“We feel the gap is closing and we feel that we are close and we want a proof of point,” he said.

“The stadium is sold out, it will be very exciting, the motivation cannot be higher to play against the world champions.”

England also play the Czech Republic twice and Croatia once during the upcoming international window.

World.title: Troops rescue 6 kidnapped victims in Kaduna, Katsina
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The Army said on Friday that its troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have rescued six kidnapped victims during separate operations following fighting patrols in Kaduna and Katsina States on 17 September 2026.

Lieutenant Colonel Aliyu Danja, Media Information Officer, made this known saying that while three were rescued in Kaduna, another three were rescued in Katsina.

He said, “In Kaduna State, troops of Sector 1 OPFY, while acting on intelligence on a kidnapping incident in Igabi Local Government Area, made contact with suspected terrorists moving some kidnapped victims.

“On sighting the troops, the terrorists abandoned the victims and fled in disarray.

“Troops rescued three victims, identified as Enock Hussaini, Abba Dauda and Kalif Haruna.

“The victims were confirmed to have been abducted by terrorists at Gidan Gulbi Village on 11 September 2026.

“They were subsequently debriefed and reunited with their families, while troops continued to dominate the general area.

“Similarly, in Katsina State, troops of Sector 2 responded to a distress call concerning the abduction of civilians along the Dandume-Damari axis in Dandume Local Government Area.

“Troops swiftly mobilised to the area and made contact with the terrorists, engaging them with overwhelming firepower and forcing them to flee into the surrounding bushes, abandoning their victims.

“Troops pursued the fleeing terrorists and subsequently rescued three kidnapped victims, identified as Abubakar Abdulkadir, aged 25; Mansir Idris, aged 26; and Abubakar Aliyu, aged 21.

“Troops also recovered a black Golf vehicle belonging to the victims

“The victims were later escorted and released to continue their journey.

“The latest successes underscore the continued efforts of Operation Fansan Yamma to secure innocent civilians, disrupt terrorist activities and deny them freedom of action across the Joint Operations Area.

“The Joint Task Force appreciates members of the public for their continued support and urges them to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities to the nearest security agency.”

World.title: Court Declares NYSC Not Disqualification Ground for Senatorial Election
World.content:
* Dismisses suit against APGA, Stella Oduah

Alex Enumah in Abuja

A Federal High Court in Abuja, has held that non possession of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) is not a ground for disqualification of a candidate in a senatorial election.

Justice Joyce Abdulmalik stated this on Friday while delivering judgment in a suit seeking the disqualification of Senator Stella Oduah as the candidate of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) in the 2027 senatorial election in Anambra North Senatorial District.

The suit dated July 24, was filed by an aspirant of APGA, John Okechukwu Emeka, challenging the nomination of the former senator as the candidate of the party in the forthcoming general election.

Oduah, APGA and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) were first, second and third defendants respectively.

The plaintiff, through his lawyer, A. C. Ozioko, claimed that Oduah was not qualified to be on the ballot, on account of allegedly providing false information to INEC in her Form EC9, in aid of her qualification for the 2027 general election.

In a 23-paragraph affidavit he deposed to in support of the originating summons, the plaintiff alleged that Oduah in column E6 of her form EC9 submitted to INEC on July 11, 2026 denied on oath that she has never presented any forged certificate to INEC whereas in her affidavit of facts that she deposed in 2015 in support of her INEC form CFOOQ1 she deposed that she lost her First School Leaving Certificate and NYSC Corps certificate, whereas the issuing authorities had stated that she was never issued with those certificates.

While submitting that the First School Leaving Certificate is among the minimum requirement for anyone contesting for Senate, the plaintiff claimed that the first defendant is a graduate with a B.Sc. in Business Administration.

“That I know as a matter of fact that anyone who is a graduate in Nigeria must undergo the compulsory one year National Youth Service unless the person is exempted.

“That the first defendant had procured a letter from Nigeria Employers Consultative Association (NECA) presented same to the third defendant in order to make the third defendant believe that she completed her one year youth service whereas she absconded from the camp. Attached herewith as exhibit “M” Is a copy of the NYSC letter on the subject and a copy of the police investigation report on the matter which unveiled the fact that her name was not among those deployed for primary assignment.”

Delivering judgment on Friday, the court however dismissed the suit for lacking in merit.

The court, among others, faulted the commencement of the suit by an originating summons, stating that the case of forgery is a criminal offence which must be proved beyond reasonable doubt.

On the issue of non-possession of NYSC certificate, the court held that it was not a ground for disqualifying any candidate in a senatorial election.

The court also agreed with Oduah’s lawyer, Onyechi Ikpeazu (SAN) and APGA’s lawyer, Ifeanyi Mberi, that the issue of the former senator’s qualification to contest public office has been resolved by the election petition tribunal in 2019.

Meanwhile, the court struck out the case of the plaintiff for been statute barred, having been filed outside the 14 days provided by law.

APGA had submitted Oduah’s name as its candidate for the Anambra North Senatorial election on July 7, whereas the suit was filed on July 24, three days outside the time allowed by law.

World.title: Okumagba Lauds Kings, Advocates Peace in Warri
World.content:
Former Delta State Commissioner for Finance, Olorogun Bernard Okumagba, has reiterated his call for all indigenous ethnic nationalities in Warri Federal Constituency — Itsekiri, Ijaw and Urhobo — to promote peace and live in peace with one another, anchored on mutual respect.

In a statement issued on Thursday, September 17, 2026, Okumagba who holds the traditional chieftaincy titles of Udu of Okere-Urhobo Kingdom and Eruvwu R’Ovie of Agbarha Warri Kingdom, both in Warri South Local Government Area, stated that: “Peace and brotherliness amongst all ethnic nationalities in Warri Federal Constituency will ensure that all our energies are devoted to bringing development to Warri and enhancing the livelihoods of all our people in Warri.”

According to Okumagba, “The paramount ruler of the Itsekiri Nation is the Olu of Warri Kingdom. He is the paramount ruler over the Itsekiri people/territories in Warri Federal Constituency. Similarly, there are other separate, independent kingdoms and kings in Warri Federal Constituency namely the Oroseun of Okere-Urhobo Kingdom, the Ovie of Agbarha Warri Kingdom, the Pere of Gbaramatu Kingdom, the Amakusu of Ogbe-Ijoh Warri Kingdom, the Agadegba of Egbema Kingdom and the Pere of Isaba Kingdom. This is the position of the law and duly recognised by the hovernment.”

Okumagba noted further that: “The new era of peace is that all the kings in Warri Federal Constituency are now determined to respect each other and promote peaceful co-existence and mutual respect between the various kingdoms and various tribes in Warri Federal Constituency. This peaceful coexistence and mutual respect should be embraced by all indigenes of our Warri Federal Constituency.

“It is heartwarming to see that the kings of the various kingdoms are in the forefront of the renewed initiative at peaceful coexistence and mutual respect. I commend the recent meetings that have taken place between the Olu of Warri Kingdom and the Amakosu of Ogbe-Ijoh Warri Kingdom as well as the Olu’s subsequent meetings with the Ovie of Agbarha Warri Kingdom and the Oroseun of Okere-Urhobo Kingdom. I urge that these meetings continue.

“We will all need to rise above our past hurts and rise above our traumas and commit to a peaceful coexistence with mutual respect. However, where there are unresolved grievances in our Warri Federal Constituency that dialogue cannot resolve, the courts should be approached for peaceful resolution of the issues.”

Okumagba stated that: “The focus for all our people should now be on working together across all ethnic nationalities — Itsekiri, Ijaw and Urhobo — to attract infrastructure projects and investments to Warri Federal Constituency and working together to ensure gainful employment and thriving businesses for our people from all ethnic nationalities in Warri.”

He further called for “all to work towards unity among all our people of Warri Federal Constituency with mutual respect for our various kingdoms, inter-ethnic harmony and love for one another. Let us all work towards promoting harmony among all ethnic nationalities in Warri Federal Constituency and all our people”.

World.title: Access Bank Launches Campaign to Shield Teens from Scam
World.content:
Jessica Erobomhan

Access Bank has launched the Spot the Scam Initiative, a nationwide fraud awareness campaign designed to equip young teenagers and students aged 12 to 19 with the knowledge to recognise and resist financial scams.

Speaking at the event, Chief Conduct and Compliance Officer of Access Bank, Solomon Abiakalam, said the main target for fraud are young people

“Frauds they all target young people, all of them they target young people to either make them victims or to make them perpetrator, they have a special interest in young people, and that’s why they rebuilding their armies over the years,” he said

Solomon described financial crimes as non-violent yet often more destructive than physical violence. Citing the bank’s corporate mantra, he declared Access Bank’s resolve to raise a generation that remains unbent, unbowed and unbroken in the face of pressure to engage in or fall prey to fraud.

The initiative is said to have two main components. The first is a nationwide education drive open to schools across Nigeria, Students can enrol through their schools or as independent learners on a dedicated digital platform that features interactive quizzes, scam or legitgames, leaderboards and progress tracking. The goal is to turn participants into scam busters.

Speakers emphasised the critical role of parents they said Homes, must remain safe spaces where children can report online experiences without fear of shame or judgement.

The bank plans to expand engagement with parents and teachers as the programme develops.

According to the executive’s What distinguishes the initiative, is its focus on the age group most aggressively targeted by those recruiting for fraud, trafficking and other crimes that feed money laundering.

World.title: Singapore President Invites Tinubu for State Visit
World.content:
‘I’ll deliver your message, with positive response,’ Jimoh Ibrahim assures Singaporean ambassador

The President of Singapore, Tharman Shanmugaratnam, has invited President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to visit Singapore as the country seeks to strengthen its relationship and deepen cooperation with Nigeria.

Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, disclosed this in a statement by the Nigerian Mission House at the United Nations, New York.

Ibrahim said Singapore’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Burhan Gafoor, visited the Nigerian Permanent Mission House, where he delivered a letter from President Shanmugaratnam inviting Tinubu to Singapore.

Gafoor also congratulated Ibrahim on his emergence as Chairman of two prominent UN committees—the Fifth Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Matters and, more recently, the Special Committee on Peacekeeping Operations, also known as the Committee of 34 or C-34.

Receiving the letter, Ibrahim thanked Gafoor for the invitation and assured the people and government of Singapore that Tinubu would find time to visit the country in the nearest future.

He said the President’s economic reforms had attracted international attention and generated interest from countries such as Singapore in sharing experiences with Nigeria, particularly on multilateralism and national development.

Ibrahim compared the boldness of Tinubu’s reforms with the transformation associated with Singapore’s first Prime Minister, the late Lee Kuan Yew.

“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is making bold economic reforms like the first Prime Minister of Singapore , Lee Kuan Yew. His achievements are enviable and continue to generate concern to countries like Singapore to share experience in multilateralism,” Ibrahim said.

He said Tinubu holds President Tharman in high esteem and congratulated Singapore on the reforms that transformed the country.

According to Ibrahim, Nigeria is also undergoing reforms aimed at transforming the country into a modern contemporary state where the interests of everyone would be protected and Nigerians would begin to enjoy a viable economic proposition.

“Nigeria is currently going through reform in order to transform herself to a modern contemporary state, where interests of everyone is protected and Nigerians begin to enjoy a viable proposition,” he said.

Ibrahim also disclosed that his office at the United Nations had witnessed increased diplomatic engagements in recent weeks.

He said the British Ambassador to the UN visited him last week, followed by the Ambassador of Guyana a few days later, before Gafoor’s visit.

The envoy said his leadership of the UN committees would be guided by fairness, accountability and efficiency.

On the Fifth Committee, Ibrahim assured member states of equitable treatment in the allocation of resources.

“I will be fair to all in allocation of resources under the Fifth Committee, and every country will have a say. The United Nations will be impartial to member states under the reform of accountability and efficiency,” he said.

The Fifth Committee is responsible for the administrative and budgetary matters of the United Nations, while the C-34 deals with issues relating to UN peacekeeping operations.

World.title: Customs Intercepts Police Uniforms, Explosives, Pistol, 17 vehicles, Others  in  Oyo
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

The Oyo/Osun Area Command of the Nigeria Customs Service has intercepted 573 Nigeria Police Force crests, 92 yards of police camouflage uniform fabric, a pistol, six pistol magazines, a pump-action magazine and 60 detonating cords in its anti-smuggling operations in August 2026.

The acting Customs Area Controller of the Command, Deputy Comptroller of Customs Wale Adewole, made the disclosure yesterday in Ibadan while briefing journalists at the Command’s Operational Headquarters on the revenue performance and anti-smuggling activities of the command.

He said the interception of the police-related materials was particularly concerning because of the potential security implications of the unauthorised possession and movement of security agency uniforms and insignia, stating that such materials could be exploited by criminal elements to impersonate law enforcement personnel, obtain unauthorised access to restricted locations or facilitate criminal activities.

“Of particular concern was the interception of police crest and camouflage uniforms. The unauthorised possession and movement of security agency uniforms can create serious security concerns, particularly in view of the prevailing security challenges in the country,” he said.

Adewole added that the seizure demonstrated the importance of preventing security-related materials from being diverted into the wrong hands, stressing that the command would continue to pay particular attention to items with implications for national security and public safety.

According to him, the command also intercepted a pistol, six pistol magazines, a pump-action magazine and 60 detonating cords during the period under review

Other items seized included 2,012 bags of 50kg foreign parboiled rice, 550 bags of 25kg foreign parboiled rice, 2,440 wraps of cannabis sativa, 1,150 used tyres, 101 used compressors and 48 packs of 225mg tramadol.

The list of intercepted goods also included 105 bales and 28 sacks of used clothing, 18 sacks of used shoes, 450 25-litre kegs of Premium Motor Spirit, equivalent to 5,000 litres, 33 three-litre bottles of foreign vegetable oil, and 30 bags of foreign sugar weighing 60kg each.

The command further seized 17 used vehicles, otherwise known as tokunbo vehicles, 10 means of conveyance and 10 containers of corrosive mercury.

Adewole said the seizures recorded during the period had a cumulative Duty Paid Value of N4,106,951,689.00., explaining that the interceptions were part of the command’s statutory responsibility to protect the national economy and prevent the smuggling of prohibited and restricted goods.

“In line with our statutory responsibility to protect the nation’s economy and prevent the smuggling of prohibited and restricted goods, the Command has continued to intensify its anti-smuggling operations across its areas of jurisdiction,” he said.

The acting Controller said the interception of corrosive mercury was also significant because of the danger posed by the substance when improperly handled, stored or transported.

He said uncontrolled movement of the hazardous material could expose members of the public to fire, explosion, injury and property damage, and, in extreme circumstances, loss of lives.

“The uncontrolled movement of such materials can expose members of the public to risks of fire, explosion, injury, property damage, and, in extreme circumstances, loss of lives,” Adewole said.

He said the interception therefore prevented potentially hazardous material from entering circulation and being handled by unauthorised persons.

Adewole attributed the seizures to the vigilance and professionalism of officers and men of the command, as well as the deployment of intelligence-driven operations and collaboration with sister security agencies and other relevant stakeholders, stating that the command would sustain its anti-smuggling operations while ensuring that legitimate businesses and law-abiding members of the public were not subjected to unnecessary impediments.

On revenue generation, Adewole disclosed that the Oyo/Osun Area Command generated N65,661,343,026.94 between January and August 2026.

He said the figure represented a 13.88 per cent increase over the N57,656,161,990.24 collected during the corresponding period in 2025.

The acting controller attributed the improved revenue performance to the command’s sustained commitment to effective revenue collection, trade facilitation, stakeholder engagement and the deployment of strategies designed to improve compliance.

“I am pleased to inform you that between January and August 2026, the Command generated a total revenue of Sixty Five Billion, Six Hundred and Sixty-One Million, Three Hundred and Forty-Three Thousand, Twenty-Six Naira, Ninety-Four Kobo,” he said.

Adewole added that the command remained committed to improving revenue generation while facilitating legitimate trade and sustaining the fight against smuggling and other forms of economic sabotage.

“The Oyo/Osun Area Command remains committed to improving revenue generation, facilitating legitimate trade and sustaining the fight against smuggling and other forms of economic sabotage.” he said.

Adewole further assured residents and legitimate businesses within the command’s jurisdiction that the Customs Service would continue to strike a balance between enforcement and trade facilitation.

“We will continue to pay particular attention to items that have implications for national security and public safety, while ensuring that legitimate businesses and law-abiding members of the public are not unduly impeded,” he said.

The acting controller also pledged that the command would continue to discharge its responsibilities professionally and in accordance with the provisions of the Nigeria Customs Service Act 2023.

Adewole commended journalists for their continued partnership with the Nigeria Customs Service and urged the media to sustain responsible reportage of the activities of the service.

“We also appreciate the gentlemen of the press for their continued partnership and responsible reportage of the activities of the Nigeria Customs Service,” he added.

World.title: 2027: Oborevwori Tasks Stakeholders on MORE Agenda, Mobilisation
World.content:
Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has charged political leaders, stakeholders and supporters of his administration to take the achievements of the MORE Agenda to the grassroots ahead of the 2027 general election.

Oborevwori gave the charge while declaring open a one-day seminar for Special Assistants, Senior Special Assistants and Executive Assistants on political matters, organised by the Senior Political Adviser to the Governor, Senator Emmanuel Aguariavwodo.

Represented by the Chief of Staff, Government House, Sir Johnson Erijo, the governor said stakeholders must communicate the administration’s achievements with facts, stressing that the Renewed Hope Agenda of the federal government and the MORE Agenda of his administration were driving reforms aimed at strengthening the economy, expanding opportunities and promoting development.

He said his administration had remained focused on delivering results through major roads, bridges and urban renewal projects, as well as investments in education, healthcare, human capital development, youth empowerment, enterprise development and security.

“We promised more, and our record speaks for itself,” he said.

Oborevwori also highlighted the partnership between the state and federal governments, saying the relationship had created new opportunities for Delta.

He said the 2027 elections should be viewed beyond politics, stressing the need to consolidate progress, sustain stability and ensure that ongoing projects and programmes continued to benefit the people.

The governor urged political leaders, appointees, stakeholders and supporters to remain united, disciplined and focused, charging them to take the administration’s message to every ward, community and local government area.

Earlier, Aguariavwodo urged the participants to effectively communicate the achievements and impact of the Renewed Hope Agenda and MORE Agenda to the grassroots, adding that political appointees must move beyond announcing government programmes to explaining their benefits in ways that were visible, relatable, verifiable and understandable to ordinary citizens.

He described the seminar as a platform for introspection, assessment and strategic planning, saying governance should ultimately be measured by the results it delivered in the lives of citizens.

He said the MORE Agenda — Meaningful Development, Opportunities for All, Realistic Reforms and Enhanced Peace and Security — was focused on improving the lives of Deltans.

In separate goodwill messages, Mr Francis Onuora and the Secretary to the State Government, Dr Kingsley Emu, urged participants to equip themselves with facts, figures and statistics to effectively communicate the achievements and challenges of the administration.

They warned that inadequate knowledge could make them vulnerable to criticism and misinformation.

The Deputy Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Arthur Akpowowo; Provost, Southern Delta University, Orerokpe Campus, Prof. Akpovughaye Taiga; and Maxwell Idama Omamuyo, presented keynote addresses at the seminar.
