World.title: Kudiwave Protests at Police HQ over N750m PalmPay Funds
World.content:
Wale Igbintade

Kudiwave Technologies Nigeria Limited yesterday protested at the Force Headquarters in Abuja over the alleged movement of N750.34 million from its PalmPay account, demanding an independent investigation by the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu.

The protesters, comprising staff and supporters of the company, carried placards with inscriptions including: “IG save our business,” “PalmPay and PSFU return our N750m,” “Kudiwave is not a fraudulent organisation,” and “Stop extortion of fintech companies.”

They also submitted a petition to the IG, alleging that the Police Special Fraud Unit (PSFU), Ikoyi, Lagos, and PalmPay were involved in the restriction and subsequent movement of the funds.

The protest followed a dispute over N750,339,399.99 allegedly transferred from Kudiwave’s PalmPay account while the company was challenging a court order relating to the funds.

Addressing reporters, Kudiwave’s Company Secretary, Prince Oko Kalu, said the company’s account had been placed on a Post-No-Debit (PND) restriction since April, preventing it from accessing its funds.

Kalu said the company later traced the restriction to the PSFU and approached the unit for clarification.

He alleged that a police officer demanded N50 million for lifting the restriction.

He said an intermediary subsequently requested a lower amount, following which N5 million was allegedly paid.

The allegations could not be independently verified.

Kalu said the restriction nevertheless remained on the account.

He said the company subsequently learnt that a Federal High Court order had been obtained on June 29 directing the movement of funds in the account to a designated police account.

Kudiwave challenged the order and, according to Kalu, filed an application for a stay of execution on July 3.

He said the court subsequently set aside, vacated and discharged the June 29 order on July 22 and directed the removal of restrictions placed on the company’s account.

However, Kalu said Kudiwave discovered that N750,339,399.99 had been transferred from the account on July 15, before the court delivered its ruling.

“Now we came with the order to ask PalmPay to release our account so that we’ll resume our business, only to realise that the entire fund in our account up to N750,339,399.99 was moved,” he said.

Kalu alleged that Kudiwave’s transaction records showed that the money was transferred to an Access Bank business account, rather than the police exhibit account referred to in the earlier court order.

He urged the police to investigate who authorised the transfer, where the money was sent and who currently has custody of it.

PalmPay, however, disputed Kudiwave’s account of the transaction.

In a response signed by its Legal Counsel, Caleb Aluya, PalmPay said the transfer was made strictly in compliance with the Federal High Court’s June 29 order, which it maintained was valid, binding and enforceable when the transaction was effected.

PalmPay also disputed Kudiwave’s reliance on an earlier letter in which it had indicated that it considered it appropriate to await the determination of the pending application before taking further steps.

According to the fintech company, the letter was intended to mitigate the consequences of non-compliance with the court order and allow Kudiwave an opportunity to obtain a valid order staying or varying the substantive order.

PalmPay said the communication did not amount to an admission that its obligation to comply with the existing court order had been suspended.

It further stated that Kudiwave was covered by an earlier ex-parte order and that PalmPay was expressly listed as a respondent.

“PalmPay therefore acted strictly in compliance with the express terms of the Court’s Order and not on its own initiative,” the company said.

On the N750.34 million debit, PalmPay said it had consistently complied with valid court orders served on it and would continue to do so.

The company added that following the July 22 ruling, it formally engaged the Nigeria Police Force and requested compliance with the court’s decision.

PalmPay maintained that the funds were transferred to the designated Police Recovery Account pursuant to the June 29 order and that any further action required to implement the July 22 ruling should be directed to the police, which it described as the custodian of the funds.

The position has become the central point of the dispute, with Kudiwave alleging that its records indicate that the money was transferred to an Access Bank business account, while PalmPay maintains that the funds were transferred to the designated police account.

Kudiwave has also rejected suggestions that it did not have a verifiable business address.

Kalu said PalmPay representatives had previously visited the company’s office and held meetings there.

“How will you open an account to a customer that you have no KYC of the customer?” he asked, referring to the Know Your Customer requirements for account holders.

Kalu said Kudiwave had submitted four petitions to the IGP over the matter and appealed for an independent investigation.

“We are here to create awareness. Let the public hear us. Let the IGP come out from his seat. Let him come and look into our matter, appoint independent investigation over this matter,” he said.

Responding to the protesters, the Commissioner of Police in charge of Federal Operations, Wilson Akpan, assured them that their petition would be considered.

Akpan, who addressed the demonstrators outside the Force Headquarters, said the matter would be critically examined by the police authorities.

“This matter you have brought before the head of the force will be critically looked into and solved,” he said.

He added: “The IG, Olatunji Disu, is a well-vested police investigator. Don’t panic and don’t be afraid. Whatever is due to you, you will get it. Just have that at the back of your mind.”

The protesters later proceeded to the Central Bank of Nigeria, where they submitted a copy of the petition and sought the regulator’s intervention.

The company’s protest has therefore brought renewed attention to the unresolved status of the N750.34 million following the July 22 court ruling.

While Kudiwave is demanding the return of the funds and an independent investigation into their movement, PalmPay maintains that it acted pursuant to a valid court order and that responsibility for any further action concerning the funds rests with the police.

World.title: No more swoosh! Kylian Mbappe boots Nike for On
World.content:
France captain Kylian Mbappe has signed with Swiss sportswear brand On, ending a long association with Nike. Image: X @FIFAcom

France captain Kylian Mbappe has signed with Swiss sportswear brand On, ending a long association with Nike that stretched back to the start of his career, the company announced on Friday.

“Today, Swiss sportswear brand On announces its entry into football alongside football champion Kylian Mbappe, marking the beginning of the brand’s journey into the world’s biggest sport,” read a company statement.

On also announced that 1998 World Cup winner Thierry Henry had been appointed its football director. The company plans to launch its first football boots next year.



Build something new

“From the beginning, what drew me to On was the opportunity to build something entirely new together that will help shape tomorrow’s game,” said Mbappe.

“I want to bring my experience and perspective into what we create, push what’s possible through innovation, and always stay true to the joy of football.

“We have a shared dream, and this is only the beginning.”



On, which is making a major move into the football market with the signing of Mbappe, did not disclose the value of his contract.

Roger Federer among shareholders

Founded in 2010 and previously focused on running and tennis footwear, On counts tennis great Roger Federer among its shareholders.



Federer also left Nike towards the end of his playing career to join the Zurich-based company.

Mbappe’s departure is a blow to Nike, the world’s largest sportswear company, which had been involved with the Real Madrid forward since 2006 and made him one of the leading faces of its football business.

The 2018 World Cup winner and all-time leading scorer in the tournament’s history with 22 goals had gradually emerged as Nike’s foremost football ambassador, succeeding Portuguese great Cristiano Ronaldo, who at 41 is approaching the end of his playing career.



Biggest stars

His exit follows that of Lamine Yamal, a recent World Cup winner with Spain, who swapped Nike for Adidas in 2024.

Nike retains under contract several of football’s biggest stars, including Norway striker Erling Haaland and Brazil forward Vinicius Junior.

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: MK Party mourns former SABC sports presenter Owen Ndlovu
World.content:
The uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party has described the death of former South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) sports broadcaster and music rights activist Owen Ndlovu as a devastating loss to South Africa’s broadcasting, sports and cultural sectors.

Ndlovu was allegedly hijacked and kidnapped in Katlehong, east of Johannesburg. His body was later discovered by residents in Thokoza, near Johannesburg on Wednesday.

Police have launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death and a manhunt for the suspects.



MK PARTY MOURNS OWEN NDLOVU

Ndlovu was a familiar figure in South Africa’s sports broadcasting and entertainment industries. He worked for the SABC and was involved in sports broadcasting, while also pursuing a career in the music industry.

He was a music promoter and founded Artists United, an organisation focused on issues affecting artists and the music industry.

Ndlovu was also involved in a long-running dispute with the SABC over its Summer Song of the Year campaign. In late 2019, he approached the courts seeking to stop the broadcaster from announcing the Song of the Year, arguing that the concept and voting system were his intellectual property. He later withdrew the application.

Ndlovu continued to raise concerns about the campaign in subsequent years, including in 2022, while the SABC disputed his claims.

At the time of his death, Ndlovu was also involved in a legal dispute with the Southern African Music Rights Organisation (SAMRO), of which he was a long-standing member.

In July 2026, the Johannesburg Magistrates’ Court dismissed a harassment application brought against Ndlovu by SAMRO chief executive Annabelle Lebethe.



WATCH🚨



Owen Ndlovu Speaks On SAMRO Legal Dispute Before His Death



Owen Ndlovu, founder of Artists United, spoke about his ongoing legal dispute involving SAMRO and his efforts to have its CEO, Annabel Lebethe, removed from office.



Ndlovu has since been found dead with gunshot… pic.twitter.com/JwL5kuBN2W — MDN NEWS (@MDNnewss) September 17, 2026

PARTY CALLS FOR A PROBE

The MK Party said the circumstances surrounding Ndlovu’s death were deeply disturbing and called for a full investigation.

“The MK Party is particularly concerned by the continued vulnerability of ordinary South Africans to violent crime, kidnapping and hijacking. No family should have to ensure the trauma of seeing a loved one taken away from them in such circumstances,” MK Party spokesperson Sifiso Mahlangu said.

Mahlangu called on law enforcement authorities to prioritise the investigation, support Ndlovu’s family and ensure those responsible face justice.

The party also called on the Department of Sport, Arts and Culture, as well as the broadcasting, sports and entertainment fraternity, to acknowledge and honour Ndlovu’s contribution to South African sports and cultural life.

World.title: Explainer: What is Operation Shanela?
World.content:
Operation Shanela is back in the headlines following the killings in Ekurhuleni.

Operation Shanela is the South African Police Service’s (SAPS) ongoing nationwide, high-density crime-fighting initiative. This operation was designed to flood specific areas with visible police presence.

So, how does it work?



Each operation is led by the Provincial Commissioner of the relevant province, and typically runs across all districts at the same time with the intention of combining several tactics at once. This includes roadblocks, vehicle checkpoints, stop-and-search actions, high-visibility foot and vehicle patrols, and the tracing of wanted suspects.

Operations are intelligence-led. So, police are targetting specific areas, networks or individuals based on prior information rather than simply patrolling at random. Shanela operations also often include compliance inspections at second-hand goods dealers, liquor outlets, and both formal and informal businesses.

What is the purpose of these check? These checks are aimed at disrupting the resale of stolen goods and unlicensed trade. SAPS often partners with other law enforcement bodies, including the Department of Home Affairs, metro police, private security companies and local Community Policing Forums.

The operation focuses on serious and violent crimes such as murder, attempted murder, rape, carjacking, and business or house robberies. However, it also includes illegal firearms possession, drug trafficking, immigration offences, and organised crime linked to illicit trade as well as counterfeit goods, untaxed cigarettes and smuggled alcohol.

WHY IS OPERATION SHANELA UNDERWAY IN EKURHULENI RIGHT NOW?

WHAT IS HAPPENING IN EKURHULENI

A total of nine dead bodies have been found in Ekurhuleni over the past two months. The latest victim, which was another woman, was found half-naked and wrapped in a sheet on the side of the road on Thursday morning (17 September), in Dawn Park, Ekurhuleni.



Investigators are still working on finding her identity as well as the circumstances surrounding her death. Between 15 July and 15 September 2026, Gauteng police discovered five bodies of mostly half-naked women in the Ekurhuleni area.

The first case was a 37-year-old woman found half-naked and dead in an open veld near the R21 highway, with a suspect arrested two days later and remaining in custody since.

One victim has been formally identified: 38-year-old Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo, a runner from Rhodesfield, Kempton Park. A second victim has been identifed as 32-year-old Itumeleng Kekana. A third victim has also been identified as 38-year-old Dineo Evelyn Motapane.

OPERATION SHANELA IN EKURHULENI PARK

SAPS have intensified Operation Shanela in Ekurhuleni area this week, marking the end of a promised “lockdown” of the area. This takes place as a seasoned team of investigators have been brought in to uncover whoever is responsible for the deaths of nine women across Ekurhuleni since July.

Acting provincial commissioner Major-General Fred Kekana led the intensified operation on Wednesday and Thursday this week alongside the Gauteng police. This was done by combining roadblocks, high-visibility patrols and other crime-prevention measures. The intention of this was to deter further attacks but also to gather information from residents. Law enforcement agencies from across Gauteng have been deployed, backed by national police units. Reinforcement has also been drawn in from other provinces.

The escalation follows Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia’s announcement earlier this week that police would “massively expand visibility through Operation Shanela in Kempton Park and the surrounding areas,” alongside the team of seasoned investigators, who were brought in.

Cachalia said residents can expect to see a sustained SAPS presence “in the weeks ahead,” describing it as a full mobilisation of available law-enforcement capability rather than a short-term show of force.

Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi confirmed the province had formally requested additional national assistance to support the operation. This was referred to ask a “lockdown” of the area. Crime expert Yusuf Abramjee has cautioned that the term should be understood as an intensified enforcement operation, not a literal shutdown of the town.

“The objective must be twofold: to prevent further attacks and, equally importantly, to gather the evidence needed to identify and arrest whoever is responsible for these horrific killings,” said Abramjee.

One of the scariest parts of what has happened in Ekurhuleni area is that it is still ongoing. The number of bodies found dead in the area of Ekurhuleni rose to nine within a matter of days. South African women constantly live in fear and feel as though there is no protection for them.

The urgency reflects a death toll that has continued to rise even as the operation gets underway. The bodies of most of the victims were found dumped near rivers or roadsides. Many also showed signs of sexual assault. Police have arrested one suspect in connection with the earliest case and are actively searching for others, backed by a R400 000 reward for information leading to a breakthrough.

The community itself has been standing up and portesting against what has happened. Silent marches and tribute runs have been held in Ekurhuleni area with the intention of standing in solidarity with the women whose lives have been lost.

However, there has been mixed reactions to the police response itself. Many social media users expressed how enraged they felt following SAPS asking women to be vigilant, and not to walk or exercise alone in isolated areas. Take a look…

🚨 SAPS UPDATE | SAPS has urged women in and around Kempton Park to avoid walking or exercising alone in isolated areas and, where possible, travel in groups.



A dedicated multidisciplinary task team has been established to investigate the recent murders and determine possible… pic.twitter.com/i2xpQVqNc6 — South African Government (@GovernmentZA) September 14, 2026

Social media users are questioning why women are being asked to avoid exercising or walking alone. Non-profit organisation Women For Change, which advocates against Gender-based Violence (GBV) and femicide, also questioned why the responsibility is being placed on women and not the SAPS themselves, to keep women and children safe.

Take a look…

“The lengths women have to go just to stay alive! Stop placing the responsibility for our safety back onto us. Women should not have to organise their entire lives around surviving violence and not being next,” read the caption.

“It is the responsibility of SAPS and the state to create a country in which women and children are safe. We are tired. We are angry. And we deserve to live freely, not constantly calculate how to stay alive,” read the caption.

World.title: JUST IN: Ekurhuleni fires suspended EMPD deputy chief Julius Mkhwanazi
World.content:
Suspended EMPD deputy chief Julius Mkhwanazi has been fired by the City of Ekurhuleni following a disciplinary process. Image: Flickr

The City of Ekurhuleni has fired suspended Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Police Department (EMPD) deputy chief Julius Mkhwanazi following a lengthy disciplinary process.

The city suspended Mkhwanazi on 11 November 2025 while it investigated allegations of misconduct and pursued disciplinary action against him.

His dismissal comes as he faces several criminal cases and remains behind bars after the Brakpan Magistrate’s Court denied him bail this week in the murder case of businessman Emmanuel Mbense.



Mkhwanazi and five co-accused face charges of murder, robbery with aggravating circumstances and defeating or obstructing the administration of justice.

They have denied involvement in Mbense’s murder.

CITY FIRES MKHWANAZI AFTER DISCIPLINARY PROCESS

The City of Ekurhuleni suspended Mkhwanazi in November last year after an internal audit investigation raised allegations of misconduct.

The municipality initially stressed that the suspension served as an administrative measure and did not amount to a finding of guilt.

Mkhwanazi later approached the Labour Court in an attempt to stop the disciplinary process.

However, the Johannesburg Labour Court dismissed his urgent application in March, clearing the way for the city to continue with the proceedings.



The disciplinary case also included allegations linked to the blue lights fitted to vehicles associated with businessman Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala.

Earlier this month, the city added another charge against Mkhwanazi over allegations that he unlawfully authorised the installation of blue emergency lights on private vehicles linked to Matlala.

Mkhwanazi has denied wrongdoing over the blue-light allegations.

MKHWANAZI REMAINS BEHIND BARS

Mkhwanazi’s dismissal follows several court appearances this week.

The Germiston Magistrate’s Court granted him R10 000 bail on Monday, 14 September, in the separate blue-lights corruption case.

He could not leave custody because he still faced a bail decision in the Mbense murder case.

The Brakpan Magistrate’s Court later denied bail to Mkhwanazi and his five co-accused.

The court postponed the murder case to 24 November 2026 for further investigation.

Mkhwanazi also appeared in the Johannesburg Magistrate’s Court on Friday, 18 September, alongside Kgomotso Makhubo, Adrian Norman Mackenzie and Keisha-Leigh Stols in another case involving precious stones allegedly worth more than R14 million.

The State alleges that the accused took the precious stones during a bogus law-enforcement operation at a Killarney property in 2023.

Mkhwanazi has denied the allegations.

Despite the dismissal with the EMPD, the criminal cases against him continue in court.

World.title: Heavy rain hits Durban as homes collapse and power outages spread
World.content:
eThekwini Municipality is on high alert following continuous heavy rain across the region, with mudslides causing about three houses to collapse and many power outages reported across the city.

The municipality’s Disaster Management and Emergency Services Directorates have been monitoring the situation as heavy downpours continue to affect vulnerable areas.

Homes collapse in Tshelimnyama

Fire and Emergency Services responded to an incident in Ward 15, Tshelimnyama, in Mariannhill near Pinetown, on Friday morning, 18 September, after localised mudslides caused approximately three houses to collapse.



Emergency responders secured and cleared the affected site.

The municipality confirmed that no fatalities, injuries, or entrapments were reported, although 14 residents were affected by the incident.

Disaster Management teams are conducting detailed assessments in the area and coordinating immediate humanitarian and relief assistance for the affected families.

The municipality has also taken steps to reduce the risk of wider flooding in vulnerable areas.

Disaster Management teams, working with municipal technical units, have opened the Isipingo Estuary mouth to help relieve water build-up and reduce the risk to surrounding communities.

The move comes as saturated ground conditions increase the possibility of further mudslides and localised flooding. Residents are being urged to remain cautious while the heavy rain persists.



High number of power outages around Durban

The heavy weather has also affected electricity supply across Durban.

The municipality’s Electricity and Energy Directorate is dealing with a high number of power outages in various parts of the city as a result of the inclement weather.

Its Contact Centre is receiving a high volume of reports from residents, while additional teams have been deployed across eThekwini to assist with repairs and restore electricity.

However, the large number of faults has resulted in prolonged outages in some areas as repair teams work through the backlog.

Residents can use the municipality’s following platforms for real-time updates on reported electricity faults:

WhatsApp: 064 761 7930

064 761 7930 USSD: 1343532#

1343532# Online: eThekwini electricity fault portal

Motorists also urged to take care

The municipality has also issued a warning to motorists as flooding and saturated conditions continue.

Drivers are advised to:

Keep their headlights on.

Reduce their speed.

Avoid flooded roads.

Avoid crossing low-lying bridges where water has accumulated.

Residents should also be alert to the possibility of further mudslides, particularly in areas where the ground has become soaked.

Storm-related emergencies and infrastructure damage can be reported to the eThekwini Central Disaster Call Centre on 031 361 0000.

World.title: Shark kills swimmer off popular beach near Perth
World.content:
A shark killed a man as he swam off a popular beach near Perth in Western Australia on Friday, police said. Image: Steven Markham / AFP

A shark killed a man as he swam off a popular beach near Perth in Western Australia on Friday, police said.

It was the fourth death from a shark attack in Australia this year.

“It was reported a male swimmer had been bitten by a shark while swimming along the coast,” a Western Australia state police spokeswoman said in a statement.



“The swimmer died as a result of the attack.”

Closed beach

Police helicopters and boats scoured waters off Sorrento Beach after emergency services were called to the beach in the morning, officials said.

Authorities closed beaches in the area until further notice.

Local media reported that witnesses had seen blood in the water.

“It was like a scene off Jaws where a body is flicked around like a rag doll,” an unidentified male witness on the beach told local broadcaster Seven.

Surf Life Saving WA said in a social media post that an unidentified species of shark was involved in the incident about 50 metres offshore.



Second attack in a week

It was the second shark attack in Western Australia this week, after a man lost part of his leg when he was bitten at Glenfield Beach, north of Perth.

There have been multiple shark attack fatalities around the country this year.

A 12-year-old boy died after he was bitten by a shark while swimming in Sydney Harbour in January.

Three divers were fatally mauled in separate incidents between May and June – two in Western Australia and the third in Queensland.

Also in June, a woman had to have part of her left arm amputated after she was mauled by a shark at one of Australia’s most popular beaches, Coogee, in Sydney.

There have been around 1 300 shark incidents around Australia since 1791, of which more than 260 resulted in death, according to a database of their encounters with humans.

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs to part ways with Nkosingiphile Ngcobo?
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs could part ways with Nkosingiphile Ngcobo after more than seven years at the club.

The midfielder is entering the final season of his contract, with a possible early termination now reportedly on the cards, according to Soccerbeat.

Ngcobo came through the Chiefs academy and was once regarded as one of the club’s promising young talents. However, despite spending several years with the senior team, he has struggled to establish himself as a regular and make a significant impact.



Former Orlando Pirates winger Lebohang Mokoena believes Chiefs may have shown too much patience with the midfielder and feels a move away could benefit both player and club.

“Should have left last season or two seasons back. I think he was given grace. He’s been there as a youngster and we’ve been saying youngster, youngster, but he hasn’t really done much,”Mokoena said on Soccerbeat.

“He is a quality player and has a good left foot, as you’ve seen the club try him in different positions.



“He hardly creates and hardly scores, so it was bound to happen. A move was supposed to happen a long time ago, according to me.

“He needs to leave to get more game time and probably work on other aspects of his game which he couldn’t do at Kaizer Chiefs.”

There was an expectation that Ngcobo would eventually develop into one of the senior figures at Chiefs, but his career has not quite followed that trajectory.



The 31-year-old has made around 98 league appearances and more than 105 total professional appearances for Amakhosi during his senior career, having also featured in the MultiChoice Diski Challenge earlier in his career.

Ngcobo only has a year left in his Kaizer Chiefs contract

With his contract entering its final season, Ngcobo’s future at Naturena is now uncertain, and the coming months could determine whether his long association with the club comes to an end.

Where should Ngcobo go?

World.title: SAWS warns parts of South Africa are in for a wet weekend
World.content:
South Africa is in for a weekend of unsettled weather, with the SAWS warning of rain, snow and thunderstorms across several provinces. Image: Wikimedia Commons

South Africa is in for a weekend of unsettled weather, with the South African Weather Service (SAWS) warning of disruptive rain, snow, thunderstorms and damaging winds across several provinces.

Very cold and wet conditions are expected over high-lying areas of the Eastern Cape and south-western parts of KwaZulu-Natal on Friday.

SAWS has issued multiple weather warnings, with some areas facing a significant risk of flooding, dangerous fast-flowing water and difficult driving conditions.



KwaZulu-Natal faces flooding risk

An Orange Level 6 warning has been issued for disruptive rain along the KwaZulu-Natal coast and adjacent interior up to Richards Bay.

SAWS warns that flooding could affect formal and informal settlements, roads and other infrastructure.

Fast-flowing streams and deep water could pose a danger to life, while communities, livestock and livelihoods could be affected.



An additional Yellow Level 4 warning is in place for the eastern and southern parts of KwaZulu-Natal, where disruptive rain could result in flooding.

Eastern Cape rain and snow

The Eastern Cape is also facing significant weather impacts.

An Orange Level 5 warning has been issued for the Port St Johns, Ingquza Hill, Winnie Madikizela-Mandela and Ntabankulu local municipalities.



Disruptive rain could lead to flooding of settlements, roads and bridges, as well as interruptions to essential services.

Meanwhile, a Yellow Level 2 warning has been issued for coastal areas and the adjacent interior between KuGompo City and Port St Johns, including the extreme north-eastern interior of the province.

SAWS has also warned of disruptive snow over the Matatiele and Elundini local municipalities.



The snow could result in isolated losses of vulnerable livestock and difficult driving conditions.

Thunderstorms and damaging winds

Thunderstorms are also expected in parts of the Northern Cape, Free State and KwaZulu-Natal.

A Yellow Level 4 warning has been issued for the extreme east-central parts of the Northern Cape.



Severe thunderstorms could bring heavy downpours, damaging winds, excessive lightning and hail, potentially resulting in injuries, danger to life and localised flooding.

A Yellow Level 2 warning covers the eastern parts of the Northern Cape, the western Free State and north-western KwaZulu-Natal.

Meanwhile, damaging winds are expected over the southern and western parts of the Northern Cape and northern parts of the Western Cape.



SAWS warns that the winds could cause localised damage, power and communication interruptions and difficult driving conditions.

What to expect this weekend

The weather is expected to remain unsettled into Saturday and Sunday.

SAWS forecasts partly cloudy and cold to cool conditions, although some areas will be warm.



Isolated to scattered showers and thundershowers are expected, becoming widespread over western parts of the country on Saturday.

Residents in affected areas are urged to take weather warnings seriously, avoid crossing flooded roads or fast-flowing streams and exercise caution when travelling.

Motorists should also be prepared for reduced visibility, wet roads, strong winds, snow and localised flooding depending on their route.

World.title: Mbappe ends Nike partnership to join Swiss brand On
World.content:
PARIS - France captain Kylian Mbappe has signed with Swiss sportswear brand On, ending a long association with Nike that stretched back to the start of his career, the company announced on Friday.

"Today, Swiss sportswear brand On announces its entry into football alongside football champion Kylian Mbappe, marking the beginning of the brand's journey into the world's biggest sport," read a company statement.

On also announced that 1998 World Cup winner Thierry Henry had been appointed its football director.

"From the beginning, what drew me to On was the opportunity to build something entirely new together that will help shape tomorrow's game," said Mbappe.

World.title: Turning pages, changing futures: Corporate-government partnership celebrates National Book Week with three library donations
World.content:
Turning pages, changing futures: Corporate-government partnership celebrates National Book Week with three library donations

On Monday, 7 September 2026, AVBOB in partnership with the Department of Basic Education (DBE), donated a container library to Thongwana High School in Ingwavuma, Manguzi, and two trolley libraries to Mengu Primary School in Kwalulwane, both in KwaZulu-Natal, to commemorate Book Week and Literacy Month. The donations are aimed at strengthening literacy, learning and access to educational resources in underserved rural communities.

“The container library is stocked with over 3 000 books and learning resources. It is the 77th AVBOB Container Library donated and the first to be awarded to a high school since the inception of the project in 2013. Mengu Primary School is also the first school to receive two trolley libraries. They include learning materials and educational toys for the early childhood development centre to Grade 7,” says Eugene Strauss, AVBOB Group CEO.

World.title: Julius Mkhwanazi fired
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Suspended Deputy Ekurhuleni Metro Police Department Deputy Chief Julius Mkhwanazi has been fired.

Mkhwanazi had been on suspension since November 11, 2025.

He is currently behind bars after he was denied bail earlier this week.

He and five other co-accused have been denied bail.

He is facing murder, robbery and defeating the ends of justice charges in connection with the killing of businessman Emmanuel Mbense.

Mbense was allegedly killed at his Brakpan home before his body was dumped at a dam near Nigel in April 2022.

Mkhwanazi is also facing multiple criminal matters for which he had been granted bail.

He has also been implicated at the Madlanga Commission.

World.title: Billionaire Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
World.content:
WASHINGTON - Influential billionaire investor Warren Buffett will step down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway, the conglomerate announced Friday.

The news brings to an end the revered investor's more than half-a-century of running the group, which he turned into a financial behemoth.

Buffett's resignation is "effective immediately," and he will remain a member of the board of directors, Berkshire Hathaway said in a statement.

Buffett's son Howard Buffett will take over as chairman, the statement added.

The 96-year-old had announced plans last year to retire from leading the business group.

Berkshire Hathaway, a former small textile company, has grown over the years into a gigantic conglomerate under Buffett's leadership, and is now worth over $1 trillion on Wall Street -- a first for an American group outside the tech sector.

Today, his conglomerate owns dozens of businesses, from Duracell batteries to US insurer Geico, and shares in carefully selected companies, from Coca-Cola to Bank of America.

World.title: ‘I have forgiven them’: Zolani Tete’s father as accused denied bail
World.content:
MDANTSANE – The father of former boxing world champion Zolani Tete says he is relieved that the men accused of his son’s murder have been denied bail but has forgiven them.

Speaking outside the Mdantsane Magistrate’s Court after Uzuzole Goqwana and Sinebhongo Qase were denied bail, Zolile Tete said holding a grudge would not bring his son back.

Goqwana and Qase are among four men facing eight charges linked to Tete’s murder. The two other accused, who are alleged to be the hitmen, have already abandoned their bail applications.

READ | Zolani Tete murder accused denied bail

“I have forgiven all of them and their families. It will never bring Zolani back, but I have made peace with the fact,” Zolile said.

He said he was relieved by the court’s decision to deny the accused bail but maintained that he did not want to engage with their families.

“It is still painful and I don’t want to speak to their families, but I’m not fighting with them. There is nothing I can do. I repeat, it will never bring Zolani back,” he said.

Zolile said Tete’s eight-year-old son, who was in the back seat of the vehicle when the former boxer was gunned down outside his home in Mdantsane last month, was still struggling to recover from the incident.

He said the boy remains traumatised and is startled by loud sounds. Three children were in the car when Tete was ambushed.

World.title: ‘Money’s everywhere, except where it is needed’: Fikeni tells Madlanga SA has spending problem
World.content:
PRETORIA - South African does not have a money issue, says Public Service Commission (PSC) chair, Prof. Somadoda Fikeni. It has a spending problem.

Speaking at the Madlanga Commission on Friday, Fikeni said, "money is everywhere, except for where it is needed."

The PSC aims to promote professionalism in the public service. They also look at employee grievances, administrative failures and service delivery issue.

World.title: Police launch manhunt after two EC cops killed
World.content:
MTHATHA - Police have launched a manhunt after two Eastern Cape police officers were killed in Libode, near Mthatha, in the early hours of Friday morning.

The officers, aged 30 and 52, were from the Mthatha National Intervention Unit and the Mthatha Public Order Policing Unit. They were responding to reports of an attack on a spaza shop when they came under fire.

READ | Three EC police officers killed in shooting

It is alleged that armed suspects were attacking the shop and demanding money from the operator. The officers responded to a call for assistance and were later found with gunshot wounds.

Their service pistols were also reported missing.

Police are investigating two counts of murder, two counts of attack on police, two counts of robbery of police firearms and one count of attempted business robbery.

World.title: UPDATE: Zolani Tete murder accused denied bail
World.content:
MDANTSANE - Two men alleged to have played key roles as the mastermind and middleman in the murder of former boxing world champion Zolani Tete have been denied bail.

Uzuzole Goqwana and Sinebhongo Qase appeared in the Mdantsane Magistrate’s Court on Friday, where their bail applications were denied.

READ | Zolani Tete family chooses forgiveness as accused killers await bail ruling

The pair are among four men facing eight charges linked to Tete’s murder. The two men accused of carrying out the shooting have already abandoned their bail applications.

Tete was gunned down outside his home in Mdantsane last month. Another person was wounded in the shooting.

World.title: Inside Parliament's probe into secondary school fees and capitation
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Pangani Girls School Chief Principal Dr Millicent Odhiambo before the National Assembly Public Investments Committee on Governance and Education. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

Parliament’s scrutiny of the Auditor-General’s report on public secondary schools has exposed inconsistencies in capitation funding, student enrolment figures and the National Education Management Information System (NEMIS).

The National Assembly Public Investments Committee on Governance and Education has raised concerns over the impact of funding shortfalls on school operations and called for discussions with Ministry of Education officials to address the challenges.

The committee is also exploring whether the secondary school fee structure should be reviewed amid concerns that current capitation is insufficient to meet rising operational costs.

Chaired by Luanda MP Dick Maungu, the committee raised the concerns after the Auditor-General’s report showed that several national schools (C1) had sought additional fees from parents above the approved Sh53,000 annual amount, citing rising costs and inflation.

MPs also questioned disparities between capitation disbursements and the actual number of students in schools, which principals said had contributed to underfunding.

For the first time, administrators of national schools appeared before a parliamentary committee to respond to audit queries, with several saying discrepancies between NEMIS figures and actual school records had affected the amount of capitation they received.

Chief principals from Alliance High School, Alliance Girls, Bishop Gatimu Ngandu Girls, Limuru Girls, Mang’u High, Kenya High School, Pangani Girls and Kabare Girls, among others, said they had experienced difficulties validating learner data on NEMIS.

They said capitation received by their schools did not cover all students, with principals reporting that they receive less than the Sh22,244 expected per learner annually. The amount, they said, averages about Sh15,000.

Schools defend additional fees

During the committee’s examination of Alliance High School’s audit report, the Auditor-General flagged the irregular increase in school fees, including Sh17.6 million collected from parents.

“The school charged fees of Sh68,554 whereas the fees as per the Ministry’s guideline is Sh53,554 and the school thus raised fees by Sh15,000 per student annually contrary to Regulation 44 of Basic Education Regulation 2015, which states that no public school or institution shall issue alternative fee structure other than that approved by the Cabinet Secretary,” the auditor read. ‎Alliance High School's Principal David Kamau before the National Assembly Public Investments Committee on Governance and Education. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

Alliance High School Chief Principal David Kamau admitted that the school had sought alternative funding but said the initiative came from parents.

He said the approved Sh53,000 fee was insufficient to sustain the school’s budget amid rising costs and expectations of maintaining the institution’s standards.

“We have a certain lifestyle we have to maintain and that is why parents came in – in fact it was their idea – and asked us to maintain that. They came in and suggested they can do a budget support so that we maintain the same standards. For us, to acquire the results, we have to do a lot of activities to make sure we give a holistic education associated with the school over the years,” he explained.

“Parents approve that at an Annual General Meeting and we write to the Ministry but that letter of authority has never been granted. We have followed the process to the letter in terms of seeking approval for extra levies from parents,” he added.

The audit also flagged fee arrears in almost all the schools, with Alliance High School reporting arrears amounting to Sh36 million.

Kenya High School Chief Principal Rev Edith Koech was also required to respond to an audit query over unapproved fees under the parents’ association support programme, through which parents were charged Sh25,000 above the set amount per student without approval from the county education board.

Koech said the school had written to the Ministry seeking approval and, although it did not expressly receive authorisation at the time, it had since obtained it.

She said additional funds were approved during annual general meetings, where two budgets were presented — one based on Ministry guidelines and another reflecting what parents felt should be covered.

“Kenya High has its standards, for instance we have tea three times a day and they eat githeri once, they will burn the school if we change,” Koech explained.

Kiminini MP Kakai Bisau said the issue of additional levies had emerged in many schools, with principals arguing that the funds were necessary for students’ wellbeing.

“Looks like this issue is conflicting the law yet public participation is conducted among parents of respective schools. This is something we need guidance on and embedded in policy,” he said.

Other MPs questioned what happens to students from poor backgrounds who cannot afford the additional charges.

Lungalunga MP Chiforomondo Munga said principals had been entrusted with following the law, which states that public schools should not issue alternative fee structures without approval.

“I was a parent of Alliance but all said and done, you have done contrary to the law because approvals must come from the CS and I can assure you there is nobody who will approve that because they know they will be breaking the law and will be held accountable,” he said.

He said the situation presented a dilemma because schools were expected to maintain certain standards while operating within existing regulations.

Embakasi West MP Mark Mwenje said the issue of additional fees had existed for years, noting that he had paid about Sh40,000 while he was an Alliance High School student about two decades ago.

“We just need to sit down with the Ministry because it is becoming obvious that this money is no longer sufficient but we need to inform the principal that whenever such things are happening, there should be concurrence of the Principal Secretary but when we meet with the CS that issue should come out because we can no longer bury our heads in the sand,” Mwenje said.

Igembe Central MP Daniel Karitho described the issue as a “tricky” one, given rising inflation and the need to comply with the law.

“We cannot allow parents from any institution to just sit down and agree because there are those who are voiceless. This is an issue that needs to be discussed even in the House on the fees structure and if there is something that needs to be done, even on the basic regulation so that we can have a level,” Karitho said.

Alliance principal, however, maintained that the school’s process was transparent, with parents being provided with budget documents during annual general meetings and informed why additional funds were required.

“We tell the parents that is their decision to make and if they want to stick to the Sh53,000 but what we can offer as a school will reduce. I can assure we are conscious of the needy and we do not send anyone away because of the fees, either for statutory or additional,” he explained.

Kenya High echoed similar sentiments, saying additional contributions were based on public participation among parents and that no child was sent home over fees. The school also has endowment funds, it said.

NEMIS discrepancies

In another case, MPs questioned how Limuru Girls High School received an additional Sh785,946 in capitation after discrepancies emerged between its student enrolment records and figures captured in NEMIS.

The committee noted variances in Limuru Girls’ records and those of other national schools for the financial years 2020/2021 to 2024/2025.

The Auditor-General’s report for the year ended June 2024 showed that NEMIS recorded 2,099 students at the school in September 2023, 2,300 in January 2024 and 2,354 in May 2024.

However, records presented by the school showed enrolment of 2,062 students in September 2023 and 2,253 students in both January and May 2024.

The difference resulted in Sh785,946 in excess funding, raising concerns over whether the variance affected service delivery in other schools that did not receive capitation and made it difficult to confirm value for money.

Limuru Girls Chief Principal Susan Kariuki acknowledged the discrepancies but attributed them to differences between physical enrolment records and learner information captured in NEMIS.

“The difference arose from variations between the school’s physical enrolment records and the learner information captured in NEMIS at the respective reporting periods. The school did not intentionally provide inflated enrolment figures,” Kariuki said.

“So, because you are given more money, where do you take it?” Maungu posed.

Kariuki, however, said the school had not received the full amount of capitation due per learner and therefore did not consider itself overfunded in the ordinary sense. She said the Government was expected to provide Sh22,244 per learner but the school had been receiving about Sh15,000.

Narok Woman Representative Rebecca Tonkei questioned how Limuru Girls received higher funding for learners who were not captured in NEMIS, noting that other schools appearing before the committee had complained of underfunding caused by incomplete NEMIS records.

Maungu questioned the reliability of NEMIS, saying a system used to determine public funding should be predictable, consistent and dependable.

“This is not a good system. A good system should be predictable, consistent and dependable. But this system gives some people less and others more, sometimes the data is missing,” Maungu noted.

Starehe Girls raises fresh questions

Starehe Girls presented a different case that the committee said contained several grey areas after it emerged that 70 per cent of the school’s 776 learners are fully sponsored while the remaining 30 per cent are self-sponsored.

The school explained that all learners receive about Sh16,000 in Government capitation. For the 70 per cent, their upkeep is sourced through the board of trustees, while self-sponsored learners cover their own costs.

“Being a C1 school, by law it should pay Sh53,000. Instead, some are paying Sh150,000 meaning Sh96,000 extra to take care of the vulnerable. On this other side, you are saying they have a sponsor who take care...are you seeing the kind of confusion because they are already sponsored?” posed Maungu.

Despite the school’s unique funding arrangement, the committee said Starehe Girls remained a public institution and should therefore be audited.

The committee noted that not all financial years had been covered in the audit, unlike other C1 schools, and directed the institution to present all relevant documents for review.

Meanwhile, Mang’u High School surprised the committee when its administration said the school also faced challenges posed by snakes and hyenas that sometimes invade the institution.

World.title: Ruto faults Uhuru for undermining his government
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto join traditional dancers in Homa Bay on September 17, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has renewed his public criticism of former President Uhuru Kenyatta, accusing his predecessor of undermining the government and urging him to withdraw from active political mobilisation.

Ruto said he had supported Uhuru throughout their political partnership and expected reciprocal support when he sought the presidency.

“I stood by you through four elections; I stood by you, helped you, took care of you, and worked for you.”

Ruto claimed the two had discussed an arrangement in which each would serve as president for ten years. He accused Uhuru of failing to honour that understanding, saying:

“When the time came for you to help me, after you said ‘ten years for you, ten years for me,’ not even for a single day did you support me.”

Ruto also appealed to Uhuru to respect the position of former President and withdraw from political activities that he said were aimed at destabilising his administration.

“A former president! Surely, my brother, you are lowering the dignity of the office of the former president. You are a retired president respect your office, go and relax. Let us plan for this country of ours, Kenya,” Ruto said.

Ruto made the remarks on Thursday, September 17, 2026, in Sindo, Homa Bay County, as he concluded a four-day development tour of Nyanza.

The tour covered Kisumu, Siaya, Migori and Homa Bay and focused largely on roads, markets, housing, water and other development projects. The Star+1

The latest confrontation adds another chapter to the complicated political relationship between the two leaders.

Ruto served as Uhuru's deputy from 2013 to 2022, after the two politicians formed a political alliance that won the 2013 and 2017 presidential elections.

Contemporary accounts describe their original arrangement as involving support for Kenyatta for two terms, followed by support for Ruto's presidential ambitions. The Washington Post

The President nevertheless acknowledged Uhuru's democratic right to oppose his government but urged the former president to respect the office he once held.

“You are running schemes to sabotage the government. You are a retired president respect your office, go and relax. Let us plan for this country of ours, Kenya,” he said.

His criticism centred instead on what he described as continued political mobilisation against his administration.

He said his administration had stabilised the economy and pointed to investments in education, housing, markets and infrastructure. During the Homa Bay leg alone, the government highlighted a Sh3.5 billion plan for 21 modern markets.

World.title: Five killed as bandits ambush police search team in Isiolo
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Five people, including two police officers killed by bandits at the troubled grazing field of Gotu in Isiolo County on Wednesday.

The victims are a senior police officer, a police constable who was the driver of the vehicle that was ambushed by bandits, a livestock farmer and two National Police Reservists (NPR). The police officers were attached to an Anti-Stock Theft Unit (ASTU) located near Gotu trading centre.

The victims were part of a search team that was looking for an elderly man who reportedly went missing within the Gotu area and was last seen around Madho Gurba Huka, a grazing area in Chari Ward in Merti sub-county.

Isiolo County Police Commander Isaac Sang said the mentally challenged man from Barambate sub-location, Kulamawe location was reported missing a day ago.

The Isiolo camel keeper, reported to be related to the man who went missing, had requested police to search for him.

The mission turned tragic when the group was ambushed by armed bandits, killing all five on the spot.

The incident took place near the junction of Lososia-Merti road and Gotu-Merti route.

Mr Sang said the bodies of the officers and other victims were removed to Isiolo County Teaching and Referral Hospital awaiting postmortem.

"A reinforcement (of security personnel) had been sent to the area which includes an armoured vehicle to pursue the attackers," said the police chief.

The police boss called for calm and cooperation from the residents while police pursue the suspects.

He said that investigation into the incident had commenced.

On Wednesday afternoon, a gunfight was reported between police reservists and the bandits on the western bank of the river.

"The reservists in the area pursued the attackers minutes after reports of the killings that led to an exchange of gunfire. We are told an unknown number of people have been injured," said a herdsman from Gotu who sought anonymity for security reasons.

A source from Isiolo County and Teaching and Referral Hospital revealed that two ambulances had been sent to Gotu to attend to the injured persons.

Gotu, along with Kom in Merti sub-county is a bandit hotspot in Isiolo that is attributed to competition over scarce pasture by rival herders from Isiolo, Samburu East and parts of Marsabit with local leaders calling for eviction of pastoralists from outside the County. Several people have been killed in the two locations since last year and hundreds of livestock stolen.

On August 1, two people were killed in the Garse Dabata area in Gotu and nearly 700 goats and sheep were stolen. Nearly all the stolen animals were recovered in operation undertaken by a multi-agency security team stationed in various locations along the Isiolo-Meru border.

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen on two occasions called for an operation in parts of Isiolo, Laikipia, Samburu and Meru Counties that had experienced frequent cases of banditry and rustling.

However, leaders fault the CS for failure to take decisive action on insecurity that keeps on recurring in parts of Isiolo and Meru Counties. The leaders including Governor Abdi Guyo want herders from outside Isiolo who are in Kom and Gotu areas to be evicted.

World.title: Muthaiga Golf Club restores access after KFS standoff
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Muthaiga Golf Club has restored access to a section of its course that was temporarily taken over by the Kenya Forest Service (KFS), hours after the agency moved into the area, claiming it forms part of Karura Forest.

The disruption affected the Front Nine, covering Holes Two to Nine, before the club’s board intervened to restore normal operations.

In a statement issued Tuesday, Muthaiga Golf Club Chairman Dennis Mwirigi said the board had taken the necessary steps to facilitate the resumption of activities after the temporary disruption.

“We are pleased to confirm that access to the affected part of the course has been restored and members may proceed with their scheduled activities as usual,” Mwirigi said.

He said the board remained committed to protecting the club’s interests, assets and members while addressing the matter through the appropriate channels.

The development follows an earlier communication to members informing them that KFS had taken over access to the affected section, claiming it was part of Karura Forest.

The club had initially said the Front Nine would not be accessible until further notice as it sought to resolve the matter. The driving range and parking areas were not affected.

The incident sparked criticism over the manner in which KFS handled the dispute, with Prof Karanja, Chairperson of Friends of Karura Forest, urging the agency to pursue dialogue and legal channels.

Prof Karanja said KFS should have first engaged the club’s management and clearly explained its claim over the disputed land instead of deploying dogs, guns and heavy security.

“If they don't agree that it was your land, go to court. The court will determine,” he said.

He questioned whether KFS had adequately demonstrated that the disputed section was forest land or explained how it was allegedly acquired by Muthaiga Golf Club.

“They should have come publicly and said, look, Muthaiga, that area and that area belong to the forest,” Prof Karanja said.

He said KFS should identify the specific portion of land it claims belongs to the forest and explain the basis of its claim before taking further action.

Prof Karanja argued that the dispute should be resolved through established legal procedures rather than force. “Trees are not protected by guns,” he said.

He described the deployment of armed personnel as the wrong way of resolving a land dispute and called for engagement between KFS and the golf club.

Prof Karanja also warned that actions by government agencies could have wider implications for the administration of President William Ruto, saying confrontational conduct could lead members of the public to associate such actions directly with the government.

“When government departments behave like this, everybody now starts thinking, oh, it's Ruto's whatever,” he said.

He further recalled a previous dispute involving Friends of Karura Forest, where he said armed personnel were deployed and the group removed from an area before senior government officials intervened.

According to Prof Karanja, officials from the Treasury and forestry departments eventually intervened and encouraged dialogue to resolve the matter.

He urged KFS to adopt a similar approach in the Muthaiga dispute, saying the agency and the club should present their respective claims and seek a court determination if they cannot agree.

For now, the restoration of access means members can resume their scheduled activities, while the underlying dispute over the contested section remains subject to further engagement between KFS and the club.

World.title: Juja couple's surprise blessing of five babies
World.content:
Mercy Kanini, 28, from Juja, Kiambu County, gave birth to five children at Thika Level Five Hospital. [Gitau Wanyoike, Standard]

A couple from Juja, Kiambu County, is celebrating the unexpected arrival of five babies after scans during pregnancy showed they were expecting quadruplets.

Mercy Kanini, 28, delivered four girls and a boy through normal delivery at Thika Level Five Hospital, in a rare case believed to be among only a handful of quintuplet births recorded in Kenya.

World.title: Police to restrict access to CBD during Linda Mwananchi Nairobi rally
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi officials during a rally. [Courtesy]

Organisers of the Linda Mwananchi rally and their supporters will not be allowed to access Nairobi’s Central Business District (CBD), Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud has warned.

According to Mohamud, police had received notification of the planned rally, which is scheduled to take place at Jacaranda Grounds on Sunday, through Embakasi East MP Babu Owino.

However, he warned that the CBD would remain off-limits, saying police would not allow Nairobi to become a battleground for political supremacy.

“The National Police Service respects the constitutional right of every Kenyan to assemble, demonstrate, express political views, and participate in public affairs, but that right must be exercised peacefully, lawfully, and with respect to the rights and safety of other Kenyans,” Mohamud stated.

According to Mohamud, they had received a tip that some individuals were planning to mobilise goons to disrupt the rally, prompting the directive to keep the CBD out of bounds.

“We have received some information, some credible information, that some individuals may seek to mobilise groups of unruly youths and goons to outnumber and intimidate and confront rival groups.”

“Therefore, I make a direct appeal to all political leaders, organisers or influencers to restrain their supporters and control their crowds. No political objective is worth the blood of a Kenyan,” he added.

Mohamud assured the organisers and those planning to attend the rally that police would provide security throughout the event and facilitate all lawful activities.

The Linda Mwananchi movement is set to hold its Nairobi rally on Sunday, September 13. The procession will start at All Saints Cathedral before proceeding to Jacaranda Grounds.

World.title: Egypt bans social media accounts for under-13s and mandates “safe mode” for ages 13-15
World.content:
Egyptian authorities declared a major digital crackdown on Thursday, barring children under the age of 13 from holding independent social media accounts and slapping strict mandatory restrictions on users under 15.

In a joint decree issued by the Supreme Council for Media Regulation (SCMR) and the National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (NTRA), social media platforms operate under a tough new mandate designed to shield children and young teenagers from digital risks. Under the newly unveiled regulations, platforms are strictly forbidden from allowing children under 13 to create or activate independent personal accounts.

For young teens aged 13 to under 15, personal accounts will still be permitted—but with a heavy catch. Platforms must automatically and mandatorily activate “Safe Mode” on these accounts, and the setting cannot be unilaterally disabled by the underage user as long as they remain in that age bracket.

To ensure the rules are not easily skirted, the decree compels tech platforms to deploy effective age-verification protocols and actively prevent users from manipulating age boundaries. Companies must audit existing accounts and take immediate action against any profile confirmed or suspected to belong to a user under 15. However, a formal appeals process must be provided to correct any legitimate age-verification errors.

Officials frame the sweeping measures as a direct response to directives from President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi aimed at safeguarding youth from the dangers of social media misuse and forging a safer online ecosystem.

Underscoring the broader vision, Khaled Abdel Aziz, Chairman of the SCMR, emphasized that digital child safety has become “a shared responsibility between the state, the family, society, and digital platforms.” He insisted that the objective is not to strip technology away from children, but rather to guarantee its safe, responsible, and age-appropriate use.

Echoing this stance, NTRA Chief Executive Mohamed Shamroukh explained that the framework operates on the principle of “age- and risk-proportionate protection,” delivering varying tiers of security based on a user’s developmental age and exposure to online hazards.

Tech firms have been put on a strict clock: platforms must bring their operations into full compliance within three months of the decree taking effect, and must submit a comprehensive operational blueprint and technical timeline detailing their execution strategy within the next 30 days.

World.title: Sisi warns against mounting conspiracy to destabilize Egypt
World.content:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi warned Thursday that persistent schemes to destabilize the state remain an ongoing threat, declaring that the unrest witnessed between 2011 and 2013 “has not ended” and that underlying plots “have not stopped.”

Speaking during an address at the Egyptian Military Academy, President Sisi emphasized that while methods may evolve, the push to dismantle the state persists, underscoring public awareness as the nation’s primary defense against continuous challenges.

Reflecting on regional volatility, Sisi noted that while several neighboring nations suffered catastrophic destabilization during that period, Egypt miraculously survived.

He described the nation’s survival as a divine blessing, asserting that events across the region were systematically orchestrated and planned, imposing a heavy responsibility on Egypt to safeguard its stability—particularly given its finite national resources.

The President stressed that protecting the state is a collective civic duty rather than a mandate tied to any single authority or leadership figure. Framing national preservation around the institution of the presidency, he cautioned, distorts the true purpose of state resilience, which rests on the joint responsibility of the government, institutions, and the Egyptian public.

World.title: Egypt to witness gradual drop in temperatures over next few days
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority announced a noticeable shift in the weather across Egypt, as the country experiences a gradual drop in temperatures ranging between 3 to 5 degrees Celsius in most areas, starting Friday, and continuing through next Tuesday.

This drop comes after a heatwave that swept the country over the past few days, bringing temperatures back to seasonal averages for this time of year.

Moderate to warm and humid weather will prevail in the early morning, turning hot and humid during the day across the north of the country down to Greater Cairo and North Upper Egypt, while remaining extremely hot in South Upper Egypt.

Maximum temperatures in Greater Cairo and the Nile Delta are expected to reach around 33°C on Friday, dropping to 32°C on Saturday and Sunday, while in South Upper Egypt, temperatures will decrease from 43°C down to 39°C by the beginning of next week.

Meteorologists warned of dense morning fog forming at times between 4:00 AM and 8:00 AM on roads to and from northern Egypt, Greater Cairo, the Canal Cities, and Central Sinai.

There are also chances of light to occasionally moderate rain over parts of the northern coasts and the northern Nile Delta. Winds will pick up across most areas at speeds between 30 and 40 km/h, helping to cool the atmosphere, with a chance of kicking up sand and dust in parts of the Western Desert.

World.title: New Princess Diana documentary featuring confidential audio tapes
World.content:
Nearly three decades after her death, Princess Diana remains a compelling subject for arts and literature, most recently featuring in the new three-part documentary series “Diana Unheard”, which presents previously unreleased audio recordings of the late royal.

Global rights to the three-part series have been acquired by Cineflix Rights from the independent British production company Love Monday TV, known for producing royal programs for ITV and Channel 5.

The series features “the People’s Princess” reflecting on her life, personal relationships, and the royal family.

Producers gained access to secret conversations recorded in 1991 between Diana and her close friend, Dr. James Colthurst—tapes that served as the primary source for Andrew Morton’s groundbreaking biography, “Diana: Her True Story”.

Both Colthurst and Morton appear in the documentary alongside Diana’s audio tracks, where she discusses Prince Charles (his title at the time), Camilla, and Prince Andrew.

Speaking to Deadline, Kieran Barfield, Creative Director at Love Monday TV, stated: “With this series, we wanted to challenge the long-standing narrative depicting Diana, Princess of Wales, merely as a victim of her circumstances. Here, we do not see Diana as a passive victim of events, but as a woman taking control of her own narrative and risking everything to make her voice heard.”

“Diana Unheard” is set to premiere at the MIPCOM trade market in Cannes, France, nearly 30 years after the Princess died in a Paris car crash at age 36 in August 1997. The debut comes amidst a public rift between Buckingham Palace and Diana’s brother, Earl Spencer, over his new memoir, “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister”, which examines his sister’s life and tragic death.

World.title: Egyptair plans Sydney flights in major Asian expansion
World.content:
Egyptair is preparing to relaunch flights from Cairo to Sydney via Singapore in 2027, marking a potential return to the Australian continent after a nearly 25-year hiatus. According to Sydney Airport officials and industry reports from Aviation Week, the route remains subject to regulatory approvals.

Crucially, the flag carrier is seeking “Fifth Freedom” traffic rights, which would allow it to sell tickets independently for the Singapore-Sydney leg alongside its primary Cairo connections.

Simultaneously, Egypt is accelerating its diplomatic and tourism push into Southeast Asia. It has officially granted Vietnamese citizens visas upon arrival at Egyptian airports to boost bilateral travel and trade ties, a decision highlighted by Deputy Foreign Minister Ambassador Mohamed Abou Bakr Saleh during Vietnam’s National Day celebrations in Cairo.

Complementing these policy changes, Egyptian carrier Air Cairo is exploring direct commercial flights to Vietnam to capitalize on growing Asian tourist demand. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism officials welcomed the initiative, framing Egypt as a key North African gateway to expand reciprocal travel and cultural exchange.

World.title: Pakistan calls for implementing “Mecca Agreement” to safeguard Saudi security amid Houthi attacks
World.content:
Pakistani Defense Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif affirmed that the time has come to implement the “Mecca Agreement,” amid escalating tensions and attacks launched by the Houthis toward the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

During statements to the local Pakistani channel Geo News, Asif emphasized his country’s commitment to Saudi Arabia’s security and the protection of holy sites, stressing that Pakistan does not need a formal treaty to fulfill its responsibility toward safeguarding the sanctities, as Islamabad considers it a binding “duty.”

Diplomatic channels and messages to Tehran

Asif confirmed that Pakistan will continue its diplomatic efforts to contain the escalation and prevent the conflict from spreading to new fronts, underscoring the importance of maintaining regional stability. The Pakistani Defense Minister also revealed that his country relayed a Saudi message to Iran, which detailed growing concerns regarding the attacks carried out by the Houthi group.

The strategic scope of the Mecca pact

The Mecca Joint Defense Agreement is a collective defense pact signed in August 2026 by Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey that enshrines a mutual defense framework committing each nation to treat an attack against one as an attack against all. Expanding upon a prior 2025 bilateral defense deal between Riyadh and Islamabad, the agreement aims to bolster regional security cooperation and deter foreign aggression targeting the signatories’ territories and holy sites.

Historical ties and mediation

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia share deep-rooted defense and security ties, with Islamabad historically pledging to protect the Kingdom’s territorial integrity and the Islamic holy sites in Mecca and Medina against external threats. Pakistan has frequently acted as a diplomatic bridge between Saudi Arabia and Iran to reduce regional friction, utilizing its military and diplomatic channels to de-escalate proxy conflicts in the Arabian Peninsula.

Escalating threats from Yemen

Over the past few days, tensions escalated significantly following a series of long-range drone and missile attempts launched from Yemen targeting Saudi Arabia’s western region. These intercepted strikes close to the Holy City raised sharp international alarm and prompted widespread condemnation across the Islamic world regarding the security of Mecca’s sacred sites.

World.title: Saudi Arabia accuses Huthis of ‘red line’ attack on Mecca as rebels face outrage from Muslim world
World.content:
Saudi Arabia said it shot down a Huthi drone near Mecca, Islam’s holiest city, on Tuesday, drawing swift regional condemnation of the Iran-backed Yemeni rebel group.

Turki al-Maliki, spokesperson for the Saudi-led Coalition Forces, accused the group of targeting the city, saying it was the first time in almost a decade that the Huthis had targeted Mecca.

The security of the holy site is “a red line,” he said, adding that the kingdom “will not hesitate to take the necessary and deterrent measures” against the Yemeni group.

The claim was strongly denied by the Huthis, who follow the Zaydi branch of Shiite Islam and also revere Mecca as a sacred city.

The group’s military spokesman, Yahya Saree, said early Wednesday that its targets were Saudi oil facilities and military bases “far removed from the holy places.”

“The fabrications and lies propagated by the criminal Saudi regime regarding targeting Mecca cannot deceive anyone,” Saree said. “There is no threat whatsoever from Yemen to the holy sites.”

Saudi Arabia said it intercepted and destroyed the drone “before it entered” Mecca’s restricted airspace, without specifying how close it was to the city.

The rebel group’s swift advance in Yemen and attacks on neighboring Saudi Arabia in recent weeks have put the kingdom in an increasingly difficult position, facing the prospect of being drawn into a wider conflict as the US-Iran war drags on.

Mecca is the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad. All Muslims worldwide are required, if they are able, to make the pilgrimage to the holy city at least once in their life, with millions making the journey each year.

“This hostile attempt will also remain a black mark in the record of violations by the extremist terrorist Huthi militia, as a deliberate act intended to provoke the feelings of millions of Muslims,” al-Maliki said in a post on X.

A ‘dastardly and heinous’ act

The Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), a 57-member body representing 1.5 billion Muslims, also condemned the incicdent, saying the strikes “violate the sanctity of holy sites and mosques” and “instill fear in innocent civilians.”

The prime minister of Pakistan, which recently signed a joint defense agreement with Saudi Arabia, called it a “dastardly and heinous” act. While Shehbaz Sharif did not mention the Huthis in his statement, he affirmed his country’s support for Saudi Arabia.

The interception comes amid heavy fighting. The Huthis launched ballistic missiles and drones at several Saudi cities earlier this week, including Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif, injuring 13 civilians. On Sunday, they claimed responsibility for an attack on a Saudi military base. And on Wednesday, the Huthis said they attacked a Saudi Aramco facility in Yanbu, a port city on the Red Sea.

In response, Saudi forces launched airstrikes across Huthi-held areas of Yemen last Saturday and this Tuesday, according to the Huthis.

The Huthis have recently stepped up their fighting against Yemen’s Saudi-backed government and have expanded their area of control. Last week, they captured a Red Sea port city in Yemen and an island near an important waterway that has, for months, acted as a backup to the Strait of Hormuz, allowing for the export of Saudi oil and refined products.

Over the weekend, Saudi Arabia suspended oil loadings at Yanbu, its primary Red Sea export terminal, after it came under attack from militant groups within Iraq.

No date has been given for its resumption, Ashley Hikmet, head of crude at Axis Limited, a trading subsidiary of the Onyx Capital Group, told CNN. Satellite tracking indicates no Saudi crude has left the Red Sea ports since Saturday, he said.

On Tuesday, Saudi Arabia also cut supplies to Europe with immediate effect, Hikmet said, adding that Aramco notified some customers that supplies would be halted until mid-November. The supply disruptions to Europe were first reported by Reuters.

CNN has reached out to Aramco for comment.

The Huthis’ tightening grip over shipping in the Red Sea has fueled fears that the main escape valves for the region’s oil are slamming shut, as Iran and the US continue battling for control of the Strait of Hormuz.

Oil prices climbed back above $100 per barrel last week following further US strikes on Iranian oil tankers in the Persian Gulf and the fighting in Yemen, sparking protests around the world as people demand government action and economic relief.

CNN’s Nadeen Ebrahim and Thomas Gould contributed reporting.

World.title: Gaza building collapse kills more than 20, dozens remain trapped under rubble
World.content:
More than 20 people, including several children, have died after a war-damaged residential building in Gaza City collapsed early Wednesday, local authorities said, with dozens more feared trapped under layers of rubble.

Dr. Mohammed Abu Salmiya, the director of al-Shifa hospital, told CNN at least 21 people have been killed in the disaster, including 11 children, and that many others have been injured.

Search and rescue operations are underway at the site of the collapsed al-Sa’ada building in the city’s Rimal neighborhood, where around 100 people are missing, according to Gaza’s Civil Defense agency.

The building, which is six stories high with four apartments on each floor, was targeted by Israeli airstrikes at the beginning of the war in Gaza, the Civil Defense agency said. The Israeli strikes followed the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attack on Israel.
