Mexico City’s archdiocese, Cardinal Carlos Aguiar Retes, announced Sept. 9 that the festivities will be inaugurated Oct. 12 and run through Oct. 12, 2027. The designation marks 50 years since the basilica was founded, and 131 years since the pontifical coronation of the Virgin of Guadalupe by Pope Leo XIII.

According to Catholic media outlet The Tablet, the Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe attracts roughly 20 million visitors annually, making it Catholicism’s most popular Marian shrine. Church doctrine holds that visions of Mary appeared to St. Juan Diego at the site in 1531. Today, it hosts several churches and sanctuaries.

While Jubilee years traditionally take place every 25 years, a sitting pope can call for one in special circumstances. The designation is intended as a time of grace, forgiveness and renewal.

“May Holy Mary of Guadalupe, Mother of the True God for whom we live, help us make fruitful use of this Jubilee and accompany us on this journey of spiritual renewal and conversion,” Aguiar said in a statement.

Hyde Hotels makes its Latin America debut

If you’re visiting the city throughout Jubilee Year and need a place to stay, Hyde just opened its new boutique hotel, mere steps away from the Ángel de la Independencia in Colonia Juárez.

Hyde Mexico City Reforma boasts 106 rooms, some with views of the famed monument, as well as a sushi restaurant dubbed Enzu, and a café-turned-cocktail lounge, Sun & Moon.

According to Hyde Hotels, the brand is all about “that feeling when the right music, people and places come together to create a sense of belonging.” The Ennismore-owned brand leans into “bohemian design and global flavors,” paired with wellness offerings and what it calls a signature “festival spirit.”

Hyde Mexico City Reforma marks the boutique hotel brand’s entry into the Latin American market. In a news release, Ennismore noted that the new location is “Housed within two towers constructed during the era of Mexican modernism, breath(ing) new life into the existing architecture through adaptive reuse that preserves the building’s original facade and infrastructure.”

Ennismore also acquired “Vulcano,” a sculpture by Mexican architect Javier Senosiain, which takes center stage in the hotel’s atrium, while its furniture “echoes the geometry of the city’s urban grid, softened by floral arrangements and natural materials.”

That atmosphere, however, comes at a cost. Rooms start at around 2,930 pesos (US $170) per night, while a “Headliner King Suite With City View” tops out at 7,234 pesos, or roughly US $422. However, the company is currently offering a grand opening deal. Book a room by Sept. 30 for any dates between now and Dec. 28, and you can save up to 25%, plus free breakfast.

Smart Fit to end 2026 with 70 new gyms

Lastly, Brazilian fitness chain Smart Fit said it will wrap up 2026 with a combined 70 new locations across Mexico, totalling 1.5 billion pesos (US $88 million) in investment throughout the country.

The company plans to open an additional 40 outposts through the second half of 2026, culminating in a 20% year-on-year growth. While exact locations haven’t been revealed, some are expected to open in Mexico City, Milenio reported.

According to Mexico Business News, Smart Fit Mexico General Director Darío Coronado said the company is “entering a new phase of acceleration in Mexico that does not respond to short-term trends but is based on data intelligence, automation, real estate efficiency and a deep understanding of the consumer.”

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Smart Fit México (@smartfitmx)

He added, “With this, we reaffirm our confidence in the country to continue investing, generating jobs, and democratizing access to high-quality health and well-being.”

Smart Fit said the real estate development and construction phase will create more than 1,000 jobs, with another 900 direct and indirect positions expected once the facilities are operational.

The company currently operates more than 500 locations across Mexico, serving more than 1.3 million members.

Drew Pittock serves as Mexico News Daily’s features director. He is based in Mexico City. Have an idea for a feature story or unique event in CDMX? Send an email to drew.pittock@mexiconewsdaily.com.

World.title: Taxes in Ghana for Expats 2026: Residency Can Raise Your Rate
World.content:
GHANA · TAXES

Key Facts — The resident scale Residents pay nothing on the first US$514 of income, and up to 35% at the top.

— Where the top starts The 35% band applies above 600,000 cedis a year, about US$52,445.

— The catch Non-residents pay a flat 25%, so residency can raise the rate for a high earner.

— The exempt slice The tax-free band is 5,880 cedis a year, roughly US$514.

— How it compares Morocco reaches its top rate at about US$18,967, well below the Ghanaian threshold.

— What comes next Residents are taxed on worldwide income, with a narrow exemption for work done abroad.

Taxes in ghana for expats turn on one question that most guides get backwards. Residency is not automatically the cheaper status.

Accra. Ghana's 35% top band begins near US$52,445, while non-residents pay a flat 25%. Photo: Synth85, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

Where This Fits

Taxes in ghana for expats are usually presented as a single top rate of 35%. That figure is correct and it hides the decision that matters.

Ghana charges residents on a progressive scale and non-residents at a flat rate. The two systems cross over at a particular income.

Above that crossover point, being resident costs more than not being resident. That is the reverse of the assumption most people arrive with.

This guide sets out both scales, converts the thresholds, and identifies where the crossover sits.

The Resident Scale

The resident scale runs in seven steps. All conversions here use a rate of 11.44 to the dollar published by open.er-api.com on 18 September 2026.

Cedi thresholds move against the dollar, so the equivalents drift. The first 5,880 cedis of chargeable income each year, about US$514, are taxed at nothing.

The next 1,320 cedis, roughly US$115, are taxed at 5%. The next 1,560 cedis, about US$136, are taxed at 10%.

Those three opening steps are narrow. Together they cover the first 8,760 cedis, around US$766 a year.

The next 38,000 cedis, close to US$3,322, are taxed at 17.5%. The next 192,000 cedis, about US$16,783, are taxed at 25%.

The next 366,240 cedis, roughly US$32,012, are taxed at 30%. Income above 600,000 cedis, about US$52,445, is taxed at 35%.

The shape of that scale is worth noting. The low bands are tiny and the upper ones are wide, so most earners land in a single rate.

The General Post Office in Accra. Ghana’s income tax scale has seven bands, more than most of its neighbours. Photo: Treysam, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

Where the Top Rate Actually Starts

The threshold that matters is the last one. The 35% rate applies above 600,000 cedis, about US$52,445, of chargeable income.

That is a high threshold by regional standards. Few foreign employees in Ghana will reach it on salary alone.

Compare it with Morocco, covered separately in this series. There the top band of 37% begins at about US$18,967.

Ghana therefore reaches its top marginal rate at close to three times the Moroccan income level. The headline rates are similar and the practical burden is not.

For a professional salary in the middle of the range, Ghana sits mostly in the 25% band. That is the rate most foreign employees will actually experience.

The Non-Resident Flat Rate

Non-residents are taxed differently and more simply. They pay a flat 25% on their Ghanaian-source income.

There is no progressive relief and no exempt band. The first cedi is taxed at the same rate as the last.

For a low income that is unattractive. A resident earning modestly pays nothing on the first slice and single digits on the next.

For a high income it inverts. A non-resident on a large Ghanaian salary pays 25% throughout, while a resident pays 30% and then 35% on the upper portions.

The crossover is not a single clean number, because the resident scale is cumulative. What is clear is the direction of travel above the 600,000 cedi line.

Salt pans at Weija. The flat non-resident rate can beat the resident scale once income is high enough.

The Residency Question Cuts Both Ways

Residency also changes the scope of what is taxed, not only the rate. Resident individuals are generally taxed on their worldwide income.

Non-residents are taxed only on income sourced in Ghana. For someone with substantial foreign investments, that difference dwarfs the rate question.

One narrow exemption exists for employment income. It applies where a person exercises their employment outside Ghana and is present outside Ghana for more than 183 days.

That is a specific relief rather than a general one. It does not extend to pensions, dividends or business income earned abroad.

So the residency decision has two separate consequences. One is the rate on Ghanaian income, and the other is whether foreign income enters the net at all.

For most arrivals the second consequence is larger. It is also the one least often modelled before the move.

The practical step is to map your income streams before choosing a status. A salary, a portfolio and a pension each behave differently here.

Only after that does the rate table become useful. Applied to the wrong base it produces a confident and wrong answer.

How Ghana Compares in This Series

Set against the other jurisdictions covered here, Ghana sits in the middle. It is not territorial like Costa Rica, Guatemala or the Dominican Republic.

It has no introductory holiday of the kind Chile and Uruguay offer new residents. Residency brings worldwide income into scope immediately.

What it does offer is a high threshold before the top rate applies. That is worth more to a salaried professional than to a retiree living on foreign income.

A retiree with a foreign pension is better served by a territorial system or by Morocco’s pension abatement. Ghana taxes that pension as a resident’s worldwide income.

The country’s tax case is therefore strongest for people earning in Ghana. It is weakest for people earning elsewhere and living there.

What We Could Not Confirm

Three points are left open rather than resolved here.

The first is an arithmetic inconsistency in the published bands. Adding the stated band widths gives a figure slightly above the threshold named for the top rate.

That gap is not reconciled in the source used, and it is left standing here rather than smoothed over. It does not affect any of the conclusions above.

The second is the full statutory test for individual residency, which the rate summary did not carry. The third is the treatment of foreign pensions specifically.

None of those is guessed at. The Ghana Revenue Authority is the authority on all three, and the difference matters most to retirees.

What Taxes in Ghana for Expats Come Down To

The top rate of 35% is real but distant. It begins around US$52,445 of chargeable income, which most salaries do not reach.

The band that matters for a professional is 25%, and that is also the flat rate charged to non-residents. At that level the two systems converge.

Above it they diverge, and not in the direction people expect. Residency starts costing more once income clears the 30% and 35% steps.

The larger question remains scope rather than rate. Residency pulls worldwide income into the Ghanaian base, and there is no holiday and no abatement to soften it.

Read taxes in ghana for expats as a decision about status before a calculation about rates. Work out whether you want to be resident, then look at the scale.

World.title: Taxes in Morocco for Expats 2026: The 37% Band Starts Early
World.content:
MOROCCO · TAXES

Key Facts — Who is taxed Residents are taxed on worldwide income, and non-residents only on Moroccan-source income.

— Where the top rate starts The 37% band begins above 180,000 dirhams a year, about US$18,967.

— The catch That top rate arrives at an income many countries would still treat as modest.

— The pension relief Foreign pensions are reported to carry an 80% abatement, leaving a fifth taxable.

— What triggers residency A permanent home, a centre of economic interests, or 183 days in any 365.

— What comes next The abatement requires the pension to be transferred into a Moroccan bank account.

Taxes in morocco for expats depend almost entirely on where the money comes from. Salary and pension are treated very differently.

Tanger Med. Morocco taxes residents on worldwide income, and its top 37% band starts near US$18,967.

Where This Fits

Taxes in morocco for expats are usually summarised with a single top rate. That summary is accurate and almost useless.

The rate scale matters far less than what kind of income you have. A salary and a pension face very different treatment.

This guide sets out the residency tests, the rate bands with dollar equivalents, and the relief that applies to foreign pensions.

It also marks clearly where the sourcing is thinner than it should be.

One point belongs up front. Morocco is not a territorial system, so residency pulls foreign income into scope unless a relief or a treaty removes it.

That is the opposite of the Central American systems covered elsewhere in this series. The difference matters more than any single rate.

Who Counts as Resident

Morocco applies three alternative tests, and meeting any one of them is enough. The first is having a permanent home in the country.

The second is having your centre of economic interests there. The third is spending 183 days or more in any 365-day period.

The 365-day framing is worth noticing. It is a rolling window rather than a calendar year, so a stay that straddles New Year still counts.

The consequence of residency is broad. Residents are taxed on worldwide income, and non-residents only on income sourced in Morocco.

That makes the residency question the first one to settle. Everything below applies only once the answer is yes.

The permanent home test is the one people underestimate. Keeping a house available for your use in Morocco can satisfy it on its own.

Counting days is therefore not a complete defence. Someone who owns a home there and spends four months a year can still be resident.

The phosphate works at Khouribga. Morocco taxes residents on worldwide income once any residency test is met.

The Rate Scale, and Where It Bites

The individual scale is progressive and short. Annual taxable income up to 40,000 dirhams is exempt, which is about US$4,215.

All conversions here use a rate of 9.49 to the dollar published by open.er-api.com on 18 September 2026. Dirham thresholds move against the dollar, so the equivalents drift.

From 40,001 to 60,000 dirhams the rate is 10%. That upper limit is roughly US$6,322.

From 60,001 to 80,000 dirhams the rate is 20%, with the band ending near US$8,430. From 80,001 to 100,000 it is 30%, ending around US$10,537.

From 100,001 to 180,000 dirhams the rate is 34%. Above 180,000 dirhams the rate is 37%.

That top threshold is about US$18,967 of annual taxable income. A professional salary in most Western countries clears it several times over.

This is the structural point of the whole guide. Morocco is not a low-tax country for income earned inside it.

The bands are also narrow. Only 140,000 dirhams separate the exempt threshold from the top rate, about US$14,750.

A salary rising through that range hits successive rates quickly. There is little of the long middle band that flattens the curve elsewhere.

A Moroccan smallholding. Locally earned income runs into the top band far sooner than most arrivals expect.

The Foreign Pension Abatement

The picture changes for retirees. Foreign-source pensions received by Moroccan tax residents are reported to benefit from an 80% abatement.

In practice that means only a fifth of the pension enters the rate scale above. The other four fifths are disregarded.

The effect is large. A pension taxed on its full value would face a mid-band rate.

Taxed on a fifth, the same pension sits near the bottom of the scale. The saving is the difference between those two positions.

Three conditions are described. The recipient must be a Moroccan tax resident and the pension must come from a foreign source.

The third is mechanical. The funds have to be transferred into a Moroccan bank account.

The transfer condition is not a formality. The relief rests on demonstrating that the money genuinely arrived in the country.

This is also the part of this guide with the weakest sourcing, and that is said plainly below.

The relief is described as permanent for as long as tax residency continues. It is not a time-limited window of the kind Chile and Uruguay operate.

That distinction matters for a long retirement. A permanent abatement and an eleven-year holiday look similar at first and diverge sharply after a decade.

The Treaty Layer

Morocco has an extensive network of bilateral tax treaties, several of them long-standing. They determine which country gets the first claim on a given stream of income.

Agreements are in place with France, the United Kingdom, the United States, Germany, Spain, Belgium, Italy and the Netherlands. Several date from the 1970s and 1980s.

For a pensioner the treaty usually decides whether the pension is taxable in Morocco at all. Public-sector pensions are frequently treated differently from private ones.

That distinction cannot be resolved in a general guide. It turns on the wording of the specific treaty and the specific pension.

The age of several treaties is itself worth noting. An agreement signed in the 1970s was not drafted with remote work or modern portfolios in mind.

Where a treaty is silent, domestic law fills the gap. That is another reason the residency tests above carry so much weight.

What We Could Not Confirm

Three points are left open rather than presented as settled.

The first is the statutory provision that establishes the 80% pension abatement. The source describing it did not cite the article number, and the figure should be confirmed with a Moroccan adviser.

The second is whether the abatement is capped above a certain pension size. The third is the withholding rates on dividends and interest, which the rate table consulted did not carry.

None of those is estimated here. The tax administration and the applicable treaty are the authorities on all three.

What Taxes in Morocco for Expats Come Down To

Two different countries exist inside one tax code. For income earned locally, Morocco is demanding by any standard.

The 37% band starting near US$18,967 is the number that defines that half. Anyone taking a Moroccan salary or running a Moroccan business should plan around it.

For a foreign pension the arithmetic inverts. An 80% abatement moves a retirement income from the upper bands into the lower ones.

That is why Morocco appears on retirement shortlists and rarely on relocation shortlists for working professionals. The code rewards one and not the other.

Read taxes in morocco for expats as a question about the source of your income. Confirm the pension relief in writing before it becomes the reason for the move.

World.title: São Paulo Nightlife Tonight: Verdi at the Municipal, Alsop at Sala São Paulo, September 18, 2026
World.content:

One email, every weekday morning. What moved in Latin American markets, politics and expat life.

São Paulo · Nightlife

If You Only Go to One Place Don Carlo Opens at the Theatro Municipal Verdi’s opera returns to the house for the first time in twenty-one years, on its 115th anniversary. Roberto Minczuk conducts at 7 p.m., with Paulo Szot and Ailyn Pérez in the cast. Seats run from 47 to 290 reais, about 9 to 56 dollars.

Tonight at a Glance — Opera at 7 p.m. Don Carlo opens at the Theatro Municipal, 47 to 290 reais or about 9 to 56 dollars.

— Marin Alsop at 8 p.m. The Osesp plays Bernstein, Mahler and Villa-Lobos at Sala São Paulo, 50 to 100 reais.

— Two sets at Blue Note Maria Alcina at 8 p.m., then a Gipsy Kings tribute at 10.30 p.m., both still open.

— Free from 6 p.m. MASP on Avenida Paulista stays open until nine, with free entry for the last three hours.

— Four rooms in the centre Casa de Francisca runs a free DJ set at 7 p.m. and three ticketed shows after ten.

— Weather Cool and mostly dry, between 14 and 22 degrees, with a jacket needed for the late set.

— Tomorrow is tighter The Blue Note Sade tribute is down to its last tickets, and the Oktoberfest opens at Ibirapuera.

Tonight, Friday 18 September 2026, São Paulo runs an unusually classical evening. An opera premiere and a birthday concert sit within a mile of each other, and all times below are São Paulo time.

What’s On Tonight in the Old Centre

The Theatro Municipal opens its run of Verdi’s Don Carlo at 7 p.m. It is the first staging in the house for twenty-one years and marks the theatre’s 115th anniversary.

Roberto Minczuk conducts the Orquestra Sinfônica Municipal, with Caetano Vilela directing and lighting. Tonight’s cast has Atalla Ayan in the title role, Ailyn Pérez as Elisabetta and Paulo Szot as Posa.

Seats run from 47 to 290 reais, about 9 to 56 dollars. The run continues on 19, 20, 22, 23, 25 and 26 September.

A few blocks away, Casa de Francisca opens four spaces. A free DJ set with Zinco starts in the Largo at 7 p.m., before three ticketed shows after ten.

Bernardo Lobo sings his father Edu Lobo and his grandfather Fernando Lobo in the Salão at 10 p.m. Luca Frazão launches his first solo album in Sala B at the same hour, and a party fills the Porão from eleven.

Marin Alsop’s Birthday Concert at Sala São Paulo

The Osesp plays Histórias de Amor at Sala São Paulo at 8 p.m., conducted by Marin Alsop. The programme marks her seventieth birthday.

It runs from Bernstein’s Candide overture and West Side Story through Mahler’s fifth symphony. Prokofiev’s Romeo and Juliet and Villa-Lobos’s Choros No. 10 complete the bill, with the Osesp choirs and the narrator Joyce Ribeiro.

Tickets are 50 to 100 reais, roughly 10 to 19 dollars. The concert repeats tomorrow at half past four in the afternoon.

Sala São Paulo sits inside the old Júlio Prestes railway station in Campos Elísios. Luz station on the metro and the rail network is the closest stop.

Jazz on Paulista

Blue Note São Paulo lists two separate ticketed shows tonight. Maria Alcina sings at 8 p.m. in a set the club bills as A Turma da Tijuca.

Her repertoire is Roberto Carlos, Erasmo Carlos, Tim Maia and Jorge Ben Jor. Those songwriters met around the Rio district of Tijuca in the late 1950s, and the set is built around Fio Maravilha.

A Gipsy Kings tribute with Flavio Rodrigues follows at 10.30 p.m. The club’s own page displays the title as Gibpsy Experience, and spells it three different ways across the same listing.

Neither set carried a sell-out label when we checked today. Several other September dates do.

The two sets are not one long evening. The club clears the room within fifteen minutes of the first session, and the second needs a new ticket and a new queue.

Where the Prices Actually Live

The club publishes no prices on its programme index, and none on the individual show pages either. The figure appears only once you reach Eventim through the Comprar button.

That is worth knowing before you plan around a budget. There is no way to compare the two sets on the club’s own site.

The box office is not one desk but four. A ground-floor desk runs from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday to Saturday, and a second-floor desk runs 7 p.m. to 11 p.m. from Wednesday to Saturday on show days only.

Sundays are 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. on the second floor, and Tuesdays 7 p.m. to half past eight on show days. The box office number is (11) 93000-4555.

Tables are allocated by arrival order rather than at booking. Some are held back for the club’s members, press and band guests, so early still beats late.

Forró, Rock and the Rest of the Night

Canto da Ema in Pinheiros has Janayna Pereira tonight at 10 p.m. She fronted Bicho do Pé and now tours her solo record, and forró is a couples dance from Brazil’s northeast.

The venue itself did not list the date. Its published agenda shows only a New Year event, so telephone (11) 2503-2915 before crossing the city.

At Espaço Unimed in Barra Funda, Marcelo Falcão plays the last São Paulo date of his Legado tour. Doors are at half past eight and the show at half past ten, for over-18s, and Eventim marks it as last tickets.

Nação Zumbi perform Afrociberdelia in full at Audio in Água Branca, thirty years after the record. Doors open at 8 p.m. and entry starts at 80 reais, about 16 dollars, for over-18s.

5 Seconds of Summer play the Suhai Music Hall at 9 p.m., from 520 reais or roughly 101 dollars. The Japanese band toe play Cine Joia in Liberdade, an extra date added after last night sold out, and both nights are now gone.

Vintage Culture runs Komplexo Tempo from 10 p.m. until ten tomorrow morning, for over-18s. Leci Brandão’s fiftieth-anniversary show at Sesc Belenzinho at 8 p.m. is sold out.

Free, and Free After Six

MASP opens until 9 p.m. on Fridays and is free from six, under its sponsored Free Friday scheme. Full entry the rest of the day is 85 reais, about 17 dollars, and online booking is required even when entry is free.

The museum is showing Damián Ortega, Carolina Caycedo and its Latin American histories survey. It is the single best free hour in the city on a Friday evening.

The Centro Cultural São Paulo screens Hitchcock’s Rear Window in its hanging garden at 7 p.m., free, with sign language and audio description. Tickets are handed out an hour before.

DJ Zinco’s set in the Largo at Casa de Francisca is free from 7 p.m. Two more free shows run at the Vila Itororó cultural centre and at Alvenaria in Perdizes, both from 7 p.m.

What the Weather Will Do to Your Evening

The city’s own forecasting centre puts today between 14 and 21 degrees Celsius, cloudy through the day with little storm potential. The state government’s forecast is a degree warmer at the top and calls it settled.

Both agree on the useful part, which is that it stays dry. Morning fog is possible in the centre and east, and humidity drops sharply in the afternoon.

Take a jacket if you are staying for the 10.30 p.m. set. Fourteen degrees on Avenida Paulista after midnight is colder than the number suggests.

The Rest of the Weekend

Blue Note marks tomorrow as down to its last tickets. A Sade tribute plays two sets, at 8 p.m. and half past ten.

The São Paulo Oktoberfest opens tomorrow at the Ibirapuera events arena and runs to 4 October. Several listings still give today as the opening date, but the official calendar starts on the 19th.

There is football in the city tomorrow night. São Paulo host Internacional at the Morumbis at 9 p.m., and Corinthians play Fluminense on Sunday afternoon.

The SP Open reaches its semi-finals tomorrow from 1 p.m. at Parque Villa-Lobos, with the final on Sunday from three. Cirque du Soleil is in the same park, which makes traffic there worse than usual.

Where to Go

Theatro Municipal — Centro The city’s 1911 opera house on Praça Ramos de Azevedo, celebrating its 115th anniversary this year. Tonight it opens Verdi’s Don Carlo for the first time since 2005. Tonight Don Carlo at 7 p.m., conducted by Roberto Minczuk.

Cast Atalla Ayan, Ailyn Pérez, Luiz-Ottavio Faria, Ana Lucia Benedetti and Paulo Szot.

Entry 47 to 290 reais, about 9 to 56 dollars.

Run Also 19, 20, 22, 23, 25 and 26 September.

Address Praça Ramos de Azevedo, Centro. Anhangabaú station is nearest.

Sala São Paulo — Campos Elísios The concert hall built inside the old Júlio Prestes railway station, home to the state symphony orchestra. Tonight it marks Marin Alsop’s seventieth birthday. Tonight Osesp and Marin Alsop, Histórias de Amor, 8 p.m.

Programme Bernstein, Mahler’s fifth, Prokofiev and Villa-Lobos, with the Osesp choirs.

Entry 50 to 100 reais, roughly 10 to 19 dollars.

Repeat Tomorrow at half past four in the afternoon.

Address Praça Júlio Prestes 16, Campos Elísios. Luz station is nearest.

Blue Note São Paulo — Paulista The São Paulo branch of the New York jazz club, open since February 2019 and now running a second room as well. The audience sits at tables on the second floor of the Conjunto Nacional. Tonight Maria Alcina at 8 p.m., then a Gipsy Kings tribute at 10.30 p.m.

Status No sell-out label on either set, checked on 18 September.

Box office Ground floor 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday to Saturday; second floor 7 p.m. to 11 p.m. Wednesday to Saturday on show days.

Prices Not published by the club at all. They appear only on Eventim.

Between sets The room clears within fifteen minutes, and the second session needs a new ticket.

Address Avenida Paulista 2073, second floor, Consolação. Consolação station is nearest.

Casa de Francisca — Centro A four-room music house near the Theatro Municipal, running a free set in the Largo and ticketed shows inside. Tonight it fills all four spaces. Free at 7 p.m. DJ Zinco in the Largo, a funk and soul selector.

At 10 p.m. Bernardo Lobo in the Salão and Luca Frazão in Sala B, both seated.

From 11 p.m. Festa Brasix with DJ Zé Pedro in the Porão, standing.

Tomorrow The first floor is closed all day for a private event.

Address Avenida São João 93, Centro. São Bento station is nearest.

Money and How Paying Works

Any dollar figure here uses 5.1521 reais to one US dollar. That is the closing sell rate the Banco Central published for Thursday 17 September, the last business day before today.

Take tonight’s Blue Note price from Eventim rather than from the club’s own pages, which carry none. Food and drink are billed separately from the ticket.

Restaurants usually add a service charge of about 10 per cent, called serviço. Brazilian law makes it optional, and staff remove it if you ask.

The free events tonight are genuinely free and need no ticket, except the cinema screening, which hands out passes an hour before. MASP still requires an online booking even for its free evening hours.

Getting Home Safe

The 7 and 8 p.m. shows finish inside normal metro hours. The 10.30 p.m. set at Blue Note and the later gigs will not, so plan a car if you take one.

Check the last train for your own line on the Metrô or ViaQuatro sites. Closing times differ by line and by night.

Avenida Paulista stays busy and well lit late into the night. Wait for a rideshare on the avenue rather than on a side street.

The centre around the Theatro Municipal empties faster after an opera than Paulista does after a gig. Book a car before you leave the foyer rather than on the pavement.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is on at the Theatro Municipal tonight?

Verdi’s Don Carlo opens at 7 p.m., conducted by Roberto Minczuk, with Paulo Szot and Ailyn Pérez in the cast. It is the first staging in the house for twenty-one years and seats run from 47 to 290 reais, about 9 to 56 dollars.

What is on at Blue Note tonight?

Two separate shows. Maria Alcina sings A Turma da Tijuca at 8 p.m., and a Gipsy Kings tribute with Flavio Rodrigues follows at 10.30 p.m.

How much are Blue Note tickets?

The club does not publish prices on its programme index or on its individual show pages. The figure appears only on Eventim, reached through the Comprar button.

Is MASP free tonight?

Yes, from 6 p.m. until 9 p.m. under its sponsored Free Friday scheme. Online booking is required even on free days, and full entry earlier in the day is 85 reais or about 17 dollars.

What is free in São Paulo tonight?

MASP from six, a DJ set in the Largo at Casa de Francisca from seven, Hitchcock’s Rear Window in the hanging garden at the Centro Cultural São Paulo at seven, and two free concerts at Vila Itororó and Alvenaria.

Is there football in São Paulo tonight?

No. São Paulo host Internacional at the Morumbis tomorrow at 9 p.m., and Corinthians play Fluminense on Sunday afternoon.

When does the São Paulo Oktoberfest start?

Tomorrow, Saturday 19 September, at the Ibirapuera events arena, running to 4 October. Several listings still give today’s date, but the official calendar starts on the 19th.

World.title: Kenya Residency Visa Requirements 2026: Class K Starts at 35
World.content:
KENYA · VISA

Key Facts — The retirement route Class K requires an assured annual income of at least US$24,000 from a pension or annuity.

— The age bar Applicants for the Class K permit must be not less than thirty-five years old.

— The catch The annual issuance fee is about US$1,930, roughly eight percent of the required income.

— The remote-work route Class N covers people living in Kenya and working for foreign-registered companies.

— What Class N costs It takes US$200 to apply and US$1,000 a year to hold, renewable annually.

— What comes next East African Community citizens pay nothing for these permits.

Kenya residency visa requirements are unusually explicit. The figures are published, and two of them are higher than most people expect.

Nairobi. The ordinary resident permit asks for an assured US$24,000 a year and a minimum age of thirty-five. Photo: This Photo was taken by Timothy A. Gonsalves. Feel free to use my photos, but please menti, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

Where This Fits

Kenya residency visa requirements are easier to research than most in the region. The immigration directorate publishes the classes, the thresholds and the fees.

That transparency is the useful part. It also means the numbers are harder to talk around than in countries where the rules are discretionary.

Four routes matter for most foreigners moving to Kenya. They are Class K, Class N, Class G and the special pass.

This guide sets out what each requires, what each costs and where the awkward details sit.

Class K: The Ordinary Resident Permit

Class K is the permit for people living in Kenya on a fixed income. It is the closest thing the country has to a retirement route.

Two conditions define it. An applicant must be not less than thirty-five years of age.

They must also have an assured annual income of not less than US$24,000. That income has to come from a pension or an annuity.

The wording on source matters. The published requirement covers income derived from sources outside Kenya and remitted into the country, or derived from a pension or annuity.

The documents are conventional. Form 25 and a cover letter to the Director General open the file.

A recent colour passport photograph and the passport bio-data pages follow. So do current immigration status documents.

The document that decides the application is the proof of assured income. Everything else is administrative.

Applications are submitted through the electronic Foreign Nationals Services portal rather than over a counter.

Nairobi. Permit applications are filed through the immigration directorate’s online portal rather than in person. Photo: Matti Blume, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

What Class K Costs

The processing fee is 20,000 Kenyan shillings and is non-refundable. That is about US$154.

All conversions here use a rate of 129.53 to the dollar published by open.er-api.com on 18 September 2026. Shilling fees move against the dollar, so the equivalents drift.

The issuance fee is 250,000 shillings per year, roughly US$1,930. That is the figure most applicants underestimate.

Set it against the income requirement and the proportion becomes clear. The annual fee is about eight percent of the US$24,000 the applicant must prove.

For a retiree on exactly the minimum, the permit is a meaningful line in the budget. It is charged every year rather than once.

That recurring structure is the part worth planning around. A one-off cost can be absorbed, and an annual one has to be funded.

It also changes how the two routes compare. Over five years the difference between Class K and Class N runs into thousands of dollars.

Class N: The Remote Work Permit

Kenya created a formal route for remote workers, which few countries in the region have done. Class N covers people residing in Kenya while working for foreign-registered companies.

It came into force on 16 December 2024 under Legal Notice 198 of 2024. Applications opened in April 2025.

The application fee is US$200 and is non-refundable. The issuance fee is US$1,000 a year.

The permit runs for one year and is renewable. Payment is made by card or mobile money through the same online portal.

Compared with Class K the arithmetic is different. There is no age bar and no pension requirement, and the annual cost is roughly half.

The trade is what the permit assumes about your work. Class N presumes an employer or client registered outside Kenya.

Someone earning from Kenyan clients does not fit it. That case belongs under Class G, with its heavier conditions.

Class G: Trade, Business and Consultancy

Class G covers a specific trade, business, consultancy or profession. It is the route for someone setting up or buying into a Kenyan company.

The capital requirement is US$100,000, and documentary proof is required. That is the same headline threshold Guatemala applies to its investor route.

The processing fee is about US$155 and the issuance fee about US$1,930 a year. Those figures match the Class K structure closely.

The paperwork is heavier than for the other classes. Kenyan company registration, an incorporation certificate, a tax PIN certificate and a shareholders certificate are all required.

This is a business permit rather than a residence-by-investment scheme. The company has to exist and operate, not merely hold an asset.

Nairobi National Park against the city skyline. Kenya publishes its permit thresholds in full, which is unusual in the region. Photo: This Photo was taken by Timothy A. Gonsalves. Feel free to use my photos, but please menti, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

The Special Pass and the Community Exemption

A special pass covers temporary business, trade or professional activity. It runs for a maximum of six months.

The fee is US$200 a month for non-citizens of the East African Community. An organisation stamp or sponsorship is mandatory.

That monthly rate makes it expensive as a bridge. Six months at US$200 costs more than a year of Class N.

The East African Community exemption is the largest single discount in the system. Citizens of member states pay nothing for these permits.

For everyone else the fees are uniform and published. There is no negotiated rate and no discretionary reduction documented here.

That uniformity is worth something when planning. A published fee cannot quietly become a different fee at the counter.

What We Could Not Confirm

Three points are left open because the sources used did not settle them.

The first is the stated validity period of the Class K permit. The official page sets an annual issuance fee without naming a term.

The second is the renewal procedure for Class K, which is not described alongside the initial requirements. The third is whether the assured income test is applied gross or net of tax.

None of those is guessed at here. The immigration directorate is the authority on all three, and the portal is where a current answer can be obtained.

What Kenya Residency Visa Requirements Come Down To

Kenya sets out its terms plainly, and the terms are not cheap. That combination is rarer than it should be.

For a retiree, the binding constraints are the age of thirty-five and the assured US$24,000 a year. The annual fee of about US$1,930 then takes a real bite out of that income.

For a remote worker, Class N is the better-designed option. It costs half as much annually, carries no age bar and was written for exactly this case.

For anyone building a business, Class G asks US$100,000 and a functioning Kenyan company. It is a work permit with an investment condition attached.

Read kenya residency visa requirements as a published price list. The advantage is that you can plan against it, and the disadvantage is that you cannot argue with it.

World.title: Morocco Residency Visa Requirements 2026: The Ninety-Day Line
World.content:
MOROCCO · VISA

Key Facts — When it applies A residence permit becomes compulsory once a stay passes 90 days in the country.

— What it is called The document is the certificat or carte d’immatriculation, issued through the police.

— The catch The law has no category written for retirees or investors, so both apply as visitors.

— What you must show A home-country criminal record, a medical certificate and documented means of support.

— Where you apply The Bureau des Etrangers at a police prefecture, or the Gendarmerie in rural areas.

— What comes next The permit lapses after six months of absence, whatever validity it carries.

Morocco residency visa requirements begin with a date rather than a form. Ninety days is the line.

The parliament in Rabat. Residence in Morocco runs on Law 02-03, which grants categories at the administration's discretion. Photo: "Parlement Rabat" by Taha ahh, via Wikimedia Commons, CC0.

Where This Fits

Morocco residency visa requirements are less about a visa than about a deadline. Most Western nationals do not need a visa to arrive at all.

What they need is a residence permit once the stay gets long. The rules around that permit are specific, and some of them are not obvious.

This guide covers the permit itself. When it is required, what it is called, what documents it takes and how long it lasts.

It also covers two points that catch people out, which are the missing categories and the bank account decision.

The Ninety-Day Line

Nationals of most Western countries enter Morocco without a visa. The permitted stay is 90 days.

The limit is framed as a maximum within a six-month window. A tourist stay cannot exceed three consecutive months in any six-month period.

Once a stay passes that line, a residence permit stops being optional. It is required rather than advisable.

That is the practical trigger for everything below. Anyone planning to stay longer should start the file before the ninety days run out, not after.

What the Permit Is and Where You Get It

The document is a certificate of registration, the certificat or carte d’immatriculation. It is handled by the police rather than by a consulate.

In urban areas the application goes to the Bureau des Etrangers at the local police prefecture or central police station. In rural areas it goes to the Gendarmerie.

The office is the one local to where you actually live. That is why a lease or an equivalent proof of address has to come first.

Applications are made in person. You receive an interim receipt, the recepisse, on the day.

The card itself follows weeks later. The cost is modest and paid locally.

Casablanca. Most residence files are opened at a police prefecture in the city where the applicant lives. Photo: Milamber's portfolio, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

The Documents

The list is consistent across sources and it is longer than most people expect. A legalised copy of the passport is the starting point.

Eight photographs are required, taken within the previous three months. Proof of address follows, which can be a lease, a utility bill or a hosting attestation.

A medical certificate is required, confirming the absence of contagious disease. So is a criminal record extract from the country of origin.

Proof of financial means is required in every category but one. A bank attestation showing the balance of a local Moroccan account is the usual form.

Documents are generally submitted as notarised copies. Two notarised copies of each is the standard expectation.

The only documented exception on means is for applicants aged sixteen to eighteen declaring an intention to settle. Everyone else shows money.

The Categories, and What Is Missing

Morocco’s framework for foreigners is Law 02-03. It sets out discretionary mentions rather than entitlements.

The mentions named in that law are visitor, student, work, family regrouping and long-term medical treatment. Each is granted at the administration’s discretion.

There is no statutory mention for a retiree, and none for an investor. That is the single most consequential fact in this guide.

A retired person moving to Morocco does not apply under a retirement route, because there is not one. They apply as a visitor and satisfy the means test.

An investor is in the same position. Capital brought into the country does not create a residence category of its own.

Sources differ on the total number of categories in current practice. One official page refers to eight, while the statute names five, and that discrepancy is not resolved here.

Validity, Renewal and Absence

The permit is issued for a period between one and ten years. It is renewable for the same period it was granted.

The range is wide because the term is discretionary. A first permit is commonly short, and longer terms follow a record of renewals.

Renewal requires a Moroccan criminal record certificate, the casier judiciaire. It is obtained from the Ministry of Justice in Rabat with birth and passport copies.

One rule overrides the stated validity. The permit lapses after six months of absence from the country.

That matters for anyone intending to split the year between two countries. A ten-year card does not survive a seven-month trip.

Rabat. Renewal files require a Moroccan criminal record certificate obtained from the justice ministry in the capital. Photo: "Honor guard at Mausoleum of Mohammed V, Rabat, Morocco" by Petar Milošević This photograph was taken with a Panasonic Lumix DMC-G85/G80, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.

The Bank Account Decision

This is the part that is irreversible, and it is rarely explained before arrival. Moroccan bank accounts come in convertible and ordinary forms.

A convertible dirham account is funded by selling foreign currency, by transfer from another convertible account, or by investment deposits. Money in it can be converted and sent out again.

Money that enters as ordinary dirhams never becomes convertible. That status is fixed at the moment of deposit.

So funds must arrive through banking channels as foreign currency to keep the option of leaving later. Cash converted at a bureau and then deposited does not qualify.

One day you may sell a property or wind down and leave. This single mechanical detail decides whether the proceeds can follow you.

What We Could Not Confirm

Three points are left open because the sources used did not settle them.

The first is the exact fee schedule for the permit. It is described as modest and paid locally, without a published figure.

The second is the number of categories in current administrative practice, where an official page and the statute do not agree. The third is the penalty for failing to register after ninety days.

None of those is guessed at here. The prefecture handling your file is the authority on all three.

What Morocco Residency Visa Requirements Come Down To

Entry is easy and staying is procedural. The ninety-day line is the moment the process becomes compulsory.

The documents are conventional except for their volume and the notarisation. Building the file takes longer than submitting it.

The two traps are structural rather than bureaucratic. There is no retiree or investor category, and the bank account status cannot be changed later.

Tax residency is a separate question with its own tests. They are a permanent home, a centre of economic interests, or 183 days in any 365-day period.

Residents are taxed on worldwide income, and non-residents only on Moroccan-sourced income. The residence permit and the tax test are not the same thing.

Read morocco residency visa requirements as a deadline, a document list and one irreversible banking choice. The first two are work, and the third is the one to get right before arriving.

Get the brief

One email, every weekday morning. What moved in Latin American markets, politics and expat life.

Rio de Janeiro · Nightlife

If You Only Go to One Place Fafá de Belém Under the Arches, Free She opens the fourth Amir Haddad theatre festival at the Arcos da Lapa at 10 p.m. with her Guitarradas do Pará show. Entry is free, the bill starts at 7 p.m., and the forecast has the rain gone by then.

Tonight at a Glance — Free at 10 p.m. Fafá de Belém with guest Manoel Cordeiro at the Arcos da Lapa, Praça Cardeal Câmara.

— Free at 8 p.m. Mart’nália opens the Próxima Parada Samba season at the Palácio Capanema, Rua da Imprensa 16.

— Angra at Vivo Rio Doors 7 p.m., show 9 p.m., R$150 full or R$75 half, about US$29 and US$15.

— Samba in Lapa Dani Coimbra at Carioca da Gema, R$35 or about US$7, with two sets on a Friday.

— A silent film with a live score Quarteto Kalimera play Nosferatu at the Sala Cecília Meireles, 7 p.m., R$40 or about US$8.

— Weather Between 17 and 25 degrees, showers in the afternoon and a dry, cloudy evening.

— No football Flamengo went through last night, so the Maracanã is dark and Lapa has the city to itself.

Tonight, Friday 18 September 2026, Rio runs one of its fullest free programmes of the year. The Semana de Arte and a new theatre festival overlap, and all times below are Rio time, four hours behind London.

What’s On Tonight in Lapa

Fafá de Belém opens the fourth Festival de Teatro Amir Haddad under the Arcos da Lapa at 10 p.m. She brings her Guitarradas do Pará show, with the guitarist Manoel Cordeiro as guest, and entry is free.

The bill under the arches starts earlier than that. Baque Mulher, Bárbara Vento with Carimbaby and the Festa Xêpa fill the stage from 7 p.m. onwards.

Rio de Janeiro Nightlife Tonight — Friday, September 18, 2026 Photo: Carlos Lucio, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

A few hundred metres away, the Circo Voador has Samba do Sacramento with Hugo Ojuara from 8 p.m. Tickets run from R$60 at half price, roughly US$12, through Eventim.

The Sala Cecília Meireles takes the other direction entirely. Quarteto Kalimera play a live score to Murnau’s Nosferatu at 7 p.m., for R$40 or about US$8.

That programme also ran last night, which is unusual for the hall. Tonight is the second and final showing.

Samba at Carioca da Gema

Carioca da Gema on Avenida Mem de Sá has Dani Coimbra tonight. The house describes her as a singer, actor and dancer whose repertoire runs from samba to jazz, pop and xote.

She is one of the voices of Empolga às 9, a Rio street carnival bloco. A bloco is a neighbourhood carnival group that parades through the streets rather than the Sambadrome.

Entry is R$35, about US$7, the Friday and Saturday rate. Tuesday to Thursday costs R$30, roughly US$6, and holiday eves are charged at the Friday rate.

Tickets go through Zig, linked from the venue’s own listing. The Zig page itself shows no price, so that R$35, about US$7, comes from the house information rather than the seller.

The Start Time Needs Checking

The venue publishes two different Friday timings on the same page. Its entry for tonight gives 7.30 p.m., while its standing Friday block gives doors at 6.30 p.m. and a main show at 9.30 p.m.

Neither figure carries a correction, so we report both rather than choose. The gap between the two published start times is two hours.

The published door is 6.30 p.m., which makes 7.30 p.m. a time half an hour into the happy-hour set. Arrive at 7 p.m. for the early show or 9.30 p.m. for the main one.

Telephone (21) 98556-0834 if the exact hour matters. Tables reserved in advance are held until 9 p.m.

This is not carelessness peculiar to one bar. Small Rio houses run their websites alongside the kitchen, and a fixed weekly block rarely matches a per-event field.

Free Music Across the Centre

Mart’nália sings at the Palácio Gustavo Capanema at 8 p.m., on Rua da Imprensa 16 in the Centro. Entry is free with no ticket, subject to capacity, and a vinyl set follows at 10 p.m.

The concert opens Próxima Parada Samba, an occupation of the building built around a tribute to Beth Carvalho. It is the strongest free bill of the Semana de Arte so far.

At Praça XV, the Festival Sotaque Carregado runs a fair from 5 p.m. until half past eleven. Orquestra Voadora play at half past six and BNegão at half past seven, with a samba circle at half past eight.

The XXI RioHarpFestival gives two free concerts today. A naval wind sextet with the harpist Giovana Sanches plays the Espaço Cultural da Marinha at half past twelve. The Camerata do Uerê follows at the Palácio Tiradentes at 6 p.m.

Several smaller rooms are also free. Fausto Fawcett is at the Teatro Glauce Rocha at 7 p.m. and Amanda Magalhães at Arte SESC Flamengo at the same hour.

Angra, Theatre and the Rest of the Ticketed Night

Angra play Vivo Rio tonight, performing Holy Land in full for the album’s thirtieth anniversary. Doors open at 7 p.m. and the show starts at 9 p.m., with Throw Me To The Wolves supporting.

Tickets are R$150 full and R$75 half, about US$29 and US$15, and the show is for over-18s. The venue sits at Avenida Infante Dom Henrique 85 in the Parque do Flamengo.

Thaís Fraga’s trio marks more than thirty years of bossa and jazz at the Vinicius Show in Ipanema, at 8 p.m. Entry is R$120 full and R$60 half, roughly US$23 and US$12.

At the Teatro João Caetano on Praça Tiradentes, the musical O Neguinho da Beija-Flor plays at 7 p.m. Stalls are R$80 full and R$40 half, about US$16 and US$8.

Rio Gastronomia runs at the Jockey Club in Gávea from 6 p.m. until midnight, from R$80 or roughly US$16. ArtRio is open at the Marina da Glória until 9 p.m., at R$100 full or about US$19.

What the Weather Will Do to Your Evening

Today runs between 17 and 25 degrees Celsius, with showers in the afternoon and a 56 per cent chance of rain. Forecasters put the total at under two millimetres.

The useful part for a night out is what happens after dark. The forecast has cloud but no rain overnight, which matters for the free outdoor bills under the Arcos and at Praça XV.

Sunset falls at 5.48 in the afternoon. That leaves a long evening and a mild one by Rio standards for September.

The Rest of the Weekend

Andrezão do Cacique plays Carioca da Gema tomorrow, with doors at 8.30 p.m. and the main show at 10 p.m. Entry is R$35 again, about US$7, and the house then closes on Sunday and Monday.

The MIMO Festival takes over the Circo Voador tomorrow and Sunday, free both nights. Saturday starts at 8 p.m. and Sunday at 6 p.m., with Tiken Jah Fakoly, Fernanda Abreu, Capicua with Emicida and Tinariwen among the names.

MIMO also shows fourteen free films at the Cine Santa Teresa across the two days, from 4 p.m. Entry is first come, subject to capacity.

The Semana de Arte do Rio has been running since 16 September and continues until the 27th. The Centro Cultural Lavradio at Rua do Lavradio 15 is free from Wednesday to Sunday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.

That building is a five-minute walk from Carioca da Gema. It is the easiest way to see the festival’s daytime side before the evening starts.

Where to Go

Arcos da Lapa — Praça Cardeal Câmara The eighteenth-century aqueduct that gives Lapa its outline, used as an open-air stage. Tonight it opens the fourth Amir Haddad theatre festival. Tonight Fafá de Belém with Manoel Cordeiro at 10 p.m.; the bill starts at 7 p.m.

Entry Free, no ticket.

Also on Baque Mulher, Bárbara Vento with Carimbaby and Festa Xêpa from 7 p.m.

Festival Fourth Festival de Teatro Amir Haddad, running 18 to 25 September.

Address Praça Cardeal Câmara, Lapa. Metro Cinelândia, then a short walk.

Carioca da Gema — Lapa A two-storey samba house on Avenida Mem de Sá, open since 2000. The room is small and the tables sit close to the stage. Tonight Dani Coimbra. The event entry gives 7.30 p.m.

Friday block Doors 6.30 p.m., happy-hour set 7 p.m., main show 9.30 p.m.

Entry R$35, about US$7, Friday and Saturday; R$30, roughly US$6, Tuesday to Thursday.

Tables Held for reservations until 9 p.m., then released.

Tickets Through Zig, linked from the venue’s own event page. Zig does not show the price.

Address Avenida Mem de Sá 79, Centro. Metro Cinelândia, then a short walk.

Vivo Rio — Parque do Flamengo A 4,000-capacity hall inside the Modern Art Museum complex, facing Guanabara Bay. Tonight it hosts a thirtieth-anniversary metal show. Tonight Angra performing Holy Land. Doors 7 p.m., show 9 p.m.

Entry R$150 full, R$75 half, about US$29 and US$15.

Support Throw Me To The Wolves.

Age Over-18s only.

Address Avenida Infante Dom Henrique 85, Parque do Flamengo.

Palácio Gustavo Capanema — Centro The 1940s modernist ministry building designed with Le Corbusier’s involvement, now a cultural centre. Tonight it opens a samba season in tribute to Beth Carvalho. Tonight Mart’nália at 8 p.m., then a vinyl set at 10 p.m.

Entry Free, no ticket, subject to capacity.

Season Próxima Parada Samba, part of the Semana de Arte do Rio.

Address Rua da Imprensa 16, Centro.

Money and How Paying Works

We convert at 5.1521 reais to one US dollar. That is the closing sell rate the Banco Central published for Thursday 17 September, the last business day before today.

Entry at the samba houses is a fixed price rather than a per-artist one. Food and drink are billed separately, at the table.

Bars usually add a service charge of about 10 per cent, called serviço. Brazilian law makes it optional, and staff remove it if you ask.

The free concerts tonight are genuinely free, with no ticket and no registration. They fill on a first-come basis, so arriving early is the only currency that helps.

Getting Home Safe

A 10 p.m. start under the Arcos will outlast the metro on some lines. Check the last train for your own line on the MetrôRio site, and plan a car if you stay to the end.

Rideshare is the reliable way out of Lapa after midnight. Book from inside the venue and wait in a lit, busy spot.

Keep your phone in a pocket on the quieter streets around Mem de Sá. The avenue stays busy, and the side streets do not.

Tonight’s free bills are outdoor and crowded, which is safe in the middle and thinner at the edges. Stay where the lights and the people are.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is free in Rio tonight?

Fafá de Belém under the Arcos da Lapa at 10 p.m., Mart’nália at the Palácio Capanema at 8 p.m., the Festival Sotaque Carregado at Praça XV from 5 p.m., and two RioHarpFestival concerts at half past twelve and 6 p.m.

What time does the show at Carioca da Gema start?

The venue publishes two figures. Its event entry gives 7.30 p.m., and its standing Friday schedule gives doors at 6.30 p.m., a happy-hour set at 7 p.m. and the main show at 9.30 p.m.

How much is Carioca da Gema?

Entry is R$35, about US$7, on Fridays, Saturdays and holiday eves. Tuesday to Thursday costs R$30, roughly US$6.

How much are the Angra tickets?

R$150 full and R$75 half price, about US$29 and US$15. Doors open at 7 p.m. and the show starts at 9 p.m. at Vivo Rio.

Is there football in Rio tonight?

No. Flamengo drew 1-1 with Independiente del Valle at the Maracanã last night and went through 3-1 on aggregate to face Estudiantes in the semi-finals.

Will it rain tonight?

Showers are forecast for the afternoon, with a 56 per cent chance and under two millimetres of rain. The evening is expected to be cloudy and dry.

What is on tomorrow?

Andrezão do Cacique at Carioca da Gema, doors 8.30 p.m. and show 10 p.m. for R$35 or about US$7. The MIMO Festival is free at the Circo Voador from 8 p.m.

Sources: Carioca da Gema, events and house information, retrieved 18 September 2026; Dani Coimbra and Andrezão do Cacique ticket pages on Zig; Vivo Rio event page for Angra; Sala Cecília Meireles programme; Riotur event calendar for Circo Voador; Eu Rio on the Amir Haddad festival and Fafá de Belém; Folha do Leste on Mart’nália at Capanema; Rota Cult on the Festival Sotaque Carregado and the Centro Cultural Lavradio; Pressenza on the RioHarpFestival; MIMO Festival programme; Climatempo forecast for Rio de Janeiro; Banco Central PTAX close, 17 September 2026.

World.title: Cost of Living Arequipa Peru 2026: Less Than Half of Lima
World.content:
PERU · COST OF LIVING

Key Facts — What rent costs A one-bedroom in the centre averages about US$362 a month, and US$241 outside it.

— Against the capital Lima charges about US$767 for the same flat, more than twice the Arequipa figure.

— The catch The average net salary is about US$629, so central rent still takes nearly three-fifths of it.

— What bills cost Basic utilities average about US$24 a month, the lowest figure in this series.

— What eating out costs A meal at an inexpensive restaurant averages about US$3.56.

— What comes next The figures rest on 23 contributors, so treat them as indicative rather than exact.

Cost of living arequipa peru is the cheapest entry in this series. The utility bill is where the gap becomes hard to believe.

Arequipa's Plaza de Armas. A central one-bedroom costs less than half the Lima equivalent. Photo: PsamatheM, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

Where This Fits

Cost of living arequipa peru produces the lowest figures in this series of city guides. That holds on rent, on bills and on eating out.

Arequipa is Peru’s second city, built in white volcanic stone at around 2,300 metres. It is not a small town or a resort.

The comparison that makes the point is with Lima rather than with anywhere abroad. The two cities sit in the same country under the same currency.

What follows sets out the figures, converts them, and then tests them against the local wage.

Less Than Half of Lima

A one-bedroom apartment in the centre of Arequipa averages 1,218 soles a month. That works out at about US$362.

All conversions here use a rate of 3.37 to the dollar, published by open.er-api.com on 18 September 2026. Sol prices move against the dollar, so the equivalents drift.

The same flat in central Lima averages about US$767. Arequipa is therefore cheaper by more than half on the single line most people check.

That is a wider internal gap than most countries show between their first and second cities. It is the practical case for looking beyond the capital.

The trade is not nothing. Lima has the international airport, the largest job market and the bulk of the country’s professional services.

Arequipa answers with climate and scale. It is large enough to have what a city needs and small enough to cross without planning around traffic.

The altitude is the other variable. At around 2,300 metres the air is thinner than most arrivals expect. That is a health question rather than a cost one.

The Plaza de Armas in Arequipa. The colonial centre carries a premium of about half over the outlying districts. Photo: PsamatheM, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

What Housing Costs

Outside the centre a one-bedroom averages 812.17 soles, about US$241. The discount for leaving the middle is roughly a third.

A three-bedroom in the centre averages 2,488 soles, close to US$739. Outside the centre it falls to 1,440 soles, about US$428.

A family-sized flat in central Arequipa therefore costs about what a one-bedroom costs in central Lima. That comparison is the one worth carrying.

The central premium here is real but moderate. It is narrower than Curitiba’s 42% and far narrower than the gap in the small expat towns covered earlier.

That suggests a housing market shaped mainly by local demand. Where foreign money dominates, the central premium tends to be much wider.

The Bills Are the Surprise

Basic utilities for a standard apartment average 81.67 soles a month. That is about US$24.

Set that against the same line elsewhere in this series. Nassau runs about US$397.50, Punta del Este about US$114 and Curitiba about US$99.

Arequipa therefore costs roughly a sixteenth of the Nassau figure. That is the widest single gap recorded across these guides.

Part of the explanation is the climate. At this altitude the city needs little heating and almost no air conditioning.

Broadband adds about 80 soles, close to US$23.75, and a mobile plan around 34.98 soles, about US$10.39. Connectivity costs roughly what the electricity does.

Laguna de Salinas in the Arequipa region. Altitude shapes the climate, and it keeps the heating and cooling bill small. Photo: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

Food, Transport and Schooling

A meal at an inexpensive restaurant averages 12 soles, about US$3.56. That is the lowest figure in this series by a clear margin.

For comparison, the same line is US$6.50 in Boquete, US$6.81 in Antigua Guatemala and US$38.75 in Nassau. Arequipa is an order of magnitude below the island.

Local transport costs one sol a trip, roughly US$0.30. Petrol runs about 5.15 soles a litre, close to US$1.53.

Preschool is reported at about 257.50 soles a month, near US$76. For a family that is the kind of line that decides a city.

None of these figures is a rounding error against rent. Together they make the difference between the two Peruvian cities larger than rent alone suggests.

A single person eating out daily would spend about US$107 a month at that price. The same habit in Nassau would cost more than a thousand.

That is the kind of gap that changes how a person lives rather than only what they pay. Eating out stops being an occasion here.

Rent Against the Local Wage

The average monthly net salary in Arequipa is 2,117.60 soles, about US$629. A central one-bedroom averages about US$362.

Rent therefore takes close to three-fifths of the average net wage. That is a heavy share by any standard.

It is still a better ratio than most of this series. In Antigua Guatemala, Boquete and Punta del Este, central rent exceeds the average wage outright.

The difference matters for what kind of city this is. Arequipa is priced by people who live and work there, not by visitors or foreign buyers.

For someone arriving on a foreign income, that has a practical consequence. Your money goes further here than in places where foreign money has already set the price.

What We Could Not Price

Three items are not stated here because the source did not carry a dependable figure.

The first is the monthly transport pass, which the data lists as unavailable rather than free. The second is health cover, which varies by provider and age.

The third is altitude adjustment, which is not a cost but is a real factor at 2,300 metres. Some arrivals need weeks rather than days.

The first of those is the only one that changes a budget, and single fares suggest it would be modest.

What Cost of Living Arequipa Peru Comes Down To

This is the cheapest city covered in this series, and the margin is not narrow. Rent, bills and eating out are all the lowest recorded.

The utility line is the one that stands out. At about US$24 a month it is a sixteenth of what the same bill costs in Nassau.

Against Lima, the case is straightforward. A family-sized flat in the centre costs roughly what a single person pays in the capital.

The honest qualifier is the wage. Local salaries are low enough that rent still takes most of a typical pay packet.

That is also why the city stays affordable to outsiders. Nothing here has been repriced upward by foreign demand.

Read cost of living arequipa peru as Peru without the capital-city premium. What you give up is the airport and the job market, and what you gain is most of your budget.

World.title: Cost of Living Punta del Este 2026: Half Again Above Montevideo
World.content:
URUGUAY · COST OF LIVING

Key Facts — What rent costs A one-bedroom in the centre averages about US$1,094 a month, and US$815 outside it.

— Against the capital That is roughly 49% above the Montevideo figure for the same size of flat.

— The catch The average local net salary is about US$1,031, below the cost of a central one-bedroom.

— What the season does Reported three-bedroom rents outside the centre span US$598 to US$2,789.

— What bills cost Basic utilities average about US$114 a month, and a cheap restaurant meal about US$13.

— What comes next The figures rest on 29 contributors over 18 months, with some lines estimated.

Cost of living punta del este is a resort price attached to a small permanent population. The season is inside every figure.

Punta del Este. Rent runs about half again above Montevideo, and the summer season sits inside every average.
