World.title: Hungary’s Corvinus University breaks into global business rankings with multiple top positions
World.content:
Corvinus University of Budapest has entered all five QS Business Master’s Rankings, standing as the only Hungarian institution in four categories and the highest-ranked Hungarian university in Management, while its MBA placed 58th in Europe.

The latest rankings published by Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), one of the world’s best-known higher education ranking organisations, mark a significant expansion of the University’s international presence. Released on 16 September, the 2027 edition covers Business Master’s programmes in Finance, Management, Marketing, Business Analytics and Supply Chain Management, alongside the global and regional rankings of full-time MBA programmes.

Among the five subject rankings, Corvinus’ Advanced Supply Chain Management Master’s programme ranked 85th, its Marketing programme placed 101–110th, while its Management and Leadership Master’s programme ranked 131–140th. Both the Finance Master’s programme and the Business Analytics programme placed in the 151–200 range. Corvinus also ranked 161–170th in the Global MBA ranking and 58th in the European MBA ranking. Corvinus is the only Hungarian institution represented in the these rankings except the Management category, where it is the highest-ranked Hungarian university (the University of Pécs is placed in the 201+ band).

The highest-ranking programme associated with Corvinus remains the CEMS Master in International Management. Available in Hungary exclusively at Corvinus, the programme once again ranked 4th out of 256 programmes in the QS Masters in Management global ranking, placing it among the top 2% worldwide.

If you missed it: Major international success: Budapest Corvinus University advances in the Financial Times’ latest ranking

“This year’s results mark an important milestone for Corvinus’ international visibility. It is particularly valuable for us that our own Master’s programmes have entered the QS global rankings for the first time, while CEMS continues to rank among the very best in the world. This is strong recognition that our programmes are gaining increasing attractiveness in international higher education comparisons,” said Bruno van Pottelsberghe, Rector of Corvinus University of Budapest.

The QS Business Master’s Rankings 2027 assess business Master’s programmes across five subject areas. In addition to the 256 programmes included in the Management ranking, this year’s rankings feature 286 Finance, 234 Business Analytics, 214 Marketing and 142 Supply Chain Management programmes. QS ranked 423 programmes in its Global MBA ranking and 113 programmes in its European MBA ranking. The assessment considers graduate employability, the professional, leadership and entrepreneurial achievements of alumni, value for money, academic performance in the relevant subject areas, and student and faculty diversity.

Among the institutions leading the rankings, HEC Paris took first place in Management and Marketing, while the US-based MIT, topped the Business Analytics, Supply Chain Management and Global MBA rankings. Oxford Saïd Business School ranked first in Finance, and Cambridge in the European MBA ranking.

Corvinus University of Budapest has been the exclusive Hungarian academic partner of CEMS since 1996. The CEMS Master in International Management network brings together 33 business schools and more than 70 corporate partners. Students gain international experience through a semester abroad, business projects, skills seminars and professional internships.

World.title: Police launch investigation into Hungary’s controversial residency bond scheme
World.content:
Hungarian police have launched an investigation into the country’s former residency bond programme after Transparency International Hungary filed a criminal complaint over suspected mismanagement causing significant financial damage to the state.

According to 444.hu, the Budapest Police Headquarters (BRFK) is investigating the case following a complaint filed in late July by Miklós Ligeti, then legal director of Transparency International Hungary, who was elected to the Constitutional Court earlier this week.

The complaint was initially submitted to the Prosecutor General’s Office before being transferred to the Central Chief Prosecutor’s Office for Investigation and subsequently to the BRFK. In August, authorities said they had ordered supplementary investigation of the complaint. Police have now confirmed that a criminal investigation is under way, although they have not disclosed when it officially began or provided further details.

How did the residency bond scheme work?

The residency bond programme was introduced in 2012 on a proposal by Antal Rogán, then head of Parliament’s Economic Committee. Under the scheme, non-EU citizens could obtain Hungarian residency permits after investing EUR 250,000 or EUR 300,000 through the programme.

Eight intermediary companies were authorised to handle the bonds. According to Transparency International’s calculations, these companies could have made around HUF 60 billion (approximately EUR 165 million at the time) in profits from public funds.

The programme ended in June 2017. By then, 6,621 residency bonds had been sold, while a total of 19,855 foreign nationals, including family members, had received Hungarian residency permits. These permits allowed them to travel freely within the Schengen Area.

The investors were required to keep their investment for five years, after which most of the money was returned, while the residency status remained valid for life.

Transparency raises concerns over state losses

Transparency International now alleges that the scheme caused at least HUF 21 billion in damage to the state budget and argues that the authorities failed to properly examine who ultimately owned the intermediary companies.

The organisation also claims that the state could have handled the bond transactions itself, for example through the Government Debt Management Agency, rather than relying on companies with unclear ownership structures.

Transparency previously filed a complaint over alleged abuses connected to the approval of the intermediary companies in 2018, but the investigation was rejected by the Central Chief Prosecutor’s Office for Investigation. The latest complaint instead focuses on the alleged financial damage to the state.

The organisation argues that the case has not become time-barred, partly because the state was still buying back bonds in 2022.

However, the Government Debt Management Agency previously argued that the scheme had saved the state more than EUR 9.6 million between 2013 and 2017 compared with issuing Premium Euro Hungarian Government Securities.

The current investigation will determine whether the allegations raised by Transparency International amount to a criminal offence.

World.title: NATO chief: Putin unlikely to attack us – we are stronger
World.content:
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte says he does not expect Russia to attack the alliance in the coming years, arguing that its strength makes such a move unlikely.

Speaking to the BBC during an official visit to London on Thursday, Rutte said the lessons of the war in Ukraine meant that NATO should not be “naive” about what Russian President Vladimir Putin is capable of.

At the same time, he said he did not believe Russia would attack NATO in the next few years because the alliance is currently too strong for Putin to risk such a move, the Hungarian News Agency (MTI) wrote.

Rutte calls for NATO to maintain its strength

Rutte stressed that NATO must ensure it remains equally strong over the next “two, three, five years”. His comments come as European countries continue to increase defence spending and strengthen their military capabilities amid Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen also highlighted the need for stronger European defence in her State of the Union address on Wednesday, saying the war in Ukraine had demonstrated the importance of capabilities including air and missile defence.

She said Europe needed to reduce its dependence on a single supplier and announced plans to develop an affordable, modular missile-defence system together with Ukraine. The proposed Freyja project would combine Ukrainian battlefield experience with European technology and production capacity.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official Telegram channel!

EU continues military support for Ukraine

The EU is also continuing to provide military assistance to Ukraine. According to the sources, von der Leyen announced a further EUR 3.3 billion in support for Ukrainian purchases of missiles and drones.

The EU has already approved substantial additional defence funding this month. On 11 September, the European Commission approved EUR 6.1 billion for Ukrainian purchases of air and missile defence systems, missiles, ammunition, drones and electronic warfare equipment. The package also enables Ukraine to acquire Patriot equipment and PAC-3 missiles.

The Commission has said the remaining funds from the EU’s SAFE programme will also be used for joint defence projects with Ukrainian companies, with the Freyja missile-defence project at the centre of the planned cooperation.

World.title: Hungarian conservative CitizenGO falsely accuses British same-sex couple of abusing their daughter
World.content:
A Hungarian conservative organisation used a British family’s photograph in a campaign against same-sex adoption, falsely claiming the two fathers had abused their adopted daughter and been jailed.

A Hungarian branch of the conservative advocacy organisation CitizenGO has apologised after using a photograph of a British same-sex family in a social media campaign and falsely claiming that the two fathers had abused their adopted daughter and been imprisoned.

The photograph showed British couple Ian Tomney-Bell and Darryl with their daughter. It had previously appeared in a 2023 UK Government article in which Tomney-Bell described their experience of adopting their daughter as a same-sex couple.

CitizenGO Hungary used the image in a Facebook post promoting a petition against adoption by same-sex couples.

The post claimed that the two men had “abused their adopted daughter for years” before being sent to prison, and used the case to argue that “rainbow families” are dangerous for children.

Family member denies ever being investigated

Tomney-Bell, who was on holiday in Japan with his family when the post appeared, said the allegations were completely untrue.

In a statement shared on Facebook and LinkedIn, he said neither he nor his partner had ever been investigated by police in connection with their daughter, let alone convicted or imprisoned.

He also said the family had never given permission for their photograph to be used in a political campaign.

The photograph had originally been published as part of Tomney-Bell’s account of the couple’s adoption journey on the UK Government’s Children’s Social Care blog in October 2023. The article describes how the couple went through the adoption process before being matched with their daughter, Aspen.

Tomney-Bell said the family had received numerous messages after the Hungarian post was published and had reported the content to Facebook.

“We simply want our family left out of a political campaign that we never agreed to be part of,” he said.

CitizenGO removes post and apologises

Telex contacted CitizenGO Hungary and campaign director Béla Teleki, asking what information had been used to support the allegations and whether the family had been asked for permission to use their photograph.

The organisation initially did not respond, and the Facebook post was subsequently removed.

After Telex published its report, Teleki responded to the questions and said the post had not been lawful. He also said CitizenGO Hungary had publicly apologised to the family.

In its apology, the organisation acknowledged that the people shown in the photograph had never been subject to the criminal proceedings described in the original post.

CitizenGO said the photograph had apparently come from a social media post circulating online, but that it had failed to verify the connection between the image and the allegations before publishing it.

The organisation described this as a mistake and said it had removed the content from all of its platforms.

It also said it would only use photographs of identifiable private individuals with documented consent in future, and would publish allegations concerning criminal offences only on the basis of verifiable official sources.

Photo originally published by UK Government

The photograph used by CitizenGO had a very different context when it was originally published.

Tomney-Bell’s 2023 article on the UK Government’s Children’s Social Care blog recounts how he and Darryl decided to adopt, worked with an adoption agency and social worker, and eventually welcomed their daughter into their family.

The blog is described as a Department for Education platform for professionals working in children’s social care.

CitizenGO Hungary’s campaign was promoting a petition opposing adoption by same-sex couples, but the family featured in its post said they had never agreed to have their photograph used for that purpose.

World.title: Discontent Simmers in Kosovo as Protesters Denounce Hague War Crimes Verdict
World.content:
The KLA War Veterans’ Organisation, which staged Friday’s protest, called for the dismissal of Justice Minister Donika Gervalla, the repeal or amendment of the Law on the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, unlimited funding for the defence of the four former KLA leaders in their upcoming appeal against the verdict, and the engagement of top international experts for their defence.

Hysni Gucati, head of the organisation, accused minister Gervalla of submitting evidence for the case to the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague.

“We are telling [Prime Minister] Albin Kurti to remove these people from the government starting today; he should not keep them in the government. People who collaborate with the enemy are enemies of my nation, and we do not want them among us,” Gucati said.

“Donika Gervalla has still not come forward to apologise,” he added. Gervalla has not commented publicly about the allegation so far.

World.title: Fining Bosnia’s Parties for Campaign Violations Won’t Deter Them, Expert Warns
World.content:
The unprecedented fines imposed this week by Bosnia’s Central Election Commission won’t stop ruling parties from exploiting state resources to secure votes, Dario Jovanovic, project manager of the fair-elections campaign group Pod Lupom, told BIRN on Friday.

“Parties in Bosnia view these fines as a minor, predictable cost of doing business,” Jovanovic said. “When a ruling party controls millions in public budgets, a few thousand euros will not stop them from exploiting state resources to secure votes.”

The state Election Commission imposed unprecedented penalties exceeding 100,000 euros during a single session in Sarajevo on Thursday, heavily targeting major political entities for premature campaigning and abusing public resources ahead of the polls on October 4.

The primary target of Election Commission’s sanctions was the Alliance of Independent Social Democrats, SNSD, the Bosnian Serb ruling party led by Milorad Dodik.

The SNSD, which holds power in Bosnia’s Serb-led entity, Republika Srpska, was directly fined about 41,900 euros, while individual sanctions against its candidates brought the party’s total penalty to 52,700 euros, effectively accounting for over half of the entire session’s fines.

The regulatory body cited multiple severe violations of Bosnia’s Election Law, focusing on the unlawful exploitation of public infrastructure projects for partisan gain and the illegal use of children for political marketing.

Dodik himself was personally fined around 4,600 euros over an Instagram post in which he took direct credit on behalf of his party for taxpayer-funded public works. A member of the state parliament, Sanja Vulic, was fined 4,100 euros for inaccurate media statements and premature campaigning during a television broadcast.

The financial sweep extended beyond the SNSD. The Drasko Stanivukovic – Safe Srpska Movement coalition received the second-highest cumulative penalty, of some 13,000 euros. Following the ruling, Stanivukovic, mayor of Banja Luka, the main city in Republika Srpska, criticised the decision.

“They are fining us simply for doing our jobs and presenting infrastructure projects to the citizens,” Stanivukovic stated to media. “These decisions are rigid and politically targeted to diminish our campaign visibility.”

Other penalised entities included the Social Democratic Party, SDP, which was fined 8,700 euros, and Nedeljko Stevandic’s United Srpska, at 7,200 euros.

Major political entities from Bosnia’s other entity, the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, including the Party of Democratic Action, SDA and a five-party Croat coalition, were also hit with financial sanctions.

With voters set to elect the state’s tripartite Presidency and entity parliaments in less than three weeks, the watchdog’s latest financial targeting represents an aggressive institutional effort to enforce compliance in a highly polarized race.

World.title: Greece Mourns Margarita Papandreou, Pioneering Feminist
World.content:
Margarita Papandreou with her three sons Photo: Nikos Papandreou/Facebook.

Greek feminist and author Margarita Papandreou, who was the wife of prime minister and centre-left PASOK party founder Andreas Papandreou, died in Athens on Friday. On September 20, she would have turned 103 years old.

Margarita (Margaret) Chant-Papandreou, originally from the US, studied journalism and pursued postgraduate studies in Public Health. Her name became linked to one of the most prominent political dynasties in Greek history, as well as to a series of significant reforms regarding gender equality.

She was the second wife from 1951 to 1989 of Andreas Papandreou; together they had four children, including former PM George Papandreou and PASOK MEP Nikos Papandreou.

“Margarita Papandreou linked her name to the struggle for women’s rights and social progress,” stated PASOK’s current leader, Nikos Androulakis.

Margarita met Andreas in the US in 1948 and the couple moved to Greece in 1961. Following the military takeover and Andreas’s arrest in 1967, she campaigned for his release. They left Greece for Sweden, and then Canada, returning to Greece after the fall of the military junta in 1974, when Andreas announced the founding of PASOK.

Margarita did not remain in her husband’s shadow; in 1976, alongside other women, she founded the Women’s Union of Greece, a women’s non-profit.

She played a pivotal role in promoting, drafting and passing legislation that improved the social status of Greek women. Key measures included the introduction of civil marriage in 1982, the abolition of the dowry system, the legalisation of divorce by mutual consent, the right of women to retain their maiden names after marriage in 1983, and the legalisation of abortion in 1986.

In her book, Love and Power, she recounted her turbulent relationship with her husband – marked by infidelity, their acrimonious divorce and his subsequent marriage to a younger woman.

Her son, Nikos Papandreou, wrote in the preface: “She may have stood by the side of the Greek politician who transformed Greece – Andreas – but she also created and led the country’s most significant feminist movement, the one that exerted the greatest influence regarding women’s rights in Greece.”

World.title: Turkey Arrests Fund Managers Over Stock Market Manipulation Scandal
World.content:
Turkish authorities arrested four suspects on Friday, including investment fund board members, and imposed travel bans on 51 others, as part of an investigation into alleged manipulation of the stock market, Justice Minister Akin Gurlek announced.

Courts have also imposed precautionary measures on accounts and other assets linked to those under investigation, to prevent their transfer, Gurlek said.

“Those who exploit the sweat, labour and savings of our citizens will be held accountable before the law,” he added.

Turkey’s Capital Markets Board, SPK, has filed criminal complaints about alleged manipulative transactions in several funds and listed shares.

In a separate investigation, a court ordered access blocked to 246 social media accounts accused of publishing speculative material capable of causing fear or panic among investors.

Another investigation by prosecutors in Istanbul’s Bakirkoy District has resulted in 16 arrests over social media posts allegedly intended to manipulate capital markets, Gurlek said.

Turkish Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci on Thursday said operations related to the stock market investigation would continue, suggesting further action is likely.

On Thursday the SPK ordered the liquidation of 130 funds managed by seven portfolio management companies after liquidity problems contributed to sharp market losses.

Trading on Istanbul Stock Exchange was temporarily suspended on Wednesday after the benchmark BIST 100 index fell by more than 6 per cent, triggering a market-wide circuit breaker.

Estimates of the combined size of the 130 funds differ.

According to Reuters, their assets are worth around 21.4 billion US dollars, involving about 353,000 investors. CNBC-e puts the total at about 19.8 billion US dollars and the number of investors at more than 514,000.

Liquidation does not mean that the investors’ money has been confiscated. Instead, banks are being tasked to deliver citizens’ money in these funds. Is Bank has been appointed to handle the liquidation of funds managed by Tera Portfoy, while state-owned Ziraat Bank will oversee funds belonging to the six other managers.

The proceeds will be distributed to investors according to their holdings. However, investors may not recover the last reported value of their holdings, as the final amount will depend on prices achieved when the assets are sold.

The crisis intensified after regulatory changes targeted risks associated with funds concentrated in thinly traded shares.

“It has been observed that some funds have caused price movements that cannot be explained by the financial realities of companies,” the SPK said on Thursday, adding that the new measures were aimed at preventing market manipulation and increasing transparency.

World.title: Expelled by Greece’s Ruling Party, Ex-PM Samaras Plots His Revenge
World.content:
At the beginning of September, former Greek prime minister Antonis Samaras seized on a newspaper report that users of the online platform of the Greek health service were allowed to specify gender options beyond ‘Male’ and ‘Female’, to include ‘Other’ and ‘Undetermined’.

Samaras was expelled from Greece’s ruling New Democracy party last year, and still bears a grudge.

He promptly took to Facebook to accuse the conservative government of promoting a “woke agenda” and echoed erroneous claims that school textbooks were depicting families with same-sex parents.

“The only thing ‘undetermined’ here is the extent of the ideological shift within the ruling party,” Samaras wrote. Greek families “need support, not redefinition”, he claimed.

World.title: EU Should Not Turn a Blind Eye to Montenegro’s Bloody Clan War
World.content:
When Montenegro declared independence in 2006, it identified EU and NATO integration as its strategic priorities. The country applied for EU membership in 2008, accession negotiations began in 2012, and NATO membership followed in 2017.

Yet, beneath the language of democratisation and Europeanisation lies a far less reassuring reality: a country where rival organised crime clans have waged a conflict for more than a decade, with dozens of people murdered, including innocent bystanders – and where allegations of links between criminal groups, police officers, and senior judicial figures have repeatedly surfaced

The question is not merely why Montenegro has struggled to defeat organised crime. It is why this conflict appears to have become increasingly peripheral to the European Union’s public assessment of the country.

The origins of Montenegro’s interclan war are generally traced to a dispute involving the disappearance of almost 200 kilograms of cocaine in Valencia, Spain, in 2014. What followed was a violent confrontation between two criminal groups based in the coastal town of Kotor – the Kavac and Skaljari clans. Most of the country’s organised crime groups eventually aligned themselves with one of the two rival groups.

Kotor itself became a symbol of the problem. The UNESCO World Heritage Site and historic home of both clans was described by then Interior Minister Goran Danilovic as a “hostage town.” Investigations subsequently alleged the existence of surveillance networks used by criminal gangs and the disclosure of confidential police information to members of the Kavac clan.

World.title: Democracy Digest: Hungary Opens Way for Adoption by Gay Couples
World.content:
Poland and Russia trade threats after drone strike; far-right MEP in headlines again

As Moscow steps up its hybrid war campaign in Europe, a Russian drone struck the locomotive of a Ukrainian passenger train travelling from Kyiv to Warsaw on Sunday afternoon, just 2 kilometres from the Polish border. The 206 passengers had already been evacuated after the crew received advance warning of the drone threat and no one was injured. The strike came shortly after a train carrying former British PM Boris Johnson, former Swedish PM Carl Bildt and other European security officials had passed through the same border station. Ukrainian Railways said it was possible that their train had been the intended target. Kaja Kallas, the EU’s High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, said Monday the train attack was “clearly meant to scare Western countries from supporting Ukraine, from going to Ukraine to show support”. In response to the incident, Polish PM Donald Tusk convened an emergency meeting on Sunday with cabinet ministers and the security services. “What we should expect is that the coming weeks and months will be a period of greatly intensified Russian activity, and unfortunately we cannot rule out that this escalation will also affect our territory,” he said.

Meanwhile, Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski told the BBC on Monday that he was “outraged, but not shocked” by the attack. “The Russians do liquidate people that criticise them, so I wouldn’t put it past them that they tried to hit the train with foreign officials,” he said. Asked about a recent assessment by the US-based Institute for the Study of War arguing that NATO should reconsider its policy of intercepting Russian aerial targets only after they enter allied airspace, rather than over Ukraine, Sikorski said the issue was being discussed both in Poland and within NATO and that he personally supported the idea. Earlier in the week, Sikorski travelled to the Yalta European Strategy conference in Kyiv, where he said he was confident NATO would “defeat Russia quite quickly”, even without US help, if Moscow attacked the alliance. “We have overwhelming superiority over Russia in air power,” he said, adding that if the Ukrainians had managed to destroy half of Russia’s refining capacity in six months, NATO “could do it in six weeks and take out the other half.” The remarks fit Sikorski’s longstanding argument that NATO enjoys a substantial economic and military advantage over Russia, and that, as he put it in a 2024 statement to parliament, “Putin’s only hope is our lack of determination”. His Kyiv comments drew a sharp response from Moscow. “If Poland enters into hostilities against Russia, our country will employ its entire arsenal of available forces and assets, and the Polish state will cease to exist within two to three days,” Nikolai Patrushev, an aide to President Vladimir Putin, told the Russian newspaper Argumenty i Fakty.

It’s been a busy week for professional provocateur Grzegorz Braun, the far-right Polish MEP. On Tuesday, the European Parliament lifted Braun’s immunity over allegations of Holocaust denial, clearing the way for Polish prosecutors to pursue a case against him. It was the sixth time the parliament has waived his immunity. Braun leads the far-right Confederation of the Polish Crown party and has become notorious for confrontational incidents, including an assault on a pro-choice gynaecologist and using a fire extinguisher to put out a menorah during a Hanukkah celebration in parliament. Braun also posted a video last week showing him vandalising a memorial to soldiers of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, UPA, in eastern Poland. “The UPA monument in the Dolhobyczow municipality, Hrubieszow county, must be removed,” Braun wrote alongside the footage. Police have been searching for those responsible since September 7. The memorial stands on the burial site of UPA soldiers killed fighting the Soviet NKVD in 1946 and has been damaged before. Earlier this summer, it was sprayed with paint and part of its decorative arch was cut away. The UPA is celebrated by many Ukrainians for fighting for Ukrainian independence during WWII, but its members were also responsible for the massacre of tens of thousands of Polish civilians in Volhynia and Eastern Galicia. “Representatives of Poland’s political fringe could find nothing better to do than wage war on graves,” Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry said, calling the act “shameful and immoral”. It added that Ukrainian memorials in Poland and Polish ones in Ukraine should both be protected. Polish Foreign Minister Sikorski condemned the incident on September 12 in Kyiv. “This is a great shame for our country,” he said, and, referring to Braun, added that “a man like this, who should already be behind bars, should not be seen anywhere in the world as the voice of Poland.” The footage of the vandalism has been submitted to prosecutors.

World.title: New Passenger and Hospitality Complex Coming to Split Port
World.content:
September the 18th, 2026 – A brand new passenger and hospitality complex is coming to Split Port, finally giving the entire area a much needed proverbial facelift.

What was once the Dalmacijavino winery, a work by architect Stanko Fabris and a gem of Croatian modern architecture, has over time become a dilapidated, abandoned building in what is definitely one of the most beautiful locations in the entire city. A place where Katalinića brig meets the port, the sea, and the rest of the world.

Morski reports that the Split Port Authority, the manager of that part of the port, has received a permit for the changes. After more than two years of waiting, the Split Port Authority has finally obtained a location permit – a permit for the changes according to which the building will be repurposed, under strict conservation guidelines. The building is under the protection of the Conservation Department of the Ministry of Culture.

After all the necessary studies (economic and legal) in cooperation with the constituents of the University of Split, and according to conservation guidelines, we conducted an international expression of interest from potential concessionaires and submitted all the necessary documentation to the City of Split, and we finally have it.

As part of the city’s project for the arrangement of Split’s Eastern Coast, according to the existing city Master Plan (GUP), two garages with 500 parking spaces can be built at that location, which would solve the problem of stationary traffic in the city port; passenger space can be expanded, accompanying hospitality facilities, and even a hotel with around a hundred rooms.

Now that the location permit has arrived, an international tender will be announced for the concession of the building and the space around it. The significance of this investment can best be shown through numbers, and that is the estimated value of the concession, which totals a massive 600,000,000 euros.

World.title: New Croatian Price Comparison System Coming Next Month
World.content:
September the 18th, 2026 – A brand new Croatian price comparison system is coming next month, with additional technical obligations awaiting traders and service providers.

As of the 1st of October 2026 in Croatia, the prices highlighted on the shelves, in the menus or on the price lists will no longer stand alone. Poslovni reports that alongside the current price an additional, so-called anchor price will also have to be stated. The new obligation applies to all retailers and registered service providers in Croatia. This means that the new rules will not cover only supermarkets, but also clothing and footwear shops, technical goods, furniture and building materials stores, as well as restaurants, cafes, hair and beauty salons, car mechanics, various service workshops and other craftsmen who offer their products or services to consumers.

The anchor price will be the regular price that applied to a particular product or service on 10 September 2026, without promotions, discounts and other special forms of sale. A hair salon will thus have to state, alongside the current price of a haircut or colouring, also the price of the same service on that date; a car mechanic will have to do the same alongside the price of a working hour or a particular service; and a restaurant alongside the prices of food and drinks in the menu or price list.

The anchor price is neither frozen nor the highest permitted price. A trader or craftsman can still change prices, but the consumer will at any moment be able to see how much the current price differs from the one that applied on the 10th of September, explain lawyers Dora Ljevar and Danijel Pribanić. The obligation also applies when advertising prices. If a trader or service provider publishes a price on a leaflet, poster, digital , outdoor advertising space or website, they will also have to highlight the anchor price alongside it. An exception applies to traders who for food, drinks, cosmetics, cleaning agents, toiletries and household products already had to highlight an additional price. For those products the relevant price remains the one that applied on the 2nd of May 2025.

Additional technical obligations await traders and service providers who already have their own website. On it they will have to publish a price list in XML or CSV format, which enables the automatic collection and comparison of data. Traders will update the price list every working day by 08:00 at the latest, and service providers after every price change, also 08:00 on the day of the change at the latest. Previously published price lists will have to remain available for 30 days. Those who do not have their own website are not obliged to set one up solely because of this obligation. Traders and craftsmen should therefore keep proof of the prices that applied on the 10th of September and, by the start of application of the new rules, adapt the price lists in business premises, s and websites.

World.title: Croatia’s Zvijezda Marks 110 Years of Successful Business
World.content:
September the 18th, 2026 – Croatia’s famous brand Zvijezda has celebrated 110 years of doing successful business and engaging in market leadership.

Zvijezda mayonnaise and Zvijezda oil occupy first and second place on the ranking of the strongest brands in Croatia according to Ipsos research. Poslovni reports that the very well known Zvijezda, a market leader and Croatian manufacturing company whose values are founded on tradition, quality and innovativeness, celebrated 110 years of successful business.

The ceremony was held at the Zagreb City Museum, on the day when in 1916 the First Croatian Oil Factory was founded in Zagreb, in the presence of numerous company partners as well as representatives of institutions and the media. Zvijezda’s strong position is also confirmed by data on the habits of Croatian households: every second edible oil used in Croatia is Zvijezda’s, two out of three cakes are baked with Zvijezda margarine, and nine out of ten people, when it comes to mayonnaise, first think of Zvijezda.

According to the BRANDpuls research by the Ipsos agency from spring 2026, as many as five Zvijezda brands are among the 20 strongest brands on the Croatian market, with Zvijezda mayonnaise and Zvijezda oil occupying the first two places.

“I’m proud that we’re the market leader in almost all categories in which we have decided to compete, and the historically high result in the mayonnaise category of more than 70 percent confirms this. Zvijezda has for years been the number 1 brand among all brands of fast-moving consumer goods, and we continuously achieve these results thanks to our consumers, employees and partners,” emphasised Dinko Jurišić, member of the Management Board of Zvijezda. From the very beginnings of production in the First Croatian Oil Factory right up to the present day, the company has over the decades followed the needs of consumers, developed new products and set standards for the domestic food industry.

As such, back in 1956, it became the first producer of margarine in the country, in 1959 it introduced mayonnaise to the market, and in 2016 it launched the production of its own ketchup. The company today operates through the brands Zvijezda, Margo and Omegol. “Today, Zvijezda is a large and modern company, which is best proven by these figures: €150 million in annual revenue, more than 400 employees and presence on more than 15 markets. We look at these 110 years with pride, but even more with a sense of responsibility towards what is coming, therefore we continue to invest in the development of our products, the modernisation of production, the digitalisation of processes and sustainable solutions that will further strengthen Zvijezda’s competitiveness,” stated at the ceremony Karmen Rosan, member of the Management Board of Zvijezda.

Since this year Zvijezda has been operating as part of the Žito Group, one of the leading Croatian food groups. By entering the Žito Group a new development chapter has begun for Zvijezda, directed towards further strengthening of business, market position and the creation of new opportunities for growth.

“Zvijezda is one of the best-known Croatian food brands and a company that for 110 years has had a special place in the lives of generations of consumers. Its entry into the Žito Group represents a great responsibility for us, but also an opportunity to jointly build a new chapter of one of the most successful Croatian business stories, so that in the years to come we remain competitive and recognisable among consumers,” said Josip Bičvić, President of the Supervisory Board of Zvijezda. Zvijezda marked the anniversary also with a donation to the Croatian Down Syndrome Association, with which it has been cooperating for more than ten years, and as part of the cooperation the labels of a special edition of Zvijezda sunflower oil were decorated with drawings by children from the Association.

World.title: Croatian Scientists Concerned by Adriatic Sea Test Results
World.content:
September the 18th, 2026 – Croatian scientists are becoming more and more concerned by Adriatic Sea test results following 75 years of frequent measurements.

Scientists from the Ruđer Bošković Institute have analysed 75 years of measurements showing that the warming and salinisation of the Mediterranean Sea are accelerating, and the changes are becoming increasingly clear even in the deep layers. The Adriatic-Ionian area stands out particularly in this regard. Morski reports that when a warmer sea in summer is discussed, it usually means the temperature that is more or less suitable for swimming near the coastline itself. However, what we see and feel near the surface is only a small part of the story. Below it lie hundreds and thousands of metres of seawater, whose deep layers change much more slowly and are considerably harder to monitor.

It was precisely in these layers of the sea that scientists from the Ruđer Bošković Institute sought an answer to the question of how much the Mediterranean has really changed over the past decades. Dr Elena Terzić and Dr Ivica Vilibić, in a paper published in the leading international geoscience journal Geophysical Research Letters, collected and connected data from different periods, from historical measurements from research vessels to modern autonomous Argo floats that today regularly dive into the depths of the sea. In this manner, they obtained a kind of cross-section of the Mediterranean from 1950 to 2025 and tracked what is happening with the temperature, salinity and density of the sea at different depths. The results show that the Mediterranean is not only warming and becoming saltier, but that the speed of these changes is increasing, and their signal can be tracked hundreds and thousands of metres below the surface.

the sea’s warmth is increasing and the process is accelerating…

We have known for a long time that the sea is warming, and this process is most often described by the average rate of warming, i.e. by how much the sea temperature increases on average over one decade. “The average rate of warming tells us how much the sea temperature changed over some longer period. However, when we describe the entire period with a single average rate, we do not see whether the speed of warming itself is also changing. Our results show that it is increasing, so the average can conceal how much faster the changes of recent decades actually are,” explains Dr Elena Terzić.

In other words, a single straight line showing average warming no longer describes well enough what is happening in the Mediterranean. That is why the scientists also analysed the acceleration of warming, i.e. whether the speed at which the temperature is rising is itself changing. The clearest signal is seen near the surface, but the more interesting part of the story begins when one looks deeper. In the last years of the analysed period the temperature in the first hundred metres or so of the Mediterranean was about two degrees higher than the average of the second half of the 20th century. Warming is clearly visible also between 300 and 1,000 metres, and a measurable signal appears even at depths between one and two kilometres.

This is important because the deep sea does not react quickly to what is happening in the atmosphere. The surface can warm up during one exceptionally hot summer and cool down again a few months later, while changes in the deep sea take place much more slowly. “When the signal of change is no longer seen only near the surface but also deep in the water column, we are talking about a much broader change in the properties of the sea. The deep layers are a kind of memory of what has been happening in the system over a longer period,” emphasises Dr Ivica Vilibić.

why does the adriatic stand out here?

The temperature is not the only thing that is changing, because the Mediterranean Sea is simultaneously becoming saltier as well, especially in its central and eastern parts. Salinity and temperature together determine the density of seawater: the higher the salinity, the denser the water, and the higher the temperature, the lower the density. It is precisely the differences in density that drive the main circulation cells in the sea, i.e. the processes by which water mixes, sinks and transfers heat and salt from one part of the Mediterranean to another. Because of this, changes that begin near the surface do not necessarily stay there.

The Adriatic has a special place in this story because it is one of the areas of the Mediterranean in which dense water is formed. During cold winter periods the surface water can cool strongly, become dense enough and begin to sink. In this way the properties that the water acquired near the surface can be transferred into the deep layers of the Adriatic, and then further towards the deep Ionian Sea and the eastern Mediterranean.

The Adriatic-Ionian system in this research proved to be one of the areas with a particularly pronounced acceleration of changes. In the southern Adriatic a strong signal of accelerated warming appears even at a depth of around 1,000 metres, accompanied by simultaneous changes in salinity. This indicates that areas in which surface water sinks can be important places for the early detection and monitoring of changes that are transferred towards the interior of the sea.

how are measurements from 1950 and 2026 connected?

One of the biggest challenges in the research was to compare the properties of the sea that over the decades were not measured in the same way. In the 1950s and 1960s the data mostly came from research vessels, while today scientists have a network of Argo floats that independently pass through the water column and regularly send data on temperature and salinity. The authors therefore combined several large data sources, checked their quality and specifically tested whether the larger number of modern measurements could introduce bias into the results, i.e. artificially create the impression of acceleration. They repeated the analyses for different time periods and with different statistical approaches, and the basic pattern remained visible.

the wider mediterranean is an early indicator

The Mediterranean is a relatively small and almost closed marine basin that reacts strongly to changes in the atmosphere. Precisely for that reason it can serve scientists as a kind of natural laboratory for understanding what is happening to the oceans in a warmer climate. The research does not give a final answer to the question of which individual process is responsible for the observed acceleration. The changes can be connected with the warming of the atmosphere, evaporation and precipitation, the exchange of water with the Atlantic through Gibraltar, and changes in the circulation of the Mediterranean itself.

For the scientists the next step is to determine the contribution of each of these processes, and what they can already conclude is that the change in the Mediterranean is no longer only a story about a warmer sea surface. The sea is changing ever faster, and the signal of these changes has reached deep below the surface.

World.title: How Diaspora Professionals Use Croatian Citizenship to Work in Europe’s Top Hubs
World.content:
September the 17th, 2026 – The Croatian diaspora is vast, and many professionals are using their right to obtain Croatian citizenship as a key to unlocking work in Europe’s top hubs.

If we sift back through time, we’ll notice that the overarching pitch for securing Croatian citizenship by descent has targeted two distinct groups: those with a mysterious granny from a now abandoned Dalmatian village seeking a sentimental connection to their ancestral homeland, and retirees with similar stories looking to stretch their 401k to the maximum in a sun-drenched, slow-paced Mediterranean paradise.

It isn’t that those reasons don’t still largely exist, but it has to be said that times move (and more and more quickly), bringing marked shifts for the diaspora. A totally different demographic is suddenly digging up dida’s old birth certificates from curious settlements few have ever heard of. They’re the young, ambitious US corporate professionals who, for whatever reason, aren’t quite ready to give up on the grind and embrace the pomalo lifestyle just yet. Faced with the infamously gruelling American corporate world, hyper-competitive job markets, and a desire for global experience, millennial and Gen-Z professionals are realising that a Croatian passport isn’t just a nod to their heritage and genetic makeup, it’s also the ultimate professional fast-track into the booming, wide open EU economy.

croatian citizenship as a way to clear the corporate visa wall and unlock the european dream

Ask any young American professional who has tried to land a job in London, Amsterdam, Paris, or Berlin about their experience, and they will tell you the same thing: the visa barrier is nearly insurmountable. For a European company to hire an American citizen, they must generally prove to their local government that no qualified EU citizen could fill the role. This requires months of bureaucratic red tape, thousands of euros in legal fees, and an incredibly patient HR department. Unless you are a C-suite executive or a highly specialised niche engineer, most corporate resumes with a “Requires Visa Sponsorship” box checked are filtered out by automated tracking software before a human ever lays eyes on them.

Pulling a trusty little Croatian passport out of your pocket completely demolishes this dizzyingly high wall.

Because Croatia is a full Member State of the European Union, Croatian citizens possess the absolute right to live, work, and do business in any of the 27 EU member states, completely visa-free. As a dual citizen, an American professional can apply for a corporate job in Dublin, Amsterdam, or Frankfurt exactly like a local. No sponsorship is required, no legal fees are incurred for the employer, and there are no bureaucratic delays.

trading the american “live to work” for the european “work to live”

The motivation for young Americans to make the leap across the Atlantic goes far beyond geographic novelty. It is a fundamental rejection of the “hustle culture” that dominates US corporate life. When American professionals leverage their Croatian citizenship to work in Western or Northern Europe, they enter a completely different professional landscape where things like mandatory paid time off are completely normal.

While the US remains the only advanced economy without guaranteed paid vacation, all EU countries legally mandate between 20 to 30 days of paid annual leave, and employees are fiercely encouraged to actually use them.

Then comes the strict work-life balance: Countries like France and the Netherlands have strict laws regarding the “right to disconnect,” making it illegal or completely culturally unacceptable for managers to email or call employees after standard working hours are over for the day.

Robust healthcare as a fundamental human right will also likely be music to the ears of any US citizen sick of paying an arm and a leg just in case they happen to become unwell. Health insurance ceases to be a terrifying golden handcuff tied to a specific, often exhausting job. Across Europe, high-quality healthcare is decoupled from employment status and heavily subsidised or entirely free at the point of use. No premiums, no back pay, and nobody has ever heard of the term “reaching their out of pocket maximum”.

career acceleration, all while exploring europe

Living and working abroad for two or three years isn’t a career pause, it’s a massive career accelerator, and you can do it all while enjoying free healthcare and actually being paid to sit back and relax. In an increasingly globalised economy, American companies place an immense premium on candidates with international operational experience. Navigating foreign markets, managing cross-cultural teams, and understanding EU regulatory landscapes (like GDPR) are skills that cannot be taught in any kind of US lecture hall. When a young professional decides to return to the US corporate ladder, a resume featuring a stint at a global hub in Munich or Amsterdam instantly stands out from a sea of applicants who have never left their home time zone.

how croatianbydescent.com can help you get the ball rolling

For young Americans, particularly those who barely have a second for themselves when they get home, the process of tracking down old archives, certifying documents, and dealing with troublesome Croatian ministries can feel daunting. Turning to not only experts, but members of the Croatian diaspora themselves who have personal experience of the process streamlines it all and makes you feel understood. It transforms journeying through sometimes complicated ancestral roots into a modern, powerful career tool.

It may never have really occurred to you outside of donning those checkers during the World Cup or enjoying a dish you struggle to pronounce that grandma used to make, but if you have a parent or grandparent who left Croatia, you aren’t just sitting on a family history. You might actually be sitting on the key to your next major career upgrade and a lifestyle that the USA could never realistically provide.

World.title: Dubrovnik Mayor Claims “Most People Don’t Even Know Where Istria is”
World.content:
September the 17th, 2026 – Dubrovnik Mayor Mato Franković has caused a stir and claimed that “most people don’t even know where Istria is”, adding that “Dubrovnik is the only tourism champion in Croatia”.

Dubrovnik Mayor Mato Franković assessed the tourist season as excellent at a session of the City Council and claimed that Dubrovnik is “the only champion of tourism in Croatia.” Index reports that in his review of the results, which according to him exceed expectations, he directed criticism at the “Istrian lobby,” reports Dubrovački dnevnik.

“The season has been excellent, and what is ahead of us looks very good. So far it looks above expectations,” Franković said.

He also expressed satisfaction that the number of visitors in the historic centre is not exceeding critical levels, after which he sent a message to the competition. “We’re the only champion of tourism in Croatia and no one can measure up to us. Istria with its lobby is trying to present itself as successful. People exclusively from Istria, such as Veljko Ostojić, comment on tourism and they push it. We are alone, but we have shown that we are above everyone,” Franković said, concluding with the statement: “Most people don’t even know where Istria is.”

4.7 million people have come to dubrovnik so far in 2026

On Facebook he was answered by the president of IDS and mayor of Poreč, Loris Peršurić. Peršurić replied to Franković that Dubrovnik is one of the symbols of Croatian tourism and that one should be proud of its successes, but he ironised the claim that people do not know where Istria is.

“Just this year 4.7 million people successfully found it, and we’re only in the 9th month because the season with us lasts almost the whole year,” he wrote. He emphasised that Istria’s reputation was not created overnight, but was built over decades by private renters, owners of agritourism facilities, taverns and wineries, olive growers, caterers, hoteliers, craftsmen and farmers. He also pointed out that in tourism it is not only the numbers that matter, but quality, sustainability and the preservation of space for the people who live in it.

Peršurić added that Dubrovnik also has strong state and tourism tools for promotion at its disposal and concluded that one can be proud of one’s own successes without diminishing those of others. “I therefore invite you to personally convince yourself of the qualities of Istria, but hurry with the reservation because these days quite a few people manage to find us,” he said to Franković.

World.title: Russian Ambassador Summoned for Talks in Croatia Following Russia’s Threats
World.content:
September the 17th, 2026 – The Russian Ambassador has been summoned for talks in Croatia following Russia’s recent threats against various European countries.

Russian Ambassador to Croatia Alexander Nurizade was summoned today for talks at the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs, where the Croatian side expressed concern over security threats from Russia towards European countries, the Russian Embassy in Zagreb announced. Index reports that according to the Russian side, Croatian representatives mentioned incidents in the airspace, territorial waters and on the infrastructure of EU member states, including in Denmark, Lithuania, Romania and Germany. The Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs lists Nurizade on its official website as the current Russian ambassador to Croatia.

the russian ambassador has rejected all accusations

The Russian Embassy states that Nurizade “firmly rejected” the accusations as unfounded. He described them, according to the embassy’s statement, as a “coordinated provocation” aimed at further worsening relations with Russia. He also expressed regret that Croatia, as the Russian side claims, “is pandering to the Kyiv regime and its foreign patrons interested in the continuation of the conflict.” These are the claims of the Russian Embassy. During the talks, Nurizade also repeated the official Russian positions on the causes of the war in Ukraine and accused the West of turning Ukraine into an “anti-Russian project.”

an attempted leipzig drone attack was discussed

Among the cases that the Croatian side, according to the Russian Embassy, cited was the incident in Leipzig. At the beginning of September, the German government officially accused Russia of being behind an attempted drone attack on Leipzig/Halle Airport on 4 August. A drone with explosives was found near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane. Berlin claims that the investigation traces the point to the Russian state, while Moscow rejects responsibility. After that case, the European Union and several member states summoned Russian diplomatic representatives for talks. EU High Representative Kaja Kallas said at the time that the incident had the characteristics of state-sponsored terrorism, while Russia claimed that Germany had not provided evidence for its accusations.

a russian vessel fired signal rockets at a danish aircraft

Tensions rose further this week after an incident out in the Baltic Sea. The Danish military announced that a Russian frigate, during routine surveillance, fired two signal rockets at a Danish military Fennec helicopter. One passed at a short distance from the helicopter. Denmark therefore summoned the Russian ambassador for talks. The Russian side countered with an accusation that Danish military helicopters had performed dangerous manoeuvres near Russian warships.

nato had to shoot down a drone over lithuania

In Lithuania a couple of days ago, an Italian fighter jet as part of a NATO mission shot down a drone that had entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus. Lithuanian authorities announced that the drone was carrying explosives. Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said it “most likely” came from Russia, but Lithuanian authorities warned that the investigation into its origin is still ongoing and that a final conclusion has not yet been reached. A similar incident was recorded last week in Romania, where a drone that Romanian and Moldovan authorities linked to Russian attacks on Ukraine entered deep into Romanian airspace before returning towards Moldova.

The Russian ambassador in the talks in Zagreb, according to a statement from his embassy, also spoke about Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure. He conveyed that Moscow considers railway junctions, trains and other facilities in Ukraine used for the transport of the army or cargo intended for the Ukrainian armed forces to be “legitimate military targets.”

In recent days Russia has further intensified attacks on Ukrainian railway infrastructure, including areas near the border with NATO members. Ukrainian authorities claim that civilian trains and infrastructure have also been hit in the process. The summoning of Nurizade for talks comes at a time of heightened warnings from European and NATO officials about incidents involving drones, sabotage and other hybrid threats. The European Commission today also proposed a new mechanism for a coordinated response by EU members to such security incidents. An inquiry was also sent to the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs about today’s talks with the Russian ambassador. We asked for confirmation of the meeting, the specific reason for his summoning, and clarification of which incidents Croatia cited and whether it plans further diplomatic steps after the talks.

World.title: Croatia to Get a New Road Worth Over €200 Million
World.content:
September the 17th, 2026 – Croatia is set to get a new road worth over €200 million, and it’s being widely compared to Pelješac Bridge.

The project includes two interchanges, five viaducts, four overpasses and two bridges. Poslovni reports that the Chinese company China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC) is building a 16-kilometre expressway that will finally directly connect Požega with the A3 Zagreb – Lipovac motorway. The new road will link Požeški Brestovac with the Godinjak interchange, where it will then connect to the motorway.

This is one of the largest infrastructure projects in Slavonia, which should significantly improve the transport connectivity of Požega-Slavonia County with the rest of Croatia. The route of the expressway runs south of Daranovci, after which it enters the forested area of Babja gora. There, a single-tube tunnel 1,650 metres long will be built, and the route then descends along a natural valley towards Tisovac and Godinjak. The project includes two interchanges, five viaducts, four overpasses and two bridges. The construction deadline is 48 months, meaning the new road should be completed by the end of 2029.

požega will get a faster link towards both zagreb and slavonski brod

The expressway is being built along the route of the existing state road D51, which has so far been the main transport link between Požega and surrounding settlements with the rest of the country. The new road should bring a safer and higher-quality connection to the A3 motorway, and thereby also to Zagreb and Slavonski Brod.

“This expressway represents the largest single project of Croatian Roads after the Pelješac Bridge. This is a big day not only for Croatian road construction, but also for Požega-Slavonia County, because it will be better and more safely connected to the motorway,” said Transport Minister Oleg Butković at the ceremonial introduction of the contractor into the works in Godinjak in November last year. For the residents of Požega-Slavonia County, the project represents the end of long-standing transport isolation. Due to frequent landslides and damage, the D51 does not fully meet modern standards of safety and traffic flow, so the new expressway will take over an important share of the traffic.

the požega interchange on the A3 motorway is also being built

At the beginning of February, a contract was also signed for the construction of the Požega interchange on the A3 motorway. The Požega interchange is part of the integral project for the construction of the expressway, which will connect to the motorway precisely at that point. The investor for that part of the project is Croatian Roads. When the works are completed, after decades of waiting Požega will finally get a direct fast road link with the A3 motorway, which should further improve the transport accessibility of the city and the entire Požega-Slavonia County.

World.title: England can build on World Cup ‘spirit’, says Tuchel
World.content:
London – Thomas Tuchel said England will build on the “fantastic spirit” of their World Cup campaign as he targets glory on home soil at Euro 2028.

The England boss was speaking at Wembley after naming a 27-man group for a four-game Nations League camp, starting with a clash against world champions Spain on September 26.

It comes just nine weeks after the end of the World Cup, where England conceded two late goals in a painful semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold and Chelsea forward Cole Palmer were the headline picks after both were controversially overlooked for the World Cup.

Tuchel also included Liverpool’s teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, uncapped Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite in his first squad since the tournament in North America.

A number of players who were in the World Cup squad including John Stones, Djed Spence, Dan Burn, Jordan Henderson and Dean Henderson missed out through injury.

Former Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Tuchel said he did not see the Nations League as a new start, instead focusing on continuity.

“I feel that it’s not a new beginning that we are starting now, so we build on a solid and very valuable foundation, and the target is to win the home Euros,” he told reporters on Friday.

Euro 2028 will be co-hosted by England, Scotland, Wales, and Ireland.

The German said his side’s ultimate failure at the World Cup had left him unfulfilled but stuck by his squad picks.

“I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic,” he said.

“I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.”

Tuchel said Palmer had impressed for Chelsea early in the season.

“He has his numbers back, he has assists back, he has decisive goals back, so that’s why he’s in the squad and I think he has a point to prove,” he said.

“The same goes for Trent. He was never off the list, he was never in a non-selectable class, and he has this chance to show, to be the best version of himself.”

Tuchel said it was his “duty” to play Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo after he failed to feature for a single minute at the World Cup.

The England boss welcomed the challenge of taking on Spain at Wembley.

“We feel the gap is closing and we feel that we are close and we want a proof of point,” he said.

“The stadium is sold out, it will be very exciting, the motivation cannot be higher to play against the world champions.”

England also play the Czech Republic twice and Croatia once during the upcoming international window.

World.title: Anti-Assad music star makes triumphant return to Syria
World.content:
Damascus – Syrian singer Assala Nasri has made a triumphant return to Damascus with a sold-out concert following 15 years of exile due to her opposition to ousted ruler Bashar al-Assad.

Thousands of fans welcomed the 57-year-old, known mononymously as Assala, at a venue in the Syrian capital where she bowed and opened the show with songs hailing the Syrian people.

“Souls of my heart, I missed you,” she repeatedly said to endless cheers on Thursday night.

“My loves, my people, I swear, until this moment I could not believe that I am among you. I want to tell you how much I dreamt of this.”

There was a heavy security presence for the concert, after some religious conservatives launched a campaign calling for its cancellation.

Half of the show’s proceeds will be donated to charity.

Syria’s new Islamist authorities, who overthrew Assad in 2024, have welcomed Assala. Culture Minister Mohammed Yassine Saleh has dubbed her “the daughter of Damascus”.

Joining her on stage, he said her return was that of “every honest Syrian and every free person”.

– ‘Moving forward’ –

Assala was among the first artists to express support for the peaceful anti-Assad protests that erupted in 2011, refusing to partake in events supporting his government.

She was booted from the Syrian artists’ union for her stance and was the target of media campaigns.

She went into exile, living in Cairo with her family and playing shows in various Arab countries.

The bloody repression of the protests led to a 13-year civil war that killed more than half-a-million people.

At Assala’s show, small Syrian flags rippled in time with the music, with many in the crowd unable to hold back their tears.

“I never thought this day would come. It’s like a beautiful dream,” concert-goer Sawsan Wadha, 56, said.

“We are very happy that our country is moving forward,” added 40-year-old Lynn Nahas.

On her new record, “The Syrian Album”, Assala covers folk songs from all 14 of Syria’s provinces as an homage to her country’s cultural diversity.

She sings for the cities scarred by war, but also for the coastline in mourning after last year’s killing of hundreds of members of Assad’s Alawite minority, and for Druze-majority Sweida, which also saw sectarian violence.

– Recovery through art –

Assala’s piercing, powerful voice rang out as she made her way through the album’s tracks at Thursday’s concert.

She also performed fan favourites like “Samehtak” and “Sandooq”, with the jubilant, tearful crowd singing along.

Assala and her family only returned to Damascus this week. An antiques dealer in the capital returned the oud, or Oriental lute, that had belonged to her father, a celebrated musician.

Conservative Muslim figures had expressed criticism in the run-up to the concert.

Egyptian preacher Hani Dahab, who lives in Syria, launched a social media campaign with the slogan “Cancel the Sinful Concerts”. He accused the culture ministry of seeking to “give society a secular character”.

Syrian Salafi preacher Abdul Razzaq al-Mahdi condemned what he called a “concert of music and debauchery”, while a group of preachers in Damascus called on the culture minister to take into account “the religious identity of society”.

While not addressing the critics directly, Assala said at the show that “recovery will only happen with art and music”.

Syria has seen a cultural boom since 2025, but also the rise of preachers and conservative religious movements in public spaces and at universities, raising fears of restrictions on freedom.

Farah Al-Atassi, political advisor to the government, said poetry, language and thought were “an integral part of Syrian identity”.

“This is the Syria that we know and that will endure,” she told AFP.

World.title: UNESCO can be ‘moderator’ in AI debate: chief to AFP
World.content:
Paris – UNESCO chief Khaled el-Enany has proposed in an interview with AFP that the UN culture and education agency become a facilitator in the worldwide wrangling on the risks of artificial intelligence.

“I believe we are uniquely positioned to make UNESCO a true moderator in this global debate,” he said as he prepared to welcome Pope Leo XIV, a key advocate for international AI governance, in Paris next week.

The UN educational, scientific and cultural organisation has long stressed that its remit covers more than heritage, looking to advance in areas ranging from access to education to the ethical use of artificial intelligence.

The debate over the potential dangers of self-improving algorithms has surged in recent weeks, with some researchers warning the technology could end humanity, and leaders of AI companies suggesting development needed to be slowed down.

US President Donald Trump has on the other hand called the fears a “hoax”.

Enany told AFP: “There is a risk that it will get out of control if we don’t intervene.”

“This break, this dialogue that has taken place over the past few weeks, is something very positive,” he added in the interview on Thursday.

He said the cultural agency had found an “indispensable partner” in the pontiff, who is to visit the UNESCO headquarters in Paris on Friday next week at the start of a four-day trip to France.

“This visit will be the beginning of a very solid partnership to strengthen and protect human dignity in this industrial revolution,” Enany said.

It will be the first visit by a pope to UNESCO headquarters since John Paul II in 1980.

– AI ‘must be governed’ –

Pope Leo, the first US pope, this week warned against delegating to algorithms decisions that should be taken by humans alone.

In his first major document, the encyclical “Magnifica Humanitas” (Magnificent Humanity), published in May, the pope issued a call to “disarm” AI in order to “prevent it from dominating humanity”.

Enany said UNESCO had long been concerned with regulating AI, in 2021 issuing a “Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence”.

The guide warned about the risk of violations of privacy and the concentration of technological power in the hands of a few states or companies, and well as potential effects on democracy and the environment.

AI is “an extraordinary tool, but one that must be governed in an ethical, inclusive, and fair way,” Enany said.

Trump has since returning to office withdrawn the United States from UNESCO, alleging that it is biased against Israel and promotes “divisive” causes.

China — one of the major global AI players — has become the agency’s largest donor.

Trump had already ordered a departure from UNESCO in 2017 during his first term, before President Joe Biden reestablished US membership.

As the United States rejoined in 2023, then US secretary of state Antony Blinken said it was key Washington was present at UNESCO for decisions “that actually matter”, including on “rules, norms and standards for artificial intelligence”.

China was among countries to oppose the move.

World.title: Bahrain’s Ramsis Engineering expands into Iraq with Basra office
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Bahrain-based Ramsis Engineering has opened a new branch in Basra to serve Iraq’s growing energy and industrial sectors.

The new office will put the mechanical engineering firm closer to its clients and partners in southern Iraq, where the majority of the country’s oil, gas, and heavy industrial activities are located.

Ramsis stated that its Iraq operations would concentrate on manufacturing, maintenance, and specialized engineering services, building on its expertise in the oil and gas, petrochemical, aluminum, power, and desalination sectors.

The Basra opening establishes the company’s local foothold as Iraq invests in oilfield development, gas processing, and large industrial infrastructure.

Ramsis offers mechanical engineering, building, manufacturing, maintenance, and oilfield services to industrial operators.

World.title: Most Asian stocks track Wall St rally, yen drops after BoJ rate hike
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks mostly rose on Friday in line with a rally on Wall Street as a drop in oil prices eased inflation concerns, while the yen dropped against the dollar even after the Bank of Japan hiked interest rates to a three-decade high.

The Federal Reserve’s lift in borrowing costs this week provided some relief to traders concerned that policymakers were not moving quick enough to address a spike in inflation that could deal a blow to the world’s top economy.

That has been helped by news that Saudi Arabia was moving to restore within days about half of crude shipments disrupted by the stoppage of its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea.

The conduit, even more important since the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz by Iran, was shut last week after being targeted by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.

Crude prices, which had soared around a fifth in September, have fallen around five percent from recent highs, with West Texas Intermediate dipping below $100 for the first time since last Friday. WTI was down more than one percent Friday and Brent lost two percent.

The surge in oil this month has been among the main catalysts for rising inflation since the United States and Israel began their war on Iran at the end of February.

And the latest fall-off provided some much-needed support to stocks.

Seoul, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Taipei, Mumbai and Bangkok all advanced, although there were losses in Singapore, Wellington, Jakarta and Manila. Sydney was barely moved.

London, Paris and Frankfurt dipped.

The latest moves in oil and the Fed’s action reassured investors and kept the 10-year US Treasury bond yield — a key indicator of borrowing costs throughout the world’s biggest economy — back below five percent.

Japan’s Nikkei was also helped by a drop in the yen against the dollar that came in the wake of the BoJ’s well-telegraphed decision to lift rates to their highest level since 1995.

Pressure has increased on officials to further tighten monetary policy as a spike in oil prices caused by the Middle East crisis — which shows little sign of ending anytime soon — is expected to keep putting a floor under inflation.

“Given that underlying CPI inflation has been approaching two percent and financial conditions have been accommodative, the bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate,” the BoJ said on its website.

But the yen slipped to more than 157 to the greenback, compared with around 156 earlier.

Stephen Innes at Quintex Intel suggested traders were jolted by the fact that the hike was not unanimous, passing by a 7-2 majority.

“For a market looking for evidence that the BoJ could shorten the distance between hikes, those dissents mattered,” he wrote.

“Traders were looking for signs that the Bank could move faster from here, yet two members were already arguing that even today’s move had come too soon.”

Focus will now turn to Governor Kazuo Ueda’s news conference due later in the day.

“Attention should fall on the forward swaps curve and the Bank’s guidance around the pace and urgency of further tightening,” wrote Chris Weston at Pepperstone.

“The market will be looking for confirmation that further normalisation remains firmly on the table, while assessing whether the Bank sees any urgency to move again.”
