World.title: KBR and AKT sign engineering deal for Iraq’s West Qurna gas capture project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – KBR and AKT have signed a contract to complete the comprehensive engineering design for Iraq’s West Qurna Gas Capture Project, which advances Basrah Gas Company’s efforts to collect associated gas and minimize flaring in southern oilfields.

KBR will offer engineering expertise for the design work in partnership with AKT, since the project is part of Basrah Gas Company’s (BGC) larger gas collection initiative.

The project aims to collect associated gas generated with crude oil from West Qurna, which would otherwise be burnt, enabling more of the resource to be processed and consumed domestically.

Expanding gas capture is critical to Iraq’s attempts to prevent flaring, enhance local gas supplies, and make better use of its energy resources, especially as the country seeks to reduce its dependency on imported gas and fuel for power production.

The West Qurna development is one of many gas projects now underway in southern Iraq, where some of the country’s major oilfields are located and significant amounts of associated gas are generated.

KBR said that the deal strengthens its role in gas monetization and energy infrastructure projects in Iraq and the broader Middle East.

The companies did not disclose the contract’s amount or the timeframe for completing the detailed engineering design.

World.title: Iraq PM to meet Trump in New York as US ties shift to investment
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi will visit the United States next week to address the UN General Assembly and meet with President Donald Trump, as Baghdad aims to pivot its relationship with Washington away from security cooperation and toward long-term commerce and investment.

According to government spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi, Al-Zaidi will give Iraq’s presentation to the UN General Assembly in New York, as well as meet with Trump and other international leaders.

He is also slated to attend an economic-related conference of the United States Chamber of Commerce.

The trip comes barely two months after Al-Zaidi’s first official visit to the United States, during which Baghdad announced 48 agreements and collaborations with American corporations spanning energy, infrastructure, technology, healthcare, and finance.

During discussions in Washington and Houston, Al-Zaidi advocated for more US investment in Iraq and met with leaders from key American corporations.

According to the US Chamber, the agreements and memorandums announced during the visit were worth more than $60 billion and included corporations such as Chevron, ConocoPhillips, GE Vernova, Google, JPMorgan Chase, and PepsiCo.

Al-Zaidi also met with Chevron officials in Houston as Iraq explored agreements for large oilfields and new export infrastructure aimed at diversifying the country’s pathways to international markets.

The current visit takes place only days before the conclusion of the US-led coalition operation in Iraq on September 30.

Al-Aboudi regarded the date as a watershed moment for Iraqi sovereignty, stating that relations with Washington will shift toward long-term economic collaboration, boosting Al-Zaidi’s desire to make investment and private-sector links the basis of the next phase of the Iraq-US relationship.

World.title: Palestinian state more distant than ever, a year after recognition
World.content:
Ramallah – When France, Britain and other Western powers last year recognised a Palestinian state, entrepreneur Adam Bader felt a sense of hope.

“I was happy when I heard about it,” said Bader, 27, who lives in the occupied West Bank’s city of Tulkarem, which has seen repeated Israeli raids in recent years.

“Now a year on, we’re not seeing any improvement. On the contrary,” he said. “The situation is getting worse by the day and no one can do anything.”

A year after the recognition, Palestinian statehood in real, tangible terms looks more distant than ever.

Israeli settler violence has soared, Palestinians are being pushed into ever-smaller areas and the Palestinian Authority has only been weakened.

French President Emmanuel Macron, vowing to find a new path forward amid global outrage over Israel’s offensive in Gaza, on September 22, 2025 led a special UN summit to recognise a Palestinian state.

Ten countries, also including Britain, Canada and Australia, recognised Palestinian statehood, bringing the number of UN member-states doing so to around 157, more than four-fifths of the UN membership.

But Israel, which enjoys support from the United States, adamantly rejects Palestinian statehood, and has stepped up efforts to isolate the Palestinian Authority of president Mahmoud Abbas.

While Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stopped short last year of formally annexing the West Bank, observers say unofficial annexation is creeping as his right-wing government approves an unprecedented number of settlements.

“Recognition makes the two-state solution a reality politically and diplomatically, but unfortunately on the ground it still depends on the illegal behaviour of Israel, which is not implementing international resolutions,” Omar Awadallah, deputy foreign affairs minister of the Palestinian Authority, told AFP.

Ines Abdel Razek, a Palestinian political analyst, said that recognition of a state of Palestine amounted to little without measures to support its existence and counter Israeli actions.

“The two-state solution’s become a diplomatic refrain to avoid looking at reality in the face,” she said.

– ‘No future’ –

Across the West Bank’s limestone hills, thousands of Israeli flags line roads used by Israeli settlers, with the occasional graffiti “No future in Palestine” stencilled on walls, as a call for Palestinians to leave.

Netanyahu argues that a Palestinian state would be a “reward for terrorism” after Hamas on October 7, 2023 carried out the deadliest attack ever on Israel, which responded with a massive military operation in Gaza.

“As long as I am prime minister, an Iranian-controlled Palestinian state will not be established — neither in Gaza nor in Judea and Samaria. Period,” Netanyahu said last month, using the biblical name for the West Bank.

Iran, which the United States and Israel attacked in February, backs Hamas in Gaza. The Palestinian Authority, centred in the West Bank, is led by Fatah, Hamas’s archrival.

Ahead of the anniversary, Israel ordered the closure of the UK consulate serving Palestinians from Jerusalem, angered after Britain led France and Canada in sanctions over rising attacks by settlers.

Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, explaining the move, said Britain’s Labour government was attempting to “force upon Israel” a Palestinian state but the attempt was “doomed to fail”.

– Rising attacks –

The Palestinian Authority, established in the 1990s, has been starved of cash in part by Israel’s decision not to give it customs revenue it collects on its behalf, and struggles to pay its civil servants.

Israel has objected to the Palestinian Authority’s historic payments to families of imprisoned or slain Palestinians, including those who carried out attacks against Israelis.

In early 2025, Israel built nearly 1,000 gates in the West Bank, at the entrances of nearly all villages and towns, which it closes on occasion to control Palestinian movement.

Palestinians have also decried a policy of “maximum land, minimum Arabs” whereby settlers push out isolated herder communities from rural areas in order to establish settler outposts.

The UN says extremist settlers have been responsible for an average of six attacks per day on Palestinians and Palestinian property in the West Bank in 2026.

Palestinians complain that Israeli perpetrators of violence are almost never brought to justice, and are protected by the army.

Defence Minister Israel Katz has called for police to take over civilian matters from the military in the West Bank, a move observers see as a further step towards annexation.

Sameh, a software engineer in Nablus, still sees last year’s move as a positive sign, but concedes the difficulties.

“There is still a big distance between international recognition and seeing that recognition translated into reality on the ground,” he said.

World.title: CM Vijay to launch one-gram gold ring scheme for babies born in Tamil Nadu govt hospitals
World.content:
Tamil Nadu govt to provide one-gram gold rings to newborns

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay will launch the one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns on September 28, the state government said. The one-gram gold rings will be provided to babies born in government hospitals under the scheme.The rings will have a unique serial number and be packed in tamper-proof packaging, the government said. As many as 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings have been procured for the first instalment of the scheme.The government said beneficiaries must be permanent residents of Tamil Nadu to be eligible for the one-gram gold ring scheme.Vijay had announced the one-gram gold ring scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of âThaimaaman Seerâ. The scheme will have retrospective effect from June 22, Vijayâs birthday. A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of âThaimaamanâ.The state has allocated around Rs 755.83 crore annually for the scheme, which will cover newborns delivered at government institutions. The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings and supply them based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee the implementation and monitoring of the scheme.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The scheme is open to Tamil Nadu residents whose children are born at government institutions. Mothers will have to submit proof of residence, with documents including ration cards, voter identity cards, Aadhaar, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates accepted.The government said the initiative was aimed at combining cultural significance with public healthcare.

World.title: Mamata gets 'footballer', but can she win TMC 'khela'? Maharashtra has a red-card warning
World.content:
For 28 years, TMC has been

and

has been TMC in West Bengal; the two are almost synonymous with each other. And for voters, the political shorthand for Mamata Banerjee has been almost absurdly simple: two flowers on grass.

Now, that shorthand has been taken away.

The Election Commission on Friday allotted Mamata's faction a new name - 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress', with a football player as its symbol. The rival Arup Roy faction will contest as 'Democratic Trinamool Congress', with an 'envelope' as its symbol. The decision follows the commission's September 17 order freezing the original All India Trinamool Congress name and its reserved 'flowers and grass' symbol for the upcoming bypolls.

Mamata Banerjee is now fighting to save her own party name and symbol.

But the EC's interim arrangement is only the first chapter. The substantive question of who gets the original TMC name and symbol will have to be decided under Paragraph 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.

And here, the story might look familiar.

The same movie was played out twice in Maharashtra in recent years, first with the Shiv Sena and then with the Nationalist Congress Party.

They do not know that I cannot leave TMC. It will always be with me until I leave this world. Absolutely dirty game, but we are also ready to fight it out. I want the BJP to go from India. We want solidarity in INDIA alliance. Mamata Banerjee

What Shiv Sena and NCP cases tell us

When Shiv Sena split between Uddhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde in 2022, the EC first froze the party's 'bow and arrow' symbol and allotted separate interim identities to the two factions.





In its February 2023 decision, the commission eventually recognised the Shinde faction as the Shiv Sena and allowed it to use the original name and symbol.

The NCP followed a similar path. After Ajit Pawar's rebellion in July 2023, the EC decided in February 2024 that the faction led by Sharad Pawar had a weaker numerical claim, while Ajit Pawar's group had superior support in the organisational and legislative wings.

It consequently recognised Ajit Pawar's faction as the NCP and allowed it to use the party's 'clock' symbol. The EC order specifically recorded that the Ajit Pawar group had "far superior numerical support" in the organisational and legislative wings.

That is a crucial part of the precedent for the ongoing TMC dispute.

The conclusion from the Maharashtra cases may be that the EC followed the majority of legislators.

The legal position is more nuanced. Paragraph 15 allows the election commission to examine rival claims through the party's organisational structure as well as its legislative strength.

In its May 11, 2023 Constitution Bench judgment in Subhash Desai vs Principal Secretary, Governor of Maharashtra, the Supreme Court held that the EC need not determine a party's identity solely through the numerical strength of its MLAs or MPs while adjudicating a dispute under Paragraph 15 of the Symbols Order.

The court said the EC could consider the majority in the organisational wing, the party constitution and, where appropriate, "any other appropriate test", underlining that a split among legislators is not necessarily the same as a split in the political party itself.

The timeline of TMC split.

The observation is particularly relevant to the TMC case, where the eventual contest could involve competing claims over the party's organisational structure and not just a headcount of elected representatives.

The Supreme Court, however, did not itself decide which faction should receive the Shiv Sena's name and symbol, leaving the merits of that EC decision to separate proceedings.

That distinction could matter considerably in the TMC case.

The Shiv Sena and NCP rebels who ultimately secured the original party identities had substantial support among sitting legislators. The TMC's internal arithmetic, however, has to be examined on its own terms.

The 2026 assembly election setback changed the party's internal arithmetic sharply. Its tally fell from 215 of 294 seats in 2021 to 80, and within weeks, 58 MLAs backed expelled leader Ritabrata Banerjee as their legislature party leader. He was subsequently recognised as leader of the opposition, while the rebel camp rejected Mamata's nominee, Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay.

The revolt then spread to Parliament, with 20 Lok Sabha MPs led by Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar joining the NCPI and backing the BJP-led NDA.

The TMC challenged their move before the Lok Sabha speaker and sought their disqualification. What began as a post-election leadership challenge had thus expanded into a contest over control of the party's legislative and parliamentary wings.

Mamata Banerjee, however, remains the founder and central political figure of the organisation, and her camp's claim is not based only on her position as party leader but also on its organisational and electoral support.

The 'new' Mamata party

The names allotted on Friday were revealing because neither faction chose to abandon the Trinamool identity. Mamata's camp was given 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress', while the rival Arup Roy camp became 'Democratic Trinamool Congress'. Both were, in different ways, laying claim to continuity with the party Mamata Banerjee founded on January 1, 1998.

The distinction lies in the source of legitimacy each side is emphasising.

The rebels' use of 'Democratic' fits their argument that the TMC's organisational functioning should be more representative and less centred around one leader. Mamata's faction, meanwhile, has effectively put the founder's name where the old party identity used to be, making 'Mamata' part of its temporary electoral brand. That is particularly striking for a party whose political identity has been inseparable from its founder for almost three decades.

They had said beforehand, 'naam bhi rakhne doonga, nishaan bhi nahi rakhne doonga' (Neither let you keep the name nor the symbol). Who are these people? They are in power today; they might not be in power tomorrow. They should understand their limitations. Mamata Banerjee

The football-player symbol allotted to Mamata's faction also carries its own political resonance in Bengal. Football has long had a deep cultural presence in the state, but there is also a direct connection to the TMC's campaign vocabulary: 'Khela Hobe', the slogan that became a defining part of Mamata's 2021 assembly campaign against the BJP.

The symbol does not automatically recreate that campaign, but it gives the Mamata faction a ready-made visual association at a time when it has lost the party symbol voters have known for nearly three decades.

The test, however, has now changed in a rather dramatic way for the Mamata faction.

Nandigram changes the bypoll test

Mamata faction's candidate, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew her nomination from the Nandigram contest altogether, a day before the deadline. Her withdrawal came minutes after she met West Bengal chief minister and BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari, although the circumstances surrounding the meeting and her decision remain a matter of political speculation.

Mamata Banerjee later announced in a press conference that her party will now back the Congress candidate in Nandigram, and mentioned that the decision was taken "for the greater interest of the nation" and to strengthen the INDIA bloc.

"Rahul Gandhi rang me up yesterday, Arvind Kejriwal also expressed solidarity; we will all fight together against BJP. We will support Congress in the Nandigram bypoll to strengthen the INDIA bloc," Mamata said.

The Congress candidate, however, was also arrested by the cops late in the evening in a land-grab case.

That makes the October 6 bypolls a very different test from the one that appeared possible 24 hours earlier. The Mamata faction will now not be testing its new 'football-player' identity in Nandigram, but instead, ask its supporters to transfer their support to a Congress candidate, even as the rival TMC faction contests the seat under its own new identity.

The political significance is difficult to miss. At precisely the moment when the EC has stripped Mamata's faction of the old TMC name and symbol and given it a new identity, the faction is now out of a direct fight in Nandigram, a constituency that carries an unusually strong personal history for both Mamata and Suvendu Adhikari.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Nandigram was where Mamata lost to Adhikari in the 2021 assembly election, after making the constituency the centrepiece of her campaign.

Adhikari, who had moved from the TMC to the BJP before that election, defeated her by a narrow margin in a contest that became one of the defining episodes of Bengal politics. He subsequently retained Nandigram while also winning Bhowanipore, which he vacated to retain Nandigram, necessitating the October 6 bypoll.

The EC may eventually decide who owns the TMC name and symbol, but the October 6 bypolls will offer the first test of how much of the old Trinamool identity survives without 'flowers and grass'. In Rejinagar, the football player and envelope will face each other directly; in Nandigram, Mamata's decision to back Congress will test whether her political support can travel even when her own new party name and symbol are not on the ballot.

World.title: 'Will take all necessary actions': India's stern warning amid reports of Bangladesh reviewing 101 bilateral pacts
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India on Friday said it would take 'all necessary actions' to safeguard its interests after reports that Bangladesh is reviewing 101 agreements and memorandums of understanding signed with New Delhi during the previous Awami League government.

Responding to news agency ANI, at the ministry of external affairsâ bi-weekly briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said New Delhi had not received any formal communication from Dhaka on the review.

âWe also have seen some media reports on this matter, but nothing has been conveyed to us officially. Obviously, India will take all necessary actions to protect its interests,â Jaiswal said.

Bangladeshâs ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has said the agreements are being examined with the countryâs national interests in mind.

chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni said last week, âWe are reviewing the agreements that mean 101 MoUs and you will get its (review) result soon.â

The review covers arrangements signed under former prime minister Sheikh Hasinaâs Awami League government. Among the areas under scrutiny are agreements linked to the use of Chattogram and Mongla ports, connectivity and other bilateral projects. Dhaka has not announced a blanket cancellation of the agreements.





The developments come as India-Bangladesh ties face scrutiny over trade, transit, energy, border management and water-sharing issues. India has previously extended more than $7 billion through Lines of Credit for infrastructure projects in Bangladesh, while bilateral arrangements have also enabled the movement of Indian cargo through Bangladeshi ports.

Water-sharing remains another key issue. The 1996 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty is due to expire in December 2026, while the long-pending Teesta agreement remains unresolved.

On Friday, Jaiswal said existing mechanisms for discussions on shared rivers remained operational.

âIn the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty between Bangladesh and India, we have the Joint Rivers Commission mechanism to discuss all water-related issues. Technical-level meetings on water matters continue to be held,â he said.

India and Bangladesh share 54 rivers, Jaiswal said, adding that water-related issues are handled through the Joint Rivers Commission and other established bilateral mechanisms.

The review of the 101 agreements is now expected to provide a clearer indication of whether Dhaka intends to retain, amend or renegotiate specific arrangements.

World.title: ‘Vitiate regional security’: India on Houthi Red Sea attacks, flags threat to Bab-el-Mandeb
World.content:
The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Tuesday stated that India remains deeply concerned about escalation of the situation in the Red Sea region, amid latest strikes exchanged between Yemenâs Houthi group and Saudi Arabia.

NEW DELHI: India on Friday expressed deep concern over the deteriorating security situation in the Red Sea region, condemning attacks on Saudi Arabia and warning that the escalation threatens regional peace and freedom of navigation through the Bab-el-Mandeb. The Ministry of External Affairs also said the Indian embassy remains in contact with Saudi authorities over the case of an Indian citizen who has reportedly received a prison sentence.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said attacks on Saudi sovereign territory, including those targeting civilians and economic assets, were unacceptable and could further undermine security in the region."About the situation in the Red Sea area and in Saudi Arabia, we are deeply concerned with the escalation in the security situation in the Red Sea area. You would have seen our statement earlier as well; we have expressed our condemnation of the attacks on Saudi sovereign territory, including on civilians and on economic assets. You would have also seen our statement which we issued following the attempted attack on the holy city of Mecca. Such attacksâI need not elaborate or reiterateâthey vitiate the regional security, they impact or undermine regional peace and security, and also threaten freedom of navigation through the Bab-el-Mandeb.And obviously, for various reasons, this is totally unacceptable to us. We hope that there is early restoration of peace and stability in the region."Jaiswal said India was particularly concerned about the implications for maritime security and navigation through the Bab-el-Mandeb, a key waterway connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.India monitoring case of citizen in Saudi ArabiaResponding to concerns over an Indian citizen in Saudi Arabia who has reportedly been sentenced to prison, Jaiswal said Indian diplomatic authorities remain engaged with local governments in cases involving the safety and welfare of Indian nationals."Concerns have been expressed regarding the situation of an Indian citizen in Saudi Arabia. Regarding this matter where you mentioned that they have received a prison sentence, I do not have a specific answer for you right now on what their current situation is, but I will gather the details and update you. However, I would like to say one thing: wherever Indian citizens are in any corner of the world, it is our commitment that we remain constantly dedicated to their safety, care, and welfare."

World.title: Over 5.10 lakh people benefited from govt pilgrimage scheme: Punjab minister
World.content:
Punjab tourism minister Tarunpreet Singh Sond on Thursday said

government's 'Mukh Mantri Tirath Yatra' scheme has facilitated pilgrimage for 5,10,807 devotees to various religious destinations in and outside the state.

He said the scheme aims to facilitate elderly residents who wish to visit religious places by providing them free travel and other essential facilities.

The scheme was launched on November 9, 2025, and in its first phase, around four lakh pilgrims undertook journeys to Sri Amritsar Sahib, Sri Anandpur Sahib and Mata Naina Devi, he said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The scheme was expanded on August 12 to include additional religious destinations such as Shri Khatu Shyam-Salasar Balaji Dham, Haridwar-Rishikesh and Mathura-Vrindavan, he said.

Under the expanded scheme, people aged 50 years and above are eligible to undertake the pilgrimage. The Punjab government provides AC sleeper bus travel, accommodation and food free of cost to eligible pilgrims, the minister said.

Special arrangements have been made to ensure the safety, security and convenience of pilgrims during the journey. A team of general and medical attendants is deployed on every bus, while dedicated teams are stationed at the destinations to facilitate the pilgrims, according to Sond.

Arrangements for pilgrims include air-conditioned accommodation with adequate washroom facilities, along with food and other necessary amenities during the pilgrimage, he added.

World.title: Lack of battery car forces passengers to slog longer distance at Virudhunagar junction
World.content:
The elderly, physically-challenged and the sick passengers are made to slog for long distance from one platform to another at Virudhunagar railway junction as the battery-operated car has been rendered “out of order” for long.

The car had been useful to ferry young children, old passengers, pregnant women and those carrying heavy luggages from one platform to another through the trolley pathway at the end of the platforms.

The junction has been handling several trains, including Vande Bharat, express trains from Tirunelveli, Thoothukudi, Kanniyakumari, Coimbatore, Chennai and Bengaluru and passenger trains to various places like Sengottai.

The battery-operated car had higher utility considering that the junction lacked lift and escalator facility. The passengers were ready to pay ₹10 to cross the platforms and to get picked up and dropped at the entrance. They are put to untold sufferings as the car is not being operated for the last few weeks. In addition to walking for longer distance, the passengers are also forced to lug their luggage all the way.

World.title: VACB arrests police officer while accepting bribe
World.content:
The Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) apprehended a civil police officer attached to the Nedumangad police station while accepting a bribe on Friday (September 18, 2026).

The accused, identified as Biju, was caught by the Vigilance officers. He was arrested on the basis of a complaint by a Panavoor native who had approached the Nedumangad police station for documents related to a road accident that occurred in March in order to claim compensation.

Biju purportedly demanded that the paperwork be routed through a lawyer of his choice, despite the complainant having a different legal representative. The officer then contacted the lawyer directly, demanding a bribe of ₹10,000 to hand over the case documents.

The complainant subsequently informed the VACB authorities who laid a trap. Biju was allegedly caught while accepting the money outside the police station premises.

World.title: Hyderabad man caught with 14 ecstasy pills, leads to Goa-Mumbai supply trail
World.content:
A 29-year-old man who allegedly travelled from Mumbai to Hyderabad carrying ecstasy pills for two acquaintances was apprehended near the Miyapur Metro Station, with the investigation now pointing to a wider Goa-Mumbai-Hyderabad drug supply network.

The Elite Action Group for Drug Law Enforcement (EAGLE), along with Miyapur police, apprehended Pola Suresh Gopi, 29, and seized 14 ecstasy pills containing MDMA, weighing about nine grams, and two mobile phones.

According to investigators, Gopi, a native of Miryalaguda in Nalgonda district, who currently resides in Hyderabad, moved to Goa in July 2024 and entered the rental-property business. It was during his stay there that he allegedly came in contact with people involved in the sale of narcotics and began procuring drugs for acquaintances and selling them at higher prices.

The investigation has identified two alleged suppliers, one Baba in Goa and Danish Alam Ansari of Mumbai, both of whom are absconding.

Police said Gopi initially procured drugs from Baba through cash transactions in Goa. He later allegedly came into contact with Ansari, who would visit Goa and sell drugs.

The immediate trail to Hyderabad began around 10 days before Gopi was apprehended, when two acquaintances in the city allegedly contacted him seeking ecstasy pills.

Investigators said Gopi travelled to Mumbai on September 16 and allegedly bought 29 ecstasy pills from Ansari for ₹22,500, paying through a bank transfer. The pills were purchased at ₹750 each.

Of the 29 pills, he allegedly sold 15 in Mumbai to an acquaintance identified only as ‘Munna’, a resident of Goa, and retained the remaining 14. He then boarded a private bus from Nerul in Mumbai and travelled to Hyderabad with the pills, allegedly intending to supply them here.

Acting on information, EAGLE personnel and Miyapur police intercepted him while he was passing through the vicinity of Miyapur Metro Station, and recovered the pills.

Investigators are now examining his two mobile phones and other evidence to identify those allegedly involved in procuring, transporting and distributing the drug, as well as customers and financial transactions linked to the network.

A case has been registered at Miyapur police station under relevant provisions of the NDPS Act. Efforts are under way to trace Baba and Ansari and establish the full extent of the interstate supply chain.

World.title: Alumni network key to institutional growth: BITS Pilani Group V-C
World.content:
A strong and globally connected alumni network can contribute greatly to the growth of educational institutions and create opportunities for future generations, said BITS Pilani Group Vice-Chancellor V. Ramagopal Rao.

Speaking at the Alumni Ruby Reunion of the third batch (1982-86) of Kakatiya Institute of Technology & Science, Warangal (KITS-W), here on Friday, Mr. Rao, an alumnus of the batch and former director of IIT-Delhi, urged alumni to further support the institution by setting up an endowment fund for underprivileged students.

He said KITS-W alumni had stayed closely connected despite living in different parts of the world, creating a robust global network. He urged past and present students to uphold the institution’s legacy through integrity, professionalism and social responsibility.

KITS-W principal K. Ashoka Reddy said the alumni had been supporting the institution through seminars and workshops on emerging technologies, industrial visits, internships, support for start-ups, procurement of advanced laboratory equipment and training programmes to improve placement opportunities for undergraduate and postgraduate students.

The 40-year reunion was inaugurated by KITS-W chairman V. Lakshmikantha Rao, treasurer P. Narayana Reddy, vice-president K. Deviprasad and former faculty members. More than 120 alumni from across the globe attended the reunion.

World.title: Devikulam range in Keralam’s Idukki witnesses three deaths due to wild elephant attack in four months
World.content:
Areas under the Devikulam forest range in Idukki continues to remain a death trap for people amid recurring wild elephant attacks. According to officials, three people have lost their lives in encounters with elephants here over the past four months.

The latest victim was identified as Shiv Kumar, 30, a migrant labourer hailing from Madhya Pradesh, who was trampled to death by a wild elephant near Ayyanpara in Santhanpara on Thursday night.

Shiv Kumar worked at a cardamom plantation in Ayyanpara and lived in a temporary shed with his colleagues. On Thursday evening, he and a co-worker visited Pethotty. On the way back, they were attacked by a wild elephant. His companion managed to escape without injuries.

The post-mortem examination was conducted at the Idukki Government Medical College Hospital. Officers confirmed that the department will bear the expenses to transport his mortal remains to his native place and will provide compensation to the bereaved family.

“It is suspected that a tusker from Mathikettan Shola National Park attacked the workers,” said a forest officer.

In similar incidents, on August 27, S. Ochappan, 68, a farmer from Tamil Nadu, was killed at Thalakkulam near Pooppara. Earlier, on June 8, Mari, 36, a Chinnakkanal resident, was trampled to death, and her 11-year-old son sustained injuries in a similar attack.

Following the incident on Thursday, the BJP Santhanpara panchayat committee staged a protest in front of the Bodimettu forest section office on Friday, alleging that the negligence of the Forest department led to the tragedy.

World.title: CM to attend cleanliness drive at Beach Road
World.content:
Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu will take part in the State government’s flagship programme - ‘Swachch Andhra – Swarna Andhra’ at the Beach Road in Visakhapatnam Saturday. As part of the programme, he will take part in a cleanliness programme and also interact with the sanitation staff.

During the programme at AU Engineering College grounds, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu will launch five key water supply and infrastructure projects worth a total of ₹1,838 crore, being undertaken by Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) to further strengthen Visakhapatnam’s drinking water supply system.

Of the five projects, the Chief Minister will lay foundation stones for the ₹725 crore 24/7 water supply project, ₹117 crore modernisation of bulk and semi-bulk water supply connections, ₹150 crore dedicated industrial water supply pipeline, and ₹400 crore water supply and sewerage works under AMRUT 2.0. He will also inaugurate the ₹446 crore NRW Reduction and 24/7 Water Supply project, the Commissioner said.

Traffic curbs

Visakhapatnam traffic police on Friday issued an advisory chalking out the traffic restrictions in and around Andhra University expecting thousands of attendees at the venue for the title deeds distribution programme. The traffic restriction would be in place from 6 a.m. on Saturday to facilitate smoother traffic flow through Visakhapatnam.

The police stated in the advisory that heavy vehicles travelling from Srikakulam and Vizianagaram to Anakapalli via Visakhapatnam will be diverted to Andapuram, Pendurthi and Sabbavaram from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m, while heavy vehicles travelling from Anakapalli towards Srikakulam and Vizianagaram will be diverted to Lankelapalem, Sabbavaram, Pendurthi and Anandapuram during the same period.

Meanwhile, the police have issued routes to buses and vehicles ferrying beneficiaries from various localities between Gajuwaka to Bheemili.

World.title: Eight ‘MLA wards’ gain attention as local body bypolls near in Keralam
World.content:
Of the 38 local body wards going to the bypolls on September 28 in Keralam, eight could be politically crucial as these wards fell vacant following the election of their incumbent representatives to the State Assembly.

Though the outcome of the interim polls will not have any impact on the existing political equations in the eight respective local bodies, they could be interpreted as a sign of the people’s response to the four-month-old United Democratic Front (UDF) government in the State.

Held by UDF

All but one of the eight wards were held by the UDF, and a drop in the number could be embarrassing for the ruling front that won the State elections by a landslide with 102 seats in the 140-seat Assembly.

The Left Democratic Front (LDF), meanwhile, appears to be keen to wrest the local body seats left vacant by UDF MLAs as it could help the front big time tide over the embarrassment caused by the drubbing in the Assembly elections.

Three of the eight ‘MLA segments’ are district panchayat divisions. While the Kallara division of the Thiruvananthapuram district panchayat fell vacant following the election of Congress’s Muhammed Sudeersha S. as the Vamanapuram MLA, the victory of Kerala Congress’s Vinu Job Kuzhimannil from the Changanassery Assembly constituency paved the way for the bypoll in the Thrikkodithanam division of the Kottayam district panchayat. The bypoll in the Pallasana division of the Palakkad district panchayat was necessitated following the election of CPI(M)’s T.M. Sasi as the Altahur MLA.

Ayyappankavu division of Kochi Corporation and Kuttichira of Kozhikode Corporation are going to the bypolls following the election of Congress’s Deepak Joy and Indian Union Muslim League (IUML)’s Fathima Thahiliya from Thripunithura and Perambra Assembly segments, respectively.

The bypoll in the Paruthikkavu ward of the Chittur-Thathamangalam municipality in Palakkad was necessitated by the election of Congress’s Sumesh Achuthan as the MLA of Chittur.

Pallickal ward of the Mananthavady block panchayat in Wayanad and Kalleli ward of the Aruvappulam grama panchayat in Pathanamthitta fell vacant with the election of Congress’s Usha Vijayan and C.V. Santhakumar from Mananthavady and Adoor Assembly constituencies, respectively.

On the campaign front

Both the UDF and LDF have deployed their top leaders on the campaign front in a move showing the political urgency of the bypolls. “The other day, UDF convener Adoor Prakash addressed a campaign rally in Kalleli ward and three DCC general secretaries have been given the charge of the campaign. We are highlighting the achievements of the UDF government in a short span of time,” said Mr. Santhakumar, MLA. Admitting that the voters sometimes complain about power cuts, he said the UDF workers keep explaining the circumstances that led to such a situation.

CPI(M) State committee member A.N. Shamseer said the bypolls will be analysing the four-month performance of the V.D. Satheesan-led UDF government. “The campaign is being run by respective local leadership with party secretariat and State committee members given charge for different wards. We will retain our incumbent seats and wrest more including the Thiruvananthapuram district panchayat division. The bypoll will mark the comeback of the LDF,” he said.

Mr. Sudeersha, MLA, said he has a “natural responsibility” about the poll campaign in his Kallara division. “We are aware of the political relevance of the bypoll and confident about retaining the seat,” he said.

A.A. Rahim, another CPI(M) State committee member, said the LDF looks at each bypoll, even in ward, with utmost political seriousness, and is highlighting issues including power cuts, uncertainty over welfare pension distribution and KIIFB projects on the campaign front. “Chief Minister Satheesan keeps getting exposed day by day and we are making it a discussion point among the people,” he said.

BJP State secretary Jiji Joseph, meanwhile, said the party is contesting in all wards and will make its presence felt in the bypolls.

World.title: Loan racket busted; 5 arrested
World.content:
The police have busted a loan racket and arrested five persons on Friday.

Police said businessman Jayachandran, 47, from Chennai approached one Mohammed Akhtar, 23, also from Chennai, for getting loan to the tune of ₹1 crore from private lenders. Promising Mr. Jayachandran of arranging for the loan, Akhtar asked him to give the facilitator’s commission of ₹1 lakh.

After Mr. Jayachandran agreed to it, Akhtar took him to Venkatesh of Agasthiyarpatti near Vickramasingapuram in the district, where they showed him several bundles of currency notes and took signatures in seven cheques and loan agreement documents.

When the police received information about this murky transaction, police raided the house of Venkatesh, where they found fake currency notes and genuine notes, all to the tune of ₹3.68 lakh.

Besides seizing the currency notes, the police also picked-up Venktesh and his associates Rajesh, 23, Sivasubramanian, 23, Kathirvel Pandi, 23, all from Therkku Paappaankulam near Kallidaikurichi, and Mohammed Akthar, who were present in the house.

Superintendent of Police Vishwesh Balasubramnaian Shastri said the borrowers should always approach only the nationalised and approved banks and recognised financial institutions for availing loans instead of approaching the individuals for any financial transactions.

World.title: 15 cops among 21 martyred in blast at Kohat Police Lines, more than 80 injured
World.content:
PESHAWAR: At least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred on Friday when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities, according to senior police and district health officials.

District Health Officer Dr Nasir Hassan Afridi confirmed the toll to Dawn, adding that more than 80 people were injured, with three in critical condition.

Footage aired on television showed citizens gathered next to a building with a collapsed wall, digging through rubble and helping the injured. The bomb attack caused severe damage to the mosque structure.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed told Dawn that a vehicle-borne suicide bomber initially struck the building’s gate, following which several attackers headed towards the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) building, where they were neutralised. Around three others tried to move towards the Special Branch building.

According to police, at least one attacker was holed up inside the compound and a clearance operation was underway.

Meanwhile, the CTD said the Additional IG CTD reached the site of the Kohat attack. An exchange of fire between CTD personnel and the terrorists was ongoing, the department said, adding that the Additional IG had entered the site himself to take part in the operation and lead the personnel.

The attack was claimed by the Hafiz Gul Bahadur-led Ittehadul Mujahideen.

The attack

According to IG Hameed and police statements, the attack began when a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) detonated at the boundary wall near the mosque inside the Kohat Police Lines.

At least seven attackers then breached the compound and headed towards the CTD and Special Branch buildings. One of the attackers, a suicide bomber, was killed by law enforcers along with five others, according to a police statement.

At least one attacker was subsequently cornered, prompting police personnel to launch a clearance operation. At around 3:30pm, police said the operation was “in its final stages”.

“The operation will continue until the complete elimination of Fitna-ul-Khawarij,” the IG was quoted as saying, adding that the police’s morale remained high.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

Separately, KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi sought a detailed report on the incident, saying the targeting of innocent citizens was “deeply regrettable and unacceptable,” as per a statement issued by his office.

Residents gather on a street leading to a police facility, where ambulances are parked following a suicide attack in Kohat on September 18. — Reuters

He directed authorities to ensure immediate treatment for the injured. “The nation’s morale cannot be dampened by cowardly acts of terrorism,” he was quoted as saying.

In 2010, 20 people, mostly the relatives of policemen, were killed and more than 90 injured in a remote-controlled bomb blast inside a police colony located just behind the Kohat Police Lines.

Condemnations pour in

President Asif Ali Zardari, condemning the incident, vowed that the complete elimination of foreign-sponsored terrorists was “essential for national security”.

President Zardari wished the injured a swift recovery.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif sought a report on the blast from the concerned authorities. He also directed authorities to expedite relief operations, Radio Pakistan reported.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the blast, praying for the recovery of the injured.

“The entire nation stands with the security forces to eradicate terrorism,” he said in a statement.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said in his condemnation that terrorists’ “cowardly acts cannot weaken the nation’s resolve”.

A statement posted on his ministry’s X account said Naqvi expressed grief over the loss of lives in the attack and extended condolence to the bereaved.

“The nation is standing with the families of the martyrs in this moment of grief,” he was quoted as saying.

Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi also strongly condemned the suicide attack in Kohat and expressed his condolences over the deaths of police personnel and civilians.

In a video message, he said the people of KP had sacrificed more than 80,000 lives for Pakistan and continued to bear the brunt of the fight against terrorism.

“Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is Pakistan’s frontline province in the war against terrorism,” he said, adding that peace in Islamabad and the rest of the country was due to the sacrifices made by the people of the province.

He also criticised those who, he said, labelled the people of KP as terrorists, saying such remarks reopened their wounds and disrespected their martyrs.

Referring to comments by the chief minister of another province, Afridi said it was regrettable to suggest that the threat to Pakistan came from its other provinces rather than India. He said KP and the other provinces were patriotic and had made sacrifices for the country.

“Pakistan is our country, and we will not allow any conspiracy to succeed,” he said, adding that efforts to create division, prejudice and hatred among the people would be thwarted.

This is a developing story that is being updated as the situation evolves. Initial reports in the media can sometimes be inaccurate. We will strive to ensure timeliness and accuracy by relying on credible sources, such as concerned, qualified authorities and our staff reporters.

World.title: Govt to stop anyone marching on Islamabad 'in every possible way', says Naqvi
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said on Friday that the government would stop anyone from marching towards the federal capital “in every possible way” and file contempt of court proceedings against those who violated a recent Islamabad High Court (IHC) decision.

He was addressing a press conference in Islamabad alongside other officials.

The interior minister’s remarks came in the wake of PTI’s call for a nationwide protest , including in Islamabad, on September 27 to demand the release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

Last week, the administrations of the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad started preparations to counter the PTI’s announced countrywide protest, including a request for detention of activists, arranging containers, seeking additional personnel and procuring anti-riot gear.

At the outset of his press conference on Friday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said a detailed meeting had been held to discuss the upcoming protest call and the law and order situation. Officials from all provinces and federal law enforcement agencies had also attended the meeting.

“In light of the detailed IHC judgment, there is no possibility of ravaging the federal capital or any other province,” he said.

The minister said that if anyone took to the streets, the government would first pursue legal action by filing a contempt petition against them for violating the IHC order.

At the same time, he said, “We will stop the marchers in every possible way.” All law enforcement agencies had been informed of the decision “with all clarity”, Naqvi added.

He said weapons had been used and losses suffered in protests in the past.

“This time, we are communicating very clear rules of engagement to our law enforcement agencies. They will not remain silent if a bullet is fired at them,” he said.

He urged the protesting party’s leadership to hold demonstrations in their respective provinces and cities. “Plans for locking down the capital or charging into another province will never be allowed,” he said.

“It is our responsibility to stop this protest to ensure the protection of the lives and property of the capital’s residents,” the interior minister said.

The interior minister drew a distinction between a political protest aimed at pursuing political interests and a violent campaign involving people armed with weapons.

“There is complete clarity. The organisers of this march will be held accountable if even a single life is lost,” he said.

Naqvi said there were still some “sensible” voices within the opposition and hoped they would reconsider their decision. “There is only loss in it, no sort of gain at all,” he added.

He reiterated that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had repeatedly invited the opposition from the floor of parliament to hold talks on all issues. “If you want to resolve matters through violent mobs, we are ready for it,” he said.

The interior minister reaffirmed that the government had finalised its preparations and all law enforcement agencies were ready.

“We will not allow people to spread turbulence as happened in the past,” he said.

In its judgment issued on the same day, the IHC ruled that any activity resulting in infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights amounts to a violation of the Constitution.

It warned that public office holders responsible for such violations would also be deemed to have breached their oath of office.

The court also held that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the fundamental rights of other citizens.

Kohat attack

Commenting on the attack in Kohat, Naqvi said security agencies had been fighting terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

“We have to focus on this, rather than making strategies for mobilising masses, arranging transport and collecting money,” he said.

“After such incidents, it doesn’t suit you to call for long marches and, on the other hand, lift the dead bodies of martyrs,” he added.

He further said the KP chief minister and his cabinet should work towards eradicating terrorism with the same spirit with which they were carrying out campaigns for long marches.

Earlier in the day, at least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines. More than 80 people were injured, according to the officials.

The incident was followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities, according to senior police and district health officials.

World.title: IHC rules infringement of fundamental rights breaches Constitution ahead of PTI’s Sept 27 protest
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that any activity resulting in infringement of citizens’ fundamental rights amounts to a violation of the Constitution, warning that public office holders responsible for such violations would also be deemed to have breached their oath of office.

The ruling came in a detailed 37-page judgment on a petition concerning the proposed nationwide PTI protest towards Islamabad on September 27, 2026. PTI had announced the march to demand release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

A citizen, Waqas Ahmed, had challenged the planned move on the grounds that the protest could disrupt routine life, traffic and business activities in the federal capital.

A three-member bench headed by Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and comprising Justice Muhammad Asif and Justice Muhammad Azam Khan issued the judgment.

The bench had announced its short order on September 14 after hearing Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Awan, Additional Attorney General Amir Rehman, the advocate generals of the four provinces and Islamabad, and counsel for the petitioner, Barrister Akhter Cheena.

The court described the case as requiring an “unusual degree of constitutional balance” between the right of political parties and citizens to assemble peacefully and express dissent, and the rights of other citizens to life, liberty, dignity, free movement, trade, business, property, and access to hospitals, educational institutions, courts and workplaces.

“The question is not whether a political party is entitled to protest. It plainly is, subject always to the Constitution and law,” the judgment observed.

The court held that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the fundamental rights of other citizens.

A key objection raised by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa advocate general concerned the territorial jurisdiction of the IHC over provincial authorities functioning outside Islamabad.

Rejecting the objection, the court held that Article 199(1)(c) empowered a high court to issue directions where a governmental power or function was being exercised “in, or in relation to” territory within its jurisdiction.

The court clarified, however, that the provision did not confer general supervisory jurisdiction over another province. A high court could issue directions to an authority outside its territorial seat where the governmental function had a direct and proximate legal relation with territory within its jurisdiction and intervention was necessary to protect fundamental rights there.

The bench also observed that where executive action or inaction was likely to infringe the fundamental rights of citizens within Islamabad, the court was under a “bounden duty” to assume jurisdiction under Article 199(1)(c).

The court also rejected the objection that the petition was not maintainable because KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had not been impleaded as a respondent. It noted that the Advocate General KP was representing both the provincial government and the chief minister.

The court further rejected the argument that the petitioner had an adequate alternate remedy under the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act, 2024.

It noted that no application had, admittedly, been filed under Section 3 of the Act and observed that its provisions had not been adhered to by the KP chief minister and others who had announced their intention to march towards Islamabad.

The judgment extensively referred to the Supreme Court’s decision in the Faizabad sit-in case, observing that the constitutional right to assemble and protest was protected but remained subject to restrictions where its exercise infringed the fundamental rights of others.

The IHC also referred to the Supreme Court judgment concerning the PTI march of May 25, 2022, noting that assurances regarding a peaceful rally and non-obstruction of the Srinagar Highway had not been honoured.

The judgment referred to damage to public and private property, fires in the Blue Area greenbelt, injuries to police personnel and the subsequent invocation of Article 245 to call in the armed forces in aid of civil power.

The court also cited its November 21, 2024 order directing that no protest, rally or sit-in be allowed in violation of the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act. It observed that the order had also been flouted.

During the proceedings, the court allowed the Islamabad deputy commissioner/district magistrate to place electronic material on record. Video clips of the 2022 and 2024 protests were played before the bench, which described the conduct shown in the footage as “highly disturbing and reflective of violence and aggression”.

The court noted that PTI was in power in KP during both episodes and observed that provincial government resources had been used in pursuit of political objectives.

Regarding the proposed September 27 march, the court held that the petitioner’s apprehension was not merely speculative. It noted that the date and destination of the proposed gathering were known and that statements attributed to the KP chief minister indicated that the date was firm and that he intended to lead the march.

While disposing of the petition, the court directed that no political party, political leader, provincial government or public office holder could lawfully occupy roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas, buildings or similar public places within, or leading to or from, Islamabad in a manner that obstructed free movement or hindered trade, business, professions or access to medical and educational facilities.

The provincial governments and chief ministers were directed to ensure that no government resources, public funds, officials, vehicles, machinery or equipment were used directly or indirectly to facilitate any march, rally or procession towards Islamabad.

They were also directed to ensure that no public servant was compelled, coerced or induced to participate in such activities.

The chief secretaries, police chiefs, federal interior secretary, chief commissioner and IG Islamabad were ordered to issue instructions prohibiting officials from complying with orders requiring them to facilitate such marches.

Officials facing coercion were directed to report the matter to the relevant authorities, while helplines or other communication mechanisms were ordered to be established for this purpose.

The court further directed the authorities to take departmental action against officials who violated the directions.

In a significant finding, the court held that any person whose activity resulted in a violation of the fundamental rights of citizens in Islamabad would be deemed to have violated the Constitution and would be liable for consequences under the law.

It further declared that any public office holder whose activity resulted in a violation of citizens’ fundamental rights would be deemed to have violated both the Constitution and his or her oath of office.

World.title: Lawyers' body announces boycott of court proceedings in Islamabad on Saturday to protest Imaan, Hadi's rearrest
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad Bar Association (IBA) has announced a boycott of court proceedings in the federal capital for Saturday (September 19) to protest the rearrest of human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, after the Supreme Court suspended their sentences and ordered their release on bail.

Imaan and Hadi were arrested late on Thursday in a second case after the SC ordered their release in a case pertaining to their posts on social media. The couple was sentenced to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in the case.

However, soon after their release on Thursday, Islamabad police personnel arrested the two outside Adiala jail in connection with another case and produced them before an anti-terrorism court, which sent them to jail on judicial remand.

The second case was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22, 2025 on a complaint by City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio. Imaan and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were named in the first information report (FIR).

The IBA expressed concern over the couple’s rearrest in a statement on Friday and announced that lawyers would not appear before any court in the capital on Sept 19 (Saturday).

The bar association said the arrest undermined the sanctity of judicial proceedings and amounted to a violation of fundamental rights and the rule of law.

It also expressed strong reservations over the practice of arresting individuals in connection with “unknown” FIRs. The IBA held that any attempt to circumvent or frustrate court orders was unacceptable.

It demanded the immediate release of Imaan and Hadi and called for complete details of the cases and circumstances surrounding their arrests to be made public.

The association vowed to take every possible measure to safeguard judicial independence, uphold the rule of law and protect fundamental human rights.

Amnesty International, HRCP demand immediate and unconditional release

Global rights watchdog Amnesty Inter­national condemned the arrest and held that the action demonstrated “authorities’ willingness to weaponise the legal system against critical voices”.

“Imaan and Hadi’s re-arrest dispels any pretence that the charges against them are anything other than a politically motivated attempt to punish them for their human rights work,” rights body’s South Asia director, Babu Ram Pant, said in a statement.

Pant held that charges were “not only absurd, but an insult to their lifelong commitment to human rights”.

The official called on the Pakistani authorities to release the couple immediately and “unconditionally, with no further charges to prolong their detention”.

“Imaan and Hadi should be free to meet their friends and family and to do the work they love – representing victims of human rights violations.”

Meanwhile, the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan, in a post on X, also demanded Imaan and Hadi’s release and withdrawal of all cases against them.

World.title: 'Petrol so expensive' that PTI lawmakers arrive at Sindh Assembly on donkey carts in protest
World.content:
KARACHI: PTI lawmakers in Sindh arrived at the provincial assembly on donkey carts — in protest.

“The ministers and [treasury] MPAs should also reach the assembly the same way on donkey carts,” PTI’s Sajjad Ali was seen saying in a video that showed him riding a donkey cart and holding a placard as he protested the “petrol bomb dropped on the people”.

Other MPAs, led by Ali, also held placards and raised slogans against the federal government over the recent increase in petrol prices. They rode donkey carts from areas near the assembly to its main gate and demanded the government withdraw the increase in petroleum prices immediately.

Speaking on the occasion, Ali said that the protest was aimed at highlighting the plight of the common man due to skyrocketing fuel prices.

“Petrol has become so expensive that we cannot even come to the assembly in our vehicles,” he said, adding that the people were bearing the brunt of the government’s policies.

Renewed hostilities in the Middle East, which have resulted in disruption of major oil supply routes, have caused fuel prices to rise in the past two months.

Currently, the government adjusts fuel prices daily. After the latest change on Thursday, the price of petrol stands at Rs390.79 per litre while high-speed diesel (HSD) costs Rs424.92 per litre. These prices also include Rs114 per litre levied by the government in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

On Thursday, a joint meeting of the Executive Committee and Rules Committee of the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) also strongly condemned the unprecedented daily increases in fuel prices, demanding that the government take measures to control the increases and provide relief to citizens.

Meanwhile, the government has introduced a “relief scheme” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Under the scheme, motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqis, as well as other two- and three-wheeler users, are eligible for relief on 20 litres of petrol per month. The owners of small cars with engines up to 800cc will receive the Rs100 per litre relief on 30 litres of petrol every month.

The subsidy scheme faced snags on Thursday, the first day of its nationwide rollout, as many petrol pumps declined to honour the digital app launched for the purpose, claiming that they lacked the system needed to provide petrol at Rs100 per litre less.

World.title: Lahore ATC disposes of petition by PTI leader Hammad Azhar’s mother, wife seeking permission to meet him
World.content:
LAHORE: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Friday disposed of a petition filed on behalf of PTI leader Hammad Azhar’s mother and wife, seeking permission for them to meet the former federal minister, who is in police custody on physical remand in a May 9 case.

ATC-IV Judge Sardar Muhammad Akram Khan passed the order on September 17.

The petition sought directions to the relevant authorities to allow the petitioners to meet Azhar, who is confined in police lock-up, and to grant him access to legal counsel.

In his order, the judge noted that, when asked, the prosecution’s counsel had no response regarding Rule 26.28 of the Police Rules, 1934 — the provision governing family and legal access to people in police custody.

The judge also observed that the petitioners had earlier filed a similar writ petition before the Lahore High Court (LHC), which was dismissed as withdrawn, with liberty to seek a remedy before the appropriate forum.

The judge further noted that the case file did not show that the petitioners had first approached the police under Rule 26.28 before moving the court.

In light of this, the ATC judge directed the petitioners to submit a written application to the station house officer (SHO) of Sarwar Road police and instructed that, if approached, the SHO must strictly comply with the requirements of Rule 26.28 of the Police Rules, 1934.

With these observations, the judge disposed of the petition.

Advocate Zain Sheikh appeared for the petitioners and Deputy District Public Prosecutor Nayyar Naveed represented the state.

Hammad Azhar was arrested in Multan earlier this month and handed over to Lahore police in connection with cases related to the May 9 riots, including the attack on Jinnah House.

Azhar’s mother and wife had approached the ATC against the police for allegedly denying his family and lawyer access to him.

Ishrat Azhar, the mother, and Marriam Hammad, the wife, had filed a joint petition through their counsel, Abuzar Salman Niazi.

World.title: PM Shehbaz directs inclusion of 20-year-old bikes, rickshaws in fuel relief scheme
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday issued directives to include motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqis that were registered after Jan 1, 2006 in the govt’s recently announced fuel scheme.

“All motorcycles, rickshaws, and Qingqis registered after Jan 1, 2006, will be eligible for registration in the Prime Minister Fuel Relief Scheme,” the Prime Minister’s Office said in a post on the social media platform X.

“Now, those who drive 20-year-old motorcycles, rickshaws, and Qingqis will also be able to benefit from the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme,” it said.

PM Shehbaz Sharif had on Sep 13 announced a “relief scheme” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Under the scheme, owners of motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingqis, three-wheelers and vehicles with engines of up to 800cc will receive a Rs100 per litre relief on petrol.

Motorcycles, rickshaws and Qingqis, as well as other two- and three-wheeler users, are eligible for relief on 20 litres of petrol per month. Owners of small cars with engines up to 800cc will receive the Rs100 per litre relief on 30 litres of petrol every month.

Renewed hostilities in the Middle East, which have resulted in disruption of major oil supply routes, have caused fuel prices to rise in the past two months.

In addition to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz due to the US-Iran war, trade via Bab al-Mandab — which has become a vital route for Saudi oil exports in recent months — is also facing a rising threat from Houthi rebels.

The subsidy scheme faced snags on Thursday, the first day of its nationwide rollout, as many petrol pumps declined to honour the digital app, claiming they lacked the system needed to provide petrol at Rs100 per litre less.

A day prior, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) expressed concerns that its members were unaware of the subsidy disbursement mechanism and feared they would have to run from pillar to post to recover the amount.

Amid the fuel crisis, the federal government on Thursday also reintroduced austerity measures, including setting 9pm as the closing time for markets and reducing fuel provision for official vehicles by 50 per cent for a period of three months.

World.title: 'Our commitment is unconditional': Amid Houthi attacks, DG ISPR says Pakistan will 'go to any extent' to defend Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said that Pakistan will go to “any extent” to defend Saudi Arabia, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”.

He made the remarks in an interview with Arab News, clips of which were posted on its social media account on X on Friday.

The remarks come as fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis has intensified, with the group making gains along Yemen’s Red Sea coast near the strategic waterway and launching missile and drone attacks on Saudi territory, while Riyadh has stepped up airstrikes against Houthi positions.

This week, the Saudi-led coalition battling the Houthis accused the rebels of targeting the holy city of Makkah, sparking outrage across the Muslim world. However, the Houthis swiftly rejected Riyadh’s report as a “lie”.

“Pakistan fully stands with the kingdom of Saudi Arabia, both diplomatically and physically. And I would like to underscore the word physically,” Lt Gen Chaudhry said in the interview with Arab News.

“We will go to any extent for the security of Haramain Sharifain and the kingdom of Saudi Arabia. To any extent as asked and required by our Saudi brothers,” he said.

“It should be clear that the people of Pakistan stand shoulder to shoulder with their Saudi brothers and sisters. There should be no doubt about it,” he said.

“So, in a nutshell, we are there and will continue to defend the kingdom of Saudi Arabia against any aggression,” he said.

The military’s spokesperson added that Pakistan’s politico-military leadership remained in continuous contact and engagement with the Saudi leadership.

He said that at the same time, Pakistan, “very earnestly and sincerely”, was working with the help of regional countries and others to find a “negotiated, peaceful outcome of this complex situation”.

“That’s where the position of Pakistan is,” he said.

In another clip posted on X, he said Pakistan “remained not only committed, but we are already there for the protection of Haramain Sharifain and the kingdom of Saudi Arabia”.

“We are there to protect them,” he asserted, reiterating that Pakistan would “go to any extent” as required by the Saudi leadership.

“Our commitment to Saudi security is unconditional. It stems from a deep-rooted, historical and unbreakable bond between the people of Pakistan and the people of Saudi Arabia, between the political and the military leadership of both countries,” he said.

“So, nothing stops us. Nothing bars us. Nothing is there which hesitates [sic] our commitment. So, whatever is required, whatever is asked, we will go to any extent for that,” he said.

According to the write-up of the interview, Lt Gen Chaudhry was also asked about the phone call between Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday.

“The politico-military leadership of Pakistan remains in continuous communication with the esteemed leadership of the kingdom of Saudi Arabia on all these matters,” he was quoted as saying by the publication.

Lt Gen Chaudhry added that Islamabad was consulting regional governments to seek “a negotiated and peaceful outcome” to the wider crisis.

He described the Islamabad memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran in June as “a consensus document which we think provides the only real pathway forward for getting out of this complex military situation in which we are’.

According to the publication, asked whether Pakistan expected to bring Washington and Tehran back to negotiations soon, the military spokesperson gave no timetable. He said Islamabad continued to search for common ground despite mistrust, “spoilers” and “detractors”.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

Last month, the countries and Turkiye also signed the Makkah Defence Alliance, which stipulates that an attack on one member state would be treated as an attack on all. Its inaugural meeting was held in Istanbul on Aug 31, where it was decided that Pakistan would initially head the alliance’s secretariat for three years.

Earlier this week, Lt Gen Chaudhry said that the Makkah defence pact had no “regional aspirations” and that it was intended for collective deterrence.

“It is defensive. There’s nothing aggressive. There are no regional aspirations. It is collective deterrence,” he said in an interview with Al Arabiya English.

Meanwhile, Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan on Thursday reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitments to Saudi Arabia’s security, but stressed that the Houthi conflict should be addressed through dialogue and diplomacy rather than through coercive means.

“The Houthis must also stop their activities, and in this regard, our discussions basically revolve around bringing peace and stability through dialogue and diplomacy, and not through coercive measures,” he said.

The FO spokesperson also said that Pakistan was committed “in intent and spirit” to implementing the agreements signed with Saudi Arabia. He nevertheless declined to disclose how Pakistan might respond operationally, saying such decisions involved matters of confidentiality.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
